    the layout, `click --in` each, and a scale-2 + scale-1 layout (fail on the code before).
300. **A window's `-g` and `pixel` read buffer pixels on a scaled monitor** (2026-10-14, found with
    #227). grim takes `-g` with `-T` in the window's buffer pixels, not its own coordinates: on a
    scale-2 monitor `shot --window -g "10,10 300x200"` gave the window's 150x100 at 5,5 as a 300x200
    image, which `click --in` then mapped as 300x200 of the window (clicks off by the scale), and
    `pixel --window X Y` read the window's X/2,Y/2. Since window shots took -g and
    `pixel` windows; unseen at scale 1, the only one boxes had until `--size ...,scale=S`. Both now
    scale the region to the buffer (`win_buf_geom`: each edge at the window's monitor's scale,
    rounded as Hyprland rounds the buffer, inside it), and `--fit` counts the crop at that size.
    t_scale / t_scale_nvidia: a terminal with a red band; `--window -g` against its whole shot's
    crop, `pixel --window` and `pixel --in` against its whole shot, `-g --fit` and `click --in` it
    (fail on the code before).
301. **The box count shrank the bar mark on fitted bar icons** (2026-10-14, #219). Omarchy after 4.0.4
    (omacom/omarchy#15065) fits every widget's `iconComponent` to one icon size: its `BarIconContent`
    measures the union of what the component paints, scales it to `Style.bar.iconSize` (12 px) and
    centres it. The widget's count `Text` sat in a `Row` with the `Mark` there, so with 2+ boxes both
    were scaled: the mark fell from 12 px to 7x8 (1 px strokes), the count to 3x5. Now only the mark
    paints in `iconComponent` (beside it an empty spacer as wide as the count, which a fitting shell
    does not measure, and which keeps 4.0.4's Row centring as it was), and the count is a `Text` on
    the button at the mark's painted right edge: the shell's `componentPaintedWidth` when it has one
    (mark centred), else the 16 px canvas moved left by half the count, rounded as the Row's centring
    rounds (the count on the same pixels as before). On 4.0.4 the mark no longer moves up a pixel
    when the count shows (the Row took the taller text's height). On a fitted shell mark and count are
    not centred together: that shell centres the icon in the button whatever is beside it (its own
    `labelText` goes to the left of the icon). The 8-unit mark fitted to 12 px is 1.5 px a unit, so
    its arms come out 2 and 1 px: whole pixels at 12 px need a glyph of 6 or 12 units. t_widget_mark:
    the widget's ink at 1, 2, 3 and 12 boxes (mark size and place the same, the count after it),
    on `OMABOX_TEST_OMARCHY` when set (fails on the code before, on 4.0.4 and on a #15065 checkout);
    t_unit_omarchy_contract: a fitting shell's `componentPaintedWidth`.
302. **A silent grim failure says how grim ended** (2026-10-14, #217). `shot`'s rare "grim failed"
    under the full suite's load (a second `--monitor` shot, AMD and NVIDIA boxes) came with nothing
    after it. grim's stderr was already kept and added to the message, so grim had said nothing:
    either it ended non-zero silently (`timeout`, `on_box`, a screencopy that sent no buffer) or it
    exited 0 with an empty image. The message now tells those apart ("it gave an empty image", "it
    gave nothing in 10 s", "it ended with status N and said nothing"); grim's own reason is unchanged
    when it gives one. The cause stays open on #217 until the next occurrence names the case.
303. **The Codex guard merges into a config's own `shell_environment_policy.set`** (2026-10-14,
    #221, reported from outside). Our block declares `[shell_environment_policy.set]`, so a config
    that had its own (a documented Codex setting) failed the TOML check and `on` refused, telling the
    user to add the keys by hand; keys merged that way had no markers, so `guard` read `outdated`
    forever. Now, when the table exists, the guard's keys go into it, marked, right under its header
    (`set.KEY` under `[shell_environment_policy]`, `shell_environment_policy.set.KEY` at the top for
    dotted keys); only the keys it lacks, as one with the guard's value is the user's. A key with
    another value is refused by name, never overwritten; an inline table cannot take keys, so it is
    refused with the lines to add. Every result must read back (tomllib) as the config plus the
    guard. All the guard's keys present with its values, unmarked, read as `on`; `on` takes them out
    and puts the marked block in, `off` takes them out. Codex 0.162.1 (`CODEX_HOME` scratch, `codex
    mcp add`): our start marker rides on our first key and the end marker on the next key or table,
    so a block under the header stays put; an empty table at the end leaves our end marker as the
    file's last comment, which Codex keeps last (finding 74), so its new table lands inside the
    markers and `off` keeps it. With dotted `set.KEY`s, Codex groups the user's next to ours, inside
    the markers: `off` keeps every line that is not one of the guard's keys there.
304. **`ls` calls a box nobody will take down an orphan; `down --orphans`** (2026-10-14, #220, reported
    from outside: six leaked `--idle 0` boxes took a desktop's load to ~38). A headless box at `--idle
    0` with no owner and no agent recorded (an agent in a sandbox, a harness without session variables)
    gets no reaper by design, and `ls` showed it as `never`, like a box in use (finding 203 left this
    part of #137 unbuilt). `up` now records the box's starter in box.json (`starter`: pid, start time,
    command, `terminal`), as `box_starter` finds it: the nearest ancestor that outlives the one command,
    skipping a shell given a command string (`bash -c`: each agent tool call, which Claude Code runs in
    a session of its own, so the session leader would be the wrong pick), a script's subshell (its
    command line is its parent's: `$(omabox up)`, the suite's parallel tests) and timeout, flock, time.
    VERIFIED from this Claude Code session: the walk lands on `claude` (its CLAUDE_PID). An orphan
    (`box_orphan`): up, headless, idle 0, no owner, no agent, a starter recorded and gone (pid and start
    time, as `owner_alive`). Decided: a box whose `up` had a terminal on stdin outside any agent session
    is a person's, on purpose: `terminal: true`, never an orphan, so closing the terminal of a forever
    box does not mark it; no starter found (`setsid -f omabox up`, parent gone already) or a box.json
    from before: never one either (unknown is not orphan). Nothing takes an orphan down by itself: `ls`
    says `orphan` under IDLE and names them on stderr, `ls --json` has `orphan` and `starter`, the
    widget's row says it, and `down --orphans` (no names, no `--all`) takes each down as that box
    (`DOWN_IF_CREATED`), naming its starter. `up` at idle 0 with no owner or agent, not at a terminal,
    notes that nothing will take the box down but `down`. t_unit_orphan (the walk's skips, every
    kept case, `down --orphans` with stubs), t_orphan (a starter that exits, one that stays then is
    killed, an idle limit, one under script(1)'s terminal; `down --orphans` skipped when the user has
    orphans of their own up, as it would take those too), t_widget_list's caption.
305. **The pointer out of shots and recordings: `shot`/`record --no-pointer`, `pointer hide|show`,
    `up --no-pointer`** (2026-10-14, #228). Screen shots always had the pointer (finding 82): on a
    still for people it sits on the app, and parked elsewhere it lands on a hover state. Hyprland's
    `cursor:invisible` does leave it out of every frame, on AMD and NVIDIA, at scale 1 and 2 (finding
    172's "set but still drawn" corrected), but two things stood in the way. A config reload sets it
    back (`hyprctl reload`; `omarchy-theme-set` reloads too, `configreloaded`), and the pointer is
    drawn again ~200 ms later without moving. And the frame without it (or with it again) comes 50-400
    ms after the option changes, not at once: a capture right after still has it; neither
    `force_renderer_reload`, a warp to the same spot nor `setcursor` hurried it (a real move does).
    So `ptr_seen` grabs the 64x64 around the pointer, sets the option, and waits (1 s at most) for
    that grab to change; a pointer not drawn (Omarchy's `cursor:hide_on_key_press` after `keys`, or
    off the screens) never changes it, and the second is waited out. `shot --no-pointer` (screen, -g,
    --burst; a window's capture never has it) hides it so, shoots, and puts it back as it was,
    waiting for it drawn (so the next plain shot has it), from an EXIT trap (INT, TERM, HUP exit);
    `record --no-pointer` hides it before wf-recorder starts, until `record stop`. `pointer hide|show`
    and `up --no-pointer` are a box setting (`hide` returns once a frame without it is drawn). What
    keeps it hidden is `$D/pointer` (the box dir: `hidden`, `hold shot PID`, `hold record PID`, `was
    true|false`), changed under a lock of its own: holds of an omabox that is gone are dropped (a
    recording's once `$D/record` is gone too), and once nothing holds it, `cursor:invisible` goes
    back to what it was. The box's config reads `omabox.pointer` (its runtime dir) on every load and
    hides it while that says `hidden`; a box started on an older config is told so by `pointer hide`
    (`omabox reload` takes the new one). Hidden, it still moves and clicks, and focus follows it;
    `wait`, `--changed` and `drag --wait` still leave its rect out (harmless). Decided: `up
    --no-pointer` on a box up and showing it is refused as other options are (`pointer hide` says how);
    `pointer hide|show` on the existing command, not a new one. In tests: a backgrounded `ob` is a
    subshell (signal `$CLI` itself), and a background job of a script starts with INT ignored, which no
    trap undoes (TERM there). t_unit_pointer, t_unit_record (refusals); t_no_pointer and
    t_no_pointer_nvidia, at scale 2 (a shot with and without; drawn again after; hidden over a reload
    and omarchy-theme-set, then show and hide giving the same pixels; focus following a hidden pointer
    between two terminals; TERM during a --no-pointer burst; record --no-pointer's last frame against
    a plain recording's; record start --no-pointer over a reload until stop; up --no-pointer).
306. **`record mark` in the video's own clock; `record stop --sheet` and `record sheet`** (2026-10-14,
    #176). Diogo's 45 s demo (0.5.5) needed a timeline for captions, kept by hand in ms since `record
    start` returned, and five takes, checked through ffmpeg frames, to tune a script whose ~40 omabox
    calls ran ~12 s past its sleeps. The video's clock: wf-recorder (0.6.0) stamps each frame with
    its screencopy `ready` time (Hyprland's `steadyNow()`, CLOCK_MONOTONIC, taken as it copies) less
    the first frame's; the fps pass at `stop` starts at that first frame and shows each frame from
    the output slot nearest its time (so up to half a frame early, never later than its slot).
    Nothing wf-recorder says tells the first frame's time, so it runs with `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client`: a
    reader on its stderr (a process substitution, so the recorded pid stays wf-recorder's) takes the
    first `zwlr_screencopy_frame_v1.ready(HI, LO, NSEC)`, writes it with the wall clock, the
    monotonic clock and the wall clock again (perl's Time::HiRes, which the omarchy package pulls in)
    to `first-frame` in the box, and then hands the rest to `grep -v '^\['` (wf-recorder's own lines
    go on to its log; ~10 debug lines a frame, dropped). `record mark TEXT` appends "WALL_US TEXT" to
    `$D/record.marks`, WALL_US from `$EPOCHREALTIME` at the top of the script (`CALL_US`, before the
    rest is parsed: the moment it was called), and prints its time in the video; `stop` makes them
    ms from the first frame (one before it at 0) into FILE.marks.tsv (ms, wall time as `events` has
    it, text) and FILE.vtt (WebVTT, each cue until the next mark, the last until the end; ffmpeg's
    `subtitles=` filter (libass) burns it in, mpv loads FILE.vtt beside FILE.mp4); no marks removes an
    earlier take's two files. Measured in a scale-2 box on AMD, from the raw frames (before the fps
    pass): a terminal turning red at a time it noted came in the first frame stamped 4, 4 and 19 ms
    after that time, and the frame before it (2 to 12 ms before or after) was never red. So a mark is
    exact to the frame; what lags is the app's drawing. `record mark` itself takes ~55 ms. The sheet:
    ffprobe counts the frames (-count_packets), ffmpeg selects them by number (`select=eq(n,K)+...`,
    times K/fps exact) and scales them in the box, each PNG comes out as bytes, magick montage (as
    `shot --burst --sheet`) labels each "N: T" with, under it, the marks since the tile before ("> T
    TEXT", 37 characters); 15 frames from the first to the last, or one each --every (100 at most), 5
    a row, 320 px tiles, or tiles of --fit/5 and the sheet then fitted (shot-fit by default). `record
    sheet VIDEO` copies the video into the box for that (a box must be up); its marks are VIDEO's
    .marks.tsv. Decided: marks always work (no `start --marks`); the files are named after the video
    (demo.mp4: demo.marks.tsv, demo.vtt, demo.sheet.png), the marks' paths said on stderr so `stop`'s
    stdout stays the video (then the sheet, with --sheet). Still refused for a jailed agent (#224).
    Tests: t_unit_record (refusals; record_marks' TSV and WebVTT, a mark before the first frame,
    escaping, stale files gone); record_marks_on in t_scale and t_scale_nvidia (a mark and a red
    terminal: its first red frame at most a frame early, at most 250 ms late; the TSV, the VTT; a
    6-tile sheet's width and tiles; `record sheet --every 500ms --fit 800` at 800 px).
307. **`on_box` stays out of the box's pid namespace; a kill given to it fails the suite** (2026-10-14,
    #218; the trap: finding 289). `on_box` enters the box's user and mount namespaces only, so a pid
    read from the box's /proc there and handed to `kill` names a host process. Entering the pid
    namespace too (`nsenter -p`) was looked at and kept out, for three reasons: (1) the box's
    processes would see the tool in their /proc and could reach its host fds through `/proc/PID/fd`
    (same uid): `shot`'s grim writes the host's file and `keys --pass` feeds the keyboard a pipe; (2) `nsenter -p` forks, so the
    pid a caller holds (`$!`, `follow_start`'s `pkill -P`) is nsenter's, and killing it would leave the
    command running in the box; (3) `log -f` and `events -f` run `tail --pid=<box PID 1>` with the
    host's number for it. Instead `t_unit_on_box_kill` reads every `on_box` call (and every `nsenter`
    without `-p`) in bin/omabox and share/, with the scripts quoted in it and the heredocs fed to it,
    and fails on `kill`, `pkill` or `killall` there, naming box_exec or `nsenter -p`; a kill after the
    call (`on_box x; kill $p`), a comment, `hl.dsp.window.kill` and `timeout -k` do not count. It
    found none today (74 calls read; under 60 fails, so a broken reader cannot pass on nothing), and
    on a copy with seven kills planted (each form above, `on_box timeout 2 /usr/bin/killall`,
    `$(on_box pkill …)`, `nsenter -U -m -- kill`) it finds each at its kill's line and nothing else.
    No allowlist: no caller has a legitimate kill in on_box.

308. **`--net isolated --addr ADDR`: documentation addresses on the box's loopback** (2026-10-14,
    #229). Some apps judge their network by where a connection comes from: libtorrent (qBittorrent)
    reads "firewalled" until a peer connects from a non-local address, and in an isolated box every
    peer is on 127.0.0.1, so the app shows a warning a real setup would not. Nothing in the box can
    add an address (`ip addr add`: Operation not permitted): pasta makes the user and network
    namespaces, and its child is root there with CAP_NET_ADMIN, but bwrap's own user namespace maps
    the box back to our uid with no capabilities. So `up` adds them in pasta's child, the `sh` that
    opens bwrap's info fd, before it execs bwrap (`ip addr add A/32 dev lo`; IPv6 `/128 nodad`); a
    failure there stops the box, said in box.log. Only RFC 5737's three /24s and RFC 3849's
    2001:db8::/32: no real host has one, so an address on the loopback never hides a real one, and they
    are non-local to libtorrent (it counts 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16 and 127/8 local;
    Python's `ipaddress.is_private` counts the documentation ranges private, so an app judging that way
    is not helped). Given in canonical form (`box_addr`: 203.0.113.010 is .10, IPv6 shortened), sorted
    and each once, so `up` on a box that is up compares them as it does --allow. Isolated only: a
    connected box's addresses are pasta's copy of the host's, and a nested connected one has no pasta to
    add them; the --allow forwards are unchanged (pasta splices them to 127.0.0.1/::1, so a server bound
    only to an --addr address is not reached through them). In box.json and `ls --json` as `addrs`, and
    under the box's line in `ls`. Verified in a box (`t_isolated_addr`): a server on 203.0.113.10 sees a
    client bound to 203.0.113.11 come from .11 (and 2001:db8::a over IPv6), the box still cannot add
    one, the --allow port is forwarded; `t_isolated` checks a box without --addr has only 127.0.0.1/8
    and ::1. Not tried with qBittorrent itself. The unshare recipe the issue used as a workaround is not
    in the skill: --addr covers it.

309. **A throwaway's `up` ends its box once its `run` is gone; a flaky check keeps its frames** (2026-10-14,
    #222). Two checks failed now and then under the full suite's load since NVIDIA boxes' apps draw on
    the GPU: `t_throwaway_killed`'s box took 20-21 s to go (15 s allowed), and `t_wait`'s thin-line
    checks got a last change 3 px high where the underline is 2. Neither reproduced here in 12 loaded
    runs (eight box tests at a time with the throwaway and `t_wait` among them, three runs beside 14
    busy loops, three NVIDIA boxes drawing gears; 180 thin-line waits run beside them, all 2 px).
    What timestamps in `up`, the reaper and `down` showed in every run: the test kills the `run` while
    its `up` is still starting (it looks as soon as `ls` lists the box), and that `up` goes on to the
    end, ~1.5-2.5 s more here, holding the box's lock; the reaper's first look (5 s after the launch)
    finds the run gone and its `down` takes that lock (box gone ~4.5 s after the kill). `down` itself:
    0.2-0.4 s, 18 NVIDIA boxes six at a time beside the busy loops; ups 1-7 s there. So a 20 s case
    needs an `up` ~15 s slower than here, or a PID 1 past `kill_box`'s 10 s (5 s poll + 10 s + the
    retry's 5 s poll is 20 s, which the three 20-21 s failures fit); neither was caught. Some runs also
    showed an `up` dying 0.15 s after the kill and its box left up for the reaper: its stderr is a pipe
    to the dead run, and its first write there was a SIGPIPE, which ends bash with no EXIT trap.
    - *Fixed*: an `up` with --owner checks its owner wherever it waits on the box (`starting_ok`, with
      the box_alive checks of finding 216) and once more before it ends, and on a SIGPIPE (trapped):
      with the run gone it kills the box, its reaper, its dir and its lock itself, then says so (last:
      the say itself may meet the dead pipe); a PID 1 that will not go is left, dead, to the reaper.
      By hand, eight runs killed 0.1-0.8 s after `ls` showed their box: each box gone 0.1-0.3 s later
      (before the PIPE trap, two of eight took 4.8-4.9 s: their `up` had died of the SIGPIPE).
      `t_unit_up_owner_gone` (fails on the old code, which waited out bar_settle's deadline).
    - *To catch the rest next time*: `t_throwaway_killed` keeps, on a failure, a timeline from the kill
      (every 0.25 s: the `starting` file, the reaper's last line in reap.log, which the box dir takes
      with it); a `down` that gave up says `PID 1 (N) still exiting after 10 s (wchan)` there. The
      still tool's `--dump DIR` (`OMABOX_STILL_DUMP`, a path in the box, for `omabox wait` and every
      --wait) keeps the frames before and after the last significant change, cut to it and 4 px
      around, as PPM with where they are in a comment; `t_wait`'s thin-line checks use it and copy
      them into the evidence when the height is not 2. The deadline and the 2 px stay: without the
      frames, a 3rd row has no known legitimate cause (foot's underline is 2 px, the window does not
      move, the screen is at scale 1).
310. **`record --monitor all`: the whole layout in one video** (2026-10-14, #225). wf-recorder captures
    one output, so `record` took one monitor. Now `--monitor all` (start, or `-- ACTION`) starts a
    wf-recorder an output from one `box_exec` (each in `REC_DIR/mN`, its own first-frame reader as in
    finding 306), and `stop` lays them out with ffmpeg in the box: a black `color` source the size of
    the layout as grim's whole-screen shot has it (the monitors' layout box, each side x the highest
    scale, truncated), each recording at its place and size there (`overlay`, `scale` to its size in
    the layout x that scale). Measured: wf-recorder's frames of a turned monitor are already as it is
    shown (transform 1 on AMD and NVIDIA, the flipped 5 on AMD: as a `shot` of it has it), so
    only scaling is needed. In step: the recorders' first-frame screencopy stamps are one
    CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so each is shifted by its first frame less the latest one's (`setpts`), and the
    video starts at that latest first frame (a monitor's frames before it dropped), which is also the
    0 marks are put in (`record_first_us` takes the latest). Each then goes through `fps=N:start_time=0`
    (the frame nearest each slot, as a single recording's pass) before it is laid on, so a slot takes
    every monitor's frame for that slot; the video lasts until the last monitor's recording ends (`-t`
    from ffprobe's durations; a monitor whose recording ended first goes black, `eof_action=pass`; no
    duration known: until the first ends). Started together the first frames came 2-5 ms apart on AMD
    and up to 34 ms on NVIDIA; with the starts made 0.4 s apart by hand (a `sleep` in the loop, taken
    out again) a white flash on three monitors still came in frames 58, 59 and 58, where without the
    shift they would be 12 and 24 frames apart. A change on several monitors at once is in the same
    frame give or take one: each monitor draws on its own vblank, up to 16 ms apart. Even sides
    (4:2:0): one black row or column more when one is odd. Past H.264's largest frame (level 6.2:
    35651584 px; 16384 a side here) the whole is scaled down to fit, said at start with the size
    (`as one 4000x2560 video (the layout at scale 2)`). A 2.5 s 4000x2560 layout took ~1 s at stop
    (flat colours; busy content takes longer). The record is "PID,PID... OUT,OUT... FPS START FILE"
    and the layout as composed `$D/record.layout` (host side); `status` and `stop` check every pid,
    and `stop` INTs each still running. With one monitor left (the others off or 0x0), `all` is that
    monitor's own recording. Decided: `--monitor all` (not a new option: the same place picks the
    output; a monitor named `all` cannot be recorded alone); black gaps (as a shot's are transparent).
    wf-recorder's colours are a little muted (white comes out ~#e7e7e7, the same in a single
    recording): the comparisons allow 48 of 255 (fixed in finding 312: now 8). Tests: t_unit_record (record_layout: a turned
    monitor, a scale-1.6 one, one off and a 0x0 one left out, five 4K at 16384 wide, nine 4K under the
    frame limit); t_record_layout / t_record_layout_nvidia (main 1280x720, a second turned by
    transform 1 with two terminals, a third at scale 2: start and status say 4000x2560; the video
    4000x2560 H.264 30 fps as the shot; its last frame against the shot in 10x8 cells; a white flash
    on all three in the same frame give or take one; a mark before it in the composed clock; a
    3-tile sheet; `-- ACTION`; the m-folders gone; `all` with the main screen alone).

311. **A turned monitor's size in the layout** (2026-10-14, found with #225). Hyprland lays a monitor
    turned a quarter (transform 1, 3, 5, 7: 90 or 270 degrees, flipped or not) out with its sides
    swapped: 1280x720 at transform 1 is 720x1280 in the layout, as grim and xdg-output have it. omabox
    took each monitor's size as its mode over its scale, unturned, everywhere but `record --monitor
    all` (finding 310): with a portrait monitor `extent` was wrong (a 2000x1280 layout read 2560x1080,
    `shot` said "the screen's 2560x1080 (x0.64)" of grim's 4000x2560), so `click`/`pointer` mapped
    absolute coordinates against the wrong size (off by the ratio, or refused below the old height),
    `pixel` refused points there or named the wrong gap, and `shot --monitor` cropped the unturned
    rect (partly black, part of the next monitor). Now one jq definition, `JQ_MON` (`lw`, `lh`: the
    sides swapped for an odd transform), is the only place a monitor's logical sides are computed:
    extent, shot --monitor, --fit's highest covered scale (finding 299), pixel's on-a-monitor check
    and its message, record_layout, and an interactive box's free area on the host monitor
    (desk_relay: a turned host monitor; not tested, this machine has none). Not touched: hyprland.lua's
    placement of `right`/`below` monitors at a reload (omabox sets no transform itself: a `--monitor`
    SPEC has none; one set by hand and a reload were not tried together) and its AQ_WAYLAND_LAYOUT
    file (already swapped); peek and still take xdg-output's logical size. Tests: t_unit_record
    (JQ_MON over transforms 0-7); t_monitors_turned / t_monitors_turned_nvidia (1280x720 main, a
    second turned by transform 1, a third at scale 2 turned by 3: whole shot "4720x2560 image of the
    screen's 2360x1280"; each `shot --monitor` against its crop of the whole shot in 6x10 cells;
    `click --in` each monitor's shot focusing the terminal there; `pointer move` below 720; `pixel`
    there; the gap message's sizes): 20 of their 29 checks failed on the code before.
312. **`record`'s colours: wf-recorder's limited range tagged full** (2026-10-14, found with #225).
    Every recording was muted: #00ff00 came out #0cea0d, white #e8e8e8, black #101010, red #ea0d0e,
    and ffprobe said `yuvj420p` (full range), no matrix. Measured in a box (an opaque foot in four
    bands, the shot exactly #00ff00/#ffffff/#ff0000/#000000): wf-recorder 0.6.0 on ffmpeg 9.0.1, left
    to its own pixel format, logs `yuv420p(pc)` and writes Y 232 for white, 16 for black, green
    143/55/35 (BT.601 *limited* values) in a stream tagged full range; the fps pass copied the tag and
    values through (out.mp4 tagged the same), and everything that reads the tag (ffmpeg, players,
    the contact sheet) took 16-235 as 0-255. Not the fps pass: raw.mkv decodes to the same colours.
    `-F scale=out_range=limited` changes nothing; `-x yuvj420p` or `-F scale=out_range=full` makes it
    write full-range values (white 251 of a #fbfbfb screen, black 0), still BT.601, still untagged
    matrix. `-c libx264rgb` is exact but ~5x the bytes. Now: wf-recorder `-x yuvj420p` (raw.mkv
    ~1.6x the bytes on flat colours), and the fps pass (and each monitor's `scale` in
    record_compose) converts `in_range=full:in_color_matrix=bt601` to limited BT.709 with
    `accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int` (without them red came out 251, with them 253), `setparams` tags
    the frames bt709 (ffmpeg 9 takes primaries and transfer from the frames: `-color_primaries` alone
    left them `unknown`), and the encoder is given the same tags: `yuv420p,tv,bt709,bt709,bt709`,
    which browsers, mpv and ffmpeg read alike. record_compose's black `color` background is tagged
    too: untagged, `overlay` converted each monitor to BT.601 for it and green came out 0,214,0. The
    contact sheet's `scale` (its in_color_matrix `auto`) reads the tags: a sheet tile of the bands is
    #00fe00/#fdfdfd/#fc0000/#000000. A decoded middle frame now: 0,254,0 / 255,255,255 / 253,0,0 /
    0,0,0; a whole composed frame against a shot, 0.4-1% mean error. Videos made before keep their
    wrong tag (re-tagging one with `setparams=range=tv` before a `scale` did not mend it in ffmpeg
    9: not pursued). Tests: `record_colours_on` in
    t_scale / t_scale_nvidia (the four bands at scale 2, recorded a second: the tags, the screen's
    pixels, a middle frame within 3 a channel; on the code before: 13,237,13 235,235,235 238,14,13
    16,16,16 and the tags `yuvj420p,pc,unknown,...`, 2 of its checks failed in each); t_record_layout's
    last-frame cells now within 8 of 255, not 48. Upstream (wf-recorder or ffmpeg 9's buffersink
    range negotiation): a yuv420p stream tagged pc with limited values.
313. **Audio in a box: `up --audio`, `record --audio`, `omabox audio`** (2026-10-14, #226). A box had
    no sound (PipeWire's sockets masked under `--systemd`, finding 61), so an app's sound went
    nowhere and videos were silent. `up --audio` starts the box's own `pipewire`, `wireplumber` and
    `pipewire-pulse` in share/session.sh (after the keyring, before Hyprland; wireplumber and the
    pulse server once `pipewire-0` is there), logging to `~/audio.log` (`omabox log audio`), with
    two drop-ins written into the box HOME each start (share/audio/): a null sink `omabox-speaker`
    (`support.null-audio-sink`, Audio/Sink), the default output, and `omabox-mic` (Audio/Source/Virtual,
    silent), the default input, so a pulse app that opens the default mic gets silence rather than the
    speaker's monitor; WirePlumber's alsa, bluez, v4l2 and libcamera monitors disabled. `up` waits
    (10 s) until the box's pulse server says those two are the defaults, else the box goes (as any
    failed up). Packages: pipewire, wireplumber, pipewire-pulse, pactl (libpulse); missing ones are
    named. Safety, checked: the box's `/run/user/$UID` is its own (its `pipewire-0` another inode than
    the host's), no `/dev/snd` (bwrap's `--dev`), no system bus, the session starts from `env -i`, and
    the host's PipeWire (`pw-cli ls Client`, a read-only query) had no client whose pid `omabox
    which` puts in the box while one played and recorded. WirePlumber logs its missing system bus
    and logind; pipewire its rtkit (no realtime: fine for a null sink). The box's bar (quickshell)
    joins as a client, its volume widget on the null sink. With `--systemd` the masked sockets stay
    masked and the three are started by hand all the same (checked: one of each, the defaults set).
    `record --audio`: not wf-recorder's `-a`. Arch's wf-recorder 0.6.0 has only the Pulse backend
    (no `--audio-backend=pipewire`), and it starts its audio reader after its first frame and stamps
    the first samples 0, as that frame is, whenever they came. Instead an ffmpeg in the box reads
    `omabox-speaker.monitor` through pipewire-pulse into REC_DIR/audio.mka (FLAC), started before the
    wf-recorders (`record start` waits, 5 s at most, for its first samples), INT at stop with them.
    ffmpeg's pulse input stamps packets with the wall clock less the stream's latency (`wallclock`,
    on by default) and its log says the input's `start:`; `stop` takes the samples by their own count
    (`asetpts=N/SR/TB`: the stamps themselves drift ~3% against the count early on, a time filter
    settling), delays them by silence (`adelay`) or cuts them (`atrim`) by that start less the
    video's first frame (record_first_us, finding 306), pads them (`apad`) and ends with the video
    (`-shortest`); AAC 192k, in the fps pass or as the last input of record_compose (`--monitor all`;
    its `-t` moved after that input: before it, it was the audio's input option and the video never
    ended). Measured with a paced stream (perl writing 10 ms chunks on the clock into `pw-cat
    --latency 480`, started before) that turns from silence to a 1 kHz tone as its terminal turns red,
    the tone's first sample against that moment in the video's clock (a mark just before it):
    +11 to +15 ms (pw-cat's own 10 ms buffer among them) over 4 takes by hand and 6 in the suite's,
    one monitor and `--monitor all`; 30 s into a take, +8 ms as at its start (no drift). With ffmpeg's default fragment size it
    was -21 to +19 ms (the first take of a fresh box early); `-fragment_size 1920` (10 ms) made it
    steady. A tone from `pw-play` started at the change comes ~60 ms after it: the player's own start.
    `omabox audio [SECONDS] [--json]` (3 s): ffmpeg in the box reads the monitor for SECONDS from now,
    `astats` per 100 ms (peak, RMS, dBFS); the null sink gives exact zeros while nothing plays, so a
    window above -70 dBFS is a sound. Text: "sound for 1.1s of 2.5s: peak -21.1 dBFS, RMS -24.5 dBFS
    while it sounded; at 0.4-1.5s" or "silence for 3s"; `--json` adds every window. ffmpeg's `-t`
    goes by the pulse stamps and let 7 windows through for 0.5 s: the windows are cut to SECONDS'
    worth. Decided: a silent mic as the default input (not none, not the speaker's monitor); `audio`
    exits 0 for silence too (the answer is in its text and `sound`); `--audio` is set at `up` (a box
    without it is refused by `record --audio` and `audio`, and `up --audio` on it says so). A box
    without `--audio` is as before (no PipeWire; t_main checks). Not tried: an interactive `--audio`
    box (the same session.sh path), ScreenCast now that a box can have PipeWire (finding 148). Not
    guarded: a box app pointed by hand at a host Pulse TCP server (`PULSE_SERVER=tcp:127.0.0.1:...`,
    off by default) would reach it through a connected box's loopback, with or without `--audio`.
    Tests: t_audio (the devices, no /dev/snd, its own socket, the host's PipeWire with no client from
    it, `audio` silence and a 1 s tone, two takes: one monitor and `--monitor all`, H.264+AAC, the
    tone within 50 ms of its moment and of the first red frame give or take one); t_main (no audio:
    refusals, no pipewire); t_unit_record (`mark --audio`, `audio 0`).

314. **`shot --burst` through one capture client: `tools/burst`** (2026-10-14, #196). Finding 249's
    cause was a grim a frame: Hyprland 0.56 keeps a screencast session per client and source and posts
    `screencast`/`screencastv2` `>>1` at its first frame and `>>0` once 500 ms pass without one (its
    `m_shareStopTimer`), so a client that stays is four events however many frames it takes, while
    the frames come under 500 ms apart. `omabox-burst` (bound at `/opt/omabox/bin` like still; refuses
    outside a box) takes the whole burst in one client and streams it to the CLI on stdout (`frame I T
    LEN`, then LEN bytes of PNG; the CLI writes the files, the box none). It takes grim's arguments
    (`-l`, `-g`, `-T`, `-s`) and makes the image with grim 1.5's own render and PNG code (MIT, credited
    in the file), so a frame of a still scene is grim's shot byte for byte: seen for the screen, -g,
    --fit, --monitor and --window (and its -g, --fit) at scale 1, at scale 2, and on a layout with a
    turned monitor and a turned scale-2 one, AMD and NVIDIA. The screen is wlr-screencopy's plain copy
    of each output -g touches (it redraws the output, never waits); ext-image-copy-capture's frames
    after the first wait for the next render, which an idle box never does. A window is one
    ext-image-copy-capture session (grim's toplevel path, its frames' first one dropped and 100 ms
    waited, finding 81's priming), each frame nudged by a plain copy of every output, since a window's
    frame is filled at its monitor's next render. A whole output, not a pixel: Hyprland keeps a region's
    session for the next frame only at scale 1 (`getManagedSession` compares the asked box with the
    one it scaled), so a 1x1 region of a scale-2 monitor was a new session, four events, a frame (an
    upstream bug, not filed). Measured in boxes: a 20-frame burst of one monitor posts 4 events
    (grims: 80), a window burst on three monitors 10-16 (the window's four, four for each monitor
    whose nudge got its copy in); 30 frames of a 100x100 crop back to back in 0.44 s, a 1920x1080
    screen ~25 ms a frame. Beside t_burst's 40 ms Timer and 10 ms handler, a 30-frame burst back to
    back shows 12 of its steps in 0.44 s (the grims: 0, every frame the same). `--every 0` is safe
    now, but the default stays 100 ms (decided): 12 frames back to back are 0.15 s of a crop, over
    before an `--after` action (an omabox of its own) has landed: `--burst 12 --diff --after -- keys -t
    xyz` on a foot crop, back to back, showed no change in its 0.15 s (the README's and skill's example
    is that shape). The repeated-frames line says only "nothing new
    drawn between them". A box started without the tool (an install from before) takes a grim a
    frame as before and says so. A window gone mid-burst: `frame N failed: the window is gone`; one
    resized: the frame asked again at its new size. The burst's own frames keep the layout of its
    start (an output unplugged mid-burst is left empty, one added is not in it). The tool ends when
    the CLI does: a pipe's writing end polls POLLERR once its reader is gone. Tests: t_burst (a frame
    of a still scene equal to the shot: screen, -g, window, window -g --fit; 4 events for a 20-frame
    burst; the Timer at half its own pace or more at `--every 0`, which the grims failed at 0-1 steps;
    the repeated-frames line), t_scale / t_scale_nvidia (--fit, -g --fit, window, window -g --fit at
    scale 2), t_monitors_turned / _nvidia (whole, each turned monitor, -g across them, a window on the
    turned scale-2 one, its --fit; a window burst on three monitors 16 events at most), t_unit_wait
    (the tool refuses outside a box).
315. **`up --desk-shell`: the desk's whole shell in a box** (2026-10-14, #206). Checking a bar widget
    against a real desk (a bar plugin that re-hosts other widgets, plugins reading their own files
    beside `shell.json`) took a `--plugin` per installed plugin, the unfiltered `shell.json` and those
    files written into the box HOME by hand (`--seed` refuses anything in `~/.config/omarchy` but
    `plugins/` and `themes/`, finding 228), then `restart-shell`; that mirror found two bugs the
    filtered one-plugin box did not. `--desk-shell` does it: every plugin in the desk's `plugins/`
    (one with no manifest or an id that is not a name, or one refuse_src keeps out, skipped and said:
    what omabox adds by itself is skipped, what the user names refused), mounted or linked as
    `--plugin`'s; a `--plugin` of the same id wins (a working copy). `shell.json` goes in as the
    desk's, only `idle` held off (finding 10: no real input); the desk's plugins are where it has them
    and one it has off stays off, `plugin_status` `disabled` with no warning. The other files: Omarchy's
    manifest declares no config files (its settings are inline in `shell.json`, the shell README's
    "Storage rules"), so no allow-list could come from it; a deny-list instead (decided), over
    everything but what seed_home makes (`shell.json`, `plugins/`, `themes/`, `backgrounds/`,
    `branding/`, `extensions/`): never `hooks/` (the user's scripts), nor a name that is a secret's
    (`api-keys.env`, any `.env`, anything naming a key, token, secret, password, credential, auth,
    cookie, session or private, `.pem`, `.gpg`, `id_*`...; a folder so named with all in it), a git
    dir, a backup (`*.bak*`, `~`); nor a file whose content gives a key, token, secret or password a
    value, holds a private key or a token-shaped string (GitHub, GitLab, Slack, OpenAI/Anthropic,
    AWS); regular files only, 1 MiB each, 16 MiB and 1000 files in all, 8 folders deep. A link is
    followed only to a file inside the folder (the target's path checked as its own: a `x.json` linked
    to `api-keys.env` stays out); one out of it, to a folder, or dangling is not. They are copies
    (the box's writes stay in it), made last, links on the way cleared (finding 168). `up` says what
    went in and every file left out with why; `ls --json` has `desk_shell` (config, plugins, copied,
    skipped) and `bar: "desk"`. Refused with `--stock-bar` and inside ai-jail (the desk is the
    user's, outside the jail). The suite's fake desk: `OMABOX_DESK_CONFIG=DIR` stands in for
    `~/.config/omarchy` (never the user's in a test). Tests: t_unit_desk_shell (what is copied and
    skipped and why on a fixture with planted secrets, names and contents, the caps, desk_plugins,
    the refusals), t_desk_shell (a box on the fake desk: three plugins, two loaded where its
    `shell.json` has them, the off one off unsaid; its `shell.json` key kept, idle held off; the
    plugin's JSON and folder in the box; no secret, link target, hook or git dir; plugins
    read-only). Not run on the real desk (26 plugins): the selection is said at `up`, to check there.
316. **`omabox calibrate`: the shot size a model reads click points at** (2026-10-14, #188; the last
    part finding 251 left). Whether `click X Y` off a full-size shot lands depends on the model and
    its harness (Haiku 4.5 read points 0.76x), and neither omabox nor the agent knows which it runs
    under. `calibrate` draws a test card the size of a full shot of the box (layout x the highest
    scale, as `shot` takes it, finding 299; asked through omabox's own `hyprctl`, so a jailed agent's
    goes by its broker; 1920x1080 with no box up, `--size WxH` for another): six red crosses in rings,
    A-F, one in each cell of a 3 x 2 grid at a random point of its middle, letters shuffled, on plain
    grey. Drawn on the host with magick (no box, ~0.15 s): a box's card window would have been a shot
    of the same pixels, slower. The marks go in the PNG's comment, which the model is not shown; the
    card goes to `$TMPDIR/omabox-calibrate-<default name>.png` (or CARD), so `calibrate --answer "A
    X,Y ..."` finds it without being told. The answer (lenient: case, colons, brackets, decimals; at
    least 3 marks) is fitted by least squares through the origin (a harness scales, it does not
    shift), over the marks near the median of every X and Y ratio, so one misread mark does not drag
    it, and every mark is checked against the result to within max(8, longest side / 160) px (12 on
    1920): all within at 1:1 is "read 1:1"; a consistent scale S < 1 gives `--fit N`, N = S x the
    longest side to the nearest 8 (0.758 of 1920: 1456), with the error of those readings mapped back
    as `click --in` would, the `omabox config shot-fit N` to suggest (the user's setting: printed,
    never set; "already" when it is) and a check card (`--size 1456x819` should read 1:1); marks off
    the scale (a swap names the two), x and y at different scales, or a scale above 1 are "no single
    scale fits", exit 1: a new card and another read, else points off shots are not reliable there.
    **A real run** (Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, reading the card with its Read tool): a 1920x1080 card
    read exactly (every mark within 0 px: 1:1). A 3840x2160 card was shown at 2000x1125 with
    Claude Code's "multiply coordinates by 1.92" note: following it read 1:1 (within 2 px); the
    raw readings in the image shown gave 0.521x and `--fit 2000` (2000x1125), exactly the size
    Claude Code had scaled it to. Haiku was not run here (the issue's table is the evidence for it).
    Tests: t_unit_calibrate (the marks: letters, margins, spread, seeds; the card's size, comment and
    each cross's red at its point; the fitting: 1:1, 0.758x, 0.5x, 4K at 0.379x, a portrait card,
    noise within and beyond the tolerance, a swapped pair, x and y apart, above 1; the answer's forms
    and refusals; the command's verdicts and exit codes, nothing set); scale_on (t_scale,
    t_scale_nvidia): the card is the size of a scale-2 box's shot, and of a scale-2 + scale-1 layout's.
317. **`omabox tree`: a window's accessibility tree as text, query-first** (2026-10-14, #178; the
    build finding 244 decided, on the a11y bus finding 264 starts). **A C helper, not python-gobject**:
    `tools/tree` (`omabox-tree`, bound read-only at `/opt/omabox/bin` like tools/burst, refusing
    outside a box) against libatspi and GIO. libatspi comes with at-spi2-core, which gtk3 and gtk4
    pull in (Omarchy has both), so it adds no runtime package; python-gobject is only there through
    other packages (nautilus-python, udiskie...), not Omarchy's own. Build deps: at-spi2-core (its
    headers), glib2, pkgconf (install.sh's PKGS). `tree` runs it by `box_exec` (the box's session bus
    and pid numbering): the window is `--window SEL` (default the active one), its pid as Hyprland has
    it is the AT-SPI application's (finding 244), the frame is the one named as the window's title
    (else one whose name and the title hold each other, else the application's only one); the
    applications of that pid with nothing under them are skipped (Qt's empty first registration).
    Before reading, the helper asks `org.a11y.Bus.GetAddress` (no bus: exit 4, "down and up again",
    so an AT-SPI client never aborts on a missing bus, finding 244's `dbind-ERROR`) and sets
    `org.a11y.Status.IsEnabled` when it is off, then waits up to 3 s for the pid's application to
    register again: a Qt Quick app started before the first `tree` answered on the first call. Set by
    `tree`, not at `up`: a box nobody asks keeps Qt (the shell too) with accessibility off. Output as
    the spike's compact form (role, "name", 'text', =value, [states], @X,Y WxH in window coordinates,
    anonymous containers, hidden nodes, a control's own label and nodes wholly outside the window's
    size left out; `--all` keeps them; at most 4000 nodes, 500 children a node). `--find TEXT`: only
    the lines whose role, name, text, value or states hold TEXT (any case; the bounds are not
    searched), each after its printed ancestors joined by ` > ` (the window itself left out); exit 1
    when none. `--json`: an array of the printed nodes (with `path` under --find). No tree: "no
    accessibility tree" with the reason (not on the bus: foot; on it with no window: Quickshell) and
    which apps have one, exit 1; a Chromium/Electron window that shows only its frame gets the
    `--force-renderer-accessibility` note. **Checked in boxes** (NVIDIA, renderD129): the GTK4
    and Qt Quick demos of the spike, Chromium with and without the flag, foot; a GTK4 window in a
    scale-2 box (bounds and `click --window` both in logical pixels: the click checked the box).
    ~0.1-0.25 s a call. **Left**: `click --name TEXT` (#178's item 4; with the dock-widget check);
    an unnamed control beside its label (a GTK4 switch after "Wi-Fi") is found by its role, not the
    label's text (no labelled-by relation in the demo to follow). t_tree (Qt Quick before any `tree`:
    IsEnabled off, then on, `--find` a check box's and a switch's state and an entry's text, a click
    at the bounds' middle checks it; GTK4: the whole tree's frame at 0,0 and a selected row under its
    list, `--find`'s path, `--json`, the click, a `--find` matching nothing; foot: no tree, exit 1;
    a missing window), t_unit_pointer's loop (`omabox-tree` refuses outside a box), the broker
    lets a jailed agent run it.
318. **A shot grim gives no image for is taken once more** (2026-10-14, #217; finding 302 made the
    message say how grim ended). The next occurrence, in the batch-3 full suite (t_monitors, AMD
    box, the second `shot --monitor HEADLESS-3` right after one that worked), said "grim failed: it
    gave an empty image": grim ended 0 having written nothing. t_monitors passed alone twice after.
    So a shot whose grim ends 0 with an empty file now waits 0.1 s and captures once more; a second
    empty image fails as before. Not for a jailed caller's `--to-fd` shot (its fd cannot be checked
    for size here). Why grim writes nothing is not known (Hyprland's log shows screencopy binding
    normally); not reproducible on demand, so the retry has no test of its own.
319. **`record`'s polish: input drawn into the video, a gliding pointer, still stretches cut**
    (2026-10-14, #176; findings 297, 306). The issue's scope: "...and it can record what it did,
    cleanly", grown from `docs/demo.sh`, not a video editor. Three pieces, all at `record stop` (or
    `record ... -- ACTION`), on what the recording already has:
    - **Where the input comes from.** Hyprland's events (`omabox events`) carry no clicks or keys,
      and the box can write its own events.log. What peek draws (finding 85) is omabox's own record
      of its commands, in the box dir, out of the box's reach; while a box records, `mark()` also
      writes each line to `$D/record.input` with the wall-clock times the command began and ended
      (`rec_input`; a pointer line has the tool's whole sequence, every step of a glide, where peek
      gets the moves as asked; `--pass` is its length there too). 4 MB at most. `run`'s app moving
      its own windows is not input, by design.
    - **`--show-input` / `--captions`** draw it with ffmpeg's `ass` filter (libass, in the box, at the
      end of the pass that already makes the video: no second encode): `record_overlay` writes an ASS
      script in video pixels, peek's look (accent #ff3cc8, its ring sizes, caption plates with the
      accent edge, 1.5 s caption merging, 3 s fade), times in finding 306's video clock. libass
      drawings make the rings (an annulus is two circles wound opposite ways; `\an7` puts a drawing's
      0,0 at `\pos`, `\an5` centres its bounding box instead and was 12 px off), `\move` a ring moving,
      BorderStyle 3 the plates (two layers: the accent box 2 px larger under the dark one, as peek
      draws them). Text is UTF-8 (peek's font is ASCII); `{` `}` become their wide forms and a
      zero-width space follows each backslash (ASS reads them as override blocks and `\n` breaks).
      Timing: a pointer line's span starts with the tool connecting (tens of ms), so shared out from
      its start the ring lagged the real cursor by ~2 glide steps; anchored at its end (40 ms a move,
      30 a click, ~10 ms tail) it sits on the cursor in every frame checked. In a layout video the
      captions go on the main screen's part (centred on the whole, they fell into the black gaps).
    - **`--glide DURATION`** on click, pointer and drag (and `record start --glide`, the default
      while it records): `glide_to` sends smoothstep-eased moves, one each 40 ms (the tool's own wait
      after a move), so ~25 positions a second. Without it nothing changes for agents.
    - **`--cut-idle [DURATION]`** cuts every still stretch longer than DURATION to DURATION.
      freezedetect at its default -60 dB counts a typed character or a caret as still (a 10x20 px
      change in 1280x720 is ~1e-4 of the frame), so input is "something happening" from its own
      record, with --show-input for the 3 s it is drawn; marks split stretches (so one after a cut
      lands on its frame); with sound, silencedetect's non-silence counts too (a 0.5 s tone in a
      still gap was kept, in place). Whole frames go (`select` on frame numbers, `setpts=N/FRAME_RATE/TB`),
      the sound by the same times (`atrim` + `concat`); marks and VTT are shifted by the frames cut
      before them. The first pass is encoded at crf 12 then, so the second (crf 18) loses little.
    Checked in a box (`t_record_input`, 1280x720 at scale 2): the ring's accent at the click point
    just after it and not before; the keys' caption against the frame before with record_overlay's
    caption drawn on it (7e-5 of the area off; with the --pass in clear it would be 80x that), the
    box dir's input with `secret 7`, never the value; a 1 s glide's pointer rising through 15+ frames
    over 0.6 s+; a 5 s gap cut by 4.00 s, the mark after it within a frame of its change. By hand: a
    two-monitor layout (the ring on the scale-2 monitor's cursor, captions on the main screen), and
    `--audio` with a cut.

320. **Review of the 0.6.0 run: four fixes** (2026-10-14; a code review of 2d28a4a..99aa9d9, high
    effort, every finding). (1) `record --no-pointer -- ACTION` (finding 305) released its hold from
    the traps `ptr_hold_until_exit` sets when a Ctrl-C or TERM ended this omabox during the action:
    the recording went on (kept, as documented) with the pointer back in every frame until `record
    stop`. Once `record_start` returned the hold is the recording's, so the traps are cleared there
    for both shapes, not only for a plain `start`; t_no_pointer ends an action with a TERM and finds
    the box still recording with the pointer hidden until `record stop`. (2) `record_overlay`'s
    pointer-line parser (finding 319) added the previous step's time once more for each `scroll`,
    `hscroll`, `source` and `pause` token, so a ring arrived 40 ms early for each of them (a drag
    with `--shot` pauses, a scroll after a move); those tokens take no time now (unit check at 3.06
    s where it drew 3.02). (3) `desk_content_refused` (finding 315) took any key whose name
    *contained* token, secret, password... before a colon, so a plugin's `"maxTokens": 4`,
    `"tokenizer"` or `"password_hint_shown"` kept its config out of a `--desk-shell` box with only a
    line in the skipped list. The key must end in the word now and the value be 6+ characters
    (`hunter2` still refused; `"token": ""` not), and a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer ...`,
    16+ chars) is its own pattern since `bearer` is 6 letters before a space. Not seen on the real
    desk (the check of 61e481c, same day: nothing refused by content). (4) `tools/tree` popped its
    printed-ancestor path for every printed node, pushed only up to MAX_DEPTH (64): past 64 printed
    levels a pop freed an ancestor's slot and every later `--find` path lost an ancestor. The pop
    now mirrors the push. Reported and left: `record_running` reads a 0.5.x record file (4 fields)
    into the 0.6.0 layout, which matters only for a recording running across the upgrade (Diogo:
    nobody has one); `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client` stays on for a recording's whole life for one `ready`
    line, and the mark clock depends on libwayland's trace format (finding 306; `tools/burst` could
    stamp the first frame itself); the contact-sheet montage exists in `record_sheet` and
    `shot_burst` both.

321. **`record` for a jailed agent** (2026-10-14, #224). `record` refused a jailed agent (finding 297):
    its files would be written at paths the jail names, which the broker never opens (finding 99).
    Now it goes as `shot --to-fd` does: every file is the jail's, made by the jail's own omabox
    (relay_record) as a temp beside where it goes, filled by the broker through the fd passed, and
    renamed into place once whole (removed on any failure). `start -o FILE` is resolved in the jail
    (and checked writable there) and reaches the broker as `--as NAME`, only a name: nothing is made,
    opened or looked at there (record.as in the box dir says so). `stop` asks the broker the name
    (`status --file`), opens the video, marks and captions beside it in the jail and passes them
    (`--to-fd`, `--marks-fd`, `--vtt-fd`, with `--as NAME`, refused unless it is the recording's,
    before anything is stopped); the video streams from the box's `cat` into the fd, the marks and
    captions are made in a folder of the box dir's (the jail has no way in) and copied in. `record
    sheet VIDEO` passes the video and its marks to read (`--from-fd`, `--marks-from-fd`) and the
    sheet to write; the video at most 4 GiB (its copy in the box is on the host's disk, and a sparse
    file costs the jail nothing), the marks 1 MiB. `record -- ACTION` and `stop --sheet` are run by
    the jail's omabox as their steps (start, the action relayed as any command, stop; stop, then
    sheet), so the broker refuses an action (its paths, like `click --in`, would be read here). A
    jailed recording stopped from outside the jail is written to a new file in `$TMPDIR`, never at the
    jail's name (said). Every fd is checked without opening anything (fd_file, which `shot --to-fd`
    now uses too): a regular file (a folder, socket, FIFO or device refused: a FIFO's read or write
    could wait for ever), open for reading or for writing as it is used (from fdinfo's flags; O_PATH
    refused), not on one of the kernel's filesystems (procfs, sysfs, cgroups...: some act on a write
    with the writer's rights, the broker's more than the jail's), each fd once. Bounds on what the
    broker reads of the box's files, which the box's processes can replace (by a link to /dev/zero
    too): the first-frame stamp 200 bytes, a sheet frame 64 MiB; and on marks, 1000 characters each
    and 1 MiB a recording (the box dir is in the runtime dir, memory). Tests: t_unit_record (the
    refusals and each kind of fd, before any box), t_jail_record (the broker's side with a stand-in
    jail: a name's folder never made, a link out of the project never followed, a wrong name and a
    read-only fd refused with the recording still running, the files only in the fds; then a real
    ai-jail 2.8.1: start -o ./demo.mp4, mark, stop, `-- ACTION --frames 2`, `sheet`, a take without
    marks dropping the earlier ones, -o through a link to a read-only folder refused in the jail, a
    broker-folder name given straight to the relay never written, an action given straight to it
    refused). Its fd checks and bounds were redone after a review: finding 322.
322. **omabox's own steps in a box: by their paths, bounded on the host; only the fds given** (2026-10-14,
    review of #224). box_exec runs a command with the box session's PATH, which has the box HOME's
    ~/.local/bin first, and its environment from omabox.env in the box's runtime dir: both are the
    box's processes' to write, which is right for `run` (the user's command, as the session has it)
    and not for the steps omabox takes in a box whose output it reads or keeps. Those now go through
    box_sys (BOX_SYS=1): the command by its full path, PATH=/usr/bin, an environment of the box HOME,
    the runtime dir, the Wayland, Hyprland and session bus names only, in the box HOME (/usr and /etc
    in a box are the host's, read-only). `record` (all its steps), `clip`'s, `up`'s bus checks;
    `run -d`'s launcher names its own steps by path (the command still on the session's PATH), as
    `wait cmd`'s timeout, `up`'s eglinfo (in the session's environment, as an app gets it). A box's
    files stay the box's to swap (a link to /dev/zero, a FIFO), so what the host reads of them it
    bounds on its side of the pipe, as clip did: box_copy (record's video and sheet frames) takes a
    regular file the box has the blocks for (not sparse), no more bytes than its size then, and
    checks that many came; every capture of a helper's answer is cut (`head -c`), hyprctl's at 64
    MiB, `hyprctl version`'s, a job's exit status and the last lines of its log too. The sheet's
    frames are in a folder of the box dir, gone with this omabox however it ends (a trap) and with
    the box; the video's .part too. box_exec passes only the fds a command is given: stdin, stdout,
    stderr, its --pass fd, ns_held's stderr and what a caller names (BOX_KEEP: `run -d`'s and `record
    start`'s fd 3); fds_only closes the rest before nsenter. (`omabox run -- CMD 3<FILE` no longer
    hands fd 3 in.) For #224 too: fd_file takes filesystems by an allow-list (FD_FS: ext4, btrfs, xfs,
    tmpfs, ...), not a deny-list, so an anonymous inode (eventfd, timerfd, pidfd: they say they are
    regular files) or a FUSE file is refused; a jail's marks are read in 10 s at most; `status --file`
    and a jailed stop take only a jail's recording (record.as), a recording the user started on the
    jail's box stays the user's (its file not named to the jail); record.as is written before the
    recording's record. Tests: t_unit_record (an eventfd refused), t_jail_record (a head, cat, sh,
    bash, stat and ffprobe planted in the box HOME pouring 50 MB of zeros: a jailed recording
    stopped outside the jail and a sheet through fds still come out whole and their own size, no
    folder left in the box dir; a box command gets fds 0-2 only with fd 7 open on the host, `run -d`
    still its pid; the user's recording neither named to nor stopped by the jail).
323. **What omabox copies out of a box: a fixed cap, a time, a disk** (2026-10-14, re-check of #224).
    box_copy's "not sparse" rule (blocks on disk cover the size) bounds the copy by what the box
    reserved, not what it wrote: `fallocate -l 64M` reports all 64 MiB of blocks at once, and on btrfs
    (this machine's box HOMEs) a reflinked copy does too. So every box_copy now takes a MAX: REC_MAX
    for a video, 16 GiB (an hour of 4K at 36 Mbit/s; a screen's video is mostly far less), past which
    `stop` says so and keeps the video in the box (not cut); `record sheet`'s video into a box takes
    the same cap (was 4 GiB); a sheet frame 16 MiB. $OMABOX_RECORD_MAX lowers it (the suite's). Its
    `cat` runs under a timeout of 10 s plus the size at 10 MiB/s, so a file swapped for a FIFO after
    the stat ends. A jailed recording stopped outside the jail goes to ~/.cache/omabox/records
    ($XDG_CACHE_HOME), on disk, not $TMPDIR (memory on most machines). FD_FS takes no network
    filesystem (nfs, smb2, ecryptfs were on it): a hard mount whose server is gone blocks a read or
    write for ever. Tests: t_jail_record (a fallocated 64 MiB file past a 1 MiB cap refused, said; a
    FIFO behind a stat that says a file given up in 10 s; a stop past OMABOX_RECORD_MAX=2000 refused,
    nothing written, the video kept in the box; the outside stop's file in the cache folder).

324. **#224 after its rebase onto 0.6.0: main's new helpers by path, and a third review** (2026-10-14).
    Rebased onto 41dd4f7 (findings 321-323 were 313-315 on the branch), the three commits squashed
    into one: each conflicted in the same `record` code. What 0.6.0 added to `record` after the
    branch forked (the sound's ffmpeg, the overlay's ffprobe and copy, `--cut-idle`'s ffmpeg and mv,
    `omabox audio`, `omabox tree`'s timeout) ran through `box_exec`, on the box's PATH: all of it goes
    through `box_sys` now, by path, what it prints read back bounded (finding 322's rule). With that
    `record` checks `/usr/bin/wf-recorder` and `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` exist, not the caller's PATH (a
    wf-recorder in /usr/local/bin passed the check and failed in the box). A third review of the
    branch (`/code-review`, after the two of finding 322-323) found: `relay_record` kept `-b NAME`
    for itself (its `pre`), so a jail with two boxes recorded the default one and the stop then
    failed: `-b` goes to the broker for start, stop and sheet (unit check through a relay that prints
    its arguments); `record_start` named the user's file to a jailed caller ("is recording already,
    to FILE") where status and stop mask it; `record_mark` took a jail's marks into the user's
    recording; a failed copy into the box for `record sheet` left `sheet-PID.mp4` in the box HOME
    (a 16 GiB sparse file from a jail filled the disk and stayed); `box_exec`'s own-helper
    environment read omabox.env three times a call (once now; `record stop` asks every 100 ms); and
    the jail-side placing of a video, its marks and a sheet set the umask's mode while a shot stayed
    at mktemp's 0600: `jail_place` does all four the same way (a jailed shot is 0644 under the usual
    umask now, as a file made there would be).

325. **A box command's stdio is never a file of the host's** (2026-10-14, security; found by the #218
    subagent, written up privately that day, finished on Diogo's word). The box's pid namespace is
    the command's: every process in the box sees it in /proc, and as the same uid opens
    `/proc/PID/fd/N` afresh, whatever mode it likes (a read-only fd of a file opens for writing).
    So a host file the caller gave `omabox run` as stdin or stdout (`> hostfile`, `< hostfile`),
    the caller's own terminal, a video being copied into the box for a sheet, or the jail's file
    behind a `--to-fd` was reachable from any box process while the command ran: read and written,
    though the box mounts none of it. Since 0.1.0; an agent's harness that keeps a tool's output in
    a file exposed that file to the box on every `run`. The other fds a caller left open (a lock, a
    directory fd: the way out of the box through `..`) went in too until finding 322's `fds_only`.
    Now (`stdio_relay`, in `box_exec`): each of the command's stdin, stdout and stderr that is a
    file, a directory, a terminal or a device but /dev/null (`fd_exposed`: a pipe or a socket is as
    safe as it gets, nothing of the host's is behind it) is relayed through a pipe held on the host,
    a `cat` each side of the namespace: the box sees pipes, the bytes move as they are, the caller's
    files and exit status are the caller's, output is drained before `run` returns. The stdin relay
    of a command that never read it is ended with the command (what it had read ahead is gone, as
    to a `head`; a writer such as `(sleep 20; echo) | omabox run -- true` is not waited for). A
    caller at a terminal (stdin and stdout both) gets the command a pseudo-terminal of its own
    (`box_pty`: util-linux `script` on the host holds the real terminal and the master, raw mode and
    resizes as `script` does them; the box gets the slave, which ends with the command, and its
    `ttyname` is not the box's `/dev/pts`, `isatty` is); a stderr that is not that terminal stays
    where it was. `gdb`'s and the hung shell's own `nsenter -p` lines go through the relay too.
    A review of the first version found what two relays do to one file: `> log 2>&1` makes stdout
    and stderr one open file description, and two `cat`s writing it raced on its offset (600 lines
    in, 592-599 out, `o1` overwritten every run): the two share one relay when `/dev/fd/1 -ef
    /dev/fd/2`. It found the terminal cases too: `script` puts the terminal in raw mode, so an
    `omabox run ... &` from a shell was stopped at once (SIGTTOU), and a relay `cat` reading a
    terminal on stdin alone stopped a backgrounded run (SIGTTIN), fought a pager for keystrokes
    (`run -- cmd | less`) and ate what was typed for the next prompt (every `box_sys` from a
    terminal). So: the pty only in the foreground (`fg_tty`, pgrp = tpgid in /proc/self/stat), and
    a terminal on stdin that is not that case gives the command /dev/null (it could read the
    terminal before; nothing of omabox's does, and a command that must gets stdin and stdout at a
    terminal). Also from the review: a later relay closes the earlier pipes' ends it inherits (else
    the stdout relay saw no EOF before the stderr one ended, and `gdb --watch`'s daemon, started
    through the relay without `fds_only`, kept both pipes open for its life), `fd_exposed` is bash's
    own tests on /dev/fd/N (no `stat` forked three times a `box_exec`), `box_pty` replaces the first
    `OMABOX_EFD=@EFD` word only, as ns_held does, and `disown` of a process substitution's pid is
    not a thing (dropped: a relay a background child keeps is simply left; bash does not wait for
    it at exit).
    Residual: PID 1 holds the box's own `box.log` in the box dir (a box process may read or append
    to its own log). (nsenter's own stderr during startup was ns_held's unlinked temp file, open to
    a box process for longer than the microseconds first thought: a pipe since finding 345.) Checked (`t_run_stdio`, `t_unit_fd_exposed`): pipes seen from the box, 3 MB byte
    for byte, status and stderr apart, no fd of any box process naming a host file while another
    `run` writes one, a pty of its own under `script`, a shell fed by a pipe. Cost: three `stat`s
    and up to three `cat`s a `box_exec`.

326. **`omabox-feedback`: an opt-in skill, for reporting what got in the way** (2026-10-15). The
    maintainer used an end-of-session sweep of his own: read back through the session for
    every omabox failure, refusal, workaround, missing command and misleading doc, check each against
    the issues, draft it. It found what no one would have reported by hand (most rough edges cost an
    agent a retry, and the agent says nothing). Now it ships as `skill-feedback/` (skill name
    `omabox-feedback`), **opt-in**: a skill that files issues from every user's sessions by default
    would be a "call home" that benefits no one, so a plain `omabox setup` (a fresh install, an
    update) never links it. `omabox setup --feedback-skill` links it where `skill/` goes;
    `--no-feedback-skill` and `--remove` unlink it; a later plain setup keeps a link it finds (one to
    any omabox's `skill-feedback/`, pointed at this one: a moved checkout, a package after a checkout)
    and makes none (`setup_feedback`). The `omabox` skill does not mention it, and it runs only when
    the user asks for it, never at the end of a session on the agent's own initiative. Not in
    `broker`'s ai-jail recipe: a jail reaches no GitHub. Its rules: nothing posted before one yes from
    the user (`/omabox-feedback auto` skips the question),
    a short table first and each draft shown only on request, every draft scrubbed before it is shown
    (home paths, names, hosts, emails, tokens, private repos and projects, and the session's content:
    file names, window titles, documents, media), then grepped for `$HOME`, `$USER`, the hostname,
    the git email and the user's private repo names; a safety finding is never filed, the user is
    pointed at SECURITY.md. `digest.py` cuts Claude Code's transcripts (the session and each subagent's,
    `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>/subagents/`) to the omabox moments, standard library only,
    so the sweep sees the subagents' work, which never reaches the conversation; other agents sweep
    the conversation alone. Its `GUARD` tag is the guard's own `omabox guard: ` line or a display
    failure as a program prints it (at most a short prefix, no quote, pipe or backtick before it):
    reading a file that quotes those messages (the omabox skill's description, this script) is not
    one. Checked: `digest.py` on a real session of 27 transcripts (26 subagents, ~285 K of digests),
    no false `GUARD`; `t_unit_setup` (no link from a plain setup, opt in, kept, opt out, `--remove`)
    and `t_unit_install` (none from install.sh), `t_unit_version` for the description and `--help`. The skill's flow itself (asking, filing) is not exercised by the suite.

327. **`ls` refuses what it does not take** (2026-10-16, #236). `cmd_ls` read only its first
    argument, as `--json`, and dropped the rest: `omabox ls -b NAME --json` printed the table and
    exited 0, so a script piping it into a JSON parser got a table and no error, and `ls --bogus` was
    `ls`. Now `-b`/`--box` after `ls` (or `list`) is the line `omabox -b NAME ls` already gave, "ls
    takes no -b: it is not about one box", exit 2, from one helper both use (`not_one_box`); any other
    argument is "ls: unknown argument X (omabox ls [--json])", exit 2 as well (the issue asked for 2;
    other commands' unknown options exit 1 through `die`). `--json` anywhere, or twice, is still
    `--json`. `t_unit_cli`. `saves` had the same hole (`saves --json --bogus` printed the JSON and
    exited 0, as it matched only its first argument): every argument but `rm`'s is read now, `-b`
    is `not_one_box`, anything but `--json`/`-h` is "saves: unknown argument X", exit 2 (a bare
    `saves junk` was `die`, exit 1, before). `t_unit_saves`.

328. **The guard's line goes into `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` once** (2026-10-16, #243). The Claude Code
    hook appended it with `>>` every time SessionStart fired, and that is on resume and compact too:
    a long session's env file had it once per compaction, every shell command sourced all of them
    (harmless, the `case` skips a PATH already guarded, but one 1437-char command line showed it
    twice). Now the hook writes nothing when the file already has its exact line, and otherwise
    rewrites the file with every line that names `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=omabox-guard` (an older omabox's
    line: its text changes with the guard) taken out and its own at the end, the file's other lines
    kept, in the file Claude Code gave (no rename). The hook's text changed, so an installed one reads
    `outdated` until `omabox guard on claude` (or setup's "Update it?") renews it; until then it keeps
    appending as before. `t_unit_guard_settings`.
329. **`ls --json` has every box's Hyprland version** (2026-10-16, #238). `hypr_version` ran only
    for a `--hyprland` box, so a box on the installed Hyprland had `"hyprland_version": null`, and
    the skill's "Reporting what a box showed" sent agents there for it (five in one session got
    `None`; one reported the host's `pacman -Q hyprland` instead, which is not the box's answer). Now
    `up` records `hyprctl version`'s first line from inside every box once its Hyprland is up; the
    warning about another version than the installed hyprctl's stays a `--hyprland` box's (the
    installed one's hyprctl is its own, and `Hyprland --version-json` is not run for it). `hyprland`
    stays the build's path, null for the installed one, so `ls` and `windows` print their "runs
    Hyprland" line for a build only. A box an older omabox started has no key until it is up again:
    the skill names the keys (`omarchy_version`, `hyprland_version`), says `omabox hyprctl version`
    when one is null, and that the commit to report is the project's own (`ls --json` has none).
    `t_unit_hyprland` (both kinds of box, stubbed), `t_uwsm_app` (a stock box's key against its own
    `hyprctl version`, no `Hyprland:` line under it in `ls`).
330. **The skill's loop has `wait change` again** (2026-10-16, #241). Finding 184 put it there; the
    shortening that moved the rest to reference.md (#143) left it out, and the quick list kept only
    `wait window`, `layer`, `cmd` and `still`. For an app that redraws later on its own (a server
    sync, a timer), agents of one session slept with `wait cmd --timeout 15 -- false` (a fixed wait
    ending in 124, sent to /dev/null) or ran `wait cmd -- true` (no wait at all). Now the loop has
    `omabox wait change --window myapp` (then `wait still`), the "No `sleep`" rule names it and says
    not `wait cmd -- false`, reference.md's "Waiting, in detail" has the use with `--timeout 30s`
    and says options go before or after COND, and `help wait` says what `change` is (the first
    change there). SKILL.md stays under its 14 KB by dropping what it said twice: `pixel`, `events`,
    `gdb`, `output` in the "Also" line (each is named further down), "text first" (rule 1), step 5's
    `omabox down` (the loop and the box paragraph), the interactive box's "no frame: ask" (its
    symptom row). `t_unit_version` checks the loop line.
331. **A bare `--window` word matches a hyphen-separated part of the class** (2026-10-16, #244).
    `--window portal` found nothing for `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` (finding 97 matched the class, its
    last dotted part or part of the title), and the agent retried with the dialog's title. Now, when
    no window matches a word those ways, a whole `-`-separated part of the class matches it
    (`portal`, `gtk`, `xdg`; not `port`). It is a second tier, not a fourth way at the same level:
    a selector that found one window before still finds that one (`gtk` with windows of class `gtk`
    and `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk`, or a title holding the word), so no working selector turns into
    "matches 2 windows". Within the tier several matches are refused as before (`portal` for a gtk
    and a kde portal), and `wait window`/`gone` count the same way (one jq, `WIN_SEL_JQ`).
    `t_unit_window_select` checks it on made-up windows.
332. **`shot -g` past the window or the screen is cut to it** (2026-10-16, #240). `shot --window SEL
    -g` refused a region a few pixels past the window ("not inside window", exit 1): agents retried
    by hand, or gave up on a footer taken with the screen's width. Past the screen, grim itself
    gave the requested size with the part off the layout transparent (and failed, "did not intersect
    with any outputs", with nothing on it). `geom_clip` now cuts either to the window (its logical
    size, before `win_buf_geom` scales the rest to its buffer, finding 300) or to the layout's extent,
    and says so on stderr by edge (`-g clipped to 1380,40 474x330 of window …: 6 px past the right
    edge`), exit 0, stdout still the path; the shot record has the clipped region, so `click --in`
    maps from its origin. Only a region with nothing inside is refused ("has nothing inside window",
    "has nothing on the screen"). `--zoom`'s 2000 px a side is checked on the clipped region (it
    was the typed one, before any box was asked), so a zoom that fits once cut is taken. Not clipped: `pixel` (a point cannot be), `wait -g` (a region
    watched), gaps between monitors inside the extent (grim's, as before). `record` has no `-g`.
    `t_unit_wait` (geom_clip), `t_window` (window and screen, `click --in` the clipped crop,
    `--zoom` on it),
    `t_scale`/`t_scale_nvidia` (past a window's corner at scale 2, against its whole shot).
333. **`gdb --watch`: the thread a crash hit first; `log gdb --crash` for it alone** (2026-10-16,
    #233). The watch ran `thread apply all bt` at the fatal signal, which lists threads from the
    highest number down: Hyprland's main thread (1, where most crashes are) came last, after the
    hyprgraphics, glib, dconf and pango workers, so the first `#0` under the signal line was another
    thread's, and the default `log` (the last 100 lines) could cut the signal line itself. gdb selects
    the thread the signal hit when it stops, so the watch now writes `thread` and `bt` under "== omabox:
    a fatal signal; the thread it hit:", then "== omabox: every thread:" (that one again among them),
    in gdb's own commands, not by rearranging its text. `omabox log gdb --crash` prints, for each crash,
    the watch's header, gdb's signal line and that section (-n and --grep after); none: exit 1, "no
    crash in its gdb log". gdb runs those commands after any end of `continue` (a process killed or
    exited: "Program terminated with signal SIGKILL", then "No thread selected"): a section with no
    "received signal" line before it is no crash. A log written by an older omabox (one "every
    thread" section) has no crash for --crash. Checked on a real fault, the box's Hyprland segfaulting
    in a Lua `unbind` (#232): the main thread's 24 frames right under the signal, the log 123 lines.
    `t_unit_gdb_crashes` (killed, a worker thread's crash, two single-threaded ones), `t_gdb` (the
    killed watch: no crash; the SIGSEGV: the thread it hit between the signal and "every thread", and
    --crash down to main with the signal's thread number).
334. **A call that crashes the box's Hyprland says so, with the signal** (2026-10-16, #232). `omabox lua`
    with two binds of one key both unbound segfaults Hyprland (a Hyprland bug), and lua said "its
    Hyprland did not answer (hung? …)" while `ls` said `hung`, then `dead` a moment later. Its socket
    closes as it dies, before its pid goes: the process is a zombie until labwc reaps it (and says
    "spawned child N terminated with signal 11" in labwc.log), and only then does the box end, so every
