    caller's `box_alive` check came too early and took the hung branch. `hung_text`, which every

    keys and the pointer tools, reload), now asks `hypr_lost` first: up to 2 s, the box gone, or the
    Hyprland its instance lock names (NSpid matched to a box process) not running, or labwc's line
    there, is "box 'N' went down: its Hyprland crashed (SIGSEGV) (a backtrace: the same call in a new
    box after omabox gdb --watch; boxes keep no core dumps; …)"; with a crash in the gdb log, "its
    backtrace: omabox log -b N gdb --crash" instead; a Hyprland in tracing stop with the watch's
    signal written is "crashed (SIGSEGV), held by gdb --watch while it writes the backtrace". A
    Hyprland that runs (twice, 0.2 s apart: a SIGSTOPped one is `T`, not gdb's `t`) is hung as before,
    0.2 s later. The callers' own "went down" (box gone already) and a later call's "is dead" name
    labwc's line too ("exited (status N)" for an exit). Not for an interactive box: no labwc, so no line
    (a gone Hyprland there is "went down" without the signal, after the 2 s; since finding 350
    session.sh writes the line). In a box: the repro
    plain (crashed, SIGSEGV, the gdb --watch hint, 0.1 s) and under gdb --watch (the gdb log's
    backtrace named; the held branch not hit there: gdb wrote its backtraces before lua looked).
    `t_unit_hypr_lost` (stopped, held, traced but running, gone with and without a watch, an exit's
    status, no line, a linked log), `t_hyprland_crash`, `t_hung` unchanged.
335. **A plugin under test got the desk's settings unsaid; `up` names them, `--no-seed extensions`**

    its CLI). Its on/off switch was off on the desk, so the `--plugin` box bound nothing and the test

336. **A repo path through a link out of the repo dangled in the box unsaid; `up` and `run` name it**
    (2026-10-16, #235). A build cache had swapped a Rust repo's `target/` for a link to
    `~/.cache/<cache>/targets/<hash>`; HOME is not mounted, so in the box the link dangled and `run --
    target/debug/app` said only "No such file or directory". `up` now names each link at the top of
    the repo it mounted whose target the box lacks: "note: REPO/target -> TARGET: outside the box,
    where the link dangles; up --ro-bind TARGET mounts it" (a throwaway's up: `run --ro-bind`; a target
    refuse_src keeps out: why, no mount offered; 5 at most, then a count). The top only: a walk of a big
    repo is slow. `run` names each word of its command that is a path in the repo (absolute, or
    relative to the caller's dir; not `--opt=PATH`) reached through such a link ("WORD leads through
    LINK -> TARGET: …; down, then up --ro-bind TARGET mounts it"), then runs the command all the same
    (`-q` does not hide it); a throwaway leaves the top-level links to its up's note. `repo_link_out`
    walks the path with builtins, `readlink` only at a link; whether the box has it is read from the
    host through `/proc/PID/root` (the link there, its resolved target not), no command in the box, so
    the target is "outside" whatever mount would have it (a `--ro-bind`, mise's, `/usr`) and a word in
    another repo than the box's is not taken for one. What that look sees is the box's to arrange (it
    can move its own mounts, or plant links that lead the look to the host's files), so it can be
    wrong either way: a note missed, or one made for a link the box does have. Only the two stats are
    made, and nothing of the box reaches the note. Not for a jailed caller: where its links lead
    outside its jail is not for it to learn, nor its to mount. A repo may be anyone's clone, and git
    keeps a link to any target, so the note offers the mount only where it is reasonable
    (`link_mountable`): under the cache dir (`~/.cache/…`, not itself), outside HOME, or under HOME in
    no hidden folder (another checkout's `target/`); a target in a dot-dir of HOME, or in the XDG
    config, data or state dirs, gets "no mount is offered for it (it is in a hidden folder of your
    HOME, where settings and keys live)". refuse_src also keeps out the coding agents' and the
    browsers' own stores now (`~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `~/.codex`,
    `$CODEX_HOME`, OpenCode's `~/.config/opencode` and `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.pi`,
    `~/.hermes`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.mozilla`, `~/.config/{chromium,google-chrome,BraveSoftware,vivaldi,
    microsoft-edge}`, `~/.pki`), said as the other secret stores are, for every mount. Names and
    targets are the repo's: the note prints their control characters as `?`, and a link whose name or
    target holds a tab or newline is skipped (not one line of three for the walk). Tests:
    t_unit_link_out (the walk: a link out, relative, through an in-repo link, `..`, one that stays in,
    one dangling on the host, outside the repo; the note and a refused target; link_mountable's cases;
    an agent's store; `?` for an escape; a tab or newline skipped), t_unit_mount_rules (each new
    store, the two variables), t_link_out (a scratch repo whose `target` links to a scratch folder:
    up's and run's notes, the command still run, none for in-repo words or with `--ro-bind` of it, a
    link named with an escape sequence said with `?`, a throwaway's note once with `run --ro-bind`).

337. **`run -- wl-copy TEXT` never returned to a `$(...)` or a pipe: the fork held the output**
    (2026-10-16, #239). `wl-copy` forks a server that serves the item until the next copy; the server
    points stdin and stdout at /dev/null but keeps stderr. A caller whose stdout or stderr is a pipe
    (`$(omabox run -- …)`, `2>&1 |`, a harness reading pipes) waited for its EOF, so for the server's
    life (65 s in a check, till a later copy replaced it); so does any `sh -c 'daemon &'`. Since
    0.1.0: before 0.6.1 nsenter gave the command the caller's fds as they were (a file: no wait; a
    pipe: the hang, seen with 0.6.0's bin); 0.6.1's relay (finding 325) relayed files (`run` then
    waited its 1 s bound for the relay a leftover held, every time: 1.08 s for `wl-copy` to a file)
    and passed pipes and sockets through, so the hang stayed for them. A command on a terminal of its
    own (box_pty) was never held: util-linux `script -e` ends with its child. Now, in `box_exec` for
    a user's command (`RELAY_PIPES`; not `box_sys`, whose helpers leave nothing and some run every
    100 ms), an output that is a pipe or a socket is relayed too (`relay_out`), and every output relay
    is `omabox-relay copy` (`relay_copy`, tools/relay) instead of `cat`: stdin to stdout as `cat`
    does it, till EOF. One still running 100 ms after the command ended is held by a leftover:
    `relay_drain` sends it SIGURG (every 50 ms till it takes: SIGURG's default is to be ignored, so
    one sent before the handler is set is lost, never fatal; a `cat` ignores them all), and it copies
    what the pipe holds then (FIONREAD), all the command wrote, since the command is over, and ends;
    `run` returns with the command's status, its output whole and in place before `run` ends. A child
    of the relay goes on reading the pipe into nothing, holding only that pipe and /dev/null, so the
    leftover lives on and its later writes neither fail (EPIPE) nor kill it (SIGPIPE): what it writes
    after the command ended is dropped. *Decided*: dropped, not passed on. On a desktop shell a
    `daemon &` keeps the terminal and its later lines show there, but a `$(...)` there waits for it
    too; `run`'s answer is the command's, and a process meant to outlive it belongs in `run -d`, whose
    log keeps everything. The command's own output is never cut: one still being copied to a slow
    reader after the 1 s bound is left running, as before, and ends once copied. The copy closes every
    fd from 3 up (`close_range`, else what /proc/self/fd lists: a caller's fd may be far above 1024,
    and one it waits on must not stay held), and its child keeps 0, 1 and 2 only; it unblocks SIGURG
    (a caller's blocked mask passes through exec); once the command has ended it reads without
    blocking (O_NONBLOCK on its own pipe end, cleared again in the child), so another reader of the
    pipe taking bytes FIONREAD counted cannot hold it. The children left draining are host processes,
    at most one per held output per `run` (two when stdout and stderr are separate pipes), each with
    only its pipe and /dev/null, outside a `--systemd` box's scope; they end when the last writer in
    the box goes, at `down` at the latest. relay_drain reads the state and ppid after the comm's last
    `)`. Without its tools built (another omabox's checkout), `cat` and the old behaviour. Checked:
    t_unit_fd_exposed (omabox-relay copy on a fifo under a caller with fd 1500 open and SIGURG
    blocked: it ends at SIGURG, its child holds fds 0-2 only and ends with the writer, both of which
    the first version of the copy failed; stdio_relay with a `sleep &` holding a pipe: output and
    status 3 in ~120 ms, a leftover's later lines dropped and it alive after, 200 kB byte for byte;
    with `cat` the same call took the leftover's 4 s), t_run_stdio (`$(run -- sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo
    hi')` in ~140 ms with 0, then 3; 3 MB through a held pipe byte for byte; `run -- wl-copy TEXT` in
    ~140 ms and `wl-paste -n` gives TEXT back; the same on a terminal of its own, stderr to a file, in
    ~50 ms; a caller's fd 1500 held by no relay left draining; a caller with SIGURG blocked gets
    `hi` and 0 in ~180 ms). Not checked by a test: the O_NONBLOCK read, whose race (another reader
    between FIONREAD and the read) a test cannot win on purpose.
338. **`omabox cpu --threads`: CPU per thread, an app's main thread apart from its render thread**
    (2026-10-16, #242). Measuring what an animation costs needs a Qt Quick app's GUI thread apart from
    its `QSGRenderThread`; `cpu` gave per-process figures only, so an agent wrote its own sampler (a
    host `pgrep -f`, which sees other boxes and the desktop, a `sleep` for `--settle`, then
    `/proc/PID/task/*/stat`). Now `cpu --threads` with `--pid` or `--app`: in each of `cpu`'s samples
    (same window, same settle), the processes `cpu_report` keeps (by either numbering for `--pid`, by
    tamed name for `--app`, so one that starts in the window is followed too) also have each thread's
    utime+stime read from `/proc/PID/task/TID/stat` (`cpu_threads`, builtins as `cpu_sample`), keyed
    on the process's host pid and start time plus the thread's tid and start time; a thread is
    figured as a process is (all its ticks if first seen later, up to its last sample if gone, both
    said). Rows follow their process, busiest first, one per tid even when names repeat (worker pools,
    several render threads); the tid is the box's (NSpid's last in the thread's status), as `pid` is,
    the host's as `host_tid`. `--json`: `processes[].threads[]` {tid, host_tid, name, cpu, started,
    exited}, the key only with `--threads` (the process objects keep their shape without it); no
    memory per thread (threads share it). A thread that exits between samples loses its ticks since
    the last one, so the threads can add up to a little under the process. *Decided*: `--threads`
    without `--pid`/`--app` is refused with what to name (a box's Hyprland and shell have dozens of
    threads each: every process's threads would bury the app's). Verified in a box (t_cpu): a python3
    whose main thread sleeps, one thread busy and two idle named alike (each writes its own
    `/proc/self/task/TID/comm`): the busy one 98.9%, the main thread (tid = pid) 0.0%, the two idle
    ones two rows, the tids those of the box's `/proc/PID/task`, the threads within 5% of the process.
339. **A box loads the box HOME's `~/.config/hypr` user modules** (2026-10-16, #246). A box never
    loaded them: `omabox-hyprland.lua` stands in for stock `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` and required
    only Omarchy's bootstrap, `default.hypr.omarchy` and the toggles (finding 69). So appending a
    bind to `bindings.lua` or `gaps_out` to `looknfeel.lua`, then `hyprctl reload`, answered `ok`
    and changed nothing; a plugin's "add this to bindings.lua" (erikrjohansson/omarchy-hotkey-wheel's
    Set up button) bound nothing in a box. Now `share/hyprland.lua` requires `hypr.input`,
    `hypr.bindings` and `hypr.looknfeel` where stock does (after `default.hypr.omarchy`, before the
    toggles), and before everything omabox sets (PATH, the screen's rules, debug/misc/xwayland, the
    hidden pointer), which therefore wins. A module with no file is skipped. Not loaded: stock's
    `hyprland.lua` itself, `hypr.autostart` (as `default.hypr.autostart`), and `hypr.monitors`:
    Omarchy's skel one sets `GDK_SCALE=2` and `hl.monitor({ output = "", ..., scale = "auto" })`,
    which would change every fresh box (GTK apps at 2x; a catch-all rule over a `monitor add`'s
    output), and its rules are for real screens. *Decided*: skipped rather than loaded before the
    box's own rules (a later specific rule wins for its output, but the catch-all and the env would
    not be overridden). Hyprland 0.56's `require` is its own (a C function): a module that fails to
    parse or raises is caught, becomes a config error (`hyprctl configerrors`, the red "Your config
    has errors" bar on the box's screen, as on a desktop; no bar since finding 352) and returns `{}`; what the module did
    before a runtime error stays, and the load goes on. It never reaches Hyprland's log. The pcall
    around each require is for a build whose `require` raises; it logs to Hyprland's log. *Decided*
    for the warning: `up`, `reload` and `hyprctl reload` print `hyprctl configerrors` when it is not
    empty (every config error, not only the user modules': what the red bar shows), nothing
    otherwise; a reload's `ok` alone hid them. Who gets non-skel files: the box HOME's
    `~/.config/hypr` comes from `/etc/skel` only (`seed_home`; `--desk-shell` copies
    `~/.config/omarchy`, never `~/.config/hypr`), so a desk's own bindings/input never reach a box;
    only a `--seed …:.config/hypr/…`, a save (`up --from`) of a box that wrote there, or a write in
    the box (a test, a plugin's Set up) does. On this machine the skel's input, bindings, looknfeel
    and autostart are comments only (and equal Omarchy's `config/hypr`), so a fresh box is unchanged:
    `configerrors` empty, every box test touching the config passes. An `input.lua` `kb_layout` is
    the box's layout, which `omabox keys` reads (finding 13). The Omarchy contract checks stock's
    list of user requires is still these five. Verified in a box (t_user_hypr): gaps_out 33 and a
    probe bind after `hyprctl reload`; monitors.lua and autostart.lua not run, the screen 1920x1080
    at 1; a syntax error in input.lua said by `hyprctl reload` and `reload`, the box alive, the bind
    of bindings.lua (loaded after it) still there; fixed, nothing said.
340. **On NVIDIA, Print (Omarchy's screenshot) killed the box: hardware cursors through a CPU
    buffer** (2026-10-16, #245). Hyprland segfaulted in `renderHWCursorBuffer` at the next cursor
    update after Print (a layer unmapping, the screencast's end). Cause: `omarchy-capture-screenshot`
    sets `cursor:no_hardware_cursors = 0` while it runs (so grim captures no software cursor) and puts
    the old value back after; that is also why setting `no_hardware_cursors = 1` at runtime seemed not
    to help. With hardware cursors forced, Hyprland's `use_cpu_buffer` auto (2) takes the CPU path on
    NVIDIA: with no `DRM_DUMB` allocator on the Wayland backend it takes the GBM one, `gbm_bo_map`s the
    cursor buffer and memcpy's into it without checking the map. NVIDIA's GBM cannot CPU-map a bo at
    all (a host probe on the render node: NULL for every layout and flag; Mesa maps them all), and gdb
    at the crash showed the memcpy writing to 0x40. AMD survives (a headless output has no hardware
    cursor; interactive, auto takes the GL path off NVIDIA); a default NVIDIA box rejects hardware
    cursors and draws the cursor in software. omabox's aquamarine patches are not involved (the same
    crash on plain 7bb8bdf4). Fix: `cursor = { use_cpu_buffer = 0 }` in omabox's own `hl.config`
    (after the user modules, finding 339, so it wins; every load sets it): hardware cursors drawn on
    the GPU. The same as auto on other GPUs; on NVIDIA the default cursor stays software and in shots.
    The Hyprland bug (the unchecked map) and Omarchy's forced setting are recorded for upstream
    (diogochaves/upstream#98, #99). Verified in a box (t_cursor_hw_nvidia, renderD129): the option 0;
    `no_hardware_cursors = 0` and two pointer moves, then Print, the selection layer, Escape, it gone
    and a move after: the box alive; with `use_cpu_buffer = 2` the same test fails from the first
    check on (the box died). By hand in the investigation: a region saved by Print in a headless
    NVIDIA box, and an interactive NVIDIA box in an NVIDIA stand-in (finding 26) alive under forced
    hardware cursors. Not checked: NVIDIA with VRR (auto's other way to hardware cursors).
341. **`tree` sets ScreenReaderEnabled too: AccessKit before 0.22 waits for it** (2026-10-16, #237).
    An egui app on eframe 0.36 (accesskit_winit 0.32, accesskit_unix 0.21.1) never joined the box's
    a11y bus, so `tree` said "pid N is not on the box's accessibility bus". accesskit_unix before 0.22
    watches only `org.a11y.Status.ScreenReaderEnabled`, and `tree` set only `IsEnabled` (Qt's,
    finding 244); 0.22 (AccessKit #715) watches IsEnabled and adds the cache object (#719), and
    eframe 0.37 (accesskit_unix 0.24) already worked. The window's pid was the AT-SPI app's pid; the
    bus address comes from the session bus's `org.a11y.Bus.GetAddress`, which the box has. Now
    `omabox-tree` sets each of the two that is off and waits its 3 s when it turned either on. It also
    drops libatspi's `dbind` warning "Unknown object '/org/a11y/atspi/cache'", printed on every read
    of an app without the cache object (0.21) as a stray `omabox: tree:` line after the tree; any
    other `dbind` message still shows. *Decided*: set SRE for every app rather than detect AccessKit
    (accesskit_unix has no switch to force it; Orca sets both). Box-wide and sticky like IsEnabled: an
    app that changes behaviour when "a screen reader runs" sees it after the first `tree`. Verified
    by hand in the investigation, in a box: the 0.36 app off the bus with IsEnabled on, on the bus
    within ~14 ms of SRE (label and button with bounds matching a shot, a click at the button's middle
    counted), and the patched helper printing its tree on the first call with no warning; the 0.37
    app read before and after. Not in the suite (an egui build is ~800 MB of target dir): t_tree
    checks SRE is off at `up` and on after a `tree` (fails with the old helper). Assumed: other
    AccessKit toolkits on old accesskit_unix (Slint, iced, Bevy) behave the same; SRE changes nothing
    for Qt, GTK or Chromium (finding 244: it does not turn Chromium's tree on).
342. **t_wait's thin-line checks take a 3 px change: a window drawn a fraction of a pixel off**
    (2026-10-16, #222). Under the full suite's load the toggling 2 px underline's last change came out
    3 px high now and then. The dumps: the underline's two rows plus a one-level fringe (the row above
    +1, its last row -1, one column past its end +1). The failing box's whole screen showed why: its
    Hyprland drew window U a fraction of a pixel off its integer box, Hyprland's own border included
    (top and bottom borders a level off, outward; A's edges and U's left border exact), still 10 s
    after the map and again for the next window; `clients` gave the goal geometry. *Assumed*: the
    map's animation stopped just short of its goal (Hyprland's Lua exposes only goal values). Not
    reproduced alone, nor beside CPU load (up to load 44): it seems to need many boxes drawing at
    once. omabox-still is right (those pixels changed); a 3 px change is still thin (THIN 4), so
    `thin_check` accepts 2 or 3 and keeps the frame dumps, now with a whole-screen shot beside them,
    for anything else. *Decided*: no per-level tolerance in omabox-still (it would change what every
    `wait still` counts). Verified: t_wait 3 runs, 109/0 each; a forced failure wrote both dumps
    and the 1920x1080 screen.
343. **`keys down:KEY` / `up:KEY`: a key held across other commands** (2026-10-16, #230; #81's parked
    line). `keys` only tapped, so a bind on a key's release (`hl.bind(KEY, fn, {release = true})`) or
    a gesture made while a key is held (a wheel opened on a held key, a slot picked with the pointer,
    run on the release) could not be tested. A virtual keyboard's key is released only by that
    keyboard, so the keyboard tool forks off a holder on the first `down:`: it keeps a keyboard of its
    own on the seat, presses and releases keys on it as asked over a unix socket in the box's runtime
    dir (`omabox-held-keys`; a request a connection, answered once the compositor has it), and ends
    with the last `up:`, letting go of anything still down on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP. A run with
    `down:`/`up:` goes through `box_sys`, so the holder is in the box's pid namespace and ends with it
    (`down`; for a box named after the agent's session, the agent exiting); not with `--pass` (finding
    307). A run of `down:`/`up:` (and `-s`) alone puts no keyboard of its own on the seat. *Decided*:
    a second `down:` of a held key and an `up:` of one not held are exit 1 (naming what is held); no
    time limit on a hold (a kept box keeps it until `up:`); KEY is one key, a letter its key (`down:A`
    holds a), a symbol that needs a modifier refused. Seen in a box: Hyprland joins the modifiers of
    every keyboard on the seat, for binds and for the client: SUPER held by one keyboard and `a` from
    another fired SUPER+A, shift held typed `AB` in foot. A held letter repeats in the app (Omarchy's
    40/s after 250 ms) until another keyboard's key, as on a real keyboard, and stops at `up:` (the
    release reaches it). Hyprland makes the keyboard with the latest event the active one and the
    event that switches it is lost to the client (finding 14), so the holder spends a modifiers event
    before each key and a run spends one again after a `down:`/`up:`. A holder killed outright
    (SIGKILL) leaves its key down for Hyprland: the next `down:` takes over its stale socket, and its
    `up:` fired the release bind twice (*assumed*: once for each keyboard's press; fixed: finding 347). Test: `t_keys_down_up` (the
    issue's press and release binds with `pointer move` between, SUPER+A, capitals, the repeat
    stopping, a key held at `down` gone with the box). The Hotkey Wheel gesture itself not tried.
344. **A box's own journal sockets: `omabox log journal`** (2026-10-16, #234). `dbus-broker-launch`
    connects to `/run/systemd/journal/socket` before anything else (`launcher_open_journal`) and exits
    1 without it, so a program that starts its own bus from a cleaned environment (a test harness's
    `at-spi-bus-launcher` without the `ATSPI_DBUS_IMPLEMENTATION` of finding 264) got no bus. A box's
    `/run` is bwrap's root tmpfs, with only `/run/systemd/resolve` (the resolv.conf bind of finding
    52) under `/run/systemd`. Now every box gets `--tmpfs /run/systemd/journal` (its own, never the
    host's) and `share/session.sh` starts `share/journal.py` (python3 -I, as `omabox-journal` by
    `/proc/self/comm`, so `pkill python3` in a box leaves it; a child of PID 1, gone with the box) on
    it before the session bus: the native datagram socket (`KEY=value` fields, the length-prefixed
    binary form, a big entry's memfd over SCM_RIGHTS read up to 64 KB; every passed fd closed) and the
    `stdout` stream socket (seven header lines, then text; a `<N>` level prefix dropped). Each
    MESSAGE becomes `DATE TIME IDENTIFIER[PID]: LINE` lines in `~/journal.log` (identifier from
    SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER or the sender's comm, pid from SCM_CREDENTIALS / SO_PEERCRED, in the box's pid
    namespace); other fields are dropped. Past 4 MB it is renamed `journal.1.log` (a `.log` name, so
    `save` leaves it out like the others) and started again. 12 MB RSS. *Decided*: python (in
    install.sh's packages, so in every box's /usr) over socat (not a dependency) or a mode of
    omabox-relay (a host tool, not in a box); the stdout socket too (25 lines: a `--systemd` box's
    unit output, `StandardOutput=journal`, went nowhere without it);
    no `/dev/log` (syslog: not asked; the `logger` stand-in of #151 covers Omarchy's callers); the
    `logger`/`systemd-cat` stand-ins and `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1` stay (they write where agents
    already look). `ATSPI_DBUS_IMPLEMENTATION=dbus-daemon` stays too: the a11y bus under dbus-broker
    also asks for `org.freedesktop.systemd1` on the session bus (a failed activation, harmless, seen
    in a box). Seen in a box: the issue's failure reproduced with the socket renamed away (the same
    `launcher_open_journal` trace), and with it the launcher's dbus-broker answers `busctl list` and
    logs `dbus-broker-launch[PID]: Ready`. Test: `journal_sink` in t_dbus_user_app (the tmpfs mount,
    the sink's name, `logger --journald`, `/usr/bin/systemd-cat`, at-spi-bus-launcher from `env -i` on
    a private bus and runtime dir, the 4 KB bound of a second sink), and t_systemd (a unit's output).
345. **nsenter's own messages are read through a bounded pipe, and printed only when they look like
    nsenter's** (2026-10-16). `ns_held` (#166, finding 192's part 3) held nsenter's stderr, and that of
    the box-side `env`/`bash` it starts until the command's bash takes the caller's, in a host
    temporary file, read back whole and printed as it came. Now it is a pipe, as finding 325 has for a
    command's stdio, read on the host by `ns_hold_read` (its other fds closed): the first 4 KiB
    (`NS_HELD_MAX`) come back over a pipe of their own, whose EOF says the reader is done, and the rest
    is read into nothing, so no writer waits on a full pipe. A reader still running `NS_HELD_WAIT`
    (1 s) after the command is ended, as the shell's own child: nothing of the command's writes there
    then. 4 KiB because a pipe holds two pages at the least, so the reader never waits on this side
    either. `ns_said` prints only whole lines in the shapes it is there for (`ns_own_line`:
    `nsenter: `, `prlimit: `, `env: `, and bash's `$0: line N: PID SIGNAL CMD` for a command killed by
    a signal, its words translated or not), at most 3, printable ASCII only; anything else is dropped
    and counted ("omabox: dropped N bytes of other output on nsenter's stderr"). The cost: two
    short-lived processes a call (the reader, then its `cat`) instead of `mktemp`'s one; no wait in the
    usual case (EOF at once). Checked: `t_unit_box_gone` (other lines and escapes dropped and counted,
    4 KiB read of 3 MB, a pipe kept open elsewhere does not hold the call past about a second, bash's
    line for a signal passes) and `t_run_stdio` (other output on that stderr during ten `run -- true`:
    each status 0, nothing else printed, under 8 KB in all, each back in tens of ms).
    The same rule for fds above 2: `gdb`'s steps in the box (its `pgrep`, `test`, `cat` and `sed`,
    and the header `--watch` writes) and `restart-shell`'s end of a hung shell entered the box's pid
    namespace without `fds_only`, so they had every fd omabox had open, a caller's own included
    (`omabox gdb ... 7<FILE`). All six now run through it, as `box_exec` and gdb itself did.
    `t_unit_ns_fds` reads bin/omabox for any `stdio_relay`, `nsenter ... -p` or run of the `ns`/`caps`
    arrays that does not (it finds those six in the old code); `t_gdb` checks from the box that a
    caller's fd 7 is in none of its processes over five `gdb` runs (it was, in the old code).
346. **The guard's hooks say when an upgrade changed them** (2026-10-16). What `guard on` writes is
    literal text, compared whole by `omabox guard` ("outdated"). When an upgrade changed it (#243's
    rewrite), the old hook went on working and nobody was told: the package's `post_upgrade` only says
    to run setup if the changelog asks. Now `share/guard/hook-version` holds one stamp per agent
    (Claude Code's, then Codex's: their state is apart, so a Codex-only change leaves Claude Code's
    hook quiet), each the first 12 hex of a sha256 of what `guard on` writes for it, built with no
    stamps and `$ROOT` made `@ROOT@` (Claude Code: the hook; Codex: its hook and the config.toml
    block). omabox reads the file (one `read`) and embeds each stamp in its hook, so the stamp cannot
    differ from the file it ships with; t_unit_guard_settings computes the hash again and fails with the
    new value when the hook changed and the file did not. At session start the hook reads the file
    under its own `share/guard` with the `read` builtin (no process; ~1 ms with the rest) and, when it
    holds another stamp, prints one more line after the note (or after "NOT applied"): "this hook is
    outdated (omabox changed it): tell the user to run omabox guard on to renew it". An empty or
    missing file says nothing: in ai-jail the checkout is not mapped (#203), and a checkout that is gone
    is the existing "omabox is gone" branch. *Decided*: tell the user, not run `guard on` itself (it
    rewrites the agent's own settings); CI's and CONTRIBUTING's shellcheck take `share/guard`'s
    scripts by their `#!` (the stamp file is not one). This change itself changes both hooks, so every
    installed guard reads outdated once without the line, as before. Test: t_unit_guard_settings (the
    hash, both hooks carry their stamps, a current stamp adds nothing, a changed one adds the line for
    each agent apart, no file adds nothing). Seen with `sh` (bash's POSIX mode; no dash here), not in a
    live Claude Code or Codex session.
347. **A killed key holder's keys are let go once; `down:`/`up:` checked before any key is sent**
    (2026-10-16, finding 343's loose ends). A holder killed outright (SIGKILL) left its key down for
    Hyprland: the next `down:` took over its stale socket and the following `up:` fired the release
    bind twice. The holder now keeps the keys it has down in `omabox-held-keys.keys` beside its socket
    (replaced whole on each change; saved before a press, after a release; gone with the socket). The
    first keyboard-tool run that finds the socket dead (connect refused or no socket) and that file
    not empty takes it (a rename: one run only) and sends one release for each key, on its own
    keyboard or one made for the moment, and says so on stderr ("a key holder had been killed with
    XF86Tools down: let go"). Seen in a box: a release alone, from a keyboard that never pressed the
    key, fires Hyprland's release bind once (*assumed*: it keeps the press by keycode, whoever made it);
    down:, SIGKILL, up: gave press, release (up: exit 0: the release was its); down:, SIGKILL, down:,
    up: gave press, release, press, release; down:super, SIGKILL, `keys a` fired no SUPER+A. Also a
    run checks its `down:`/`up:` against what is held (a `codes` request to the holder, or the dead
    holder's file) and against its own earlier ones before it sends anything: `keys a up:super` with
    nothing held typed `a`, then failed; now exit 1 with nothing sent (a holder's own answer still
    decides when a key is sent, for a race). Test: `t_keys_down_up` (both cases).
348. **`--version` refuses arguments too** (2026-10-16, finding 327's loose end). `omabox version

349. **`tree` keeps libatspi's warnings out of a tree it read** (2026-10-16, finding 341's loose end).

350. **`ls` says a crashed Hyprland's box `crashed`/`going`, not `hung`; interactive boxes name the
    signal** (2026-10-16, finding 334's loose ends). Between a crash of the box's Hyprland and the box
    ending (labwc reaps it, then PID 1 goes), its IPC is gone while the box is up, so `ls` (hung_boxes:
    no answer in 1 s) said `hung`. hung_boxes now asks `hypr_gone` for one that does not answer: one
    look, no wait, at the Hyprland its instance lock names (`hypr_host_pid`, split out of hypr_lost).
    None running is `crashed` or `exited` by labwc's line, `going` with none yet; `ls`'s STATE and
    `ls --json`'s `state` say it (`hung` false; the widget offers Down for any state but `up`). A
    stopped or deadlocked Hyprland (a `save`'s pause too) still runs: `hung` as before. Interactive
    boxes have no labwc: `session.sh` now appends Hyprland's wait status to `hyprland.log` ("omabox:
    Hyprland terminated with signal N" for 128+N, else "exited with N"), which `hypr_end` reads when
    there is no labwc line, so their crash is "went down: its Hyprland crashed (SIGSEGV)" at once (it
    was "went down", no signal, after 2 s). *Decided*: the word goes in `state` rather than a new
    field (a crashed box is not up, and its next state is `dead`). Seen in a box: labwc SIGSTOPped
    (nothing reaps the Hyprland, the box stays up), the crash: `ls` `going`, `--json` `going false`,
    `dead` once labwc went on; an interactive box in a stand-in host: crashed (SIGSEGV) in 0.1 s.
    `crashed` itself (labwc's line written, the box not gone yet) only in t_unit_hypr_lost: the window
    is too short to catch. Tests: t_hyprland_crash, t_unit_hypr_lost.
351. **`logger` reaches the box's journal by its bare name** (2026-10-16, #248). Finding 344 gave

352. **A box draws no config-error bar: drawing it deadlocked Hyprland** (2026-10-16, #249). Under

    gatherer's thread waiting in `asyncAssetSpinLock`, still so 20 s later. Finding 339 had chosen to
    show the bar, as on a desktop. Now `share/hyprland.lua` sets `debug = { ..., suppress_errors =
    true }` in its `hl.config` (getoption `debug:suppress_errors` `true`, `set` true): Hyprland never
    queues the bar (a reload that turns it on takes a bar already shown away), so the text is never
    drawn. `hyprctl configerrors` is IPC, read from the config manager, not the bar: it still lists

    boxes at once): before, 1 box of 4 hung (10 cycles each), 5 of 6 beside 8 nice'd CPU burners
    (15 each), within 2-10 cycles, each backtrace in the gatherer's `await`; after, beside the
    burners, 12 boxes x 15 or 30 cycles (270) with no hang. Seen in a box: with the error, a shot of the screen's top has no bar (main's
    config draws it there), `configerrors` has the error. Test: t_user_hypr (the option on over

353. **A reload into a Hyprland that then stops answering is said, exit 1** (2026-10-16, #249).

    animations off by `hl.config`), a Qt Quick app with a bar widget of its own against fixed data,
    four checkpoints shot twice 3 s apart, in seven boxes (on the NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti: the gpu setting;
    first written as the AMD iGPU, which was not checked then). **Within a run: pixel-identical** (shots
    and trees). **Across boxes ~2,000 single pixels differ** on text, and as much between two
    starts of the app in one box: Qt Quick's distance-field text is not repeatable from one start to
    the next (the glyph atlas fills in arrival order). It stays with `QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic` and on
    llvmpipe, and goes with `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software` or `QML_DISABLE_DISTANCEFIELD=1` (which
    renders text natively: 56k px from the default, not visible at 2x). Every noise pixel is below
    10% of full scale in grey; a synthetic 1 px shift of a text block survives 25%, a painted-over
    glyph too. At 10% the boxes differ only in content: the server's random port (the test's to
    pin) and "added … HH:MM" (only a pinned clock fixes that; nothing pins time in a box yet,
    no libfaketime here). Port pinned: two fresh boxes identical at 10% on all four checkpoints.
    A spacing changed from 2 to 4 px in a build of the app: caught at 10%, and the tree diff
    (`treediff.py`) named it ("moved -6,+0 button "add …"", -4, -2 down the row). The sentinel
    counts 0 in windows and the bar; a Quickshell popup is drawn in a full-screen layer, so its own
    rectangle comes from pixels, not Hyprland. The widget has no tree (finding 244): pixels only,
    which held as well. **A threshold misses subtle colour**: a row 3 levels brighter is gone at
    10% and one 5,000 px blob exactly, while the noise never made a blob over 13 px. So: exact
    pixels in the users' rendering, isolated blobs under ~32 px dropped (and counted);
    `QML_DISABLE_DISTANCEFIELD=1` an opt-in strict mode.

358. **`up --quickshell PATH`: the box's shell on a Quickshell build** (2026-10-16, #253: testing a
    shell plugin's accessibility tree needs Quickshell's 916a0dd, released in 0.3.2; up to 0.3.1,
    what Arch ships, no Quickshell window publishes an AT-SPI tree). Built as `--hyprland` is (finding
    116), on `up` and a throwaway `run`. `qs_bin` resolves PATH and refuses a missing, non-executable
    or non-ELF file; its folder is mounted read-only at its own path, checked by `refuse_src`/
    `refuse_dest` (none under `/usr`); ai-jail: the same rules as `--hyprland`'s (`W_QS`), and
    `relay_call` sends the path absolute. With `--no-shell` it is refused (nothing would run it).
    **Which Qt.** Quickshell uses Qt's private API, whose ABI may change with any Qt release, so a build
    against another Qt loads fine and dies as the shell starts. Two checks, both naming the versions:
    `qs_check` before the box dir is made reads the ELF (never runs it): it must need
    `libQt6Core.so.6`, and the `qt_version_tag@Qt_6.N` it refers to (every Qt program does: the Qt
    minor it was built against) must be the default version of the box's libQt6Core's
    (`qt_version_tag@@Qt_6.11`), else "was built against Qt 6.10, but the box has Qt 6.11.2"; then
    `ldd` (not for a jailed caller's file) for a library the box lacks. The patch release is not in
    the binary (its private symbols are all `Qt_6_PRIVATE_API`, no minor), but Quickshell has a
    hidden flag for it, `--private-check-compat` (exit 1 and a "built against Qt X but the system
    has updated to Qt Y" line when its build-time `QT_VERSION_STR` is not the running `qVersion()`;
    since 2024-11): `share/session.sh` runs it in the box before anything starts, and on a 1 ends the
    box with a `session.sh: --quickshell: built against Qt X, the box has Qt Y` line, which `up`'s
    "died while starting (...)" prints; another exit (109: a build without the flag) cannot tell and
    goes on. In the box, not on the host: it runs the build. A shell that dies anyway is said with
    the build named ("the shell crashed on the Quickshell build PATH while starting").
    **Which binary runs.** `OMABOX_QUICKSHELL` reaches `session.sh` by bwrap's `--setenv`; it links
    the build as `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omabox-quickshell/{quickshell,qs}`, puts that dir on the session's
    PATH after the box HOME's `~/.local/bin`, and unsets the variable, as `OMABOX_HYPRLAND` is unset
    for Hyprland's children, but for another reason: the shell is not only started by `shell.sh` at
    `up`, but again by whatever runs `omarchy restart shell` (a bar menu, a project's script, `omabox
    run`), with an environment of its own; a link at a fixed path reaches every one of them, and the
    apps the shell launches inherit no variable naming it. `shell.sh` (start, `list`, `kill`) and the
    `systemd-cat` stand-in (Omarchy's launcher runs `systemd-cat -t omarchy-shell -- quickshell`) exec
    the link when it is there, else `/usr/bin/quickshell`; by name, Omarchy's `omarchy-shell` (`qs
    ipc`) and restart (`quickshell kill`) find it on PATH, and `omabox run`'s PATH puts it before the
    caller's `/usr/bin` too. The host side's calls into the box's shell (`shell_hung`'s `ipc show`,
    `shell_adopt`'s `list`) run `box_qs`: box.json's `quickshell`, else `/usr/bin/quickshell` (a
    build talking to another version's IPC is not assumed to work). Through a link the process is
    still named `quickshell` (`/proc/PID/stat`, which `shell.sh` matches); `/proc/PID/exe` is the
    build.
    **What is recorded.** `box.json` has `quickshell` (the resolved path) and every box's
    `quickshell_version` (`qs_version`: `quickshell --version`'s first line, run in the box right
    after `hypr_version`). Not proof of a fix: a build of an unreleased commit says the last release
    ("Quickshell 0.3.1 (revision fae96f1..., distributed by Unset)" for a build with the 0.3.2 fix);
    its revision, when built from git, is the thing to read. `ls` prints `Quickshell: PATH (version)`
    under the box's line, `ls --json` has `quickshell` (null for the installed one) and
    `quickshell_version`, `windows` starts with `box NAME runs its shell on Quickshell PATH (...)`,
    `save` records it in `save.json` and `up --from` notes another one, and "already up, without what
    you asked for" names a different `--quickshell`.
    **Verified in a box** with a Debug build of fae96f1 (2026-09-23, with 916a0dd) against the
    installed Qt 6.11.2: the build's `qt_version_tag@Qt_6.11` matches and its `--private-check-compat`
    says 0, so it runs: the shell's `/proc/PID/exe` is the build, bar drawn (shot), `qs`/`quickshell`
    on the box's PATH are the link, `ls`/`ls --json`/`windows` name it with its version line;
    `restart-shell` and `omabox run -- omarchy restart shell` keep it; a throwaway `run --quickshell`
    too. **`tree` on it**: `omabox tree` (no selector: "no window matches active; the box's
    windows: (none)", exit 2; `--window class:quickshell` and `--window pid:PID` the same): the shell
    has no window, only layer surfaces (`omarchy-bar` 42x1080, `omarchy-background` 1920x1080), and
    `tree` selects a window from `hyprctl clients`. What AT-SPI has, read with a python3
    `gi.repository.Atspi` script run by `omabox run` (IsEnabled and ScreenReaderEnabled set first):
    two applications with the shell's pid, both named `quickshell` (`QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=gtk3`): an
    empty `gtk` one and the `Qt` one, which has two `frame`s, nameless, at 0,0 with the layer
    surfaces' sizes (42x1080, 1920x1080), both empty: Omarchy's QML sets no `Accessible.*`, and a
    Qt Quick item without a role is not published. A test config on the same build (a `PanelWindow`
    with a `Text` and a `Rectangle` with `Accessible.role: Accessible.Button` and a name) publishes
    `frame "" @0,0 1878x40 > button "a named button" [focusable] @65,0 80x30`, started before
    IsEnabled was set or after (no restart needed); on the installed
    0.3.1 the same config's Qt application has no children. So for `tree` to read the shell: select
    a layer (`hyprctl -j layers`: namespace, pid, x, y, w, h) instead of a window, take the AT-SPI
    application with that pid whose ToolkitName is `Qt` (not the `gtk` one listed first), the frame
    by size (they have no names), and add the layer's position to the bounds, which Qt gives in the
    surface's own coordinates (a Wayland client does not know where it is). Not done here.
    Checked: the refusals (a missing, non-executable or script file, an ELF without Qt, a folder
    refused as `--ro-bind`'s, `--no-shell`; a stub built against `qt_version_tag@Qt_6.10`; a stub
    whose `--private-check-compat` says 6.11.0: the box died with "--quickshell: built against Qt
    6.11.0, the box has Qt 6.11.2 ..."). Not checked: a real build against another Qt (none here),
    a jailed agent's real box. `t_unit_quickshell` (the refusals before a box, jail, relay,
    `qs_version`/`box_qs` with `on_box` stubbed), `t_quickshell` (a copy of the installed quickshell:
    exe, PATH, environment, ls/ls --json/windows, restart-shell and Omarchy's restart, already-up,
    save and `up --from`'s note, the in-box Qt check with a stub), `t_hyprland` (a box without it:
    the installed one, its version line).

359. **`omabox check` and `up --clean`: visual checks against a baseline** (2026-10-16, #252, built on
    finding 357). `up --clean`: --stock-bar on tokyo-night unless --theme, a 16x16 `#ff00ff` PNG
    (CLEAN_WALLPAPER_PNG, scaled by the background) that share/session.sh links over the background
    omarchy-theme-set chose (`OMABOX_CLEAN_WALLPAPER`), the clock's format and verticalFormat Qt
    literals in the box's shell.json, --no-pointer, --net isolated unless --net, and `animations off`
    in the run dir's omabox.clean, read by share/hyprland.lua on every load as omabox.pointer is (a
    reload kept them off). `--keep` takes animations, bar, clock, pointer, wallpaper back; box.json and
    ls --json have `clean: {keep}`; up_already compares --clean and --keep; `run` forwards both. `check
    point ID` (in a scenario, `$OMABOX_CHECK_OUT`): `wait still --quiet 500ms` (15 s; not still: taken,
    noted), a shot (screen, -g or --window, `OMABOX_SHOT_NO_BASELINE`), with --window `tree --json`,
    and ID.point (what, settled, tree, --ignore regions). `check run`: per run a fresh `up --clean`
    box (`check-PID-N`; `OMABOX_CHECK_NAME` is the suite's prefix), the scenario with `OMABOX` set,
    this omabox's bin first on PATH, its output in runN.log; exit 3 when it fails or takes no
    checkpoint. The comparison (check_regions): both shots with --ignore and unstable regions
    painted black, `difference`, `-alpha off` again (a -draw brought alpha back, and the parts'
    colour read `graya(255,...)`, so check.py saw no part at all: every masked comparison read same;
    found by t_check's moved button, caught before any release), max channel, threshold 0,
    connected components; share/check.py drops parts under 32 px (specks: the noise never made one
    over 13 on NVIDIA, 7 on AMD) and merges the rest 12 px apart. The tree diff keys an element by
    place (role#N under its parent), not by name: keyed by name, a label whose text changes each run
    (random, a time) read as one vanished and another appeared, never matched by the unstable list;
    a name change is now a `name` line, an element inserted before others of its role shifts theirs.
    **--approve runs 3 times, not 2** (--runs N): with 2, the subject's flaky status column (one
    start in eight 3-4 px left) was run 1 and became the baseline; now each checkpoint's baseline is
    the run most others match, and the regions and tree elements where any differed are its
    `ID.unstable`, said ("run 1 of 3 differed": the app or a minute that ticked; "every run
    differed": data or a time not pinned). A baseline's check.json (omabox, Hyprland, Omarchy, GPU
    driver, theme, size) is compared on each check: an AMD run against an NVIDIA baseline had 203
    regions in the app, and the report said "gpu nvidia -> amdgpu". Measured on the subject: approve
    52 s (3 boxes), a check ~15 s; the same build same but for its "added … HH:MM" when the
    minute had ticked (no clock pinning: Open); the 2 px spacing change caught (4 regions) and named
    (6 moved buttons), the ⋯ button's 2 px move only by the tree (its dots' parts are specks). Not
    inside ai-jail (refused). Tests: t_unit_check (check.py regions and tree, check diff on made
    images: specks, a block, a 3-level fill, --ignore here and elsewhere, --speck, a size; --keep;
    refusals), t_clean (sentinel pixel, literal clock, animations off over a reload, --keep, ls
    --json), t_check (a Qt Quick window: approve with an unstable random label, same, a button moved
    6 px: region and `moved +6,+0 button "Save"`, a new checkpoint, a failing scenario: exit 3).

360. **`up --clean`'s clock: a library that set every process's wall clock, built and left out**
    (2026-10-16, #252, built on findings 357-359). The bar's literal format freezes only the bar's
    text: an app's own times follow the real clock (the subject stamped an item "added today 16:37"
    and showed it, so a check made a minute later read a change). **What was built**: `tools/clock`,
    a library of omabox's own (no libfaketime here, no sudo to install it), `omabox-clock.so` in a
    clean box's own `/etc/ld.so.preload` (through `$D/etc` and the /etc overlay), so every
    dynamically linked process had it: the session, the shell, `run`'s commands (a clean
    environment: LD_PRELOAD would not reach them), D-Bus-activated services, a `--systemd` box's
    units. It read an instant file (Friday 2026-01-02 12:00 in the box's zone, and CLOCK_BOOTTIME at
    `up`) and ran CLOCK_REALTIME and its relatives from it (clock_gettime, gettimeofday, time,
    timespec_get, syscall()); CLOCK_MONOTONIC stayed the kernel's; omabox's own helpers kept the
    real clock (their stamps are compared with the host's). **Measured**: frozen, the shell, a Qt
    Quick app, a GTK 4 app and a headless Qt daemon idled (0.0-0.2% each) and their timers fired,
    but bash's `$SECONDS` and python's `time.time()` stood still, and a wait measured on the wall
    clock never ended (Omarchy has 20 scripts using `$SECONDS` or `date +%s`): so it ran from the
    instant, and the bar read "Friday 12:00" for the box's first minute only. Absolute deadlines on
    those clocks had to be moved into the real one, or the kernel returned at once (a busy loop):
    clock_nanosleep, timerfd_settime and timer_settime with ABSTIME, pthread_cond_timedwait,
    sem_timedwait, the timed locks and joins, mq, futex WAIT_BITSET/LOCK_PI by syscall(). On the
    subject: approve (3 boxes, nothing unstable), a check 2 minutes later 4 of 4 same, its item's
    time 12:00 in both. **Three bugs it found**, worth knowing for any preload of the kind: (1)
    systemd's TIME_T_MAX timerfd (how it hears of a clock set) overflowed when moved, fired at once,
    and a `--systemd` box's manager looped ("Looping too fast"; its Hyprland never came up): a
    deadline that means never must be left alone. (2) A GTK app's NVIDIA driver threads (`[vkps]
    Update`, `[vkrt] Analysis`) spun at 100% each, 400% in all: libnvidia-eglcore dlopens libc and
    looks up pthread_cond_timedwait with dlvsym at GLIBC_2.2.5, the compat version, past any
    interposed symbol; the library had to hand back its own from dlsym and dlvsym (0.1% then). (3)
    Those lookups first went through dlopen, whose allocation came back into jemalloc, which calls
    syscall() from its constructor before the library's had run: every Quickshell crashed at start;
    libc's dlsym and dlvsym had to be found in libc's symbol table (dl_iterate_phdr) instead.
    **Why it was left out**: it runs inside the app under test, which then is not the app users
    run; it needed those three crash and spin fixes to work at all, and each new runtime (another
    driver, allocator, a dlvsym of its own) could need another; it dates TLS (certificates judged at
    2026-01-02) and the box's logs (journal, apps.log); static binaries, Go programs, io_uring
    timeouts, 32-bit programs, Flatpak apps and what the kernel stamps (file times, socket stamps)
    kept the real clock anyway. What it bought can be had without it: data seeded relative to the
    real time when the scenario runs (`touch -d "9 months ago"`, a reset time of now + 2h10), an
    app's times `--ignore`d where a daemon in the box stamps them, an app's own test hooks. **Only it
    covers** absolute dates and "today" displays (a date column, a calendar's month, "added today
    16:37"), which drift from run to run without it; no project has needed one yet, so they are
    `--ignore`d. The library and its tests (t_unit_clock: a probe of every deadline call, the
    never one; t_clean's maps of the shell and the portal) are parked on the `parked/clock-preload`
    branch, to come back opt-in (never `up --clean`'s default) when a project needs it.
    `up --clean` freezes the bar's clock with the literal format again; `--keep clock` keeps the
    bar's real one.
361. **`check run`'s report: every change in one image** (2026-10-16, #252, after finding 359). A
    changed checkpoint's `ID.diff.png` is the whole shot marked, ~1.5k image tokens apiece (finding
    243's count), mostly of what did not change, and an agent read each. Now, when anything changed,
    `check run` also writes `report.png` and prints `report:  PATH` before its last line
    (check_report; share/check.py `sheet` lays it out and prints magick's arguments, the first what
    was left out). Inside one look: 1456 px wide at most, under 1.15 MP and 1568 high. Per changed
    checkpoint, each region with 24 px around it, its tree element too when that stays within
    400x120 (a label whose last word changed is read whole), crops of one checkpoint merged when
    under 24 px apart and within one side (706x360; a card's lines cost more than the pixels
    between), a crop of 160x120 or less at 2x (a 2 px move is 4 there); the baseline's crop, then
    this run's, each marked; above them the ID, the regions and up to 3 tree lines (the smallest
    changed element over a region, else the smallest element there; "+N more"). A mark is its four
    corners: a whole rectangle hid the digit beside a changed time ("16:37"). Blue marks a tree
    change with bounds no region covers: the subject's ⋯ button's 2 px move, a tree line only
    until now, is drawn (tree bounds used only when the tree's frame is the shot's size). A size
    change: both whole at one scale; more than 6 crops in one checkpoint (another GPU's 203
    regions): the whole shots, scaled, marked. When not all fit: each checkpoint's first crop before
    any's second, at full size, then with each side at half if that shows more; the rest named in
    the image and on stdout ("not in it, no room: ID, ID (2 of 5 crops)"). The legend wraps to the
    cards' width (360 px at least): unwrapped it made a small report wider than its cards. Texts
    go through -annotate, which reads % and \ as escapes and a leading @ as a file: escaped, the
    app's names made printable. Font: fc-match monospace, magick's default without one.
    `ID.diff.png` stays the full-size record. **Measured** (image tokens, w x h / 750 scaled as
    finding 243 says): t_check's shape (its window tiled to 1896x1030, the button moved 6 px, 3
    regions) 559x196, 146 against 1533 (10x less); a Qt Quick window with a toolbar whose spacing
    grew 2 px and a renamed row, checkpoints of the window and the screen (8 regions each)
    1242x320, 530 against 3066 (17%); the subject's 2 px spacing change (3 checkpoints, 10 regions)
    1329x482, 854 against 4599 (19%), each change legible at 1x, read by looking at it. `check diff
    A B --report R.png` takes the same layout, one pair named after B: an agent comparing two shots
    of its own read the marked whole shot just the same, and the plan is check run's with one
    point; `-o` stays the marked shot. Not in the report: a `new` checkpoint (no pair); the same
    change in two checkpoints (the subject's app and help) is shown twice. Seen once in t_check, not
    looked into (its files went with the suite's TMP): the bar's checkpoint changed by one region
    on the check right after --approve, in 1 of 3 runs. Tests: t_unit_check (check diff --report on
    made images: the path after the regions, inside one look and a tenth of the shot, the
    baseline's crop left and the new right at 2x by their pixels, a size, no report when same;
    check.py sheet: a region's tree line with a % doubled, a blue move under a speck, 7 crops as the
    whole shots, 12 big crops at half size and the 6 left named in the image), t_check (the report's
    path, inside one look, none and no plan left when same).
362. **`check point` finds holes: the sentinel wallpaper inside a surface** (2026-10-16, #252, built
    on finding 359). `up --clean`'s `#ff00ff` is no theme's colour, so any of it inside a window, the
    bar or a popup is a defect, and nothing looked for it. Hyprland's rectangles cannot say where: a
    Quickshell popup is drawn in a full-screen layer (`omarchy-keyboard-panel` is 1920x1080, its card
    ~400x790 at the top right). So pixels: the 8-connected parts of exactly the sentinel (antialiased
    edges blend it, so no edge pixel is ever exactly it); a part that reaches the screen's edge is the
    open wallpaper (gaps between tiled windows join gaps_out), the rest are enclosed by surfaces:
    holes. A window's own pixels (`--window`, grim -T: alpha kept, no wallpaper behind) have holes
    where alpha is 0, an edge included (all of the buffer is the window). Rounded corners: Omarchy's
    windows are square (rounding 0; GTK4 draws square, tiled), but an app's rounded background inside
    Hyprland's border leaves a pocket at each corner that the border encloses (radius 14: 42 px in a
    10x10 box); so a part at most 32 px a side filling under half its box (outside an arc: 21% of its
    square) is a corner, left out and counted. Holes 12 px apart merge (a text's counters with the hole
    it sits in). A -g checkpoint's holes come from a second, whole-screen shot, kept where they meet
    the region, in its pixels: on the region alone, a hole its edge cuts would read as open. Holes
    inside an --ignore region are left out. Off (`holes off: WHY` in ID.point) outside a clean box,
    with --keep wallpaper, and once a theme set in the box replaced the background link
    (`current/background` no longer the sentinel's PNG: checked, not assumed). Results: ID.point's
    `hole X,Y WxH PX` lines (a baseline keeps its own), said by `check point` on stderr. --approve
    says each (`holes    ID: the wallpaper shows through at ...`, for a window "the window is
    transparent") and ends with `check: HOLES in N of M checkpoints (IDs)`, exit 0: a design may be
    see-through on purpose, and an approve is a person's decision; a check fails (`holes    ID: ... at
    N places the baseline does not have`, or `hole:` lines under `changed`, marked on ID.diff.png) on
    a hole no baseline hole overlaps, even where the shots match: a hole in an unstable region, or
    one under the 32 px speck (a 5 px one in t_check). Approved holes are a note under `same`.
    Measured in boxes (NVIDIA): the stock bar, none; a Qt Quick window with a rounded transparent
    background, none (its four corners left out), with an 80x50 odd-even hole: found on the screen, by
    -g and in the window (alpha 0); a GTK4 (libadwaita) window with a transparent background and an
    80 px gap in a 60 px row, found (80x60) on both, on solitude (rounding 6) too, with no false ones
    from its rounded windows; a stock popup (KeyboardPanel) over the wallpaper and a real widget's popup
    (~400x790, its app moved to another workspace), none; a popup whose card forgot its background,
    one hole of 316x176, and by -g in the region's pixels. ~0.5 s a checkpoint. Limits: a popup over
    a window shows the window through a hole, not the wallpaper (take a popup's checkpoint over an
    empty workspace); a hole opening onto the open wallpaper (a card's gap reaching its edge) is open;
    blur is off in Omarchy's defaults; a theme or a user config that turns it on would blur and tint
    what a see-through window shows, no longer exactly the sentinel.
    Tests: t_unit_check (made images: a hole, the gap to the margin, a gap at the edge, rounded
    content in a border, a region cutting a hole, a window's alpha holes, new against a baseline's,
    when off), t_check (the window's rounded transparent background: none approved; a 5 px hole fails
    a check whose shots match; 40 px said at --approve), t_clean (the stock bar none, --keep
    wallpaper off).

363. **What a first visual check missed: specks per checkpoint, the baseline seen, a pinned locale**
    (2026-10-16, #252, after findings 357-362; a first-time user's report). **Real changes read
    "same".** A bar widget's spacing changed by 2 px made a 16 px part of the difference, and the fixed
    32 px speck dropped it; a bar widget has no tree to catch it otherwise. Nautilus's sort arrow
    vanished: a 26 px part, dropped too. 32 was what Qt Quick's distance-field text needed (finding 357:
    13 px at most on NVIDIA, 7 on AMD), applied to everything. Now each checkpoint has its own, measured
    at --approve: the baseline run against each other run with the unstable regions painted out (a part
    inside one is not noise; a part of 32 px or more is a region, so unstable), the largest part left
    twice over, CHECK_SPECK_MIN (16) at least and CHECK_SPECK at most; CHECK_SPECK_AGREED (8) when the
    runs agreed to the pixel. That one was 0 (compared exactly) first, and read noise as changes twice:
    a crop of a Qt Quick window holding one button agreed in three runs on AMD and showed a 1 px part in
    the next check, and t_check's window agreed over its 2 runs and showed 2 px of its button's text; 8
    is under what the changes 32 dropped made (16 px, 26). The 16: three runs see the text noise (it
    comes with every start of the app) but not its tail; on AMD they saw 5 px and the next check a 10 px
    part, read as changed at twice 5. And every checkpoint of one window (`of window SEL`, its crops
    too) takes the window's largest, since the noise is the app's (that crop's window had 16). `speck N`
    in the baseline's ID.point (check.py regions prints the largest speck now); `--speck N` by hand
    wins, at --approve too (stored); a baseline without it keeps 32. --approve says it (`baseline ID
    (specks under 22 px left out: the runs' largest stray part was 11 px)`, `(specks under 8 px left
    out: the runs agreed to the pixel)`, `speck    ID: under 22 px, as the other checkpoints of its
    window`), and a `same` line says what it left out (`same     app (121 specks left out, the largest
    10 px)`): nothing is dropped without a word. **Measured**, a scenario of the bar, its clock
    (160x26), a Qt Quick window of 8 text rows and a button, a crop of it holding the button and the
    screen: on NVIDIA the window's runs differed by 11 px at most (speck 22, the screen too); on AMD by
    5 (speck 16); the bar and its clock agreed to the pixel on both (8), so a bar widget's 2 px spacing
    (16 px) is caught. Four checks after each approve: all same (the window's largest speck 10-11 px on
    NVIDIA, 5-6 on AMD); the rows' spacing 1 px wider: changed on both (1 region; the tree, 7 rows
    moved). **Approve could bless a broken state**: the baseline is what most runs showed, so a wrong
    screen in most of them (an error, a page not loaded yet) becomes it, unseen. Now --approve writes
    `baseline.png` in the runs' folder (check.py `overview`, through check_report): every checkpoint as
    kept, each scaled to the sheet's width and all of them down together until they fit one look
    (finding 361's 1456 px, 1.15 MP, 1568 high), unstable regions amber (a see-through fill, so what is
    under them reads), holes red; prints `overview: PATH` and `check: look at it before you keep this
    baseline`. Five checkpoints (the bar, its clock, a window, a crop of it, the screen): 1100x1015,
    each legible. **The clean desktop did not pin the locale**: the box took the host's LC_TIME=pt_BR
    (launch.sh passes LANG and every LC_*, finding 58) and an app's dates read "Há 9 meses". `up
    --clean` now gives the session LANG=en_US.UTF-8 (when `locale -a` has it, else C.UTF-8) and none of
    the host's LC_* or LANGUAGE (`run`'s commands take the session's: omabox.env), `/etc/locale.conf`
    with that LANG for what reads the file (a `--systemd` box's user manager), and `/etc/localtime` a
    link to UTC. Both in the box's /etc (`$D/etc`); the link goes in through the overlay, never a bind:
    a bind follows the link at its destination, and would have mounted UTC's data over the host's zone
    file under its name, which Qt reads the zone's id from. A `--env TZ` still wins over the zone (and
    is what box.json records). `--keep locale` gives the host's LANG,
    LC_* and /etc/localtime back. box.json's `clean` and the baseline's check.json have `locale` and
    `timezone`; the comparison's note names them when they differ and the baseline has them (one from
    before has not). **Relative dates** ("9 months ago") come from files' mtimes: `omabox run -- touch
    -d "9 months ago" F`, run by the scenario, is relative to the real time then, as the app's "now"
    is, so each run reads the same; an absolute date drifts (finding 360). **Timing**: each run says `check: run N of M: box up in N s` (a first box
    took 31 s, the next 4, with nothing said before). **Output**: the last line counts every kind
    (`check: 2 of 5 same, 2 changed, 1 new`; missing ones count in the total, holes-only ones as `with
    new holes`); a check without a baseline exits 4, not 1 as `changed` does; a tree element with no
    name says where it is (`appeared  button  (in frame "W" > panel#1 > button#2)`: its nearest named
    ancestor, then each place). **`check point --window SEL -g "X,Y WxH"`**, refused before: a crop of
    the window in its coordinates, as `shot --window -g` takes it; `wait still` on the whole window (it
    takes a window or a region); the tree only the elements touching the crop and their ancestors
    (check.py `crop-tree`, an element without bounds going with its nearest ancestor that has some),
    each with its key from the whole window (`key`, which `load` takes as it is), so one outside the
    crop that moves or goes changes nothing inside, nor shifts the places of those inside; the window's
    node carries the crop, and the report's blue marks are drawn in the crop's pixels. `crop GEOM` in
    ID.point. Holes from the crop's own alpha. **t_check's unstable label** sat on the window's
    background: when the two approve runs' random numbers shared their first digit, that digit was in no
    unstable region and the next check read it as changed (seen once here, 7 failures); it now sits on a
    backdrop of a random colour, all of it unstable. Its 5 px hole test runs at `--speck 32`, the hole a
    speck to the shots' comparison as before; at the window's own speck it is a region as well (both
    checked). Seen by the user, not omabox's: a bar widget sometimes missed a record seeded just after
    it started. Tests: t_unit_check (regions' largest speck; a nameless element appeared and vanished,
    where; crop-tree's elements and keys, a move inside and one outside; check_approve on made runs: the
    specks (16 at least), 8 where the runs agreed, `--speck`, a window's shared, the image;
    check_compare: same with what it left out, a 10 px part changed at 8 and the same at 16, 32 for a
    baseline without, `--speck 0` by hand, new and missing counted, locale and timezone said only when
    the baseline has them; clean_locale; exit 4), t_clean (the session's
    LANG, no LC_* under a host LC_TIME, UTC, locale.conf, the shell's environment; --keep locale: the
    host's LC_TIME and zone, recorded), t_check (box up said, a crop of the window: plain baseline, its
    tree's move, the baseline's image inside one look, specks in every .point, check.json's locale and
    timezone, counts).
364. **`tree` put what is inside a Qt Quick dialog at the dialog's coordinates** (2026-10-16, a first
    real visual check of a Qt Quick app: its settings, add and help sheets are popups with the dialog
    role). The settings sheet read `@0,0 760x875` and its rows `@16,65`, though it is drawn at 568,78
    of the window: in WINDOW coordinates Qt says 0,0 for a popup with the dialog role and measures what
    is inside it from the popup (Qt 6.11.2). So a click at a row's middle hit the table behind, and
    `check point --window SEL -g` on the sheet kept the elements behind it (crop-tree's overlap test)
    and lost most of the sheet's: a 2 px move of its rows showed only as pixels, and the report named
    the background's rows for the sheet's red regions. Qt's SCREEN coordinates are right relative to
    the window's (a Wayland window's screen origin is 0,0 to Qt), so `tools/tree` now takes, for a
    dialog or window element below the frame that says 0,0, the offset of its SCREEN position from the
    frame's, and adds it to that element and everything under it (a dialog inside it sets its own).
    GTK's dialogs are windows of their own (their own frame), and every other element keeps its
    WINDOW coordinates. Measured on that app: the sheet at `@568,78`, its rows at x 584 (where `wait`
    saw one change), a click at a row's middle opened that section; the 2 px move read `moved +0,+2
    list item "Speed"` and ten more such lines. Test: t_tree's demo window has a non-modal Dialog at
    260,170: drawn there, its button in window coordinates, a click at the button's middle presses it
    (all three fail on the old helper: the button at `@6,37`).
365. **A checkpoint's `--ignore` held for its pixels, not its tree** (2026-10-16, the same check). An
    app's "added today 02:13" was `--ignore`d and its pixels left out, but its label's text still
    changed in the tree, so no two --approve runs agreed: a layout the app moved in one start of three
    read "every run differed: data or a time the scenario does not pin", not "run 1 of 3 differed",
    and a check a minute later would read changed. check.py's `tree` and `tree-keys` now take `--shot
    W H` and `--mask X Y W H` (check_tree_masks makes them from the .point's `ignore` lines and the
    shot's size, for check_one and check_approve) and leave out an element whose box is wholly inside a
    mask in each tree that has it, in the shot's pixels (less the crop's corner for a `-g` crop), as
    its pixels are; the report's marks too (marks_of reads the .point beside the new shot). Only when
    the tree's size is the shot's (not on a scaled monitor, as marks_of). Partly inside is kept, and an
    element's box can be wider than its text (that label was 368 px, the region 300), so `tree-keys`
    lines say the box now (`frame#1/label#4  (label "added today 02:13" @1512,91 368x15)`): an
    unstable line shows the region that would hold it. Tests: t_unit_check (a label wholly inside, partly,
    a shot of another size, a crop's pixels, tree-keys, an argument it does not take; the key line's box).
366. **`baseline.png` was unreadable past a handful of checkpoints** (2026-10-17, #256). Finding
    363's overview shrank every shot together until all fit one look; with 28 checkpoints (a Qt
    Quick app's window, its sheets, 17 settings sections, a bar widget's popup) each came out 40-70
    px wide, under a title strip as wide as its text, and could not tell a right screen from a wrong
    one, which is what the overview is for. Now each shot keeps OV_MIN_PX (90000 px, 400x225 for a
    16:9 window; a floor by area, since a floor by width made a tall sheet 400x460 and one row a

    does not fit one look goes on more pages, `baseline-2.png`..., written in the same magick call
    (`-write` and `+delete` in a parenthesised page each, the last the output); check.py overview
    prints the pages after the first in its first field, and approve names them all (`overview:
    .../baseline.png and 3 more pages: ...`). Measured on those 28: 4 pages (1218x782, 1218x782,
    1297x681, 1456x777), every settings section readable as itself; 5 checkpoints stay one page.
    Test: t_unit_check (14 screens: more pages, each one look, `OUT-2.png`; 2: one page).
367. **One change seen in many checkpoints filled the check's output and its report** (2026-10-17,
    #257). A 2 px margin added above a sheet's navigation moved the same 12 rows in all 17
    checkpoints of that sheet: 17 listings of 4-7 regions and 12 tree lines each (~340 lines), and

    now gives each changed checkpoint a key (check_change_key): its size change; else its tree lines
