    section's highlight sat inside the moved list, so each section had its own regions (4 to 6) for
    the same move. A checkpoint whose key an earlier one had is one line, `changed  ID: as FIRST
    (its tree lines; 6 regions, all on what they name)`, still counted as changed (`18 changed (16
    as another)`), its ID.diff.png still written, and a plan line `also FIRST ID` puts `the same in
    16 more: ...` on FIRST's card instead of a card of its own. Measured on that check: 54 lines of
    output, a report of 2 cards (the other change, a word in another sheet, beside it), every crop
    larger for the room. Tests: t_unit_check (unexplained: a region on the moved element and one
    elsewhere, a scaled shot; check_compare on made runs: two checkpoints with one change and a
    third with another, the line, the count, the diff image).
368. **at-spi2-core 2.61 has no ScreenReaderEnabled, and libatspi logs as `atspi`** (2026-10-20,
    #237 and finding 349 revisited). With at-spi2-core 2.62.1 (from 2.60.6) every `tree` printed
    `omabox: tree: could not set org.a11y.Status.ScreenReaderEnabled (... No such property ...)`:
    the bus launcher's 2.61.0 rework of IsEnabled (it now also assumes accessibility on once an AT
    registers events) left only `IsEnabled` on `org.a11y.Status` (its introspection, and the
    launcher's source at 2.61.0). The line broke `--find`'s one-line answer and `--json | jq` when
    stderr was read with stdout. `omabox-tree` now reads a "No such property" answer to its Get of
    ScreenReaderEnabled as none to set, says nothing, and only when PID is not on the bus adds that
    an egui/winit app on AccessKit before accesskit_unix 0.22 never joins it here (it waits for
    that property: not omabox's to give; `help tree` and the reference say so). Two libatspi
    changes too: dbind logs under the GLib domain `atspi` (2.61.0), so finding 341's filter of the
    cache-object warning missed it, and is now on both domains; and GetItems answered
    UnknownMethod, ServiceUnknown or NoReply warns no more, so t_tree's mute app (no objects at
    all) gave no warning to keep: it now has a cache whose GetItems fails with its own error.
    Seen in a box: GTK4 and Qt Quick trees read with no stray line, IsEnabled set; the failing
    cache's `atspi-WARNING ... Error in GetItems` shown on a failed `--find` only. Tests: t_tree
    (ScreenReaderEnabled checked where the bus has it; else the not-on-bus reason checked on foot).
369. **t_unit_install read this machine's packages** (2026-10-20). Fourteen of its checks failed
    at once after `hyprwayland-scanner` (one of install.sh's aquamarine build packages) was removed
    from the machine by hand: install.sh asked the real `pacman -T`, found it missing, and the
    test's `sudo` stub (exit 1) stopped it at the Packages step, before the tools, links and guard
    the checks were about. The test's guard checks had a fake HOME throughout; nothing reached the
    real `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`. A `pacman` stub now answers `-T` as all present, or with the
    names a test file lists, and the `sudo` stub logs what it was asked. Tests: t_unit_install (a
    missing package: `sudo pacman -S --needed` with it, install.sh stops when that fails, the
    package named; the rest as before, on any package set).
370. **An a11y launcher a harness starts can lose its bus name to an activated one** (2026-10-20,
    #234's check). t_dbus_user_app starts `/usr/lib/at-spi-bus-launcher` from a cleaned environment
    and at once asks `org.a11y.Bus` for its address, then looked for dbus-broker under that launcher.
    With at-spi2-core 2.62.1 the launcher first activates `org.gtk.vfs.Daemon` (gvfsd, whose fuse
    mount prints "fuse: device /dev/fuse not found" in a box), so the call reached the session bus
    before it owned the name, the bus activated a second launcher from its service file, and the
    first exited: the bus and its dbus-broker were up, under the other launcher. Nothing for omabox
    to change (the bus a test gets is the same); the check now looks under the name's owner
    (`busctl --user status org.a11y.Bus`) and reads only its own result line. Seen in a box: the
    started launcher gone, the activated one's dbus-broker-launch and dbus-broker serving the bus.
    Tests: t_dbus_user_app.
371. **Qt 6.12 gives a wheel's notch a pixelDelta of 15** (2026-10-20, corrects finding 287's "no
    pixelDelta"). After qt6-base and qt6-wayland 6.11.2 → 6.12.0, t_pointer's Qt Quick window got
    `angleDelta 120, pixelDelta 15` for each `--source wheel` notch, where it had 0. The compositor
    sends the same as before (Qt's WAYLAND_DEBUG in a box: `axis(…, 0, -15)`, `axis_source(0)`
    (wheel), `axis_value120(0, -120)`, `frame`): Qt now passes the axis value on as pixels for a
    wheel too, so a real mouse's wheel on the desktop gets them as well (assumed: not measured on
    real hardware), and an app that prefers pixelDelta when it is not zero scrolls 15 px a notch
    instead of its line step. QTBUG-112432 still holds: the device is still the seat's touchpad and
    a WheelHandler at its default acceptedDevices still takes nothing. `help scroll` says it; the
    checks take 0 or 15. Tests: t_pointer.
372. **Quickshell 0.3.2 warns about every Omarchy plugin dir: not the plugin's warning**
    (2026-10-20). With Quickshell 0.3.2.r7 (from 0.3.1) the shell logs, for each plugin under
    `~/.config/omarchy/plugins`, `WARN quickshell.qmlscanner: Module path "…/plugins/ID" is outside
    of the config folder.` (Omarchy's shell runs from /usr/share/omarchy/shell; its plugins live
    in the user's config), and the plugin loads as before. `up` and `restart-shell` read any shell
    log line naming a plugin as its warning, so every mounted plugin that loaded came out as
    "plugin ID loaded, with a warning in the shell log: Module path …" (t_plugin_check's good
    plugin, t_plugin_link's fixed one), and `ls --json` gave it as the plugin's `log`. The lines a
    plugin's state reads (now `shell_warnings`) leave that one message out; any other qmlscanner
    line still counts (0.3.2 also says a first-party plugin's dir, `/plugins/image-picker`, has
    characters a module name cannot: it names no mounted plugin). Not a concurrent change on the
    host: the box's own shell log, the string is in /usr/bin/quickshell. Tests: t_unit_shell_warnings,
    t_plugin_check, t_plugin_link.
373. **The registry's stand-in inotifywait waits without starting a process** (2026-10-20, #275).
    Finding 196's stand-in waited with `while kill -0 "$PPID"; do sleep 5; done`: a `sleep` every
    5 s for the shell's life, which Omarchy's `test/shell.d/shell-idle-spawn-test.sh` counts, so it
    failed in every box (`6 sleep 5` in 30 s) and hid a real poll behind omabox's. Quickshell gives
    the process a stdin pipe whose write end it holds and never writes (seen in a box: the shell's
    fd and the stand-in's are the only two on it), so the stand-in now `read -t 3600`s it: no
    process, a wakeup an hour, and end of file the moment the shell is gone. "Alive" is "still our
    parent" (`/proc/$$/stat`'s ppid against `$PPID`): a shell killed but not yet reaped is a zombie
    `kill -0` still finds, and the stand-in, reparented at its exit, outlived it in a test that way.
    A stdin that ends while the shell lives (another parent's /dev/null) falls back to a check
    every 5 s with bash's loadable `sleep` (`/usr/lib/bash/sleep`, a builtin; the external one where
    it is missing). Omarchy's idle-spawn test, run in a throwaway box from an Omarchy checkout
    (`omabox run -- bash test/shell.d/shell-idle-spawn-test.sh`): `not ok … 6 sleep 5` before, `ok -
    an idle shell starts no processes over 30s` after. Tests: t_unit_inotifywait (no child over 2 s
    on a held pipe and on /dev/null, ends within 1 s of its shell; three of its checks fail on the
    old stand-in).
374. **`down` removes a box HOME whatever modes its apps left in it** (2026-10-20, #264). A walk
    that made a read-only folder in the box HOME (`mkdir -p ~/locked/dest && chmod a-w …`, a
    destination an app cannot write) left `~/.cache/omabox/BOX` behind at `down`: `rm_box` made
    only the runtime dir writable (finding 61's mode-000 entries), `rm -rf` cannot empty a dir it
    may not write, and its failure, the last command of `rm_box` under `set -e`, ended `down` before
    it said `box 'BOX' down` (it printed only rm's complaint). The next `up` under that name
    inherited the old HOME's leftovers, and `sweep_homes`, with no chmod, failed on it at every `up`
    without a word. Both now go through `rm_tree`: `chmod -R -P u+rwX` (`-P`: a symlink in the box
    HOME, which an app can point anywhere on the host, is never followed; sweep_homes also skips a
    link in the cache dir) then `rm -rf`; if something is still left, one stderr line with rm's first
    complaint, and `down` goes on. Tests: t_unit_rm_tree (a read-only HOME, a mode-000 runtime dir,
    a gone box's HOME, a link not followed, a failure said), t_up_again (a box whose app made the
    folder: HOME gone, `down` says only that the box is down; both failed on the old code).
    Amended by finding 524: `chmod -R` without `-P` (coreutils before 9.5 refused it).
375. **While a box is up, the desktop's stranded-lock recovery waits** (2026-10-20, #277). Omarchy
    4.0.5's `omarchy-hyprland-session-lock-stranded`, which the desktop's shell asks after a crash
    with the screen locked, answers "undetermined" (exit 2) while any `quickshell|qs|hyprlock` of
    the user runs besides the caller (`pgrep -u $UID -x`), and a box's shell is one. On the host,
    Omarchy 4.0.6, only `omarchy-hyprland-session-locked` stubbed to "locked", the desktop shell's
    pid passed: exit 2 with one box up (`omabox which` named the other quickshell as the box's),
    exit 0 once it was down. So the lock is not retaken until every box is down; it fails closed.
    Omarchy's to scope (only lockers under the caller's Hyprland instance); omabox only says it:
    skill/reference.md, Mounts, HOME and the session. No `ls`/`up` warning (decided).

376. **`run -d --replace` names a job of the same program with other arguments** (2026-10-20,
    #255). `--replace` matches a job by its whole command line (finding 110), so `./build/app --demo
    details` then `--replace -- ./build/app --demo table` left the first one running beside the new
    one, and the note "no earlier job of this command" read as "nothing was running". The contract
    stays (matching by program instead would stop a second instance on purpose); when nothing matches
    and a live `run -d` job of the same program runs, the note names it: `no earlier job with these
    arguments; ./build/app (pid 115, --demo details) still runs: stop it, or --replace with its
    arguments`, under -q too. A job record now keeps `exe`, argv[0] resolved lexically against the
    caller's directory (`./build/app` and `build/app` are one program; a bare name stays a name);
    a record from before has only argv[0], compared as written. In a box: `sleep 601` then
    `--replace -- sleep 602` names the first (t_replace; t_unit_replace_others).

377. **`down` where the derived name has no box names the session's boxes** (2026-10-20, #262).
    A box's default name comes from the directory, so a session that started its box in a scratch
    folder (`default-SESSION`) and later ran `omabox down` in a worktree got "no box
    '<worktree>-SESSION'", exit 0, and its box stayed up while the agent believed it had cleaned up.
    `down` with no name now, when no box has the derived name but boxes carrying this session's id
    are up (`session_boxes`, finding 200's test: the agent session's id in the name; a box from
    `up --new` has none and is not named), says each with where `up` ran and its down: `no box 'X';
    this session has 'Y' (started in ~/…): omabox down -b Y`, and exits 1. `up` now records that
    directory in box.json (`dir`; not for a jailed caller); a box from before shows none. A plain
    "no box" (no session box up, or a name given) still exits 0. No `down --mine` (decided). Real
    box: up from a scratch folder, `omabox down` in this repo named it, exit 1 (t_unit_agent_session).
378. **`check`: refusals exit 2, checkpoint shots full size, `--ignore` in -g's space** (2026-10-20,
    #281; before `check`'s first release, so no deprecation). The CLI audit (#273) found three things
    a CI step would trip on. (1) Every refusal and setup error under `check` (an unknown option, a
    missing file, no magick, no box, a box that did not start) exited 1, `check`'s "changed": a typo
    read as a visual change. `die` now exits `$DIE_RC` (1 by default), and `cmd_check` sets it to 2;
    3 and 4 of `check run` are unchanged. (2) `check point` took its shots, and the screen shot for a
    region's holes, through `shot` without `--fit`, so the user's `config shot-fit` or
    `$OMABOX_SHOT_FIT` scaled them (verified in a clean box: `OMABOX_SHOT_FIT=800` made a checkpoint
    of the screen 800x450 and one of the bar 800x10): a baseline approved on one machine was "size
    1920x1080 -> 800x450" on another. Both now pass `--fit 0`. (3) `check point --ignore` took image
    pixels (scaled, from the crop's corner), while `-g` beside it, and every other region with
    `--window`, is in the window's own coordinates. It is now -g's space: the window's with
    `--window` (a crop's origin taken off), else the screen's; after the shot, `check_ignore_px`
    turns each region into the shot's pixels from its `shots.tsv` record (what it covers, at what
    size), rounded outwards and cut to the shot; one with nothing in the shot is said and left out.
    The `.point` keeps `ignore X Y W H` in the shot's pixels, as before, so the comparison, the tree
    masks (finding 365) and the holes filter read it unchanged. `check diff` keeps image pixels (two
    files, no box). Real box: a crop of the bar at 100,0 with `--ignore "150,5 20x10"` recorded
    `ignore 50 5 20 10`; t_clean, t_check (`OMABOX_SHOT_FIT=800` on a check against a baseline
    approved without it: all same; a window crop's `--ignore`), t_unit_check (exit 2 for nine
    refusals; the conversion at scales 1, 1.5 and 2).

379. **`--window` input names a layer surface over its point** (2026-10-20, #263). A walk's `click
    --window APP X Y` on a link near the window's top right went to an Omarchy notification toast
    over that corner, exit 0, nothing said: `win_point` checked only windows over the point (finding
    81 left layers out as full-screen surfaces). Hyprland gives the pointer to a layer surface on the
    overlay level, then the top level, before any window (`InputManager::mouseMoveUnified`), except
    that on a monitor whose workspace has a window in real fullscreen (internal mode 2; `hyprctl
    clients`' `fullscreen` is 2, maximized is 1) a top one whose `aboveFullscreen` is false (the
    fullscreen handler clears it for every layer of that monitor) is passed by; overlays always get
    it. So `win_annotate` takes `hyprctl -j layers` (optional fourth argument; read once per
    `win_point`, raising changes none) and gives each on-screen window `layers`: the top and overlay
    ones whose rectangle overlaps it, bottom to top, top ones dropped under a real fullscreen window
    of its workspace, 1x1 hidden menus (finding 146) left out. `win_layer` names the topmost over the
    point. `click`, `scroll` and `drag --window` say it on stderr and send the input; under
    `--no-raise` they refuse, exit 1 (raising would not help); `pointer --window`, which never
    raises but refuses a covering window, only says it (decided: a full-screen overlay would
    otherwise refuse every move while a toast is up). `windows` prints one line per such layer under
    its table, naming the windows under it; `--json` has `layers`. The limit: only a layer's
    rectangle is known. Omarchy 4.0.6's toasts sit in one full-screen overlay (`omarchy-notifications`,
    `anchors` on all four sides, `mask: Region { item: popupColumn }`, mapped only while a toast
    shows), so while a toast is up every point of every window is "under" it: the warning is honest
    ("where it takes input, input there goes to it"), but `--no-raise` refuses clicks far from the
    toast too. Nothing in Hyprland 0.56.2 gives a layer's input region or the surface under a point:
    not `hyprctl layers`, not Lua's layer objects (`x y w h namespace pid monitor mapped layer
    interactivity above_fullscreen`), no pointer-focus event. The way out the messages name: `omabox
    wait layer NS --gone` (a toast goes by itself; a click on it closes it). Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6,
    Hyprland 0.56.2, 1920x1080): with a `notify-send` toast up, `--no-raise` at the toast refused and
    left it up, `pointer --window` said it and moved, a plain `click --window` said it and the toast
    closed; without a toast, nothing said. t_click_layer (that; the `--no-raise` refusal fails on the
    old code), t_unit_window_select (the levels, the fullscreen rule, a maximized window, the topmost
    of two, the edges, `windows`' lines).
380. **The desk's fonts are in every box, read-only** (2026-10-20, #261). `up` seeded the desk's
    theme and `shell.toml` but not the faces in `~/.local/share/fonts`, so a theme whose labels use
    its own faces drew them in a fallback (`fc-match` gave Liberation Sans), silently: shots looked
    plausible but were wrong in widths, case and tracking. A project's box script worked round it
    with `--seed ~/.local/share/fonts/DIR:.local/share/fonts/DIR` on every `up`. Decided (Diogo): the
    desk's user fonts go into every box read-only, not into `up --clean` boxes, a flag to opt out.
    Now `seed_fonts` mounts `~/.local/share/fonts` and `~/.fonts`, each where it is (resolved),
    `--ro-bind` at the same place in the box HOME, before any `--ro-bind` of the caller's (which
    wins). Mounted, not copied: nothing to copy each `up`, the box cannot change them, and a save
    keeps only the empty mount point (it copies the HOME from the host side). They are there from
    the box's first process, so the box's Hyprland and shell (which read their fonts once, at start)
    have them; fontconfig caches them in the box HOME's `~/.cache/fontconfig` on that first read, as
    it already did the system's fonts (a box has no `/var/cache/fontconfig`): no `fc-cache` step.
    Opt out: `--no-seed fonts`, beside `--no-seed extensions` (the existing "what of the desk a box
    starts without" vocabulary); `--clean` leaves them out and `--keep fonts` brings them back (both
    lists existed; no `omabox config` key, as `--no-seed extensions` has none). Not mounted, and
    said: a folder `refuse_src` refuses (a link to a secret store, to HOME), one that is not a
    folder, and one the box HOME already has with something in it (a `--from` save's, a `--seed`
    into it: the old workaround keeps working, the box keeps its own). A link in them that leads out
    of them (not inside the folder, not into `/usr`) is not followed or mounted: it leads nowhere in
    the box, and `up` says how many and the first. A jailed caller's box gets them too, as it gets
    the desk's themes (fonts hold nothing of the user's); `OMABOX_DESK_HOME`, the suite's fake desk
    HOME, is ignored in a jail, as `OMABOX_DESK_CONFIG` is. `up` says "your desk's fonts are in the
    box, read-only: ~/.local/share/fonts (--no-seed fonts starts without them)"; box.json and `ls
    --json` have `desk_fonts` (`[]` without). The issue's other half, a warning when a family the
    seeded theme names in `shell.toml [font]` does not resolve: not done, since Omarchy 4.0.6's
    `[font]` names no family (sizes only: `base-size` and per-token px; the family is fontconfig's
    `monospace` alias, and a theme's own faces are named by plugins' QML), so there is nothing cheap
    to check. Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2, the real desk): `fc-match "Chakra Petch"`
    gave `/home/sbx/.local/share/fonts/baseline/ChakraPetch-Regular.ttf` (Liberation Sans before),
    the fontconfig cache written at the second Hyprland and quickshell started. t_desk_fonts (a fake
    desk HOME: fontconfig finds the font, read-only, `desk_fonts`; `--no-seed fonts` and `--clean`
    without it), t_unit_desk_fonts (both folders, the link out, a broken link and one into /usr not
    said, `--no-seed fonts`, `--clean`, `--keep fonts`, the box's own folder kept, a save's link
    replaced, a refused folder, a file, the jail), t_unit_check (`--keep fonts`, `clean_text`).

381. **`wait until` replaces `wait cmd`; `path --home`** (2026-10-20, #272). Subagents in their own
    git worktree (Claude Code's isolation) had 36 omabox calls refused in 46 threads (10-09..10-16).
    The worktree check does not refuse compound commands as such: it refuses words it reads as a
    shell or a builtin that runs text in an unknown program's arguments (`cmd`, `bash`, `source`,
    `enable`, `nice -n`), shell text it cannot follow (a pipe into an unknown program in `sh -c`,
    `$(( ))`, a heredoc with `cd`), and anything leaving the worktree. `omabox wait cmd -- ANYTHING`
    was refused even alone (19 of 19, half of all refusals); a probe subagent got `wait until --
    true`, `wait until -- sh -c '! pgrep -x X'`, `omabox path --home` and `help cmd` through. Now
    `until` is the condition's name (help, skill, reference, README); `cmd` is read the same, with
    "warning: wait cmd is now wait until ... (wait cmd will be refused in 1.0)" on stderr (Diogo's
    rule for renames: old form warned one release). `--json`'s `condition` is the name the caller
    wrote (`until`, or `cmd` as before), through a second probe name; until's lines say "command
    succeeded" / "command still failing". `path --home` prints `<dir>/home`, as `--run` prints
    `<dir>/run`: a literal path for the agent's Read/Write/Edit, instead of `$(omabox path)/home`
    in a command (`$(omabox path)` alone passed; what came with it did not). The reference's "For
    subagents in an isolated worktree" holds the five rules (until; several steps as a script in the
    box HOME run by path; box files through `path --home`; literal arguments; stay in the worktree,
    `scroll --source`, not `pointer -- source`), for the subagent brief to reuse; SKILL.md points to
    it. Not built (each 1-5 cases, each with a plain form already): `omabox cat` (`run -- cat` passes),
    `wait process`, `gdb --app`, `run --script`. Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2): t_wait
    (until: 0, 124, `--json`; cmd: same result, condition `cmd`, warned), t_inspect (`path --home`,
    a file the box wrote in /home/sbx read there); t_unit_wait (the warning, the same refusals for
    both names, `path` taking one of --home/--run/--logs).

382. **`log shell` lines carry their time** (2026-10-20, #276). Timing a shell plugin's retry backoff
    needed `omabox run -- quickshell log --log-times -p <the box's shell path>`, whose times come
    from the binary `.qslog` and are whole seconds there (`19:39:11.000`). Quickshell's own
    `--log-times` (in every release since 0.1.0) stamps each line it logs with `yyyy-MM-dd
    hh:mm:ss.zzz`, to the millisecond, before the level; it changes the log's lines and nothing
    else the shell does. The box's `systemd-cat` stand-in (which Omarchy's launcher runs the shell
    under) now passes it to quickshell, and shell.sh's fallback for a tree without the launcher too;
    the `logger -t omarchy-shell` stand-in stamps the launcher's lines the same way (`%F %T.%3N`,
    was whole seconds), and the crash-dialog line from hyprland.lua too. Times by default, not
    behind `--times` (pre-1.0; output wording is not the contract), read straight from shell.log,
    so `--grep` (which sees the time as part of the line) and `-f` are unchanged. Not timed: what
    Quickshell prints outside its logger (a crash handler's stderr before logging starts, Qt's own
    early stderr), and an `--omarchy` tree whose launcher runs quickshell without systemd-cat.
    Hyprland's log has no times and `omabox events` uses `HH:MM:SS.mmm`: there was no common format
    to match, so the shell keeps Quickshell's own. `shell_warnings` (plugin states at `up` and
    `restart-shell`) drops the time with the level/category prefix. The box's shell command line is
    now `quickshell --log-times -n -p ...`, which a host `pgrep -a` tells from the desktop's. Quirk:
    Quickshell writes no space between the time and a `quickshell.bare` message ("Could not open
    config file"). Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2, Quickshell 0.3.2): t_plugin_check
    (a Quickshell line timed to the ms in `log shell`, `--grep` keeping only matches, plugin states
    read from timed lines), t_dbus_user_app (the logger line timed), t_omarchy_tree, t_shell_crash,
    t_shell_restart_dup, t_omarchy_restart, t_quickshell; t_unit_shell_warnings (timed lines).
383. **Time in a recording: `record --for` and `record hold`** (2026-10-20, #259, #280; one design).
    The skill forbids `sleep`, so a recording of something that moves by itself took a dummy action
    (`record --hold 5s -- pointer -- move 5 5`: the pointer moved, the intent hidden), and a
    scripted take's pauses were `wait still --quiet 1500ms --timeout 4s || true`, which runs to its
    timeout under a clock or a spinner and returns at once on a still screen. Now `record hold
    DURATION` (between start and stop) returns once the video has DURATION from its call (from the
    first frame, if that came later), measured in the video's own clock: the recording's
    first-frame reader (finding 306) no longer hands the rest of wf-recorder's WAYLAND_DEBUG lines
    to `grep -v`, but to an awk that drops them the same way and writes each frame's `ready` stamp
    over `last-frame` beside `first-frame`; the hold sleeps on the host until 50 ms before its
    wall-clock end (in steps of 30 s, touching the box's use, so a long hold is not idle), then
    polls `last-frame` in the box every 10 ms until every wf-recorder of the recording (each output
    of `--monitor all`) has a frame stamped at or past the end, in its monotonic clock through the
    first frame's two readings. So a box slow to give frames never shortens a pause, and a `stop`
    right after a hold keeps its frames: with wf-recorder SIGSTOPped for 1.5 s, a 500ms hold
    returned after 1.47 s, and the video reached the hold's end. It prints the span ("held 0.550s
    to 2.550s"); 5 s past the end with no such frame it fails (exit 1, the recording goes on); with
    nothing recording, exit 2 naming `record start`. `record mark TEXT --hold D` is the mark, then
    the hold from the mark's time (--hold keeps its 60 s cap; `hold` and `--for` take up to 60m,
    durations as ms_duration reads them, a bare number seconds). `record --for DURATION` is start, a
    quiet hold from the first frame, stop (refused with an action, a sub-command or --hold, exit 2):
    `--for 3s` gave 3.033 s of video (the stop's one frame more), 1s of a two-monitor layout 1.03 s,
    so no trim was added. A jailed agent's omabox runs `--for` itself as start, `hold`, stop (the
    broker refuses `--for` from a jail, as it refuses an action); its one-shot now gives the polish
    options to stop, not start, which refused them. `record start/stop/status/sheet --hold`, ignored
    until now, is refused. Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2; holds on the AMD iGPU):
    t_record_hold (exit 2 with nothing recording; `--for 2s` 2.03 s; marks around a 2 s hold 2.08 s
    apart; `mark --hold` from the mark's time; the frozen recorder above), and t_scale,
    t_scale_nvidia (NVIDIA), t_record_layout, t_record_input, t_audio and t_jail_record unchanged by
    the new frame reader; t_unit_record (the refusals, the relay's `hold` and `--for`).
384. **`tree --layer SEL`: a layer surface's accessibility tree** (2026-10-20, #254; finding 358's
    plan). The machine's Quickshell is 0.3.2 now (with 916a0dd), so a plain box's shell publishes
    its layers: a python3 `gi.repository.Atspi` walk in a box showed what finding 358 saw on a build
    (an empty `gtk` application and the `Qt` one, both with the shell's pid; one nameless `frame` a
    layer at 0,0 with its size), and two facts more: the frames' AccessibleId is
    `QGuiApplication.ProxiedWindow`, the same for all (nothing names the layer), and Omarchy's open
    launcher (`omarchy-menu`, 1920x1080, the wallpaper's size) has `filler` rows (id `row`) under
    an `[active]` frame. A closed menu is unmapped on this Omarchy, its frame gone. Accessibility
    comes on as for windows: at-spi2-core 2.62.1 has only `IsEnabled` (finding 368), which `tree`
    sets; the shell, started before it, registers its frames within the 3 s `tree` waits.
    `tree --layer SEL` takes a namespace, `address:0x...` or `pid:PID` from `hyprctl -j layers`
    (`layer_select`: a 1x1 one, a closed menu kept mapped, only when nothing bigger matches, and then
    said, exit 1; none or several listed, exit 2; `--window` with it exit 2). `layer_read` runs
    `omabox-tree --pid PID --layer --size WxH --offset X,Y`: the tool takes, among the pid's
    applications with something under them (so never the empty `gtk` one, whatever the order), the
    frame of the layer's size; the bounds it prints are the surface's plus the layer's x, y, the
    screen's coordinates, since no call takes a layer's: a plain `click X Y` at a node's middle lands
    on it. Two frames of one pid and size (the launcher over the wallpaper) are told apart only by the
    keyboard: when exactly one of the tied layers holds it (`kb_layers`: mapped, exclusive), its frame
    is the one `[active]` frame (`--active yes`) and the others' are not (`--active no`), applied
    when exactly one tied frame is active; otherwise exit 6, said with the tied layers listed (exit
    1). A frame with nothing under it is exit 5: "the layer publishes no accessible items (nothing in
    it sets an Accessible role)", exit 1, which Omarchy's bar says today; no frame at all of the
    pid's on a Quickshell is "no accessibility tree" plus that Quickshell publishes from 0.3.2 on
    (and the box's version line). `tree` with no selector in a box with no window says the shell is
    layers (exit 2), and foot's "no accessibility tree" points there too. `layer_read` is the
    function a caller in bin/omabox uses for a layer's items' bounds (`--json`, depth > 0; #283).
    Seen in a box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2, Quickshell 0.3.2): a `qs -p` config with a named
    button in a `PanelWindow` at 342,200 gave `button "a named button" @492,240 120x50`, and a plain
    click at its middle renamed it; the launcher's frame and the wallpaper's (none) apart; two
    100x100 layers of one process refused. Not seen: a Quickshell before 0.3.2 (none here: its
    branch of t_tree_layer is untested), a scaled or second monitor. Tests: t_unit_tree_layer (the
    selection, the hint with the keyboard and box stubbed), t_tree_layer (all of the above, and
    the bar), t_tree unchanged.

385. **One duration grammar; short flags with one meaning** (2026-10-20, #273, part A of the CLI
    audit before 1.0). Five duration grammars became one, `ms_duration`: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` (new),
    decimals up to 6 places, a bare number seconds; `s_duration` gives it as seconds for `gpu`,
    `cpu`, `audio` and `cpu --settle`, which took plain numbers only (`gpu 5s` was refused;
    `--settle 0` stays none), and `$OMABOX_READY_TIMEOUT` reads it too (`ready_timeout`, checked
    before a box starts; `30s` was an arithmetic error). Diogo's rule for 1.0 (issue comment): the
    new form canonical, the old one kept with a one-line stderr warning that names what to write
    and says "(refused in 1.0)", for one release; a deprecated bare number is refused in 1.0, never
    read another way (no silent x60 or x1000). **The forms deprecated here, for 1.0 to refuse:**
    (1) `up --idle N` and `OMABOX_IDLE=N`, N a bare whole number other than 0: minutes (write
    `Nm`); `idle_duration`, warned by `up` and, since its box's `up` writes to a log, by `check run`;
    `run` passes `up`'s warnings on. A bare number with decimals never was an `--idle`: refused now.
    (2) `keys -s N` and `pointer -- sleep N`, N a bare whole number other than 0: milliseconds
    (write `Nms`); `pause_ms`, which hands the tools milliseconds as before and refuses (exit 2) a
    bare decimal, a negative or more than 10m before any box is asked (pointer's are read in a
    pass before `select_box` now). (3) `up -i`: write `--interactive` (`-i` is ignore-case in
    `log` and `events`). (4) `save -f`: write `--force` (`-f` is follow in `log` and `events`).
    (5) `shot` and `calibrate` given two files (positional and/or `-o`): the last was taken
    silently; now warned (`two_files`), in the jailed caller's `relay_shot` too. Additive, no
    warning: `--active` wherever `--window` goes (keys, click, scroll, pointer, drag, wait),
    `--output` beside `-o` on `check run/point/diff`, `events --grep -i RE` as `log` takes it (it
    was a regex `-i`), `check point --timeout` read when parsed (a typo was said only once the
    scenario got there). Help's comment above `usage_text` lists the internal options and
    variables (`up --owner`, `shot`/`record --to-fd --as ...`, `_reap`, OMABOX_CHECK_*...), which
    help never shows and no promise covers. Left, each for a decision (audit F-numbers): F7 `up
    --add-monitor` (Diogo's); F13 `keys --delay` (the keyboard tool's per-key delay, honoured
    only first: document it as omabox's, or refuse it as `-m/-p/-T` are); F14's gating of the
    internal options behind a marker (the broker's calls carry none today); F15 one range for
    `--fit`/`--every` (`record`'s sheet starts at 100 px for its labels, and capping its `--every`
    at 60s would refuse what works); F18 positional box names on `peek`, `reload`,
    `restart-shell` (documenting them widens the promise; warning them is the other way). Tests:
    t_unit_duration (the grammar, each warning's text, the refusals, `up`'s and `check run`'s
    warnings, `$OMABOX_READY_TIMEOUT`), t_unit_flag_forms (`up -i`, `save -f`, `--active` on each
    command, `--output`, `--grep -i`, two files, `check point --timeout`), t_unit_cli/t_unit_record
    (gpu, cpu, audio take units), t_keys (its pauses in the new form, `keys --active`).

386. **Usage errors exit 2 in every command, naming the nearest option and `omabox help CMD`**
    (2026-10-20, #273, part B of the CLI audit; audit X2, X5-X7, E1-E22). Most commands exited 1
    for an unknown option, a missing or bad value or a word too many, the same as a run that
    failed; `ls`, `saves`, `which` and an unknown command gave 2. Now one rule: `die` exits 2 while
    the command line is read (`PARSING`, set by `main`, ended by `parsed` or by `select_box`, which
    every box command calls once its words are read), 1 afterwards; `DIE_RC` still overrides it
    (`check`'s 2 throughout, `run`'s 125). A refusal then is said with " (omabox help CMD)"
    (`usage_die`), and `fail` is a failure met while still reading the words (ImageMagick missing,
    another `up --new`'s lock, a jail's or a policy's refusal: 1, never "called wrong"); `refused`
    exits as die would for a helper that said why and returned 1 (`|| exit 1` there lost a
    subshell's 2). `unknown_opt`, `unknown_word` and `unknown_command` name the nearest candidate
    (`did_you_mean`: the only one the word starts, else the only nearest within one typo, two past 4
    letters, three past 10, a swap counting one); `optarg` names the form help gives a value
    (`opt_form`: `-g needs a value: -g "X,Y WxH"`); `unexpected` says a word that is a box's name
    goes with `-b` (E4). Every command's options are in `CMD_OPTS`, which `t_unit_cli_contract`
    checks against the options its help lines show. `keys` refuses an unknown `--option`, which it
    passed to the keyboard tool (`--hold` there never returned). A given box name with characters a
    box name cannot have is warned in 0.9 and refused in 1.0 (E3; finding 176's note was `up`'s
    only); a derived one is still made to fit. The refusals that did not name the fix now do (E5-E15,
    E17, E18, E20; E16, E19 were fine, E21 was part A's, E22 is an internal option). One table of
    exit codes, `omabox help exit-codes` (also `omabox help help`) and the skill's reference "Exit
    codes"; the code meanings left as they were and put in it: a `--window SEL` matching none or
    several (2, X5), `which` for a pid gone (2, X6). Tests: t_unit_exit_codes (every command's
    unknown option, each family's usage errors, the nearest-option hints, run's 125, the E fixes,
    the table), t_unit_cli_contract.

387. **`--opt=value` wherever an option takes a value** (2026-10-20, #273, audit F9). One place,
    `eq_split` in `main`, before the jailed caller's relay or the broker sees the words: `--opt=V`
    becomes `--opt V` when `CMD_OPTS` says the command's `--opt` takes a value (`V=`, or `V?` for
    an optional one: `events --mark`, `record --cut-idle`); an option that takes none refuses a
    value (exit 2); an unknown `--x=y` is left for the parser, whose hint compares `--x`. Only words
    in an option's place: a value given as its own word stays as it is (`log --grep --x=y`, `keys -t
    --a=b`), so does everything after `--`, and for `run`, `hyprctl`, `lua` and `pointer` everything
    from the first word that is not an option of theirs (the command's, hyprctl's, the Lua source,
    the pointer's actions; `pointer`'s own `move X Y --steps=N` is split there). `--box=NAME` before
    the command too (`global_box`). Not done: short options with `=` (`-g=...`), which no tool
    takes either.

388. **`run` exits 125 for its own failures** (2026-10-20, #273, audit X3, X4). `run`'s 1 was both
    "the command exited 1" and "no box", "bad option", "the throwaway did not start": now everything
    omabox refuses or fails at under `run` exits 125 (`DIE_RC=125`, set in `main` for `run`, usage
    errors included), as `docker run` and `timeout` do; the command's status passes through as
    before, 126 and 127 being the box's exec's. A box that went down while the command ran
    (`run_gone`) is 125 too: the status is the box's end's, not the command's (t_own_processes saw
    137 or 143). From ai-jail, the relay's own failure (the broker out of reach, a call turned away)
    is 125 for `run`: `relay call` exits `$OMABOX_RELAY_FAIL` (an internal variable, 1 by default)
    for its own failures; an older relay ignores it. X4: the in-box steps' 125 (run-job's log,
    record's mkdir) never reach a caller as such: each ends in a `die`. `run -d`'s "could not start
    the command" says whether the box went down and which log to read (E9). Tests:
    t_unit_exit_codes (run's refusals), t_own_processes (125), t_jail (125 and a command's 3 through
    the broker, a usage error's 2).

389. **A jailed `shot --monitor NAME` took NAME for the output file** (2026-10-20, #284, found reading
    the code for the #273 audit). `relay_shot` knew which of `shot`'s options take a value but not
    `--monitor`: NAME became the output path, and the broker refused `--monitor` with `--to-fd`.
    Listed now; and `--after -- ACTION` keeps the action's words (they were taken for files too;
    the broker refuses `--burst` from a jail anyway, saying so). t_jail takes `shot --monitor NAME`
    and `--monitor=NAME --output=FILE` from a jail.

390. **`--json` on what lacked it, one coordinate rule announced, every option in help** (2026-10-20,
    #273, part C of the CLI audit; audit F8, F13, N1-N6, J1-J9). New `--json`, each additive: `check
    run` (`check_compare_json`: `check_compare`'s lines unsaid, each checkpoint a line of
    `CHK_JSONL` from `chk_point_json`, one object at the end; exit 3 and 4 give `result` failed /
    no_baseline; not with `--approve`, whose output is for looking at) and `check diff` (`CHK_JQ`:
    regions `{x, y, w, h, pixels}`, specks, a size change `{from, to}`; its text through an fd that
    is /dev/null with `--json`, never `> /dev/stdout`, which truncates a caller's file); `shot`
    (`shot_said`: path, kind, region in the coordinates `--in` takes, image, scale = image px per
    layout px, window, monitor, fit, zoom, and `--changed`'s result changed / nothing / whole; not
    with `--burst`); `record status`, `mode` (show only), `path --logs`, `calibrate --answer` (from
    `calib_fit`'s line: `one ERR WORST`, `fit S SX SY N SIZE ERR WORST`, `off S TOL L:ERR...`, `up S`),
    `which`, `--version` (CMD_OPTS has `[--version]` and `[which]` now), `events --mark`. Added
    fields: `ls` `scale`, `dir`, `allowed`; `ports` `addresses`; `saves` `size_kb`; `windows` `x, y,
    w, h` (top level, `cover[]`, `layers[]`), one line now. N1: `config --json` keys snake_case; the
    kebab-case copies stay for 0.9 (an older widget, a script), and the widget reads snake_case,
    copying a kebab key to its snake name when only that came (an older CLI). Deprecated here, for
    1.0 to drop or change: config's kebab keys, `ls`'s `allow`, `ports`' `address`, `keys --delay`
    (warned: the keyboard tool's own per-key delay, read only as its first word), and F8. **F8,
    decided: warn, not switch, in 0.9.** With `--window` every coordinate is the window's (click's X
    Y, `shot -g`/`--ignore`, `check point` since #281) except `wait still|change --window --ignore`
    and `--wait`'s `-g`/`--ignore` beside `--window` (keys, click, scroll, drag), which watch the
    screen in the layout's coordinates. Switching now would move a 0.8 script's region without a
    word (help said "--ignore with --window too"), and no form means "the window's" today, so
    `win_region_warn` says it at parse time (before any box), and 1.0 reads them in the window's
    own; a script that must keep the screen's watches with `-g` instead of `--window`. Help names
    every option a command takes (`-b NAME (or --box NAME)` in one paragraph for every box command,

392. **AccessKit needs accesskit_unix 0.22+ (eframe 0.37+) for a tree on at-spi2-core 2.61+**

    (`context.rs`, read in the cargo registry) subscribes to `receive_screen_reader_enabled_changed`
    only and starts its AT-SPI bus connection only on that property's value; 0.24.0 subscribes to

393. **A suite failure's message keeps its end, and failed runs' evidence outlives passing runs**
    (2026-10-20, #285). One full-suite failure (t_isolated's `up --net isolated --allow`) could not
    be explained: `no()` printed the first 300 characters of the output, which ended in `up`'s own
    "box ... up" line, so the reason after it was cut; and the run folder holding the whole message
    (`failures.txt`) was gone within the hour, since the suite kept the newest 5 runs whatever they
    held and agents' passing runs followed. 0 repeats in 91 tries since. Now `clip_out` prints an
    output past 300 characters as its first 100, `[... N characters ...]` and its last 200, and
    `prune_runs` keeps the newest 5 runs that passed and the newest 10 with a failure (a run folder
    with a test's `failures.txt`); a run still going is never removed, as before. Tests: t_unit_evidence (a short output whole, a long one's head, cut count and tail, through
    no(); 20 runs pruned to 5 passing, the failed ones and a live one, then only the newest 10
    failed).

394. **An `--allow` port is pasta's inside the box; `run -d` says a job that ended at once**
    (2026-10-20, #286). A test's `python3 -m http.server PORT` in an `up --net isolated --allow
    PORT` box never showed in `ports`: pasta's `-T PORT` listens on the box's loopback (`ss`:
    `*%lo:PORT`, no process), leading to the host's PORT, so the server died at once with "Address
    already in use", `run -d` had said "started", and `ports` skips sockets no box process holds.
    The same as finding 89's mirror for a connected box. Now: help `up` and the reference's Network
    say an --allow port is for reaching the host's, and taken in the box; `ports` lists each
    --allow port of an isolated box as `allowed` (process pasta, addresses 127.0.0.1 and ::1, from
    box.json, not read off the socket); and a plain `run -d` watches its job's first 0.3 s: the
    waiter's status file (share/run-job.sh, #215) appearing in the box's run dir (read on the host
    as `$D/run`, existence only; `job_ended` reads the status in the box) with nothing of the job's
    session left means it ended. Then it says "the command exited with status N at once in box B,
    and left nothing running (log: ...)", the log's last 5 lines, a host path the box lacks, and
    exits N (0 too; under -q a 0 is not said). A launcher that exits and leaves its child (its
    session) is "started", as is a job still running after 0.3 s. `--wait` skips this: it has its
    own answer (#215). *Decided*: 0.3 s, polled every 50 ms: a plain `run -d` of a long-lived job
    went from ~85 to ~385 ms here; one that fails is said in ~100 ms (Python's bind error included,
    unloaded). Under load a slow starter (Python ~70 ms alone) can still outlast it and be
    "started", as before. *Decided*: exit with the job's status, as run passes a command's, so a
    script sees a server that never ran. Seen in a box: Python on the --allow port (exit 1, its
    traceback's last lines), `sh -c 'exit 3'` (3), `true` (0, said), a missing command (127,
    setsid's line), `sleep 300` and `sh -c 'sleep 300 & exit 0'` (started); `ports` and `ports
    --json` with the allowed row. Tests: t_isolated (ports' allowed row; a box server on the port
    fails; run -d of a fast failure, of `true` with and without -q, of a launcher); t_replace's
    ended job now sleeps 1.5 s, past the 0.3 s (the check had dropped its record before --replace).
395. **`omabox brief`: what a subagent needs, without the skill** (2026-10-20, #271). 63 of 106
    skill loads in the 10-09..10-17 sessions were subagents', most sent to use a handful of commands
    in a box their parent had up, each loading the whole SKILL.md (~14 000 chars, ~3 500 tokens),
    again in every parallel one. `omabox brief [-b NAME]` prints what such a subagent needs, for the
    parent to paste into its prompt: a line naming the box, its main screen's size and scale (and
    how many more monitors), its windows one a line (a `--window` word, the title cut to 40 chars,
    size at x,y, on-screen/covered/off-screen and active; six at most, then "and N more"), then 11
    lines of rules with the box's name written in: `-b NAME` on every call and one literal command
    per call; the loop; sent is not landed, never resend; no sleep (`--wait`, `wait still/change/
    window/until`, never `wait cmd`, `record hold`); never the real desktop; the box HOME's host
    path for Read/Write/Edit; a script there for several shell steps; stay in the worktree (with
    `scroll --source wheel`); the box is the parent's (leave it up); `help CMD`, and load the skill
    when this is not enough. Those are #272's five worktree rules (reference.md) and the skill's
    "Driving an app" core. The window word is the class's last dot part when the selector's own
    reading of a word (class, its last part, part of a title) finds that window alone; else its
    address (two foots are both `0x…`). Size: ~1 750-1 900 chars (~450 tokens, 13-14 lines with one
    or two windows, 20 at most), an eighth of SKILL.md. *Decided*: with no box up it prints the same
    rules for a box the subagent starts itself (`up --new`, NAME as the placeholder, `down -b NAME`
    when done) and says so on stderr, exit 0, rather than refusing: a parent can hand it over
    before any box exists. *Decided*: no `--json` (the brief is prompt text; `ls --json` and
    `windows --json` carry its data). A jailed agent may run it (read-only, through the broker).
    SKILL.md names it in one line (13 997 B; cut to fit: "`click --in` it" after `--fit 1456`,
    which the sentence before says; "`omabox down` when done", which the loop says; the worktree
    line's "one literal `omabox -b NAME …` per call", the first of the rules its ref holds). Tests:
    t_unit_brief (no box: the rules, ≤ 20 lines, `-b NAME`, stderr note, `-b` before the command,
    `--json` and a word refused), t_brief (none yet; one foot by its app id, size and scale, HOME's
    host path; two of one class by address).
396. **An action's `--wait` says what changed on the desktop, and a 124 where the input went**
    (2026-10-20, #274, part A). `keys`, `click`, `scroll`, `drag` and `run -d` with `--wait` read the
    box's desktop twice: one `hyprctl --batch "j/clients; j/layers; j/activewindow; j/activeworkspace;
    j/monitors"` (with the events log's size, in one `on_box sh -c`) started in the background as
    omabox-still starts and taken before the input is sent, and one after the screen's answer.
    `DESK_FACTS_JQ` diffs them: windows opened (focused or not; on a workspace not shown, said) and
    closed by address, layers counted by namespace (drawn = over 1x1, `layer_at`'s rule: a menu
    kept mapped at 1x1 is closed; an address changes when a layer maps again), focus, titles, the
    workspace, a window moved to another workspace or turned fullscreen/floating. Geometry alone is
    no change (a tiled window resized because another opened would be noise in every line). The
    line keeps its start and adds the facts after `; `, by weight (opened, closed, layer opened,
    closed, focus, the focused window's title, workspace, moved, state, other titles), 3 at most and
    ~160 chars, titles cut to 40, the address only when two windows share class and title, then
    `+N more (omabox events --since OFFSET)`. On a 124, `DESK_TARGET_JQ` adds where the input went
    from the snapshot before it: keys, a layer holding the keyboard (`kb_layers`, finding 276) or the
    focused window; a point, an overlay or top layer drawn there (with the window under it), else the
    topmost window there (`WIN_JQ`'s stacking and `cover`) in its own coordinates, else a bottom or
    background layer; run -d, a window with the job's pid (box pid namespace = Hyprland's) or "no
    window from pid N yet"; then the facts or "no window, layer or focus changed", and stderr says
    "look before sending anything again" in place of "take a shot". `unknown` gets nothing (the box
    may be hung). `--json` adds `changes` (up to 50; null: a snapshot failed), `target` and
    `events_since`, only on an action's wait; `wait still|change` is untouched. Measured (box,
    NVIDIA headless, load ~1): `desk_snap` 11 ms, the diff 4 ms, its parsing ~4 ms, a point target 3
    ms, a keys target (with `kb_layers`) 12 ms; end to end `keys --wait` settled 338 -> 362 ms (+24),
    a 124 702 -> 739 ms (+37). Through the jail's broker the line and JSON pass as they are (the
    relay hands the caller's fds over; t_jail checks both). *Decided*: `--since` gets the offset
    itself, not a `wait` mark in `events.marks` (no host write per call, no clobbering between two
    calls, no user mark of that name overwritten). *Decided*: every kind has words (the design had
    other windows' titles and moves "counted only"): a fullscreen toggle was otherwise only "+1
    more"; others' titles come last. *Decided*: two kinds beyond the design's seven,
    `window_moved` and `window_state`. *Decided*: a layer at the point is the target although only
    its rectangle is known (Omarchy's full-screen notifications overlay would claim every click
    while a toast shows), so the window under it is named too. Known gap: a window or layer that
    opened and closed within the wait is not seen (an events tail would close it). Tests:
    t_unit_wait_facts (the diff on canned snapshots, the cap, cuts and addresses, targets for each
    kind, settle_end's line, stderr and JSON keys), t_wait_facts (run -d and a key opening windows,
    a click opening a layer, 124s naming the focused window and the layer under the click), t_jail.

397. **SKILL.md: the core every task needs, the rest one line away** (2026-10-20, #270). The skill
    was 29% of what omabox cost an agent session in the 10-09..10-17 data (106 loads at ~5.3k tokens

398. **A full-screen layer is possibly over a point, not certainly** (2026-10-20, #263). Since
    finding 379, a top/overlay layer whose rectangle covered a `--window` point was named over it
    and `--no-raise` refused; finding 396's 124 named such a layer as where a click went. Hyprland
    gives only rectangles (finding 379), and Omarchy's `omarchy-notifications` is a full-screen
    overlay that takes input on its toasts only, so while any toast showed, every point counted as
    covered: a plain click far from the toast warned that it went to the layer, `--no-raise`
    refused it, and a 124 said "on layer omarchy-notifications" for a click that reached the window.
    *Decided* (Diogo): say what is known. A layer whose rectangle covers its whole output
    (`LAYER_WHOLE_JQ`: the output named by `hyprctl layers`' key, its mode over its scale, turned by
    its transform, within 1 px) is uncertain coverage: `click`/`scroll`/`drag`/`pointer --window`
    say "a full-screen layer "NS" (…) is up over window …: input at X,Y may go to it if one of its
    items (a toast) is there; elsewhere it goes to the window (omabox wait layer NS --gone waits it
    out)" and `--no-raise` goes on; `windows` says it "is full-screen, possibly over" the windows;
    the 124 names the window (or bottom layer) under it as the target, adding "or possibly on
    layer NS (full-screen: if one of its items, a toast, is there)". A layer smaller than its output
    keeps the certain wording and the refusal, and where both are over a point the certain one wins
    (`win_layer` prints `certain|possible` first). `--json`: `windows`' `layers` and the `--wait`
    `target` gain `certain` (additive; a target's `namespace` stays its own, the possible layer is
    in the text only). An output not found in `monitors` (or without geometry) counts as smaller:
    certain, as before. #283 (the toasts' bounds from the layer's accessibility tree) would narrow
    "possibly" to yes or no where a layer publishes one. Real box (Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2,
    1920x1080): with a `notify-send` toast up, `--no-raise` at 20,20 clicked and said "may", the
    toast stayed; a 124 named foot and "possibly on layer omarchy-notifications"; a Quickshell
    `PanelWindow` stub (top, 300x150) under the same toast refused `--no-raise`; a plain click on the
    toast closed it. t_click_layer (that), t_unit_window_select and t_unit_wait_facts (scale 2, a
    turned output, a second output's origin, mixed layers).
    *Since*: with no window under the point, the 124 named the first of the bottom and background
    layers listed (the background) even where a bottom layer lay over it: the topmost now (#274).
    t_unit_wait_facts.
399. **A `run -d` job that ends in its first 30 s is said by the box's next command** (2026-10-20,
    #286). Finding 394's watch covers a `run -d` job's first 0.3 s; a server that died a second in
    (a port taken late, a file read after startup) was "started" and nothing said otherwise until a
    shot showed no window. *Decided* (Diogo): the 0.3 s stays, and the box's next command says the
    rest, once per job, as shell_note says a shell crash. `need_box` (what a command that addresses
    a box up goes through: keys, click, shot, windows, wait, tree...) and `run` call `job_note`: a
    glob of the box's run dir for the waiters' status files (`omabox.run-NS.exit`, share/run-job.sh,
    NS the job's start as in its log's name `run-NS.log`) against `$D/jobs-noted` (host-only, one
    name per line, made empty by `up`), read with builtins: ~0.03 ms with no status file, ~0.35 ms
    with 20 dealt with, no process. A new one whose time (the file's mtime) is within 30 s of its
    start and whose status is not 0 is said: `warning: run -d job CMD (pid N) exited with status 3
    after 1.0s, since the last command (omabox log -b NAME run)` (the log's path when a later job's
    log is the newest; the words from the job's record, cut to 60; "its words were not kept" when
    run -d's checks dropped it). Every new one is noted, said or not; not said: one `run -d`
    reported itself (job_ended notes it, the 0.3 s watch and --wait's alike, a 0 under -q included),
    one `--replace` stopped (noted before its SIGTERM), one that ran past 30 s, a launcher whose
    session still runs (job_live: "started" for run -d too), a file not yet written (left for the
    next command, up to 2 s), and a box an older omabox started (no jobs-noted: what is there is
    taken as dealt with). `down` removes the box with them. Said whatever `-q` (as shell_note is).
    Through the broker the command runs host-side, so a jailed caller gets the line on its stderr as
    it gets the shell's. *Decided*: status 0 is not said: a one-shot (`xdg-open` handing off to a
    running browser, `notify-send`, a script) ends with 0 and is no death; the 0.3 s watch says a 0
    only because "started" would be wrong there. *Decided*: CMD is the job's words, not argv[0]
    alone (`sh -c ...` says nothing). *Off*: `run -d --replace` of another program's arguments drops
    ended records (job_others → job_live), so such a job is said without its words. Tests:
    t_unit_job_note (said once, by status, signal, record gone, path vs `log run`, 0, past 30 s,
    noted, launcher, unwritten file, a link at the name, an older box); t_replace (`sh -c 'sleep 1;
    exit 3'`: the next `windows` says it, the one after does not; a job --replace stopped is not
    said; the ended-job check drains its line).
400. **`up --clean`'s frozen clock was lost in one start in six under load** (2026-10-20, #222's
    load flakes; the cause is Omarchy's shell). The full suite's t_check read `check: 2 of 6 same, 2
    changed (1 as another)`: the bar's checkpoint `desk` changed at 913,8 93x11 and `screen` with it,
    seconds later. Not a shot taken too early: the bar showed "Tuesday 11:15", the real time in
    Omarchy's default format, for the whole run, while the box's shell.json still had the literal
    `'Friday 12:00'`. Reproduced: 12 CPU busy loops and three `check run --approve --runs 6` of a
    scenario shooting the bar twice 3 s apart, 3 of 18 boxes showed the real time in both shots
    (finding 361's "the bar's checkpoint changed by one region on the check right after --approve, in
    1 of 3 runs" was this). **Why**: shell.qml loads Omarchy's defaults
    (`$OMARCHY_PATH/config/omarchy/shell.json`) and the user's file through two FileViews, each
    applying the config as it arrives. When the defaults come first the bar is built from them (the
    clock with `dddd HH:mm`); the user's file then differs only in the clock's inline settings, so
    Bar.qml takes `applySettingsDelta`, which patches the layout array in place and sets `settings` on
    the widget only if it exists. A slot's `moduleSettings` is bound to its Repeater `entry`, which the
    in-place patch does not change, and a widget being created gets it from `injectProps` (by
    `Qt.callLater` on `activeItemChanged`): a delta that lands before the widget exists, or between
    its creation and that call, is overwritten with the defaults' format, until the shell restarts.
    Under load the bar takes longer to build and the window is hit. **Fix**: in a clean box (unless
    `--keep clock`) the box's shell.json, as seeded (after `--seed`s), is copied to the box dir as
    `shell-defaults.json` and bound read-only over the defaults' path in the box (after `--overlay`s,
    which would hide it), so both FileViews read the same config and either order builds the same bar.
    Only Omarchy's `omarchy-shell-config` reads that file otherwise, when the user's shell.json is
    missing: in a clean box it then gives the clean box's bar. Other boxes keep Omarchy's defaults (a
    box made from a desk whose bar has the defaults' widgets but other inline settings could lose them
    the same way; not seen). **Checked** under the same load: 24 runs of the scenario, all 24 bar
    shots identical with "Friday 12:00"; three t_check in parallel, 147/0 each. Tests: t_clean (the
    shell's defaults in a clean box are its shell.json; with `--keep clock` Omarchy's own).

401. **The kernel SIGKILLed a box's shell now and then under load: PipeWire had set its
    RLIMIT_RTTIME to 0** (2026-10-20, #222's load flakes). Three full suites in four failed one `up`
    each (t_theme, t_widget, t_throwaway): `the shell exited after starting`, its launcher's
    `Omarchy shell exited with status 137; relaunching` 0.85-1.5 s after the shell started, 0.2-0.5
    s after its line `Failed to connect pipewire context`; no OOM, no second shell.sh (one exec in
    hyprland.log, shell.log not started afresh). **No process sent it**: with a kill tracer
    (LD_PRELOAD) in every box and on the suite's host side, 15 runs of the tests that ran beside the
    failures (and ~900 more starts under load) caught one: a t_check box's shell SIGKILLed 0.2 s
    after PipeWire set the limit below, no kill call to it in the box or on the host. **Why**: a box
    has no system bus, so the Realtime portal on its bus reaches no RealtimeKit and answers
    `RTTimeUSecMax` 0; PipeWire's module-rt, loaded in every client context (the shell's PipeWire
    service, the Hyprland portal), takes that as the limit and sets the process's `RLIMIT_RTTIME` to
    0/0 (traced with a backtrace; children such as the clipboard's wl-paste inherit it). On a desk
    it is RealtimeKit's 200000. A process with that limit is SIGKILLed by the kernel's RT watchdog
    the first tick one of its threads runs at a realtime priority, and an unprivileged thread gets
    one without asking: this kernel has PREEMPT_RCU with RCU_BOOST (500 ms), so a thread preempted
    inside an RCU read-side section for that long is boosted to SCHED_FIFO 1 (rcub/0 woke ~2.6 times
    a second under the suite's load). Reproduced outside any box: 12 processes with RTTIME 0/0
    reading /proc/self/maps beside 250 busy loops on one CPU, 3 SIGKILLed in 45 s; the same 12 with
    the limit left alone, none. **Fix**: share/session.sh writes
    `~/.config/pipewire/client.conf.d/90-omabox.conf` (share/pipewire-client.conf, `module.rt =
    false`) in every box's HOME at each start: module-rt cannot give a box realtime anyway (no
    RealtimeKit, no RLIMIT_RTPRIO), and without it the limit stays unlimited. (`module.rt.args` with
    the portal and RealtimeKit off did not take in a client.conf.d drop-in.) `up --audio`'s daemons
    were unlimited already (their configs turn the portal off). A JACK client (jack.conf, whose
    module-rt has no `module.rt` condition) would still get 0/0. Tests: t_omarchy_restart (the
    shell's RLIMIT_RTTIME holds unlimited once its PipeWire service has tried to connect; it read
    0/0 before).
402. **1.0: the 0.9 deprecations refused, F8 switched, one deprecation helper, the promise written**
    (2026-10-20, #287; Diogo's decision on the issue). Each form 0.9.0 warned (findings 381, 385,
    386, 390) is refused, exit 2 (`run`'s 125) with one line naming what to write, never read
    another way: `wait cmd` (refused as the word is read, so `wait cmd -- X` says it rather than
    "-- goes with until"), a bare `up --idle N` / `OMABOX_IDLE=N` (`idle_duration` says it and
    returns 2, which `up` and `check run` exit with: it runs in `$(...)`), a bare `keys -s N` /
    `pointer sleep N` (`pause_ms`), `up -i`, `save -f`, `keys --delay` (out of `CMD_OPTS`), two
    files to `shot`/`calibrate` (`two_files`, the jailed caller's `relay_shot` too), a given box
    name with other characters or past 40 (`select_box`, naming the one that fits). `cmd_probe`
    and the minutes and milliseconds readings are gone. The JSON copies go: `config --json`'s
    kebab keys, `ls --json`'s `allow`, `ports --json`'s `address`. The widget still copies a kebab
    key it gets from a CLI older than 0.9 (one install updates both; left as it was). **F8**: beside
    `--window`, `wait still|change --ignore` and `--wait`'s `-g`/`--ignore` (keys, click, scroll,
    drag) are the window's own coordinates: `settle_in_window X Y` moves the caller's `--region` and
    `--mask` (the cursor's and a drag's path are `--ignore`, the screen's, added apart), with X Y
    the point `win_point` gave less the one asked (the window where it is once raised), keys' from
    the window read again after focusing it, a drag's from its first point; `wait` moves its masks
    by the window's `at`. A 124's suggested `--ignore` is in the window's coordinates then
    (`SETTLE_ORIGIN`), beside the screen's place, so pasting it back means what it says; an
    `--ignore` outside the window is said in its own. `win_region_warn` is gone. **`deprecated OLD
    NEW`**: the one way a deprecation is said from 1.0, `omabox: deprecated: OLD: write NEW (refused
    in X.Y)`, X.Y the next minor from VERSION; `OMABOX_STRICT=1` makes it `usage_die` (2, run's
    125). Called where the words are read, never in `$(...)`. No caller in 1.0: t_unit_deprecated
    calls it and fails if another warning names a form on its way out. README "Stability": the two
    tiers, what is not covered, saves and baselines, who it is for; no versioning-scheme claim (the
    unit check greps for one). Tests: t_unit_duration, t_unit_flag_forms, t_unit_exit_codes,
    t_unit_refusals, t_unit_wait, t_unit_json (F8, `settle_in_window`), t_unit_config,
    t_unit_aquamarine/t_unit_aq_worktree/t_unit_gpu (snake_case keys), t_unit_deprecated; box:
    t_monitors_wait(_nvidia) (the window's `--ignore` and `-g`, the 124's suggestion), t_wait,
    t_ports, t_json, t_pointer (`sleep 3s`).

403. **Omarchy 4.5's omarchy-shell reaches the desktop's shell past the guard** (2026-10-20, #290,
    read from v4.5.0-rc1 and reproduced with its script). 4.0.6's took the newest `wayland-N` in
    `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` only when `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` was empty, then went through `qs ipc`, which
    the guard's qs refuses (#141). 4.5's also does it when the display names no socket, which the
    guard's `omabox-guard` never does, and then answers over the shell's own socket
    (`omarchy-shell-<md5 of config and display>.sock`) with socat, never calling qs: menus, panels,
    the bar. `omarchy shell ...` runs it by its path, so a PATH shim alone misses that caller, and
    Codex gets no PATH of ours at all. **Fix**: an empty file `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omabox-guard`
    (GUARD_MARK), made by both agents' SessionStart hooks, by `guard exec`, and by any omabox
    command run under the guard (a session whose hook predates this): the display then names
    something that exists, so omarchy-shell keeps it, finds no shell socket for it and goes to qs as
    4.0.6 did; a Wayland client connecting there gets "connection refused" instead of "no such
    file", the same failure. Plus `share/guard/omarchy-shell`, first on the guarded PATH: it refuses
    (exit 4; 0 under `-q`, which promises success) while the display is not a socket, and passes a
    real one on. The hooks changed, so their stamps did (finding 346): guarded sessions say their
    hook is outdated until `omabox guard on`. Tests: t_unit_guard_omarchy_shell (with
    OMABOX_TEST_OMARCHY on a 4.5 tree, a control shows its omarchy-shell reaching a stand-in shell
    socket without the file; under `guard exec` nothing reaches it, by path or by name).

404. **`run -d --wait` said satisfied for a job that had died at once, when something else on screen
    settled** (2026-10-20, #297). Seen twice: a Qt app started right after `omabox run -- pkill` of
    the last one (the closing window was the awaited change) and a binary given a host path the box
    lacks, in a box another agent was using (its window). The job's end (SIGABRT at 0.0 s, exit 255
    at 0.1 s) only came on the next command, as finding 399's warning. `--wait` watches the whole
    screen, and `job_ended` (#215) was asked only on a 124. Reproduced: a foot window open, `run -d
    --wait -- sh -c 'pkill -f "^foot -T K "; exit 3'` said `satisfied: settled after 0.81s ...;
    window closed: foot "K"`, exit 0. *Decided*: the liveness check, not counting only the job's own
    windows: a job that never opens one (a server, a one-shot) would have nothing to settle on, and
    the job's state is what the agent needs. **Fix**: when the screen settles under `run -d --wait`,
    `job_failed` reads the job's status file ($D/run, one stat while it runs); a job killed or ended
    with a status other than 0, nothing of its session left, turns the answer to `unsatisfied: settled
    after 0.48s (...); the command had ended by then: not its screen; ...` and run -d says its end,
    the host paths it lacked and its log's tail, and exits with its status, as for a 124. A 0 stays
    satisfied: a one-shot (`notify-send`, a dispatch, a `pkill` of a window) changes the screen and
    ends with 0. **Checked** in a box: the reproduction above now exits 3 with the job's end and log;
    `kill -ABRT $$` 134; `--json` gives `result: unsatisfied`. Tests: t_replace (a job dead as
    another window closed: 3, unsatisfied, its end and log, not said again by the next command; a
    one-shot that closes it and exits 0: satisfied).

405. **A `run -d` job's warning said "its words were not kept" for ordinary jobs** (2026-10-20,
    #298). Finding 399's warning names the job from its record (`$D/jobs/PID`), and the record went
    missing in four ways. (1) `job_record` wrote none for a job gone before it looked: the SIGABRT at
    0.0 s and the exit 255 at 0.1 s of #297. (2) It looked for the job as a session (`sid == pid`),
    but run-job.sh says the pid right after its fork, before the subshell has exec'd setsid: a host
    quicker than the box found no such session yet and wrote nothing, for a job that then ran for
    minutes (by reading; 50 starts in an idle and a loaded box all kept theirs). (3) `job_live`
    removed the record of any job it found ended, before the next command's `job_note` had said the
    end: `--replace` (its own records and, through job_others, every ended job of the same program:
    399's *Off*), `job_ended`, and a concurrent command's. (4) `job_note` read all records in one
    `jq` under pipefail: one being written or removed by another command meanwhile (jq exits 2 or 5)
    lost every record's words, and the log was matched by its full path, so a caller whose
    `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is spelled otherwise (`/run/user/1000/`) matched none. **Fix**: a record is
    always written, its start time that of the process with the job's pid, whatever its session
    (one process from fork to the app: exec keeps it; `-` when none is left); `job_procs` counts
    that process as the job before its setsid. `job_live` drops an ended job's record only once its
    end is in `jobs-noted` (`job_said`; a box from an older omabox: as before), so it stays until
    `job_note` or `job_ended` has dealt with it; those then drop it. `job_note` reads each record as
    a line of its own (`jq -R 'fromjson?'`, its exit status ignored) and matches the log by its name
    `run-NS.log`. A record whose end never comes (its waiter killed in the box) stays until `down`.
    Tests: t_unit_job_note (a record matched by its name beside a half-written one; job_live keeps an
    ended job's record until its end is noted, then drops it; job_record records a job gone already,
    and one before its setsid by its start); t_unit_cli (job_procs: the leader before its setsid).

406. **The job-ended warning fired for jobs the agent had stopped itself with `omabox run -- pkill`**
    (2026-10-20, #300). One agent's loop of start, probe, stop got finding 399's warning a dozen
    times, often on an unrelated command; it added `grep -v warning` everywhere, and the log path in
    the line then broke a `grep -o '/run/[^)]*log'` capture of its own. A SIGTERM sent through
    `omabox run` in the same box is no news. **Fix**: `omabox run` in a box up marks its time in
    `$D/runs` (host-only; `o.PID.START` while it runs, PID the omabox's, renamed `c.START.END` when it
    returns, ms), and `job_note` does not say a job that ended by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGKILL (143, 130,
    137) while one ran or up to 2 s after one ended (an app slow to quit on SIGTERM under load; the
    issue asked about a second); it is noted all the same. Exits and crashes (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT) are
    said as before, and so is a kill with no `run` around it. An `o.` mark counts only while its
    omabox lives (one killed outright leaves its mark: ignored, then dropped). Marks are names read
    with builtins; each `run`'s end drops those that ended 10 s before it began (its own `job_note`
    had every end they could cover by then). *Off*: a job killed by something else in the box during
    an agent's `omabox run` (another agent's `pkill`, the OOM killer) is not said either; `run -d --
    pkill` is not a stop through `run`. Tests: t_unit_job_note (killed during a run or 2 s after: not
    said; an exit then and a kill 3 s after: said; during a run still going: not said; a run whose
    omabox is gone: said; run marks open, then closed, old and dead ones dropped); t_replace (`run --
    pkill -xf 'sleep 611'`: the next command says nothing; a job killing itself 3 s in: said).

407. **A box's Xwayland kept no 1-byte core limit: its `-core` raised it** (2026-10-20, #294). A box
    going down (its Hyprland killed after a hang) showed on the desktop as "Process crashed:
    Xwayland": the journal's entry had `COREDUMP_RLIMIT=18446744073709551615`, SIGABRT, the command
    line `Xwayland :0 -rootless -core -listenfd …`. Everything in a box runs under `prlimit
    --core=1:` (finding 67), which lowers only the soft limit; Hyprland starts Xwayland as `/bin/sh -c
    "exec Xwayland {} -rootless -core …"` (its format string, read from the binary: by name, through
    Hyprland's PATH), and xserver's `-core` sets the soft limit to the hard one (os/utils.c). When the
    compositor goes, Xwayland's fatal error ("Couldn't add screen") aborts, and with no limit left
    systemd-coredump records it. **Fix**: `share/bin/Xwayland`, first on every box PATH (session.sh,
    and hyprland.lua puts the stand-ins first again after Omarchy's envs), execs the next Xwayland on
    PATH under `prlimit --core=1:1`: the hard limit 1 byte too, so `-core` raises the soft one to 1.
    A soft limit other than 1 byte is not omabox's (a Hyprland given `ulimit -c unlimited` on
    purpose, the core a #135 debugging session wants): passed on as it is. Lowering the hard limit
    for the whole box would have done it too, but takes away `ulimit -c unlimited` inside (the
    skill's way to get a core). Checked in a real box (`up --xwayland`): Xwayland's
    `/proc/PID/limits` 1 1 (Hyprland's 1 unlimited); its Hyprland SIGKILLed from inside, Xwayland
    aborted and the kernel logged `106(Xwayland): RLIMIT_CORE is set to 1, aborting core`, no new
    entry in `coredumpctl list`. Tests: t_unit_xwayland (a fake Xwayland next on PATH gets 1/1, and
    unlimited/unlimited passed on), t_keys (the running Xwayland's limits).

408. **The shell-crash warning was any Quickshell's, and missed a killed shell** (2026-10-20, #303).
    An agent crashing its own Quickshell instance in a box (its own config) to test Quickshell's crash
    handling got `warning: the shell crashed since the last command and was started again` after each
    crash, the box's shell alive throughout, and omabox closed that instance's crash dialog
    (`closed the shell's crash dialog`): it interfered with the very thing under test. Then its
    `pkill -9 -f /usr/bin/quickshell` killed the box's shell too, Omarchy's launcher started it again
    (a new pid), and nothing was said. **Why**: shell_crashes, shell_crash_report and output's cycles
    counted every folder under the box HOME's `~/.cache/quickshell/crashes`, where every Quickshell
    writes its reports, and hyprland.lua closed any reporter's window (told by
    `__QUICKSHELL_CRASH_DUMP_PID` in its environment). A SIGKILL leaves no report (no handler runs).
    A report's `Crashed process ID` cannot key it to the shell: it is the child Quickshell's handler
    forks to dump (`raise(sig)` there), the shell itself being exec'd again at its own pid. **Fix**:
    a report is the shell's when its `Config Path` is the Omarchy tree's `shell/shell.qml` (slashes
    squeezed; `meta omarchy` is a resolved path); a folder whose report is not written yet counts
    once it is. The dialog: hyprland.lua passes the reporter's pid and its dump pid to
    `share/crash-dialog.sh`, which finds the report naming that dump pid (written before the dialog
    shows; up to 1 s for it) and closes the dialog only when the report is the shell's; with no
    report, only when the reporter's parent is the box shell's pid. A shell killed or exiting non-zero
    is said from the launcher's own line (`Omarchy shell exited with status N; relaunching.`, the
    box's logger puts it in shell.log): shell_note keeps "MARK COUNT STATUS" (shell.sh's
    omabox-shell.mark, how many such lines, the last status) in `shell-relaunches-seen` beside
    `shell-crashes-seen` (`up`, `restart-shell` and output's cycles write both: shell_seen), and says
    `warning: the shell was killed by SIGKILL (137) since the last command and was started again`
    once; a crash said with its relaunch is said as the crash. A shell stopped on purpose (`omarchy
    restart shell`) quits cleanly and logs no such line, so it is not said; a pid change alone would
    have said it. t_unit_omarchy_contract checks the launcher still logs that line. Checked in a real
    box: a `quickshell -p /tmp/qt` of the test's own SIGSEGVed, its report and dialog left, no
    warning, `ls` running with no crash counted; the shell SIGKILLed, the next command's warning,
    once. Tests: t_unit_shell_reports, t_unit_shell_crash (reports carry their config now: one not
    written yet and another instance's are no crash), t_shell_other_crash; t_shell_crash unchanged.

409. **`run` said a command killed by a signal in bash's words** (2026-10-20, #303). `omabox run --
    CMD` whose command was SIGKILLed printed `…/bin/omabox: line 1867: 662938 Killed  prlimit
    --core=1: "$@"`: bash's job-control line for its child, which ns_held holds with nsenter's stderr
    and ns_said passed on as one of nsenter's own lines (finding 235). For run's own command
    (`NS_KILL_SAY`) that line is now said as run says a job's end: `omabox: the command was killed by
    SIGKILL (137)` (job_how), the exit status unchanged; omabox's own calls into the box keep the
    line. Checked in a real box (`run -- sh -c 'kill -KILL $$'`: exit 137, that one line). Tests:
    t_unit_box_gone (SIGKILL and SIGTERM, nsenter's own line kept), t_shell_other_crash.

410. **`tree --window` printed an app's only frame for a window it does not publish** (2026-10-20,
    #302). An egui app with a root window and two child viewports publishes one AT-SPI frame, the
    root's; `tree --window "title:<child>"` printed the root's tree for both children (one of them
    920x1056, the root 920x521), since a window whose title no frame names fell back to the app's only
    frame. **Fix**: tools/tree takes that frame only when it is the window's size (2 px either way)
    and no other window of the app's pid is that size (`omabox tree` passes the count, `--twins`):
