    else `no accessibility tree for this window: its application publishes one window, "Root" 920x521,
    and this one is 920x1056` (exit 7), or `... and 2 of its windows are this one's size ...: which
    one it is cannot be told` (exit 6); `tree` says either, exit 1. A window whose title the frame
    names is unchanged. Reproduced without egui: a GTK4 window beside bare GDK toplevels
    (`Gdk.Surface.new_toplevel`, drawn by a `Gsk.CairoRenderer`), which have no accessible. Tests:
    t_tree (a window of another size; one of two of the frame's size; the root's tree still read).

411. **`run -d` from a repo told an agent to start a second box while its session's was up**
    (2026-10-20, #296). An agent's `cd <scratch>; omabox up` made `default-<sfx>`; back in the repo
    (Claude Code resets the directory between calls), `run -d` derived `<repo>-<sfx>`, found it down
    and said `run -d needs a box that is up (omabox up <repo>-<sfx>)`, while every other command
    there says need_box's `no box '<repo>-<sfx>' is up; this session's box is 'default-<sfx>'
    (started from another directory): -b default-<sfx>`; the agent's report had both lines, which
    disagree. **Fix**: run -d with a derived name, when the session has boxes up under other names,
    gives need_box's answer alone; with none, the `up` line as before. Using the session's only box
    from any directory waits for an owner per box (#295): with parallel subagents it may be a
    sibling's. Tests: t_unit_agent_session.

412. **`up --desk-shell` loaded omabox's own bar widget, which cannot work in a box** (2026-10-20,
    #304). `chaves.omabox` polls `omabox ls --json`; a box has no omabox on its PATH, so its shell
    logged `WARN: Process failed to start ... Command: QList("omabox", "ls", "--json")` (and after
    three failures the widget would notify inside the box): a line in every count of an agent
    comparing two builds of a plugin by their warnings. **Fix**: desk_plugins leaves the desk's
    `chaves.omabox` out, said as the other plugins it skips are (`--desk-shell: not mounting
    plugins/chaves.omabox: omabox's own widget, which lists your boxes (none in a box)`), and the box's
    shell.json loses it wherever it is placed (the bar, a plugin's own list, its settings entry), so no
    layout names a widget the box has not. A `--plugin` of it still mounts it (its own tests). Checked
    on this desk: the box's shell log has no omabox line. Tests: t_unit_desk_shell, t_desk_shell.

413. **`up`'s line named only the main screen** (2026-10-20, #308). `up NAME --monitor 1080x1920`
    said `box 'NAME' up (1920x1080@60)`, though the second monitor was there (a window sat on it), and
    an agent ran `monitor list` to be sure. **Fix**: every other enabled monitor follows the main
    one, as Hyprland has it once `up`'s `monitor add`s are done: `up (1920x1080@60 + 1280x720@60,scale=1.6
    + 1080x1920@60)`. `up --json` and `ls --json` had every one already (`monitors`), unchanged.
    Tests: t_monitors_wait, t_monitors_wait_nvidia.

414. **`wait` garbled the still tool's answer when a read timed out at a space** (2026-10-20, #310;
    seen under load in t_wait: `unsatisfied: changingt=2002`). Finding 217 keeps what a timed-out
    `read -t 1` had of a line, but with the default IFS that read strips trailing whitespace from
    the part it keeps, and the next one strips the rest's leading whitespace: an answer split at a
    space lost it, so the reason ran into the fields after it. **Fix**: `IFS= read` in settle_begin
    and settle_end. Tests: t_unit_settle_read (an answer and a `ready` line split at a space).

415. **On Omarchy 4.5 the first shot after `up` could be a black screen** (2026-10-21, #291; verified
    in a box on 4.5.0rc1). A shell that finds no mark of its session in
    `~/.local/state/omarchy/background-intro.session-id` (`OMARCHY_SESSION_ID`, else
    `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`) takes its start for a new login and puts a black cover over every
    screen, the bar too (`shell/services/BackgroundIntro.qml`: a layer `omarchy-background` on the
    Overlay level), until `omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro` returns and the wallpaper is in. A box HOME
    never has the mark, so every `up` was a login. On a theme whose wallpaper has an intro (catppuccin)
    the script waits 5 s for an OWE daemon a box does not run: `up --theme catppuccin` came back with
    the cover still up (layers: overlay `omarchy-background`; the shot all black, the pointer alone),
    and `bar_settle` had settled on the black under it. **Fix**: `share/shell.sh` writes the session's
    id to that file before it starts the shell, as a shell restart finds it: no cover, no intro (none
    can play in a box anyway). `wait_ready` also waits, after the bar, until no Overlay
    `omarchy-background` layer is up (12 s at most, then says so), for an Omarchy that tells a login
    another way. Checked: `up --theme catppuccin`, a shot right after: the wallpaper and bar, no
    overlay cover. The contract checks the mark's file and ids and the cover's layer. Tests: t_theme,
    t_unit_omarchy45 (`intro_cover`), t_unit_omarchy_contract.

416. **On Omarchy 4.5 a box's screen came up on workspace 11** (2026-10-21, #292; verified in a box).
    4.5 gives each monitor a block of ten workspaces (`default/hypr/monitor-workspaces.lua`), keyed by
    its identity (make, model and serial; a box's outputs have none, so their name) and kept in
    `~/.local/state/omarchy/monitor-workspaces`. Hyprland's `FALLBACK`, its only output before the
    box's `HEADLESS-2` is made, was there at `hyprland.start` and took block 0 (`0<TAB><TAB>FALLBACK`),
    so the box's screen got 11-20, and `hyprctl dispatch workspace 2` went to a block no screen of the
    box owned. An interactive box closed with confirm-close on and opened again (a new output,
    WAYLAND-2) got a block of its own: its workspaces 1 and 2 were renumbered 22 and 23, and the
    reopened window showed an empty one (t_guard: `want [2] got [22]`). NVIDIA boxes were not hit
    (their WAYLAND-1 is there before Hyprland starts: `0 WAYLAND-1 WAYLAND-1`, workspace 1). Filed as upstream#171 (FALLBACK should own no block). **Fix**:
    `share/session.sh` writes the file at every start: the main screen (HEADLESS-2, or WAYLAND-1 for an
    interactive or NVIDIA box) and FALLBACK both on block 0, so FALLBACK, which only stands in for the
    screen while it is away, holds its workspaces under their numbers (`output drop`: 1 and 2 stay 1
    and 2 on FALLBACK, back on the screen after `output back`). confirm-close opens the new window
    under the closed one's name (`hyprctl output create wayland NAME`; hyprctl exits 0 with "Name
    already taken", so its answer is read), so it keeps that window's block. `monitor add`'s monitors
    get the next blocks as they come (HEADLESS-3 on 11-20), as a second monitor on a 4.5 desk. A save's
    file (`up --from`) is replaced: its box's. Seen, not changed: after `output back` the screen shows
    an empty workspace 3, Hyprland's next free number, with 1 and 2 back on it (Omarchy leaves a new
    monitor's own workspace in view). Host placement (workspace 9, `special`) is unchanged: an
    Open item. Tests: t_output (the main screen on 1, a monitor on 11), t_guard
    (confirm-close keeps 1 and 2), t_unit_omarchy_contract (the file's format).

417. **On Omarchy 4.5 `omarchy-theme-set` in a box reloaded Hyprland ~1 s after it returned**
    (2026-10-21, #293; verified in a box). Switching to a theme whose wallpaper has an intro, with
    animations on, 4.5's `omarchy-theme-set` takes its intro path: it returns at once and, in the
    background, asks OWE to play the intro, then reloads Hyprland. A box runs no OWE daemon (the
    per-user `owed` unit), so the intro fails and the reload comes ~1 s later: `run --
    omarchy-theme-set everforest` returned after 247 ms, `wait still` was satisfied at 1.1 s, the
    `configreloaded` event came at 1.2 s, so a shot after `wait still` could have the old theme's
    borders. **Fix**: `share/bin/omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro`, first on the box's PATH, answers
    `--resolve-only`, `--resolve-startup` and `--prepare-theme` with no intro while there is no
    `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/owe/owed.sock`, and is Omarchy's script for everything else (and for all of it
    once a daemon runs): `omarchy-theme-set` takes its plain path, which reloads Hyprland before it
    returns (configreloaded 7 ms before the return). The theme's other app configs (GTK, browsers) are
    still applied after it returns unless `OMARCHY_THEME_WAIT=1`, as on a desk. The contract checks
    that theme-set and the shell call the script by name. Tests: t_theme, t_unit_omarchy45.

418. **On Omarchy 4.5 a desk's `bar.centerAnchor` and a widget's `center` no longer place what they
    did** (2026-10-21, #293; the contract failed on the installed 4.5.0rc1). 4.5 splits the bar's
    centre into `centerBegin`, `center` (a box centred on the bar) and `centerEnd`, adds a `tray`
    section, and drops `centerAnchor` (migration `1791969355` moves what flanked the anchor to the
    sections either side). A box runs no migrations: a desk's shell.json from an older Omarchy, in a
    box on a 4.5 tree (`up --omarchy`), kept its anchor, and its centre came out as one group. And
    `place_plugin` put a mounted widget naming `center`, or no section, into `center`, beside the
    clock in its box, pushing the clock off the middle, where 4.5's registry puts it in `centerEnd`.
    **Fix**: when the box's Omarchy has the split (`center_split`: its Bar.qml reads `centerBegin`),
    the box's shell.json (desk, `--desk-shell` and the stock one alike) gets the migration's jq first
    (`CENTER_SPLIT_JQ`, only for Omarchy's own bar), and `widget_section` sends `center`, none or no
    section to `centerEnd`. On an older Omarchy, both as before. The contract drops `centerAnchor` and
    checks `centerBegin`, `centerEnd`, the sections list with `tray`, the registry's `centerEnd`, and
    the migration. Checked in a box on 4.5: a desk stand-in with `centerAnchor: omarchy.clock` and
    indicators, clock, weather in `center` came up with the clock alone in the middle, the others in
    `centerBegin` and `centerEnd`; a mounted widget naming no section was placed in `centerEnd`, the
    clock still centred. Seen too: a 4.5 shell writes a widget's settings into the HOME's shell.json
    once it runs (omarchy.elsewhen's `cities`), so a clean box's file and its shell's defaults (finding
    400, a copy made by `up`) no longer stay byte-equal; t_clean compares the defaults with that copy.
    Tests: t_unit_bar_filter, t_unit_omarchy_contract, t_clean.

419. **On Omarchy 4.5 a save's toasts came back over `up --clean --from` it** (2026-10-21, #293;
    verified in a box). 4.5's notifications keep their state in `~/.local/state/omarchy/notifications`
    (live.json: the toasts on screen; history.json; quiet.json: Do Not Disturb), read back at every
    shell start: `restart-shell` and a box `--from` a save show the toasts that were up, and the
    history has the save's. **Fix**: `up --clean` removes that folder (links on the way first): a
    clean box starts with none. A box `--from` a save without --clean, and `restart-shell`, keep them,
    as a desk does. Tests: t_clean.

420. **`up --omarchy` of a 4.5 tree on an older host** (2026-10-21, #293; read from the RC's tree, the
    host is on 4.5 now). 4.5's `default/hypr/input.lua` sets `kb_options = "omarchy:shift_caps_compose"`,
    an option of the xkb files its package installs in `/etc/xkb` (the tree's `etc/xkb`); a host
    without them has a keymap that does not compile. And 4.5 runs `owe` (video wallpapers, intros),
    `omasnap` (screenshots) and the `omarchy-hyprland-titlebars` Hyprland plugin (floating
    workspaces), which only its packages bring. **Fix**: with `--omarchy`, the tree's `etc/xkb` goes
    over the host's in the box's `/etc` (copied into the box dir's etc/, links kept as links) when
    they differ, and `up` says each of the three the tree uses and the host lacks (`up: --omarchy:
    this host has no owe: no video wallpapers and no theme intros`). Checked on this 4.5 host with a
    copy of the RC tree whose symbols/omarchy differs: the box's `/etc/xkb/symbols/omarchy` is the
    tree's. The failing keymap itself is not reproduced (this host has the files). Tests:
    t_unit_omarchy45 (`omarchy_host_gaps`), t_omarchy_tree.

421. **On Omarchy 4.5 `--no-raise` was refused over the notifications and dock with nothing there**
    (2026-10-21, #311; verified in a box on 4.5.0rc1 and on the v4.0.6 tree). Finding 398 took a
    layer covering its whole output for one that takes input on its items only. 4.5's notifications
    layer is a column the full height of the screen at its right (465x1080 at 1455,0; 399 px on the
    stock bar), mapped while idle (`Service.qml`: "It stays mapped while idle", input `mask` the toast
    deck), and its dock a strip along the bottom (1920x207, or 1878 px beside a vertical bar), mapped
    too, input on its icons (`DockWindow.qml`'s `mask`). Neither covers the whole screen, so both were
    certain: `windows` said each "is over" every window it overlapped, `click --window --no-raise`
    under either was refused ("input there goes to it") with no toast up and the dock hidden, and a
    plain click warned that it went to the layer. Checked by hand that input passes through: a
    `--no-raise` click under the idle column on an unfocused window, and one over the hidden dock,
    each focused that window. **Fix**: `LAYER_SPAN_JQ` (was LAYER_WHOLE_JQ): a top or overlay layer
    also spans its output when it covers the output's whole height or width outside the edges the
    output reserves (`monitors`' `reserved`), unless it sits on a screen edge the output reserves,
    which is a bar's (Omarchy's bar has an exclusive zone; it takes input all over). Monitors without
    `reserved` (unit fixtures) keep finding 398's rule. A canvas on the same edge as a bar is missed
    (certain, as before). The wording is now "a layer spanning the screen" / "spans the screen,
    possibly over" / "(it spans the screen: …)", and the click's hint names `omarchy-shell
    notifications dismissAll` for the notifications (not `wait layer --gone`, which on 4.5 never
    returns). The toast itself: a click on it still closes it on 4.5 (`card.activated()` →
    `closeToast`; live.json empties); only the layer stays, so t_click_layer's `wait layer --gone`
    was a 4.0 expectation, not an omabox bug. Tests: t_click_layer (both generations, OM),
    t_unit_window_select, t_unit_wait_facts.

422. **The suite on Omarchy 4.0.x and 4.5** (2026-10-21, #311). The contract checked 4.5 only (12
    items failed on a 4.0.6 tree), and three box tests 4.0's behaviour only (9 checks failed on
    4.5.0rc1, on v1.0 too). Each now expects what the Omarchy under test has, told by its tree as
    `center_split` tells it (Bar.qml reads `centerBegin`: `omarchy45` in test/run.sh), never by a
    version: `omarchy_contract` runs the shared items, then `omarchy_contract_45` (the split centre,
    the start-up cover, the intro script, per-monitor workspaces, kept notifications, the spanning
    notifications column and dock of finding 421, Print's Omasnap) or `omarchy_contract_40`
    (centerAnchor, the registry's `center` default, the full-screen notifications layer, Print's
    slurp). t_click_layer (finding 421), t_tree_layer (4.5's launcher tree starts with its search
    field, `text [focused editable]`) and t_cursor_hw_nvidia (Print's layer is `omasnap` on 4.5,
    slurp's `selection` before) branch the same way, and run their box on `OMABOX_TEST_OMARCHY`'s tree
    (`up --omarchy`), so their 4.0 branch runs on a 4.5 host. Every 4.0-only branch, in the code and
    the tests, carries `omarchy<4.5` for #312. Checked: `test/run.sh unit` on the installed 4.5.0rc1,
    the RC tree and the v4.0.6 tree; the three box tests on 4.5 and with the v4.0.6 tree; the full
    suite on 4.5.0rc1 (boxes on the AMD iGPU, NVIDIA tests on the RTX): 5076 passed, 0 failed, 2
    skipped (t_main's NVIDIA screen with the render node pinned to amdgpu; t_setup_prompts' install
    case).

423. **Host placement on Omarchy 4.5: `special:omabox`** (2026-10-21, #292; *decided* by Diogo; verified
    in a 4.5 box standing in for the host, finding 26). On a 4.5 desk a number is the first monitor's
    workspace of that number (finding 416), a workspace in floating mode floats a box's window with a
    titlebar like any other, and the scratchpad (`special`) is Omarchy's Quake console
    (`default/hypr/qconsole.lua`): a lone window there is boxed into a half-height panel (1080x540 on
    1920x1080) and the console starts `omarchy-agent` when it opens empty. The default stays 9. The
    widget offers workspaces 1-10 and "Its own (special:omabox)" and drops "Scratchpad (SUPER+S)"; a
    config naming another value (the scratchpad too) is shown as it is. `special` stays accepted (the
    1.x promise); `ws_note` says one line about the console when it is set (`config workspace`, or what
    `up --interactive` and `peek` use) on a host whose tree has `qconsole.lua` (told by the tree, never
    the version: `${OMARCHY_PATH:-/usr/share/omarchy}`). `ws_text` says how a special workspace shows
    and hides ("special workspace omabox, which the bar widget's Show opens and a workspace switch
    hides"). Checked in the stand-in (stock bar, 1920x1080, Omarchy 4.5.0rc1's config): an
    interactive box with `config workspace special:omabox` opened unfocused on special:omabox at
    1896x1030 (the whole workspace), the stand-in left on 1; its own shots a second apart differed
    while hidden (a clock in foot); `peek --focus` (the widget's Show) opened the special over the
    current workspace and focused the window, with the clock current; a workspace switch (dispatch and
    SUPER+2) hid it, and Show opened it again over workspace 2, current; a headless box's peek window
    went there too, full size, and showed current frames after a hide and a show. The README's
    binding, `o.bind("SUPER + ALT + B", …, hl.dsp.workspace.toggle_special("omabox"))`, added at run
    time, toggled it; SUPER+ALT+B is bound to nothing else in 4.5's defaults (`hyprctl binds`). The
    floating mode is documented, not changed. Tests: t_special_ws (new), t_unit_config.

424. **A test's own Omarchy shell lost plugin hot-reload in a box** (2026-10-21). Omarchy's
    `test/shell.d/runtime-smoke-test.sh`, run with `omabox run`, failed "installed plugin changes
    reload without an explicit rescan": finding 196's stand-in `inotifywait` is first on every box
    PATH, `run`'s too, so it kept the watch of the temporary shell the test starts (its HOME is a temp
    dir, whose plugins dir matched `*/.config/omarchy/plugins`) idle as well as the box's own. With
    the stand-in off PATH all 22 checks passed. **Fix**: the box's Hyprland sets `OMABOX_OWN_SESSION=1`
    for what its session starts (the shell among it), and the stand-in takes the watch only with it.
    `run` starts its command with the session's environment from omabox.env, so it leaves that one
    out. Tests: t_run_options (a `run` command has none, the box shell has it), t_unit_inotifywait
    (without it, the real inotifywait runs), t_plugin_link and t_plugin_check (the box shell's watch
    is still the stand-in). Omarchy's runtime-smoke-test.sh: 22 of 22, three runs.

425. **The CLI's Rust half, and how a command gets there** (2026-10-21, #324; **amended
    2026-10-25: the hand-off below is gone, finding 523**: `bin/omabox` is now the binary, through a
    link to `build/omabox`; **amended again the same day: the port is complete, finding 531**: bash's
    omabox, kept until then as the suite's oracle, is gone, and nothing below runs any more). The port is wave by
    wave, the suite the spec. `bin/omabox` stays the entry point (setup's links, the box's view of the
    repo, ai-jail's maps all name it): its `main` hands a command in `RUST_CMDS` to
    `build/bin/omabox` (crates/omabox, built by install.sh and the suite with cargo) right before its
    own dispatch, so `global_box`, `eq_split`, `CMD --help` and the relay have run and the words come
    as they would to `cmd_*`. Under the broker too: `broker_check` (bash's until the broker is ported)
    has passed the call by then (`broker_init` has also unset `OMABOX_BROKER_PEER`, so a check of it
    there never held), and the Rust half reads the jail from `OMABOX_JAIL` as bash does. Not with
    `OMABOX_BASH=1` (to compare the two; this call's only, not what it starts), not when the
    binary is missing. A command the binary lacks (one built before a pull) goes back to bash with
    `OMABOX_BASH=1`. The hand-off costs bash's parse of the script (~50 ms, as every call does today)
    until the end, when `bin/omabox` becomes the binary. The caller's environment goes along as it
    came (wave 2): bash's own globals (ROOT, BOXES, ...) overwrite what a caller exported under those
    names, and the exec makes /proc/PID/environ the binary's, so `rust_handoff` reads it first and hands
    it over a pipe (OMABOX_ENVIRON_FD), for `run --pass` (finding 74) and for a call handed back to bash
    (the caller's value where a global overwrote it; what the broker set or took out stays so).
    What the Rust half leaves to bash (a `--help` after other words, in lua, log and events) goes
    back before anything is done: the same call. Since wave 3a, run, tree and pixel print theirs
    there as `omabox help CMD` prints it (the help text stays bash's until the front is ported; wave
    3b's scroll and keys-to-box too), and
    `run -d --wait` is the Rust half's, on the settle machinery `wait` shares (settle.rs). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_handoff, t_unit_rust_parity, t_rust_parity.
    Where the halves still differ on signals (wave 4b; 4c): (a) an INT sent to omabox by a process
    stops the Rust half as a TERM does, once its foreground step is over (130), where bash went on
    after a child that outlived it, ended after a `$(...)` step, or at once in-process; a terminal's
    Ctrl-C lets it go on only past gdb's run or check run's scenario (finding 454);
    (b) a TERM to omabox alone while `record sheet` takes its frames ends both 143, but bash's
    subshell finishes the sheet after its main is gone, where the Rust half makes none (the safe
    side: nothing left behind); (c) a second INT, TERM or HUP while a trap's undo runs ends bash at
    once, its undo cut short, or (pending behind a code trap) picks the lowest-numbered exit code,
    where the Rust half finishes the undo and exits with the first signal's code (the safe side,
    finding 452); (d) a code trap (record stop's) runs once bash's `$(...)` in progress is over, for
    a signal to omabox alone, where the Rust half stops after the foreground child (finding 452);
    (e) a TERM or HUP runs bash's EXIT trap at once, its foreground child left running, where the
    Rust half waits for that child, bounded (~20 s at most), before the undo (finding 453); (f) a
    signal during `record --for` or `record -- ACTION` leaves bash's recording running, where the
    Rust half stops it, the video made (finding 455). Left as they are, in both halves: a signal
    between a temporary file's `mktemp` (a child) and its trap (cpu's and gpu's dir, record stop's
    input file and box-dir folder, each the next line) leaves that file; closing the gap needs the
    file made in-process, under the trap's lock, with mktemp's own words for its failures.

426. **A refused OMABOX_STILL_DUMP left a temporary dir behind** (2026-10-22, #324 wave 3a's review).
    settle_begin made its `mktemp -d` dir for the tool's two fifos, and an action's before snapshot
    its `mktemp` file (desk_snap_start: run -d --wait), before it checked OMABOX_STILL_DUMP (the
    suite's frame dump, #222); a value it refused (not a plain absolute path) ended the command there,
    and both were left in $TMPDIR. **Fix**: the check comes first, before the tool's test and before
    anything is made, in bash and in the Rust half alike; no other refusal of settle_begin's comes
    after them. Tests: t_unit_rust_parity (wait still and run -d --wait on a stand-in desktop, both
    ways, with TMPDIR a dir of the test's own: empty after).

427. **A failed `shot --burst` left a temporary file behind, and `shot --changed` its frame**
    (2026-10-22, #324 wave 3b and its review). shot_burst keeps the burst tool's (or a grim's) words in
    a `mktemp` file, and a frame that failed ended the command (the box gone, a Hyprland that stopped
    answering, the frame not taken) with those words in its message before the file was removed: one
    file left in $TMPDIR each time. shot_changed reads the box's mode after the capture: a box that
    stopped answering there ended the command with the frame just taken left in $D/changed as
    `.new-XXXXXX`. **Fix**: the words are read and the file removed first, and the frame removed
    before that end, then the command ends as before, in bash and in the Rust half alike. Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity (a burst whose frame fails on the stand-in desktop, from the burst tool and a
    grim a frame, TMPDIR a dir of the test's own; a --changed whose box stops answering once the frame
    is taken: compared both ways, nothing left after).

428. **`cpu --app` cut a name to 15 characters where the kernel keeps 15 bytes** (2026-10-22, #324
    wave 4a). A process's name (/proc/PID/comm) is the first 15 bytes of what it set, and `cpu` keeps
    the processes whose tamed name is `--app`'s, cut to the same 15 (cpu_tame's words: "bytes, as the
    kernel truncates a name"). The cut was `${app:0:15}` in the caller's locale, which counts
    characters in UTF-8: a name of characters past one byte (`ééééééééé`, 18 bytes, 15 kept by the
    kernel) kept all of its 18 bytes, matched none, and `cpu` said "ran no process". **Fix**: the cut
    is cpu_tame's own, under its `LC_ALL=C`, where a character is a byte; the Rust half cuts bytes.
    Tests: t_unit_rust_parity4 (a stand-in process named so, found by `--app` both ways).

429. **A monitor window of an interactive box could open on the user's workspace, focused, or leave
    the host rule on** (2026-10-22, #324 wave 4a's reviews; the design study after them, #349).
    monitor_add_window turned one host rule on for the box's new window (class `^aquamarine$`:
    workspace, silent, no focus, floating at its size and place) and off once the window was there;
    an EXIT trap turned it off however the add ended. Every way the rule went off before the window
    mapped put the window on the user's active workspace with focus (finding 70), and every way the
    trap was cut short left the rule on, catching every later aquamarine window (a nested Hyprland's
    too). Three rounds of trap fixes (remove the output before the rule-off, as the box handles its
    IPC in order; signals held in the trap; a rule-on cut short sent off again) each found new holes:
    - **No signal needed**: hyprctl gives up after 5 s (`SO_RCVTIMEO`: "Hyprland IPC didn't respond in
      time / Couldn't read (6)", exit 6, never `timeout`'s 124), but the box's Hyprland still reads and
      handles the request later. A box that made the window after 5 s got the rule off first: the
      window on the desktop. Released omabox had this too.
    - Two adds at once (one box or two) shared the one rule: the first rule-off ended it for both, and
      on one box both could take the same WAYLAND-N. A SIGKILL left the rule on. A Ctrl-C in Rust
      waited for the step in flight, a TERM did not, so the halves drifted.
    **Fix (design C, both halves)**: nothing to turn off. omabox's aquamarine build (+appid,
    `patches/aquamarine/0004`) gives a new Wayland output's window the app_id `aquamarine-TOKEN` when
    the file `$AQ_WAYLAND_APP_ID_FILES` + NAME holds TOKEN (1-64 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; else, and without
    the env, `aquamarine` as before). An interactive box's Hyprland gets that env
    (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omabox.appid.`, share/start-hyprland.sh; headless and NVIDIA boxes do not). Each
    `monitor add` makes a random token (16 hex digits), turns on a host rule named
    `omabox-mon-TOKEN` matching `initial_class` `^aquamarine-omabox-TOKEN$` alone, then writes
    `omabox.appid.NAME` (`omabox-TOKEN`, renamed into place: a token file only ever names a token
    whose rule is on), sends the rule again right before the create (a host config reload drops every
    rule: that narrows the gap to create-to-map), asks for the output, and finds its window by that
    class (not by counting the box's windows, which a neighbour's add could satisfy). The rule is never
    turned off: no other window will carry that class, and rules go with the host's next reload. So a
    signal at any step, a SIGKILL, a slow, dead or wedged box and concurrent adds can leave at worst a
    monitor and its window on the box's workspace, never one on the user's.
    - The EXIT trap is tidiness only: once the box was told to make NAME it removes NAME, unless the
      create's answer said clearly that none was made (`mon_answer`: ok; Hyprland's own words, exit 0
      or 7; `Couldn't connect`/`Couldn't open a socket`; the box gone). Anything else, hyprctl's 5 s
      give-up first, is unclear and removed. The trap no longer holds INT, TERM or HUP: a second one
      ends it at once (the Rust half's signal thread sets them back to default before an undo, as
      bash's trap dies of a second one). The remove must reach the box after the create: a TERM or
      HUP can land while the create is still on its way (on_box, nsenter, sh, `timeout`, then hyprctl
      connects, tens of ms), and a remove that gets there first finds nothing ("output not found")
      while the create then makes a monitor no one listed. Both halves send the remove at once (a
      second signal may end the trap before the create is over: the remove is on its way by then) and
      send it again when it is not answered `ok`: the Rust half once main's foreground child, the
      create's capture, is over (`trap::wait_foreground`; that capture is held open by `timeout`'s
      hyprctl, a process group of its own a group signal never reaches; a second signal during the
      wait still ends it at once, waiting is not holding), bash half a second on (it runs its EXIT
      trap at once on TERM and HUP and cannot wait for its `$(...)`). Left in bash only: a create still
      not at the box half a second after the signal leaves a monitor on the box's workspace, its
      window not in `monitor-windows` and its line still in `omabox.monitors` (the signal path keeps
      both). The token file goes once a remove is answered `ok` (the box made NAME, so it read the
      token: left, a later window of that name would take this add's class and rule); it stays when
      none was (the box may still read it; a remove queued
      behind a create the box handles past 5 s gives up too), and goes on success.
    - Interactive `monitor add` runs under the box's lock (`.lock-NAME`, as up and down): a second add
      on that box waits up to 60 s, then says "busy".
    - Refused without +appid (box.json's aquamarine version: the system's, or a box started before the
      rebuild): `monitor add` ("omabox setup --aquamarine, then a new box") and `up --interactive
      --monitor` ("omabox setup --aquamarine"). aq_monitor_note (the +layout/+cursor notes) went with
      it: a build with +appid has both. box.json's version alone did not show that the box's Hyprland
      has the env (review of this fix): it is the library's `.omabox-commit`, while the env comes from
      the share/start-hyprland.sh of the omabox that ran `up`. A linked worktree with no build/ runs
      the main checkout's build/prefix (aq_main_lib); once that is rebuilt with +appid, a box an older
      worktree or release started records `+appid` with no env, its windows plain `aquamarine`, and an
      add there would have turned on a rule matching nothing: the window on the user's workspace,
      focused, until the 5 s window wait gave up. So start-hyprland.sh, where it sets the env, leaves
      `omabox.appid-files` in the box's runtime dir, and both halves of `monitor add` refuse a box
      without it too ("started by an omabox that does not give a monitor's window a class of its own
      ... start a new box with this omabox"). An add that sees no window in 5 s now also takes its
      line out of `omabox.monitors` (it was left there; the trap removes the output).
    - share/passthrough.lua v5 takes `aquamarine-omabox-*` windows for box windows (toggle,
      keys-to-box, border). confirm-close (finding 70) opens its window again under a name with no
      token, as that window is meant for the user's workspace, focused: the closed window's name when
      it has none, else WAYLAND-1 to 32 in turn, skipping each that has one (looked for right before
      its create); never an unnamed output, which the box could name after a token another add left
      (one whose create got no clear answer and whose removes failed), its rule then sending the
      window to the box's workspace. It deletes no token. It first removed the one left for the
      closed window's name (third review of this fix): that token can be an add's still in flight (the
      user closes the box's last monitor WAYLAND-k while an add, after desk_prune dropped WAYLAND-k,
      picked that name and wrote its token), and a removal landing between the add's token and its
      create made the add's window plain `aquamarine`, on the user's workspace with focus. Left: the
      check and the create are two steps, so an add can write its token for that name between them;
      the box then gives confirm-close's window the add's class and rule (the box's workspace, no
      focus: the box keeps a window, out of the user's sight) and refuses the add's create ("Name
      already taken"). A stale token (an add SIGKILLed after writing it, or one whose removes all
      failed) needs no other cleanup: a name's token is read only by a create of that name, the next
      add of that name writes its own over it, and that add's success or its trap's answered remove
      deletes it (`monitor remove` leaves tokens alone: it takes no box lock, so it could race an
      add in flight); it also goes with the box's runtime dir. Until then confirm-close
      passes that name over: its window then keeps none of the closed one's workspaces (finding 416:
      a new block of ten). Adds name WAYLAND-2 and up, so the main window's WAYLAND-1 has a token only
      if an agent wrote one. An output an agent makes in the box under a name with a stale token
      still takes it: left as is (both removes must have failed first).
    - Contract changes: monitor windows' class is no longer exactly `aquamarine` (a user's rule on
      `^aquamarine$` no longer touches them; `^aquamarine` matches both), they keep `render_unfocused`
      (drawn while hidden) while their rule lasts, adds on one box take turns, and an aquamarine
      without +appid is refused. A host reload between the rule and the window's map still opens it on
      the user's workspace (no runtime rule survives a reload).
    - Signals the halves still take differently, both safe: a group INT during the create ends bash
      (its capture of the create dies of it: trap, monitor removed, 130), while the Rust half's child
      there (`timeout`, a process group of its own) does not die of it, so it takes it for an INT to
      itself alone and finishes the add, then 130 (older than this fix). A group HUP there can end
      bash's trap before it starts: a bash with jobs (on_box's capture has some) sends them a HUP of
      its own, and they share its group, so the subshell gets a second one (probed: the trap ran 3 to
      5 times in 15; a plain `$(sleep)` 15 in 15). bash then leaves a monitor on the box's workspace,
      the Rust half removes it. The parity suite checks both cases for safety on each side only.
    Verified in boxes (a stand-in host, finding 26, real Hyprland 0.56.2 and the +appid build): each
    monitor's window has its own `aquamarine-omabox-*` class and lands on 9, floating, the stand-in's
    focus and workspace unchanged (so the rule applies by `initial_class` at the first map), for `up
    --interactive --monitor`, `monitor add`, and two adds on one box with one on another at once;
    confirm-close with a token left for its name reopens a plain `aquamarine` window under another
    name, the token kept. Read in source,
    not seen: hyprctl's 5 s give-up (the stand-in models it), keys-to-box inside a monitor's window
    (passthrough v5; the suite's keys-to-box checks use the main window). `up --interactive
    --monitor`'s refusal without +appid is checked from `main` with aq_resolve answering for a private
    build without it (t_unit_refusals), not on a real one. Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity4 (its stand-in box hyprctl now gives up at 5 s, exit 6, as the real one does,
    and names a window by its token file; it exits 7 for an `error:` answer, as hyprctl does, and
    answers "output not found" to a remove of no output; signals INT, TERM, HUP and KILL during the
    rule, between the token and the create, during the create and the window wait, twice during the
    trap; a group TERM and HUP while the create is still on its way to the box (`create.arrive`:
    removed after it, the token gone); a create handled 6 s late, with and without a TERM; one never
    delivered until `timeout 10` ends hyprctl (124, no answer: unclear, removed twice, token kept); a
    create refused in words (exit 0 and 7), hyprctl unable to connect, the box gone at the create (no
    remove, token gone), an empty answer (unclear); two adds at once on one box; the box's lock held;
    unpatched aquamarine refused, and +appid on a box with no `omabox.appid-files`; no window in 5 s:
    removed, its line gone: each side checked that every window it made had its own rule on
    before it, that no rule went off, and where its class token was left), the Rust unit test
    `deskwin::tests::mon_answer_table` (mon_answer's table, the box's state with hyprctl's status and
    words), t_monitors_window (each monitor's window its own class on a
    stand-in host; two adds on one box and one on another at once: on 9, floating, focus unchanged; a real `up`
    leaves `omabox.appid-files`),
    t_guard (confirm-close with a token left for the window's name: plain aquamarine, WAYLAND-2, the
    token kept), t_unit_cli (confirm-close against a stub hyprctl: the closed window's name when it has
    no token, else the first WAYLAND-N with none, never unnamed, every token kept; one try and the box
    ended when Hyprland does not answer), t_unit_refusals
    (`up -i --monitor` on a private build without +appid).
    On port-rust after wave 4b (which judges an INT by what ran when it came): a group Ctrl-C during
    the create looks like an INT to omabox alone, since `timeout`'s hyprctl, a group of its own,
    outlives it, so it is deferred (DEFER_INT) and the add goes on; a second INT while one is deferred
    now ends the add there, its trap removing the output, as bash's subshell ends of it (the parity
    case "group-INT twice", which passed before 4b only because the thread judged that second INT
    when it read it, after the create).

430. **`cpu --app -n` listed every process** (2026-10-22, #324 wave 4a's review). cpu_tame wrote the
    tamed name with `echo`, which takes a name of `-n`, `-e`, `-E` or their mixes for its options and
    prints nothing: the empty name kept every process, and with `--threads` none of their threads. A
    process can be named so (prctl). **Fix**: printf '%s\n' (the Rust half never used echo). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity4 (a stand-in process named `-n`, `--app -n`: that one alone, both ways).

431. **`check diff --report` left its plan behind when the comparison failed** (2026-10-22, #324
    wave 4b). The report's plan is a `mktemp` file in $TMPDIR, made before the comparison; magick
    failing to compare the shots, or to draw `-o`'s marked copy, ended the command with it still
    there: one file left each time. **Fix**: those two refusals remove it first, in bash and in the
    Rust half alike (the Rust half removes it on any refusal past that point). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity4b (a magick that fails at the comparison and at the marking, TMPDIR a dir of
    the test's own: compared both ways, nothing left after).

432. **`record stop` left the recording's input behind when it could not make the video**
    (2026-10-22, #324 wave 4b and its review). The input the recording saw (`$D/record.input`, what
    --show-input draws and --cut-idle keeps) is moved into a `mktemp` file at stop, removed once the
    video is made; ffmpeg failing to make it (the single recording's pass, or the layout's compose),
    the pointer's hold not given back (its lock busy, too), the box gone under a step, or a signal
    meanwhile ended the command with that file still in $TMPDIR, and an `mv` that failed left the
    empty one mktemp made. **Fix**: the file joins REC_TMPS as soon as it is made, with rec_traps'
    EXIT trap alone (rec_exit_trap: it runs on an INT, TERM or HUP ending as well, and the signals
    behave as before; rec_traps' own `exit 130|143|129` still begin at the copy), and a failed `mv`
    removes its file, in bash and in the Rust half alike. Tests: t_unit_rust_parity4b (an ffmpeg
    that fails at stop, INT, TERM, HUP and a group INT during the encode, the pointer's lock held,
    each with input recorded and TMPDIR a dir of the test's own: compared both ways, nothing left
    after).

433. **`check run --json` ended when a run's first checkpoint had no baseline** (2026-10-22, #324
    wave 4b's review). check_compare says each checkpoint with check_one's CHK_SIZE, CHK_REGIONS,
    CHK_TREE and CHK_SPECKS, which check_one sets; a new checkpoint (no baseline) is said before any
    check_one ran, and with --json chk_point_json read them unset: set -u ended the command with
    "CHK_SIZE: unbound variable", no JSON, its .check.jsonl and report.plan.body left in the run's
    folder. **Fix**: check_compare sets them empty first (bash; the Rust half had them so). Tests:
    t_rust_parity (a scenario whose first checkpoint is new, --json, compared both ways).

434. **A signal that cut `up` short after its box started left the box running** (2026-10-23, #324
    integration review; a regression on port-rust, where finding 429's design C dropped the 1.0.1
    stopgap's `monitor_add_held`). up's EXIT trap was `[ $? = 0 ] || kill_box ...`, and bash 5.3 runs
    the EXIT trap of a shell that dies of a signal with `$?` 0 (probed: `trap 'echo $?' EXIT` and a
    TERM, HUP or INT to the shell or its group, during a foreground child or a subshell: 0 each time).
    So an INT, TERM or HUP once the box had started (its Hyprland or shell still coming, or `up -i
    --monitor`'s add) left the box up, unseen, its `starting` file kept; an interactive box has no
    idle limit, so nothing took it down, its window left on the box's workspace. And an INT to up
    alone while it waited on a child that does not die of it (the add's subshell) was swallowed:
    bash takes such a child to have handled it, trap or not, and the up went on. **Fix** (bash: up is
    not ported yet): the EXIT trap ends the box whatever `$?` is (every way out before up's `trap -
    EXIT` is a failure) and removes `starting`; INT, TERM and HUP are trapped (`exit 130/143/129`, so
    the codes are bash's own); `up -i --monitor`'s add runs in the background and is waited for with
    `wait`, which a trapped signal cuts short, its subshell then sent a TERM (its own trap removes the
    output) before the box goes. A successful up is unchanged. Tests: t_up_signals (TERM, HUP and INT
    to up's group and to up alone while it waits for the shell: the code, the box not up, no
    `starting`), t_up_signals_window (the same during `up -i --monitor`'s add, in a stand-in host: and
    none of the box's windows left on it). On the version before, both fail every case but the code.

435. **An interactive `monitor add` whose box answered late opened its window on the user's
    workspace, focused** (2026-10-22, #349; the 1.0.x stopgap). `hyprctl` stops reading after 5 s of
    its own (`SO_RCVTIMEO`, Hyprland 0.56.2's `hyprctl/src/main.cpp`): it prints "Hyprland IPC
    didn't respond in time" and "Couldn't read (6)" and exits 6, so the create's `timeout 10`
    (HYPR_LIMIT) never fires against a box that took the connection. `monitor_add_window` took any
    answer but `ok` for a refusal and turned the host rule off, while the box still had the create
    in its socket: its Hyprland handles requests in order, also those whose client has gone, and
    made the output later, with the rule off. Seen in a stand-in host (finding 26) whose Lua stopped
    the box's Hyprland for 6 s as the rule went on: the add failed at about 9 s, and the window
    opened on the stand-in's workspace 1, focused, with WAYLAND-2 left in the box. **Fix** (bash
    only, small; the 1.1 line replaces the host rule altogether): `mon_answer RC OUT` reads the
    create's answer as `made` (ok), `no` (the box gone, "Couldn't connect" or "Couldn't open a
    socket": the request never left, or any other words: Hyprland's own refusal) or `unclear`
    ("Couldn't read", "Couldn't write", no words, status 124 or 128 and up). On `made` and `unclear`
    the output counts as possibly made, from just before the create until its window is seen mapped
    under the rule. The add's EXIT trap (`mon_cleanup`) then removes it before the rule goes off:
    `output remove NAME` until the box answers one (any answer but an unclear one: it comes after
    the create), 20 s at most (MON_DRAIN), and its line in omabox.monitors dropped. An answer is not
    yet the end: a wayland output becomes the box's monitor only once the host has configured its
    window (aquamarine announces it from that configure), so a remove handled right after the late
    create says "output not found" and the output comes a moment later. The first version stopped
    there, and the stand-in kept WAYLAND-2 (its window on 9, the rule off). On "output not found"
    `mon_drain` asks again every 0.2 s for MON_SETTLE (3) s, until one says ok (both limits timed
    in microseconds: with bash's whole-second `$SECONDS` a 3 s settle was 2 to 3 s, and the unit
    case for it failed three runs in six, its 1 s settle over after one try). (Probed in a
    headless box: its Hyprland stopped, a create given up on at 5.2 s, a remove sent then answered
    ok at 6.0 s, just after the CONT: the box handled the request whose client had gone, then the
    next, in order.) A box silent past MON_DRAIN is said ("if it makes WAYLAND-N later, its window
    may open on your workspace"), and the rule goes off all the same: a rule left on would catch
    every aquamarine window, the user's own nested Hyprland's too. The trade-off taken: the rule is on
    from just before the create until the window is seen or the output removed again, a second or so
    as a rule but about 35 s at worst (a create of 10 s, 5 s waiting for the window, the 20 s drain),
    and for that span it catches the user's own nested aquamarine windows as well (on the box's
    workspace, unfocused, at the monitor's size), where 1.0.1's span was 5 s at most. The add's own
    line is dropped from omabox.monitors as the file is then (`mon_unrecord LINE`: the first line equal
    to the one it wrote), not written back as it was before the add: an interactive add or remove takes
    no lock, and the first version's write after a drain brought back a monitor removed meanwhile and
    lost one added; the second dropped every line of its NAME, so of two adds that both picked
    WAYLAND-2 the one refused took the other's line with it. Once the trap runs, only SIGKILL ends it
    before the rule goes off: it ignores INT, TERM, HUP and PIPE and turns errexit off. A second
    Ctrl-C would cut it short, and so would a stderr gone bad: a pipe whose reader has left (`monitor
    add ... 2>&1 | head -1`, or a `tee` the same Ctrl-C ended) kills it with SIGPIPE at its first
    `say`, and a hung-up terminal fails that `say` (EIO), errexit ending the trap there. Both left the
    rule on with the first version (the unit stand-ins: the said-log ended at the first remove);
    1.0.1's trap wrote nothing. That the trap runs at all is the add's own doing: it traps INT, TERM
    and HUP (`exit 130/143/129`, each ignoring the others first) as the rule goes on. With HUP at its
    default, a HUP to the group (a terminal closed, an SSH session dropped) often killed the add's
    subshell outright, its EXIT trap never run, the rule left on with no time limit (1.0.1 had the
    same hole): a `$(...)` bash it waits on (the create's, the window wait's) hangs its jobs up as it
    dies, sending the group a second HUP while the subshell is still in its own handler. A trapped
    signal is handled once that child returns, so the second HUP finds it trapped, or ignored. In
    bare bash 5.3.20 of the same shape (a subshell with this EXIT trap waiting on a `$(sleep 3; :)`,
    the HUP sent to its group from outside): the trap ran 3 times in 8 in either call shape with HUP
    at its default, 8 in 8 with it trapped (an exec'd `$(sleep 3)` hangs nothing up: 8 in 8 either
    way). How long signals are held: MON_DRAIN, the remove in flight included (each remove's limit is
    what is left of it, HYPR_LIMIT at most, 0.2 s at least; the settle cut to it): about 20 s from
    the start of the trap, after a create of up to 10 s, then the rule-off, which waits HYPR_LIMIT
    (10) s at most (`HOST_LIMIT` on host_hyprctl: a host Hyprland that took no connections held the
    trap, signals ignored, for good) and says so when it fails, naming the `hyprctl eval` that turns
    the rule off. The first version let a remove sent just
    before MON_DRAIN run 10 s more when it blocked in connect, then MON_SETTLE: about 33 s, while its
    message and the CHANGELOG said 20. After an `ok` to a remove, MON_FLUSH (0.5) s before the rule
    goes off: a late output's window and its end, sent on the box's Wayland socket before that ok,
    are read by the host before the rule-off on its IPC socket (not reproduced without it: it rests
    on the two sockets being read in that order). An add whose
    window did not come in 5 s (MON_WAIT) after an `ok` now removes the output too, and says so (it was
    left in the box, its window free to map later with the rule off). A refusal and a dead box are said
    as before, at once, with no remove; both messages fold hyprctl's lines into one ("Hyprland IPC
    didn't respond in time; Couldn't read (6)"). In the same stand-in after the fix (two runs): the add fails at about 8.4
    s, saying it did not answer whether it made WAYLAND-2; no window on workspace 1, focus
    unchanged, WAYLAND-2 gone from the box and its record, the rule off, and the next add makes
    WAYLAND-2 on 9. A box killed as the rule goes on: refused in about 2.5 s, no remove asked, the
    rule off. Left for the 1.1 line (#349): a signal during the create can still send the trap's
    remove before the create has reached the box, two adds at once share the one rule, a box
    answering after 20 s, a host taking more than 3 s to configure the late window, or a box slow to
    handle that configure after its answer, a reload of the host's config during the drain (it
    clears every window rule, this one too, and Omarchy reloads on a theme change: a late window
    then maps on the user's workspace), and a SIGKILL during the drain (a harness's KILL after its
    grace period): the rule stays on, with no time limit, until the next interactive `monitor add`
    turns it off (`down` does not touch it; a reload of the host's config likely drops it, not
    checked), where 1.0.1's window was about 5 s. `monitor add` waits for the add's subshell whatever
    the signal (`monitor_add_held`): called as `line=$(monitor_add_window ...)`, a TERM or a HUP to the
    whole group ended omabox's main shell at once while the subshell drained on, detached, so the user
    saw the command end, retried, and the retry redefined and turned off the one shared rule, the first
    add's late window then mapping on the user's workspace, focused. (A Ctrl-C was waited for: bash
    waits on a child that handles SIGINT itself. In bare bash 5.3 of the same shape, the child's trap
    taking 1.5 s, three runs each: the parent ended after 1.85 s on INT, after 0.35 s, at once, on
    HUP and TERM.) Now the subshell runs in the foreground, its line to a file, and the main shell's
    INT, TERM and HUP traps only note the first one's status (130, 143, 129), which bash runs once
    the child has returned; the command exits with it after the rule-off. `up -i --monitor` calls
    `monitor_add_held` too: it called the subshell bare in up's shell, which a TERM or HUP ended at once
    in the same way, up's EXIT trap seeing 0, so kill_box did not run, the half-started box stayed up
    and the add drained on, detached, for a retry to share the rule with. Now up exits with the
    signal's status after the rule-off, and its EXIT trap ends the box. Tests:
    t_monitors_window_late (new: the box's Hyprland stopped for 6 s, then killed, by the stand-in's
    Lua; it fails on the code before the fix), t_unit_monitors (`mon_answer`'s cases; the order the
    stand-ins were told things: create, removes until answered and "output not found" settled for
    MON_SETTLE timed to the microsecond, the line dropped, then the rule off; the same with the add's
    stderr on /dev/full and on a pipe whose reader has gone; only its own line dropped from the file
    another command changed during the drain; the four new checks fail on the first version; the
    rule off MON_FLUSH after the box's ok; a remove blocked until its limit given up on at MON_DRAIN,
    2 s there, not after HYPR_LIMIT; a HUP to the add's own group from outside while the create is
    in flight, as `monitor add` calls it, as `up` does and the subshell alone: removed, then the rule
    off. On the version before, the HUP cases failed 5 times in 6 over three runs, the other two every
    run; an INT, a TERM and a HUP to the group of `monitor add`'s call during the drain: the command
    returns, with 130, 143 or 129, only after the rule-off (TERM and HUP fail with the `$(...)` call;
    INT passes there too); a TERM and a HUP to the group of `up`'s call during the drain: the same,
    and up's EXIT trap sees 143 or 129 (all four fail with the bare call: up returned before the
    rule-off, its trap seeing 0); an `ok` with no window in MON_WAIT: removed, then the rule off; another add's line of the
    same name kept; a rule-off to a host that never answers given up on at HYPR_LIMIT, and said).
    **On the port-rust branch finding 429's design C replaces this** (each monitor window a class
    and a rule of its own, no rule turned off): mon_cleanup, mon_drain, mon_unrecord,
    monitor_add_held, the global `omabox_monitor_rule` and their tests went with the merge, 429's
    `mon_answer` replaced this one's. host_hyprctl's HOST_LIMIT, which then nothing set, went in
    wave 4c.

437. **A group Ctrl-C during the Rust half's interactive `monitor add` finished the add** (2026-10-23,
    #324 integration review). The create's foreground child outlives a group INT (`timeout` puts the
    box's hyprctl in a group of its own), so trap.rs took the INT for one to omabox alone and
    deferred it (DEFER_INT, bash's `$(monitor_add_window)`): the add went on, its monitor and window
    kept, and omabox ended 130 without its line. Bash's add ends there (its capture of the create dies
    of the INT), its trap removing the output. **Fix** (Rust over bash): during an interactive monitor
    add any INT ends it (`sig::INT_ENDS`, set by cmd/monitor.rs around the add only), its trap removing
    the output once the create is over, exit 130; an INT anywhere else is judged as before. This
    differs from bash for an INT to omabox alone (`kill -INT PID`): bash's main ends at once, 130,
    while its subshell finishes the add and keeps the monitor; the Rust half removes it (CHANGELOG,
    "Changes from the bash omabox"). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity ("group-INT during the create", alike
    now: removed both ways; "INT to omabox alone", each side's ending checked: 130 and kept in bash, 130
    and removed in Rust).

438. **A box name made of echo's options was refused with no name** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). Bash
    takes the default box name through `$(echo "$OMABOX")`, so a name of `-n`, `-e` or `-E`, alone or
    together (`OMABOX=-n`, OMABOX_RELAY_DEFAULT in a jail, a repo named so), printed nothing: "bad box
    name : a box name starts with a letter or digit...", the name missing. The Rust half copied it
    (shell::echo_sub). **Change** (Rust over bash): the name as it is, "bad box name -n: ...", exit 2
    as before (CHANGELOG, "Changes from the bash omabox"). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity ("OMABOX=-n",
    an expected difference).

439. **`--mod` words were matched against the current folder's files** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c).
    Bash splits `--mod`'s value unquoted under IFS=+, so each word was also pathname-expanded: `--mod
    '*'` in a folder holding a file `ctrl` held Ctrl, any other file name there became "'NAME' is not a
    modifier", and `.*` named the dotfiles. The Rust half copied it with libc's glob. **Change** (Rust
    over bash): click, drag, pointer and scroll split `--mod` at `+` and `,` only and take each word as
    written, so `*`, `?` or `[` are refused as modifiers, named as given (CHANGELOG). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity ("click --mod with a glob", "...a dotfile pattern", "...in a folder of a
    modifier's name", where bash held Ctrl and clicked: expected differences), input.rs's mod_words.

440. **A box command ended by TERM was said as bytes dropped, after a 2 s wait** (2026-10-23, #324
    wave 4c). Bash's own job line for a command killed by a signal lands in the nsenter stderr that
    ns_held keeps, so ns_said took it for nsenter's: `omabox run -- sh -c 'kill -TERM $$'` said
    "omabox: dropped 50 bytes of other output on nsenter's stderr" (bash's padded "Terminated" line
    counted) and, the held text not empty, polled the box for 2 s before it answered. The Rust half
    appended those same bytes to get the same count and wait (exec.rs's kill_line), said "the command
    was killed by" only for a signal whose bash line was its own (KILL, SEGV: not TERM), and passed
    each box call a flag saying whether bash's call sat inside a `$(...)`, where bash prints no such
    line. **Change** (Rust over bash): only what nsenter's stderr really held is counted; run's own
    command killed by any signal but INT and PIPE (which shells leave unsaid) is said "omabox: the
    command was killed by SIGTERM (143)"; the box is polled only when the command failed with words
    held, or died of SIGKILL (what a box's end does to what runs in it). The flag went from on_box's
    55 callers, so every box call whose command dies of SIGKILL now waits up to 2 s for the box and
    may say "box 'X' went down" where it said nothing: `timeout -k` killing what would not stop at
    record stop's copy and encode (record_stop.rs), record's start (record.rs) and audio's capture
    (audio.rs); bash waited and said so only where its call sat outside a `$(...)`. Exit codes are
    unchanged (CHANGELOG). A test leaned on the old wait: t_rust_parity's
    prep for run -d --wait ran `sh -c 'pkill -f rp-w3'`, whose -f kills that sh too, and the 2 s it
    cost let the closed window's last frames pass before the next case; the prep now waits for the
    screen to be still. Tests: t_rust_parity ("run: by SIGTERM", an expected difference), exec.rs's
    said_text_counts_what_was_held.

441. **Errors were said in bash's or another tool's words** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). What omabox
    met on its way came out as bash or a tool would have said it, which the Rust half copied word for
    word: `check run`'s scenario that could not run ("bash: X: /bin/sh^M: bad interpreter: No such file
    or directory", from bash 5.3's 128-byte sample less its last byte, so a long interpreter was cut;
    "bash: X: command not found"), pixel past its image's end and a shot's size unread ("od: cannot
    skip past end of combined input", "od: FILE: Is a directory", though no od runs), a file it could
    not write (a bare "PATH: Permission denied": bash's redirection line), a jq, hyprctl or gdb not on
    PATH ("jq: command not found"), and clip's refusal naming the omabox process "bash". **Change**
    (Rust over bash): omabox's words, the same exit codes: "omabox: check: cannot run scenario X: its
    #! interpreter '/bin/sh^M' is not there (CRLF line ends?)" (127 none such, 126 one that cannot
    run; the interpreter read whole from the first line, each CR shown ^M; a scenario with no #! is
    still run by bash, which callers rely on), "omabox: pixel: the point is past the end of grim's
    image", "omabox: cannot read FILE: why", "omabox: CMD: cannot write PATH: why", "omabox: cannot
    run jq: not found in PATH", "set for omabox, pid N" (CHANGELOG). Wave 4c-2's fix round: check's
    /usr/bin/python3 that did not start (gone after check's own test for it, or not runnable) said
    bash's "/usr/bin/python3: No such file or directory" whatever the cause; now "omabox: check:
    cannot run /usr/bin/python3: why", 127 or 126 (check.rs's py_not_run). Tests: t_rust_parity (the
    twelve scenario kinds and the one not there), t_unit_rust_parity (pixel's, shot's, clip's),
    t_clip: expected differences; check.rs's interpreters_as_the_kernel_reads_them and
    python_not_run_said, jq.rs's not_run_said.

442. **Silent set -e exits, and helpers' statuses taken for omabox's** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c).
    Where a bash step failed under set -e the command ended with that step's status and often without
    a word, and the Rust half did the same: pixel on a frame whose header was cut short or whose size
    bash's arithmetic refused, or a point at or past its end (1, unsaid); gdb on a box whose pid
    namespace this user namespace cannot read (box_pid's 3, unsaid) or a gdb that did not start (its
    status); check's mkdir and cp (1, which is check's code for "changed": a run whose base could
    not be made read as a change), its redirections (a checkpoint's .point it could not write: 1),
    its out folder it could not enter (cd's words, 1), a report it could not move into place (unseen);
    shot, record and calibrate on a path readlink -f could not resolve (1, unsaid); record stop's
    video it could not move. And whether a step ended the command at all hung on where bash's call
    sat: mon.rs and deskwin.rs passed an `errexit` flag (inside a `$(...)` or an `||`, set -e is off),
    so a box.json or monitor-windows record that could not be written ended `mode`, `output` and
    `monitor remove` with 1, and went unseen in `monitor add`. **Change** (Rust over bash): one rule. A
    step that fails says what failed (`omabox: CMD: ...`) and ends the command with its usual code: 1, or 2
    under check (its code for its own failures); a box.json record of the monitors that cannot be
    written is said and the command goes on, in every caller (mode's own record ends it: "WANT is set,
    but ls will not show it"); the errexit flags are gone (CHANGELOG). gdb's 3 there is now 1, check's
    1 there now 2. Tests: t_unit_rust_parity (pixel's, shot -o past an unreadable folder),
    t_unit_rust_parity4b and t_rust_parity (check's folder that cannot be made, a .point that cannot
    be written): expected differences; check.rs's out_folder_not_entered (no case reaches it: the
    folder was just made). gdb's unreadable namespace has no case: need_box refuses such a box first,
    so only a box changing under it reaches that step.

443. **pixel left its frame in $TMPDIR, and a failed box.json update its box.json.tmp** (2026-10-23,
    #324 wave 4c; a bug in both halves, fixed in the Rust half only: bash's is no longer run for these
    commands). pixel's three set -e exits of finding 442 came after its `mktemp`, so each left the
    grabbed frame in $TMPDIR. jq_box_json (mode, monitor, output: `jq ... > box.json.tmp && mv`) left
    box.json.tmp in the box's dir when jq or the mv failed, and take_over (an agent resumed, finding
    93) when its jq failed, and output's output.dropped.tmp when its write or mv failed. **Fix**: the
    temporary files are removed on every return (shell::Rm), and take_over says when it could not
    record the agent; pixel's frame also on INT, TERM or HUP (trap::on_exit: bash's pixel, with no
    trap, left it to a signal too). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity (pixel's cases list
    a TMPDIR of their own: the frame left in bash, none in Rust, expected differences; a TERM while
    grim takes the frame too).

444. **The Rust half ran `date` for names and stamps, and handed awk a glob that matched nothing**
    (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). run -d's log and exit file (`date +%s%N`), check run's out folder,
    record's file and record stop's video (`+%Y%m%d-%H%M%S`, `+%H%M%S`) and gdb --watch's header
    (`date -Is`) each spawned the `date` on PATH, as bash's `$(date ...)` does, and the suite named a
    log by a stand-in `date` (t_replace, finding 229's case); gpu's snapshot handed awk the literal
    `/proc/PID/fdinfo/*` of a process with no fdinfo, for awk to fail on unsaid as it did on bash's
    unmatched glob. **Change** (Rust over bash, no output changed): the clock read in-process
    (shell::date, date_iso, epoch_ns: strftime in the local zone, as date prints it), and such a
    process skipped. t_replace names the log by `OMABOX_TEST_RUN_NS` for the Rust half (digits only,
    read only under the suite's OMABOX_SUITE) and by its stand-in `date` on PATH for bash's (which
    --installed runs). Tests: shell.rs's dates_as_coreutils_prints_them, t_replace.

445. **omabox's own patterns took the locale's letters and digits** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). Bash's
    `=~` is glibc's regex in the caller's locale, where en_US.UTF-8 (and most named UTF-8 locales; not
    C or C.UTF-8) has `[0-9]` take `²` and `١` and `[A-Za-z]` take `é`: a process whose OMABOX_BOX
    was `é` was named box é by `which`, and a `²` passed every number check to be refused next by
    bash's arithmetic in its own words ("10#: invalid integer constant", exit 1: `pixel 1 ²`, `click
    ² 1`). The Rust half copied it (shell::Re in the process's locale). **Change** (Rust over bash):
    omabox's own patterns (Re::new, re_match, re_group: box names, numbers, sizes, ids, every
    validator) are compiled and matched in the C locale (uselocale around regcomp and regexec), so
    they are ASCII, and `.` takes any byte; a caller's own (`events --grep`, `--until`: Re::from_bytes)
    stay in the caller's locale, their syntax the contract (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity
    ("which: OMABOX_BOX in the locale's letters", "pixel: a digit of the locale's", "click: a digit of
    the locale's": expected differences under en_US.UTF-8, where the system has it), shell.rs's
    own_patterns_ascii_in_any_locale.

446. **Lists came in the locale's collation** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). Bash sorts a glob's matches
    with strcoll, and `sort` (run for ports' rows, gpu's processes, record's marks, check's regions)
    in the caller's locale, so en_US.UTF-8 lists `a` before `B` and skips punctuation at first,
    where C lists `B` first: a session's boxes in a refusal, the run logs, the checkpoints `check
    run` goes through, calibrate's marks and output's comm-style merge all came in an order that
    hung on LANG. The Rust half copied it (shell::coll_cmp, `sort` in the caller's locale).
    **Change** (Rust over bash): byte order everywhere, the same in every locale: shell::glob and
    glob_ext sort bytes, coll_cmp is gone, and every `sort` omabox runs gets LC_ALL=C (sig::command;
    `-n` then reads numbers as C does too). `ls` and `saves` got it in wave 5b (finding 470)
    (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity ("four: named in byte order"), t_unit_rust_parity5 ("ls
    --json: in byte order in every locale", "saves --json: ..."), expected differences under
    en_US.UTF-8; its fixture's box Zed is zed now, whose capital put the "up: ..." list of
    some 30 refusals in an order that hung on the suite's locale. Since 6b, shell.rs's
    globs_in_byte_order and t_unit_bash_changes (finding 530).

447. **Text was read in the caller's locale** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c). Bash and coreutils count
    characters as LANG and LC_* say, so under C (agents often run with LANG unset) a repo's default
    box name was cut at 31 bytes, `keys` noted `secret N` in bytes and record's `--as` and mark text
    were capped in bytes; `${V,,}` lowered option words with the locale's towlower (a Turkish locale
    made `--mod SHIFT` `shıft` and a gpu of `NVIDIA` `nvıdıa`, refused); `[[:cntrl:]]`, `[[:space:]]`
    and `grep .` followed it too (a word with one invalid byte had its C1 controls kept). The Rust
    half copied all of it: init_locale's setlocale in bash's fallback order, mbrtowc, towlower,
    iswcntrl, iswspace. **Change** (Rust over bash): text is UTF-8 in every locale. A character is a
    valid UTF-8 sequence and each byte of anything else is one (cut, `${V:0:N}`, `${#V}`); controls
    are Unicode's Cc and U+2028/U+2029 (glibc's UTF-8 class); spaces are Unicode's White_Space; a
    line with any byte in it is not empty; option words are lowered in ASCII. omabox no longer calls
    setlocale, so the process stays in C: its `%g` (a monitor's scale and rate) writes a dot whatever
    LC_NUMERIC says (the Rust half's had written a comma under a pt_BR one, where bash's awk wrote a
    dot), and system errors are said in English. A caller's own patterns (`events --grep`,
    `--until`) still read the caller's LC_CTYPE and LC_COLLATE, chosen as bash chose them
    (shell::caller_locale, uselocale around them), and what omabox runs inherits the caller's
    environment as before, but for the awk that lays typed text out on a recording
    (`record stop --show-input`): it runs with LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, since gawk's length and substr
    follow LC_CTYPE and under C made an é two pieces of a byte each (`gawk 'BEGIN { print
    length("é") }'` is 2 under C, 1 under C.UTF-8) (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity ("...by characters in C too",
    "...in characters under LC_ALL=C too": expected differences), shell.rs's
    cut_counts_characters_in_any_locale, length_controls_and_case_in_any_locale.

448. **Numbers were read as bash's arithmetic reads them** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c; decided by
    Diogo 2026-10-22). A number with a 0 in front is octal to `$((...))`: shot's `-g 010,0,100,50`
    was clipped from x=8 while grim was handed `010` (10), `--frames 010` picked 8 frames, a
    recording at `--fps 010` was counted at 8 by `record stop`, `check diff --ignore "010,010
    020x020"` masked 8,8 16x16; `08` and `09` ended the command with bash's "value too great for
    base", exit 1 (`record --fps 08` at its stop, `--frames 08` with no frame picked, a checkpoint's
    `--ignore 08,0` left out, the still tool's `ready 08x08`); `--frames 01` divided by 0; past 64
    bits a number wrapped, and an empty word was 0. The Rust half copied it all (shell::bash_int and
    arith at 67 sites, the arithmetic on them wrapping, arith_said printing bash's line).
    **Change** (Rust over bash): one reader, shell::dec: an optional sign, then ASCII digits,
    decimal whatever its zeros (`010` is 10, `08` is 8), checked at 64 bits. Every `^[0-9]+$` check
    is shell::is_num and every region goes through geom_parse, so a number past 64 bits gets the
    option's usual refusal; what the Rust half wrapped as bash did (wrapping_add, _sub, _mul, _div,
    _neg) saturates instead. Plain + - * stay where the inputs are bounded (record stop's frame
    count, cuts and marks, events' times, pixel's points: each from a {1,N}-digit check or a
    tool's answer). A number omabox
    cannot read where it expects one (a tool's answer, a record of its own) ends the command in its
    words, "omabox: CMD: cannot read WHAT as a number: 'V'" (num::read), exit 1 as before. Regions
    are written as the numbers read: shot's `-g 010,...` is `10,...` in grim's argument, the record
    and what shot says, `record --fps 010` records at 10 and says so, and `which 0123` asks about
    pid 123 (bash looked for /proc/0123; `cpu --pid` and `gdb --pid` refuse a 0 in front) (CHANGELOG).
    Tests: t_unit_rust_parity ("which: this shell, a zero in front", "run --ignore with a zero in front", "wait still: a ready size with a zero
    in front", "pixel: a width with a zero in front", "shot -g with zeros in front") and
    t_rust_parity ("check point --ignore 08: decimal, kept") and t_unit_rust_parity4b ("check diff
    --ignore 08,0", "record stop --sheet --frames" 010, 08 and 01,
    "record --fps" 08 and 010): expected differences; shell.rs's numbers_are_decimal, shot.rs's
    clip_as_bash, settle.rs's geometry.

449. **JSON numbers came in jq's decNumber forms** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c; decided by Diogo
    2026-10-22). jq 1.8 writes a number with an exponent as decNumber's scientific string, `1e3` as
    `1E+3`, `1e300` as `1E+300`, and one below 1E-6 the same way, so what omabox passed through jq
    (a box.json rewritten for a resumed agent, `lua --json`'s values, a job record's numbers) came
    in a form many JSON readers accept but few write. The Rust half copied it (json::number).
    **Change** (Rust over bash): a number with no exponent is written as read (`1.50`, `-0`); one
    with an exponent as JavaScript writes it: plain from 1e-6 to below 1e21 (`1e3` is `1000`,
    `1.5e-6` `0.0000015`), else in exponent form (`1e+300`, `1.5e-7`); one whose exponent is past
    64 bits as read. What the jq programs omabox still runs print is jq's, as before (CHANGELOG). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity ("a resumed session takes its box over": its box.json), t_rust_parity
    ("lua --json: its values"): expected differences; json.rs's numbers_in_standard_form.

450. **Built-in waits ended up to a second early, on the wall clock** (2026-10-23, #324 wave 4c;
    wave 3a's choice reversed). Bash's deadlines are `end=$((SECONDS + N))` then `[ $SECONDS -lt
    $end ]`: whole seconds of the wall clock, so a wait of N seconds ended anywhere from N-1 to N
    seconds in, and a clock step (NTP, a suspend) moved it. The Rust half copied that on purpose
    (settle::secs, time(2)) at ~20 waits: a window to appear (3 s), a mode or output to apply (5 s,
    10 s), the still tool's start (12 s) and a gone box's 2 s, peek's focus (5 s), gdb's attach
    (10 s), record's start (5 s) and wf-recorder's end (15 s), the monitors' moves (5 s), wait's
    and settle's 30 s notes. Other waits counted milliseconds of the wall clock (`date +%s%3N`,
    settle::now_ms), so a clock step lengthened or cut them: `wait --timeout` and its probes'
    budget, `events --until`'s timeout, `run -d --replace`'s 5 s before SIGKILL and 3 s after,
    `shot --burst`'s frame times and spacing, settle's time to a gone compositor, and the windows
    `cpu` and `gpu` sample over (`date +%s%N`). **Change** (Rust over bash): Instant deadlines
    (settle::after, past) and intervals (settle::mono_ms, mono_ns: the monotonic clock since the
    process's first ask), exact; now_ms is left for times written out (run marks, a shot's stamp,
    `events --since 30s`, which compares with events.log's times). `check run`'s "box up in N s" is
    the whole seconds of an Instant's elapsed time. The sleeps between the polls are unchanged
    (CHANGELOG). Tests: none pins a sub-N wait or a clock step; the box tests of those commands
    run as before.

451. **`check run SCENARIO` could run a shell builtin or one of omabox's functions** (2026-10-23, #324
    wave 4c; decided by Diogo 2026-10-22). Bash's check_run starts the scenario as `"${scen[@]}"`
    inside bin/omabox, so a SCENARIO named like a builtin (`test`, `true`, `echo`) or a function of
    bin/omabox's own (`say`, `die`, `cmd_up`) ran in omabox's own shell, not as a program. The Rust
    half never did (check.rs looks the name up in PATH and execs it): a name in PATH is that
    program, one that is not is "cannot run scenario NAME: not found in PATH", 127. **Change**
    (Rust over bash): documented, no code (CHANGELOG; skill/reference.md says SCENARIO is a
    program). Tests: t_rust_parity ("check run: a scenario named like omabox's say", an expected
    difference: bash ran its function, the Rust half finds no such program); since 6b, check.rs's
    a_scenario_is_a_program_whatever_its_name (finding 530).

452. **A signal's stop kept bash's timing: a code trap waited out a whole `$(...)`, a second signal
    picked the exit code or cut the undo short** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 4c). Bash runs a code trap
    (`trap 'exit 143' TERM`, rec_traps: record stop) for a signal to omabox alone only once the
    command substitution in progress is over (`x=$(a; b)`: b ran too), at once for a group one (its
    subshell dies of it), runs pending traps in signal-number order (TERM then INT ended 130), and
    dies of a second signal during its EXIT trap, the undo cut short. The Rust half copied all four:
    the trap's thread waited for main to leave every `$(...)` step (a depth count in sig::subst),
    told a group signal from a lone one by whether the step's child died of the same signal within
    300 ms (group_cut), folded pending signals to the lowest, and set INT, TERM and HUP back to the
    default before a plain trap's undo. record stop had a plain EXIT trap for the input's temp file
    until its copy began, so that a signal there ended the stop as bash's did (finding 432's split).
    **Change** (Rust over bash): the first INT, TERM or HUP decides. Its trap waits for the
    foreground child as before, runs the undo, and exits 128+N for that signal (a code trap) or dies
    of it (a plain one); another INT, TERM or HUP meanwhile changes nothing and the undo finishes.
    record stop has one code trap from its first temp file on. What a caller sees: a TERM or INT to
    omabox alone while `record stop --sheet` takes its frames ends after the frame in progress, 143
    or 130, the video kept and no sheet (bash made the sheet, said it, then exited with that code);
    TERM then INT ends 143, not 130; during stop's encode an INT to omabox alone stops it, 130 (bash
    went on and made the video) and a HUP ends it with 129 rather than dying of SIGHUP (the same
    `$?`). Tests: sig.rs's code_trap_first_signal_wins, second_signal_during_the_undo,
    second_signal_during_a_code_undo (which replace six cases that pinned bash's order and its
    substitution wait); t_unit_rust_parity4b ("record stop --sheet and TERM|INT (twice) to omabox
    alone while it takes the frames", "record stop --show-input and INT|HUP during its encode"),
    t_unit_rust_parity4 ("monitor add, interactive, and group-TERM twice, the second during the
    trap": bash's trap cut short leaves the token file, the Rust half's removes it): expected
    differences.
