453. **A TERM or HUP undid a command's work while its foreground step still ran** (2026-10-24, #324
    wave 4c). Bash runs its EXIT trap at once on TERM and HUP, the foreground child left running
    (an INT waits for it), and the Rust half copied that (trap.rs's wait only for INT, or with a code
    trap on). So `check run` took its box down while the scenario still drove it, and left the
    scenario running after omabox had ended (it went on to fail its next step on a box gone); an
    interactive `monitor add` sent its remove before the create had reached the box ("output not
    found") and had to send it again; gpu's and cpu's dir went while a child still wrote into it.
    The audit's own example, `check run` TERMed during its box's `up`, leaves no box in either half
    (bash's down waits for the up's lock, findings 147 and 237): parity holds there, unchanged.
    **Change** (Rust over bash): on INT, TERM and HUP the trap waits for main's foreground child,
    bounded: 10 s, then a TERM to it (not at once: a child that is itself omabox would get it in its
    own cleanup), 5 s, then a KILL, 5 s; then the undo, whatever is left. A TERM may so take up to
    the step's end, at most ~20 s; nothing it started is left running. Exit codes unchanged. Seen by
    a caller: `check run` stopped during a scenario takes that scenario's step to its end (its point
    written) before its boxes go; `monitor add`'s remove comes once, after the create, its token
    file then removed where bash's stayed. With that, the remove's second try once the foreground
    was over (trap::wait_foreground, and FG_HELD beside it) had nothing left to wait for and went:
    an unclear create (no answer, or past `timeout 10`) now gets one remove, where bash sends a
    second half a second on. Tests: sig.rs's term_waits_for_the_foreground_child and
    a_child_that_will_not_end_is_stopped (both fail on the version before: the undo saw nothing; a
    30 s hang); t_rust_parity ("check run and TERM|HUP during its scenario"), t_unit_rust_parity4
    ("monitor add ... group-TERM before the create reaches the box", "... group-TERM, the box's
    create handled 6 s late"): expected differences. The review's fix round: (1) once the wait passes
    a second, omabox says "omabox: stopping once the step in progress ends (at most 20 s)" on stderr,
    once (parity leaves the line out, it is timing); the 10 s bound is to be looked at again when
    up and down are in Rust (wave 5). (2) The TERM and KILL go through a pidfd of the child, which
    is waited for without being reaped (waitid's WNOWAIT) until it is no longer named, so no other
    process that took its pid gets them, and to its process group when it leads one (timeout's),
    so a grandchild there does not outlive it. (3) A signal while main runs an undo itself (a trap
    dropped on a refusal or at the end: check run's downs, monitor add's remove) waits for that
    undo: Drop, forget and run_undos share one lock (trap::undoing), where the thread had found the
    trap list empty and ended the process halfway through it (so before this wave too). (4)
    shot --no-pointer's release waits for the foreground child the same bounded way. Tests:
    the_stop_reaches_the_childs_group, a_signal_waits_for_an_undo_main_runs.

454. **What an INT sent to omabox alone did depended on how bash's line was written** (2026-10-24,
    #324 wave 4c; decided by Diogo 2026-10-23). Bash, given `kill -INT` of its own pid while a
    child runs that does not die of it, goes on (wait-and-continue: it takes the child to have
    handled it) and ends with the command's own code; during a `$(...)` it ends 130 at once (the
    Rust half: once the step is over); with no child running, 130. So the same `peek --focus` and
    the same INT focused a host window or ended 130 with none, by which line it landed on. The
    Rust half reproduced it: each of ~70 call sites marked by hand as bash's `$(...)` or not
    (sig::subst and run_subst, DEFER_INT, INT_DEFERRED, int_deferred_end, finding 437's INT_ENDS),
    and every in-process wait a `sleep` child (trap::sleep), so that the rule could apply there:
    a process per 50 ms poll. **Change** (Rust over bash, option (c) of the audit): an INT sent by a
    process (si_code not SI_KERNEL: an agent's `kill -INT`, a harness's `kill -INT -PGID` too) stops
    the command as TERM does (finding 453's bounded wait for the foreground child, the undo), exit
    130. A Ctrl-C from the terminal (SI_KERNEL, read with SA_SIGINFO) does too, unless the
    foreground child is one that takes a Ctrl-C itself (sig::takes_ctrl_c: check run's scenario)
    and outlives it: then the command goes on, as before and as bash's. While it waits for that
    child it still reads its signals: a TERM, HUP, a process's INT or a second Ctrl-C meanwhile stops
    the command (the review's fix round: the wait first held them unread till the child's end).
    Every other child a Ctrl-C does not kill no longer lets the command go on: it stops after that
    child, 130, where bash went on after a plain command and ended after a `$(...)`. That includes
    gdb's backtrace run (`timeout 120 ... gdb -batch`): timeout puts itself and gdb in a process
    group of their own, which the terminal's Ctrl-C never reached, so the mark it had at first only
    held the Ctrl-C for gdb's whole run; now the stop's TERM reaches gdb through timeout (finding
    453's group signal), and the command ends 130. An interactive `monitor add`
    still ends at any INT (finding 437), now by that rule. The `$(...)` marks are gone (plain
    run_output, plain calls), and trap::sleep sleeps in-process, parked at once by a stop. Seen by a
    caller: `kill -INT` of omabox during `cpu`, `gpu`, `peek --focus`, `gdb`, `record`, `check run`
    ends 130 once the step in progress is over, where bash went on to the command's end. Tests:
    sig.rs's int_from_a_process_stops_the_command and int_during_an_in_process_sleep, and three on a
    pty of their own, which type a real Ctrl-C: ctrl_c_a_marked_child_outlives_goes_on,
    ctrl_c_a_marked_child_dies_of_stops, ctrl_c_another_child_outlives_stops (they replace
    subst_step_and_int_alone, foreground_step_and_int_alone, undo_on_main_and_a_term and
    undo_on_main_with_a_subst, which pinned the marks), ctrl_c_then_a_term_stops; parity: the
    INT-alone cases (cpu, gpu, peek --focus, gdb, record --for, check run's scenario) are expected
    differences. The suite's signal wrapper (rp-sig) now starts its command with INT and QUIT at
    their defaults: a test running as a parallel job (job control off) inherited both ignored, and
    omabox keeps an ignored signal ignored, so three check run INT cases had passed with neither half
    seeing the INT (the review's fix round). Run for real, the group INTs end both halves alike; the
    INT to omabox alone is an expected difference (bash compares, 1; Rust 130).

455. **`record --for` or `record -- ACTION` stopped by a signal left the recording running**
    (2026-10-24, #324 wave 4c's review). Once the recording runs, bash sets `trap - EXIT INT TERM
    HUP` (finding 320: `record start` leaves it to `record stop`), and --for and -- ACTION kept
    that: an INT, TERM or HUP during the hold or the action ended omabox with wf-recorder still
    recording in the box, the pointer hidden, `$D/record` and `record.geo` kept, and nothing said;
    the Rust half did the same (and, since finding 454, for an INT sent by a process too). **Change**
    (Rust over bash): from a successful start on, --for and -- ACTION hold a code trap whose undo is
    their own end, `record stop` with the plain options: wf-recorder stopped, the video so far made
    and said, the pointer given back; then 130, 143 or 129. It is forgotten before their own stop
    (and on an error before it, which leaves the recording as before). Plain `record start` is
    unchanged. Tests: t_unit_rust_parity4b ("record --for 2s and group-INT|TERM|group-TERM|HUP", now
    sent 1.2 s into the hold, where they had landed before the start was over: expected
    differences, the video made in Rust and the recording's state gone; "... and INT": both make the
    video, bash at the hold's end with 0, Rust at once with 130, finding 454).

456. **`up` in the Rust half, with SECURITY.md's rules held by construction** (2026-10-24, #324 wave
    5a, #355). cmd/up.rs reads the words and makes every check bash's cmd_up makes before anything
    exists, in its order and words; cmd/up_box.rs makes the box. launch.sh comes out byte for byte
    bash's (t_rust_parity_up compares it, and box.json without its times, on real boxes), so what a
    box gets is unchanged. What changed is how the command is built: every bwrap bind goes through
    bwrap.rs's Bwrap, whose methods refuse a seat path (a DRM card node, /dev/input, seatd's socket,
    /run/dbus, the real runtime dir, or a folder holding one) as a source or a destination, take
    devices only as render nodes and NVIDIA's own nodes, the one card path only as the box dir's
    empty placeholder file (finding 294), host folders only read-only or as `--tmp-overlay`, and
    writable binds only for the box's own runtime dir, HOME and cgroup (S1, S4); the fixed system
    binds are a list of their own and what a user or a repo names passes refuse_src and refuse_dest
    (S3). render.rs's RenderNode and NvidiaDev accept only those paths. The HOME is seeded through
    seed.rs's allow list (SEED_ALLOW: each path of the user's look a box may be seeded from), with
    --seed, the desk's files under --desk-shell and a --from save the only other sources (S2). The
    host's Hyprland is reached only through host::HostSilent, which starts the launch script
    `silent` on a workspace ws_check gave, with no focus, and nothing else (S8). The isolated mode
    carries its allow list (net.rs's Net::Isolated, S5). And the started box is read back once its
    Hyprland is up (bwrap names its PID 1 before it makes its mounts: read at once, its root was
    still the host's, /dev/input there, 30 times in 30 in the wave's review): its mountinfo, through
    its PID 1, must hold none of the seat's paths (a card node that is the placeholder file is fine),
    nor /dev/input, /run/seatd.sock or /run/dbus, and its runtime dir must not be the user's own; one
    there, or a mountinfo or root that cannot be read (fails closed), ends the box, "up: box 'B' has
    ... (S1: never the seat's paths, checked on its own mounts): not started" (up_box.rs's
    seat_check), so every box any test starts is checked. Box entry is
    still nsenter. Tests: bwrap.rs's no_seat_path_gets_through (proptest: arbitrary paths at every
    bind method), net.rs's pasta_opens_what_it_should (proptest), upspec.rs's refuse_dest proptest,
    render.rs's, seed.rs's every_allowed_source_says_what_it_is; t_unit_rust_parity5 (96 refusal and
    up-already cases both ways), t_rust_parity_up (19 live cases), the suite's box tests of up.

457. **`--no-seed` and `--keep` matched their words against the current folder** (2026-10-24, #324
    wave 5a; finding 439's class). Bash split them with `IFS=,` unquoted, so each word was also a
    glob: `--no-seed 'font?'` in a folder holding a file `fonts` was read as `fonts`. **Change**
    (Rust over bash): the words are taken as written; `font?` is refused, as any word that is not
    one of the list (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity5 ("up --no-seed with a glob character:
    taken as written"), an expected difference.

458. **A plugin's settings in extensions/ went into the box HOME unchecked** (2026-10-24, #324 wave
    5a). seed_extensions copies the desk's ~/.config/omarchy/extensions (plugins' settings) into
    every box, a jailed caller's too, with seed_copy alone: --desk-shell's own files went through
    desk_content_refused, extensions/ did not, so a plugin that keeps a token or a password in its
    settings had it seeded into every box. **Fix** (the Rust half; bash's half of up is no longer
    run): each regular file seed_copy would copy from extensions/ is read by desk_content_refused
    first, as the desk's files are (exactly what tar copies: below the top, a name like `..cfg`,
    which tar's `.[!.]*` exclude lets through, is read too; the wave's review found it left out); one that holds what looks like a key, token or password stays on
    the desk, said by its name and never its value ("up: not seeded: extensions/NAME from your desk
    (it holds what looks like a key, token or password)"). A file that only names one (`maxTokens`,
    `tokenizer`) still goes in. Tests: t_extensions_secret (fails on the bash half: the token and the
    password are seeded), with a token in `plug/..cfg`; seed.rs's content_check_covers_what_tar_copies.

459. **Protected ports: host ports no connected box reaches** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5a, #355;
    decided by Diogo 2026-10-23). A connected box reached every port on the host's loopback (pasta
    forwards them both ways, finding 156) and, through the host's other addresses (its docker bridge,
    a VPN), every service listening on all of them. **Added**: `protect-ports=PORT[,PORT...]` in
    ~/.config/omabox/config (none by default; until `omabox config` is in the Rust half, written
    there by hand). A connected box gets each excluded (`~PORT`) from both of pasta's `-T` rules and
    both `-U` rules, and, set by pasta's own shell before anything of the box runs (root in pasta's
    namespaces; the box's user namespace below maps back to the user with no capability there), an
    nftables rule in the box's network namespace that rejects a connection from the box to any of
    the host's own addresses (its routing table's local IPv4 ones and /proc/net/if_inet6's, loopback
    aside) on those ports, TCP and UDP. Connections that stay in the box (its loopback, the address
    pasta gave it) are its own and pass. An isolated box reaches only its --allow ports, and a
    protected one is refused there ("up: --allow P: a protected port ..."). The value fails closed:
    blanks around each port are fine (`8080, 5432`), anything else that is not a list of ports
    1-65535 refuses every `up`, exit 2, naming the line (any other setting's bad value is said and
    ignored, which here would let boxes reach the ports). The bash half cannot hold the list, so
    with it set `OMABOX_BASH=1 up` starts no connected box ("up: protect-ports is set in CONFIG, which
    only omabox's Rust half keeps a box off"). nft is needed only with
    a list ("up: protect-ports ... needs nft"); a rule nft refuses ends the box's start. A config that
    is there but cannot be read refuses every `up` too, exit 2 (finding 482; it was read as none
    protected). Not covered: an address the host gains after the box started (until finding 581). Tests: net.rs's pasta_opens_what_it_should
    (proptest: every host-bound rule leaves out each protected port) and rules; t_protect_ports
    (throwaway servers on a port of the test's own, on 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0, tried from a box by
    loopback and by each host address; and nothing in the box can remove the rule: nft refuses it,
    no capability in that namespace; a value that is not ports refused, exit 2); t_rust_parity_up
    ("up of a connected box with protect-ports set", an expected difference: bash's half refuses),
    on a HOME of its own so the user's config cannot reach the halves; net.rs's protect_values.

460. **`up` cut short by a signal could still exit 1 and leave its box** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5a,
    #356). Bash's fix (finding 434) trapped INT, TERM and HUP with `exit 130|143|129` and ended the
    box in its EXIT trap, but under load a group HUP during `up --interactive --monitor`'s add gave
    1, not 129, with the box and its `starting` file left (t_up_signals_window; its evidence was
    pruned before it was read): most likely the add's own failure (its subshell ended by the same
    HUP) reached up's `exit "$arc"` before bash ran its HUP trap. **Change** (Rust over bash): from the box dir's making on, up holds one code trap
    (trap.rs's on_exit_code) whose undo ends the box (and removes a dir that has no box.json yet):
    a failure runs it, and an INT, TERM or HUP at any step waits for the step's child (bounded,
    finding 453), runs the undos (the monitor add's own, which removes its output, first), then exits
    130, 143 or 129, whatever the step returned meanwhile (main parks once the signal is in). That includes the ~5 ms between the
    launch's hand-off and the box's first pid (the wave's review: the undo found no box, exited 143,
    and the box came up after, adopted by its reaper), and an interactive box whose launch the host's
    Hyprland was asked for: the launch and its mark for the undo are made under one lock (a stop
    already on its way launches nothing), and the undo of a launched box waits, at most 10 s as up's
    own wait, until it shows (its PID 1, its pasta or bwrap's info file) or its launcher is gone,
    then ends it and the launcher. Tests: t_up_signals (group and alone, while it waits for the
    shell, while it seeds the HOME, once bwrap has started, and with the launcher held 2 s by the
    suite's seam OMABOX_TEST_LAUNCH_DELAY, the signal inside that hold: no box left once it is over;
    without the undo's wait and its kill of the launcher a box was left running),
    t_up_signals_window (during the interactive monitor's add, in a box standing in for the host).

461. **`up --clean --from SAVE` wrote its wallpaper through a link the save left** (2026-10-24, #324
    wave 5a; finding 168's class). seed_home clears the links on the way to what it writes, but
    --clean's `base64 -d > .config/omabox/clean-wallpaper.png` cleared the folder's, not the file's:
    a save whose HOME had a link there (a box can write anything in its HOME) had the PNG written
    onto the host file the link led to. **Fix** (the Rust half): the link at the file is removed
    first, and the PNG written in the box HOME. Tests: t_rust_parity_up ("up --from a save with a
    link at the clean wallpaper's place"), an expected difference: bash overwrote the host file.

462. **What up said in bash's or a tool's words** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5a; finding 441's class).
    **Change** (Rust over bash): `up --audio` names the programs it lacks one by one ("pipewire,
    pactl", as its code meant: bash's substitution ran on each word and wrote a bare comma); a desk
    with no shell.json is said by nothing (bash printed its own "bin/omabox: line N: ...: No such file
    or directory"; the box's bar starts from an empty shell.json, as before); a plugin validator that
    cannot start is "omabox: cannot run V: ...", and a folder or file seed_home cannot make is "up:
    could not ... in the box HOME: WHY", exit 1, where bash ended with the tool's own line; a failed
    rewrite of box.json (plugin_check, client_render_check) leaves no box.json.tmp. Exit codes
    unchanged. Tests: t_unit_rust_parity5 ("up --audio without PipeWire: the programs named"),
    t_rust_parity_up ("up with a desk that has no shell.json"): expected differences.

463. **A jailed caller's file read by up could hang it** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5a). jail_read (a
    jailed caller's plugin manifest, its --omarchy tree's files) opened the file with bash's `exec
    {fd}<`, which waits for a writer when the path is a FIFO: a jail that swapped one in hung its
    own `up` (the broker's call to it). **Fix** (the Rust half): the file is opened
    without blocking and refused unless it is a regular file. Tests: jailpath.rs's unit tests.

470. **`down`, `ls`, `save`, `saves` and `version` in the Rust half** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5b).
    cmd/down.rs takes a box down as bash's cmd_down did, step for step under the name's lock: its peek
    windows ended, its PID 1 SIGKILLed as box_pid finds it and its pasta with it (ready.rs's
    kill_box; SIGTERM does not work, finding 6), its reaper ended, its dir and HOME removed, the lock
    file with them; `--all`, `--orphans` and the `.down-` marker as before (findings 147, 237).
    cmd/ls.rs asks every box up at once on threads of its own (hung_boxes: 1 s at most, 3 s with a
    hung shell) and runs the same jq programs on box.json (checked verbatim against bin/omabox's);
    cmd/save.rs pauses the box for the copy as bash did (SIGSTOP to its pid namespace), and lets it
    go however the save ends (trap.rs's on_exit: a refusal, INT, TERM or HUP). **Changes** (Rust over
    bash): `ls` and `saves` list in byte order in every locale (finding 446's promise); `save` and
    `saves rm` say what they could not remove in omabox's words ("could not remove all of save 'S':
    rm's line", rm_tree), where bash printed rm's own; a save's keyring is read only when it is a
    regular file (a FIFO there hung bash's grep); `save` clears what a killed save of that name left
    and nothing of another save whose name starts the same (bash's `.new-NAME-*` glob took
    `.new-NAME-x-PID` too). Exit codes unchanged (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity5 (about 90
    cases both ways on boxes of the test's own: dead ones, stand-ins whose PID 1 is taken down for
    real, saves in a data dir of its own; byte order an expected difference under en_US.UTF-8),
    t_rust_parity_up (ls, save, saves and down on a box up), down.rs's and save.rs's unit tests.

471. **The idle reaper in the Rust half** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5b). `_reap` (started by `up` with
    setsid) is cmd/reap.rs, with bash's adoption of a box whose `up` ended before it recorded the
    box's pid namespace (reap_wait_pidns, finding 237) and its retries (finding 162). Bash's hand-off
    execs it, so its command line is `ROOT/build/bin/omabox _reap NAME CREATED`: kill_reapers, in
    both halves, now finds that one as well as bash's `bash ROOT/bin/omabox _reap NAME`. It sleeps
    and waits for the name's lock in-process, where bash ran `sleep` and `flock` children, so the
    suite's tests that watched those children (t_reap_race, t_agent_session) look for a process with
    the lock file open (lock_waiter) or read reap.log. A box whose `used` file is gone no longer ends
    its reaper (bash's arithmetic on an empty stat ended it); its idle limit then waits. **Change**:
    the reaper says once, in reap.log (`omabox log reap`), how often it looks ("box 'B': watching it
    every 60 s"), which nothing showed before (CHANGELOG). An interactive box's reaper asks the host
    whether passthrough's hooks are there through the session it found at its start, as bash did.
    Tests: t_unit_rust_parity5 ("_reap ..." cases, the line an expected difference), the box tests of
    the reaper (t_idle, t_reap_race, t_agent_session, t_orphan, t_run_idle).

472. **A jailed caller's down and up check the box again under its name's lock** (2026-10-24, #324
    wave 5b; S9). select_box refuses another jail's or the user's box by its box.json, which an `up`
    writes while it holds the name's lock; a jailed `down` or `up` of that name waits on the lock,
    and found nothing to refuse before it. **Fix** (the Rust half; bash's `down` stays as it was, a
    fallback): once `down` and `up` hold the lock, a jailed caller's box is checked again, and one
    that is not the jail's is refused ("box 'B' is not this jail's: ..."). A jailed `down` that finds
    no box writes its jail under its `.down-` marker's time, and only an `up` of that jail is
    cancelled by it; the user's own `down` cancels any, and a jailed one never writes over
    that marker. Tests: t_unit_down_jail_race (fails on the
    bash half: the box taken down, the box told, the up cancelled), up.rs's down_markers.

473. **`down` of a box this user namespace cannot read said it down and left it running** (2026-10-24,
    #324 wave 5b). From another user namespace (a sandbox's, `unshare -Ur`), box_pid cannot read the
    box's PID 1's namespace and answers "cannot tell" (status 3), which `up` and every box command
    stop on (#87). kill_box took that for no pid at all: `down` killed nothing, removed the box's dir
    and HOME, said "box 'B' down" and exited 0, while the box ran on with nothing left to find it by.
    **Fix** (the Rust half; bash's down keeps the bug, a fallback): `down` refuses such a box in up's
    words ("cannot tell whether box 'B' is up from this user namespace (a sandbox's?): run omabox
    outside it"), exit 1, and leaves it as it is; `down --all` goes on to the next box (CHANGELOG).
    Tests: t_other_userns (a down from another user namespace), t_unit_rust_parity5 ("down of a box
    this namespace cannot read", an expected difference: bash's said it down).

480. **`omabox config protect-ports`** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5c, #355; S10). Wave 5a's protected
    ports could only be written in `~/.config/omabox/config` by hand. **Added** (the Rust half only;
    bash's CONF_KEYS stays as it was, a fallback): `omabox config protect-ports 8080,5432` sets the
    key, checked as `up` reads it (net.rs's protect_parse: ports 1-65535, blanks around the commas
    allowed, no empty item), and written in its normal form, sorted, each once (`5432,8080`): a value
    `config` writes is one every `up` takes. `config protect-ports default` removes the line (none
    protected). `omabox config` lists it (`protect-ports=` when unset) and `--json` has
    `protect_ports` after `shot_fit`. A value in the file that is not a list of ports is not ignored
    with "ignoring", as the other keys' are: `config` says it as `up` says it ("... no box starts until
    it is one") and shows it as it is, since every `up` refuses it (S10 fails closed). The refusal of
    an unknown key lists it among the keys. Under `OMABOX_BASH=1`, `config protect-ports` is an
    unknown key, as before; a jailed agent's `config protect-ports` (reading) is still refused by
    bash's broker_check, whose key list is bash's (wave 6). A config that cannot be read: `config`
    says protect-ports cannot be kept there, and every `up` refuses (finding 482). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity5 (the cases with protect-ports are expected differences, finding 480),
    t_unit_config (`config protect-ports ' 8080, 5432'` writes `protect-ports=5432,8080`, and `up`'s
    reader takes that: `--allow 5432` refused).

481. **`config`, `brief`, `reload`, `restart-shell`, `host`, `broker`, `guard` and `setup` in the
    Rust half** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5c). cmd/config.rs (with conf.rs's key table: each key's check,
    default and help; render.rs's gpu_json and gpu_list), cmd/brief.rs (its window list is bash's jq
    program, checked verbatim), cmd/reload.rs, cmd/restart_shell.rs (on ready.rs's wait_ready and
    shell_watch; its 15 s deadline on the monotonic clock, finding 450), cmd/host.rs, cmd/broker.rs,
    cmd/guard.rs (guard.rs builds GUARD_HOOK, GUARD_CODEX_HOOK and GUARD_CODEX byte for byte as bash
    expands them, so share/guard/hook-version's stamps hold; its jq programs and Codex's python run
    verbatim, checked against bin/omabox), cmd/setup.rs (setup's links, the feedback skill, the
    widget and guard offers asked as bash asked them in a terminal, --remove, --aquamarine). Bash's
    functions stay as the fallback. `host` runs its command through host::HostAsked, the one type that
    reaches the user's desktop unsilenced: made only by `host`, whose caller asked for the real
    desktop (S8's exception, explicit in the type where bash's was implicit); everything else of
    omabox's on the host goes through HostSilent. The broker's own policy reading (broker_init: the
    jail's bwrap command line) and refusals (broker_check) stay in bash's front until wave 6; `broker`
    here is the on/off switch and its state. **Change** (Rust over bash, finding 441's rule): `host --
    CMD` and `guard exec -- CMD` whose CMD cannot run say so in omabox's words ("omabox: host: cannot
    run CMD: not found in PATH", "no such file" for a path, "permission denied"), where bash printed
    its own `bin/omabox: line N: exec: CMD: not found`; the exit codes are bash's (127 not there, 126
    cannot run). Tests: t_unit_rust_parity5 (wave 5c's cases both ways on a HOME of the test's own,
    with stand-ins for systemctl, omarchy, omarchy-shell, a Hyprland session for host and failing
    build tools for setup --aquamarine), t_rust_parity_up (brief, reload and restart-shell on a box
    up), and the suite's tests of each command, which now run the Rust half.

482. **Wave 5c's fix round: links, answers and an unreadable config** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 5c).
    Three faults of the Rust half's first port, found in review. **(a)** `config` and `guard` write a
    settings file through a link to its target; a link that cannot be followed (into a folder not
    there yet, a loop) fell back to its own path, and the rename replaced the user's link with a plain
    0600 file, exit 0 (Claude Code's settings.json, Codex's config.toml and hooks.json, omabox's
    config). Bash's `readlink -f` failed there and set -e ended it, exit 1, saying nothing. Now
    refused, exit 1, naming the link and where it leads, the link kept (conf.rs's link_target);
    `guard`'s state says it for that agent. **(b)** setup's [Y/n] questions took " n" as a yes (it
    looked at the first byte) and so enabled the widget or wrote the guard hook against a no; bash's
    `read` takes the blanks off first. Now read as bash does (setup.rs's answer_no). **(c)** S10 failed
    open: a config that is there but cannot be read (mode 000) was read as empty, so `up` started
    connected boxes with nothing protected and `config` showed `protect-ports=`. Now `up` refuses,
    exit 2, as for a bad value ("CONFIG cannot be read (...): no box starts until it can"), and
    `config` says so (net.rs's conf_protect, conf.rs's unreadable). Bash's half, a fallback, still
    reads such a config as none (bash fixes are Rust-only during the port). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity5 (a dangling link and a loop for config and guard, the unreadable config:
    expected differences, finding 482), t_unit_config (up refused on an unreadable config, nothing
    made), t_unit_setup (" n", "n " and a tab before N through script's pty, both halves),
    setup.rs's answers_read_as_bash_reads_them.

490. **The Rust half enters a box natively: setns where bash ran nsenter** (2026-10-24, #324, the
    native-entry step). enter.rs: the child of every command that goes into a box (on_box's tools,
    box_exec's command, gdb's steps, restart-shell's kill) joins the box's namespaces between fork and
    exec with one setns(2) on a pidfd of the box's PID 1, opened by the parent and checked against
    box_pid once it is open (a pid reused meanwhile is never entered). For the box's pid namespace it
    forks once more, as nsenter did: the process left outside (named `omabox-enter`, its command line
    omabox's) closes every fd, waits for the command, stops with it when a stop was asked for (a
    Ctrl-Z, not a stop of the command's own: finding 494), passes HUP, INT, QUIT, TERM, USR1 and USR2
    on to it (a terminal's own only when the command does not share that terminal), and dies of the
    command's death (not dumpable first: never a core of its own), so the caller still sees 128+N.
    With a session of its own (finding 491) there is one more process, in the box: its session's
    leader (`omabox-session`), which passes those signals on to the command's whole process group
    and kills that group when the waiter dies (finding 494). A command that is
    `timeout` (gdb's runs, record's ffmpeg, the other bounded steps of omabox's) gets neither INT nor
    QUIT from it, as its own process group kept them from it under nsenter; a stop's TERM reaches it. The caller's stderr is
    made the command's before the exec: the held pipe (ns_held, #166) carries only the entry's own
    failure, "omabox: cannot enter the box: REASON", and no box process ever holds it (bash's inner
    bash swapped it on its first line, after a box process could open it: t_run_stdio's writer found it
    in each run; now never). on_box runs its tool directly, with its five variables (no `env -i`, no
    `sh -c`). box_cwd's stat is made through /proc/PID/root with openat2's RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, no process
    started. gdb's `--keep-caps` is the entry's (inheritable and ambient, for setpriv to narrow), its
    `timeout` now starts inside the box. A command with a terminal of its own (box_pty) is entered by
    `script` running this binary's `_enter` on its pseudo-terminal (`/proc/PID/exe`, the pidfd passed
    open). `_reap`'s "in use" and `down`'s SIGCONT for a stopped launcher find what entered a box by
    its namespaces (procfs::entered: in the box's user namespace, not in its pid namespace) where they
    read nsenter's command line. Measured on this machine (median of 40): `omabox run -b B -- true`
    35.1 ms before, 24.2 ms after; `omabox hyprctl -b B version` 25.3 ms, 24.5 ms. **Changes** (Rust
    over bash): an entry that fails says so in those words, where nsenter's own line was said
    ("dropped N bytes of other output" now names "the box entry's stderr"); a TERM to the process that
    waits (as `pkill -f 'omabox run'` sends it) reaches the command in the box, where nsenter died and
    the command ran on; `pgrep -f 'omabox run'` finds that process too; `ps` in the box shows
    `omabox-session` above the command. Bash's half keeps nsenter.
    Tests: enter.rs's and exec.rs's unit tests, t_run_stdio (no box process finds the entry's stderr),
    t_agent_session (a run in use waited for by its command, not by nsenter's), the suite's box tests
    of every command that enters a box.

491. **A box command had the caller's terminal as its controlling terminal** (2026-10-24, #324, the
    native-entry step). nsenter started it in the caller's session, so where it had no terminal of its
    own (its output piped, `run -- cmd | less`, `> file` from a terminal), the command and what it left
    running could open /dev/tty: read what was typed there, write to it, or signal its session (the
    first confirmed on the bash half by t_run_stdio's check). **Fix** (Rust
    only): the command runs in a session of its own (setsid after the entry, its leader a process of
    omabox's in the box, finding 494), so /dev/tty is "No such device or address" there, for it and
    for what it leaves; gdb's steps and restart-shell's kill too. The process that waits outside the
    box stays in the caller's session and passes a Ctrl-C, Ctrl-\ and a hang-up on to the command's
    process group, as the terminal did; a Ctrl-Z stops that group (SIGSTOP: the kernel will not stop
    an orphaned process group for SIGTSTP) and the processes of omabox's with it, `fg` continues
    them all. A caller at
    a terminal still gets box_pty (finding 325): the command's controlling terminal is the
    pseudo-terminal `script` holds, never the caller's. What the box can do with that one, kept: type
    into its own input (TIOCSTI), signal its own session, and write to the caller's terminal what any
    program run there writes, escape sequences included (as `cat` of a file would); it reads only what
    is typed while it runs. Tests: t_run_stdio ("what is typed there is not the box's to read", "the
    command is in a session of the box's own", "nor of what it leaves running": each fails with
    OMABOX_BASH=1).

492. **The tools omabox runs in a box's namespaces had the caller's core limit** (2026-10-24, #324,
    the native-entry step). on_box's grim, hyprctl, tail and input tools ran with the caller's core
    limit, unlike box_exec's commands (finding 67), so one crashing from a terminal or the widget
    would have made a crash notification on the desktop. **Fix** (Rust only): they get the 1-byte
    limit too, and so do stdio_relay's commands (gdb's steps, its watching gdb, restart-shell's
    kill: the review's fix round, finding 494). Tests: t_inspect (events -f's tail, started under a
    2-byte limit: 1 byte; 2 with OMABOX_BASH=1), t_gdb (the watching gdb, the same way).

493. **`omabox env` exported a path the box could change** (2026-10-24, #324, the native-entry step).
    It printed `$D/run/wayland-N`, in the box's runtime dir, which the box writes: a box process that
    put a link there in its socket's place led a host tool run after `eval "$(omabox env)"` to
    whatever the link named, the desktop's own compositor included (confirmed on the bash half with
    two boxes, one standing in for the desktop, as t_hostile does).
    **Fix** (Rust over bash): env hard-links the socket into the box dir, which only the host writes,
    and exports that, `$D/wayland`: link(2) never follows a link, and what it made must be a socket,
    so only a socket a box process bound (always the box's own) is ever named there. A run dir whose
    socket is not one is refused ("env: box 'B': its Wayland socket (run/wayland-1) is not a socket:
    refused ..."), exit 1. A path given earlier keeps naming the box's own socket whatever the box
    does to its run dir later. The temporary link is removed after the rename, whatever it did (a
    rename between two links to one inode does nothing: each env after the first left a
    `.wayland.PID` in the box dir until the review's fix round, finding 494). Tests: env.rs's a_link_in_the_sockets_place_is_refused; t_hostile (the
    refusal, and a host grim on the earlier path captures that box's own screen); t_pointer (the path);
    t_unit_rust_parity ("env of a box whose socket is a link now" and the live boxes' env: expected
    differences).

494. **The native entry's signals reached the command, not its children** (2026-10-24, #324, the
    native-entry step's review). With the command in a session of its own (finding 491), the caller's
    group signals and the terminal's no longer reached what it started, and the waiter passed them on
    to the command's pid alone: `run -- sh -c 'sleep 40; echo after' | cat` stopped by a Ctrl-C, or a
    TERM or KILL to `run`'s process group, left `sleep 40` in the box, where bash left nothing. A KILL
    to the waiter killed only the command (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG); a TERM or KILL to omabox alone left the
    waiter and the command running; a command that stopped itself (`kill -STOP $$`) stopped the
    waiter for good, so `run` hung once the box continued it. **Fix**: in the box, the session is led
    by a process of omabox's (`omabox-session`, the keeper), which puts the command in a process group
    of its own and passes each signal the waiter passes it on to that whole group, as the caller's
    group signals reached everything in the caller's group under nsenter; its PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (a
    signal nothing else sends it) kills that group when the waiter dies. The waiter's own is a TERM,
    passed on, when the caller dies. Each stops with its child only for a stop that was asked for (a
    Ctrl-Z), never for the command's own or a tracer's. Both wait without reaping first (waitid's
    WNOWAIT), then block signals and forget the pid before reaping, so nothing is sent to a pid
    another process may have by then. gdb's steps, its watching gdb and restart-shell's kill
    (stdio_relay) get the 1-byte core limit too (finding 492). Tests: t_run_stdio (a terminal's Ctrl-C,
    a group TERM and KILL, a TERM and KILL to omabox alone, each with nothing left in the box; a
    command that stops itself and is continued in the box), t_gdb (the watching gdb's core limit, its
    caller's 2 bytes), env.rs's test (finding 493: a second env leaves no temporary link).

510. **A monitor `up --monitor` or `monitor add` made could be kept at scale 2** (2026-10-24, #379).
    t_monitors_wait_nvidia's box now and then came up with its 1280x720,scale=1.6 monitor at 2 (three
    full suites, once alone; by hand 1 up in 2). The box's Hyprland log has the cause: `output create`
    makes the output before its rule exists (`monitor add` set it only after, through
    omabox_place_monitors()), so Hyprland gives it its hardcoded rule ("No rule found for WAYLAND-2
    ... Using the default hardcoded one": scale 2.00) until the rule applies, a tick after the place's
    eval. On NVIDIA the output is a window on labwc, which starts at aquamarine's default 1280x720, so
    for a 1280x720 SPEC the add's wait (the size asked, any scale) was met in that gap; the place's own
    wait (finding 260) checks positions only, and a monitor right of the main screen is at 1920,0 at
    any scale of its own. The add read scale 2, wrote it to omabox.monitors as "Hyprland made it" (a
    scale may be rounded), and the next place, a reload, every later load set 2 for good. Any SPEC at
    the size an output starts at would do it (a headless output's too). Not Hyprland's fault: an
    output with no rule is meant to take the default one.
    **Fix** (Rust only): `monitor add` evaluates omabox_place_monitors() before `output create` (the
    line is in omabox.monitors already, so the rule is there when the output comes: its first rule
    applied is its own, logged at scale 1.60), and its wait takes the monitor only at its size and
    within 0.2 of the scale asked, as `mode` does (Hyprland rounds a scale to whole pixels, never
    further). One Hyprland makes at another scale is removed and the record put back, saying "did not
    come up as WxH@HZ,scale=S: Hyprland made it ...", exit 1, so `up` fails rather than come up at a
    scale nobody asked for. Checked on the RTX: 12 hand-made ups of the test's box and 10 runs of
    t_monitors_wait_nvidia alone, all at 1.6 (before the fix, 1 up in 2 at 2). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity4 ("its rule there before its output", the stand-in giving an output with no
    rule scale 2 for good; "Hyprland makes it at another scale": expected differences, bash keeps 2),
    t_monitors_wait_nvidia and t_monitors_wait (the monitors' scales and places read from the box,
    besides up's line).

500. **The help in the Rust half** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front, A1). bin/omabox's usage_text is
    crates/omabox/src/help.txt (`$PASS_KEY` expanded; t_unit_rust_front checks it is usage_text's
    bytes), compiled in; help.rs cuts it as bash's usage and usage_form did (bare `help`, `--long`,
    `help CMD`, the `@` and `@short` paragraphs, run with up's lines). `help`, `-h` and `--help` are
    in RUST_CMDS, and bash's `CMD --help` hands `help CMD` over; a `--help` after other words in the
    Rust half's commands prints it in-process (lua, log, events, setup and config went back to bash
    for it, the rest ran `omabox help CMD`); opt_form reads the command's lines from it, where a
    table of them was copied by hand. Until the flip bash keeps its own copy of the text (a jail's
    `bin/omabox` is mapped alone, with no help.txt beside it). **Change** (Rust over bash): a word
    is taken as written; bash gave it to `awk -v`, which reads escapes, so `help 'u\160'` printed
    up's help where it is now an unknown command (CHANGELOG). Tests: t_unit_rust_front (help, help
    CMD and help CMD --long for every command and alias, CMD --help for each, after -b, mid-argument;
    the escape an expected difference), help.rs's every_command_has_help.

501. **The front in the Rust half, and the build at build/omabox** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front, A2).
    A call that comes to the binary straight (no OMABOX_ROOT: build/omabox now, bin/omabox once it is
    the binary) runs front.rs, bash's main up to its dispatch: global_box (`-b NAME` before the
    command moved after it; not-one-box commands and unknown ones said in bash's words), eq_split
    over args.rs's cmd_opts, now every command's (t_unit_rust_front compares it with CMD_OPTS; up's
    was missing, so the Rust half's `up --sizee` named no nearest option, a wave 5a slip fixed here),
    the guard's mark, run's 125, `CMD --help`; bash's hand-off still passes shaped words, which skip
    it. The binary moved from `build/bin/omabox` to `build/omabox` (install.sh, the suite,
    bin/omabox's RUST; kill_reapers takes either, a reaper of a box started before the move
    included), and `root()` is the parent of the binary's own folder, found once at the start (D1).
    `back_to_bash` runs only for a call bash handed over and never to this binary itself: with
    bin/omabox this binary (a copy, or the flip's link), a word it lacks is one line, exit 126, not
    an exec loop. Parity runs three legs (bash, the hand-off, direct); a parity test whose binary is
    missing fails in a checkout and skips only in an install. **Change** (Rust over bash): with
    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset or empty the direct front says "omabox: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not set" (exit
    1, as before), where bash said "bin/omabox: line 13: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: ..." (CHANGELOG). Tests:
    t_unit_rust_front (the front's cases, three legs; the empty XDG_RUNTIME_DIR an expected
    difference on the direct leg), t_unit_rust_handoff (exit 126 from a copy and from a link, under
    timeout), front.rs's and ready.rs's unit tests.

502. **The broker's side in the Rust half** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front, A3; #373, #374). A call
    the broker's relay runs on the binary straight (OMABOX_BROKER_PEER set) goes through
    broker_side.rs before anything runs: broker_init (the caller made sure of by its pidfd, the walk
    up to a bwrap whose parent is ai-jail, the jail's policy from that bwrap's command line and
    ai-jail's `--args` memfd, its mounts through the jail's init, OMABOX_JAIL set for what it starts)
    and broker_check, in bash's words and codes (1, run's 125). It runs before every command, the
    internal `_` ones included: the binary's main had dispatched those with no check (rev m6); every
    one is now refused through the broker. A call bash hands over has had bash's. **Changes**: a
    jailed `config protect-ports` is refused saying why ("protect-ports is not for a jailed agent
    ..."), where bash's key list made it "a jailed agent does not change omabox's settings" (#373),
    and a jailed caller's bare `config` and `config --json` leave protect-ports out (both halves:
    config is the Rust half's), since which host ports are protected tells an agent where the
    user's services are (#374, S10); neither was listed for a jailed caller by bash, whose CONF_KEYS
    lacks the key. Tests: t_unit_rust_front (a stand-in jail, a copy of bash named ai-jail starting a
    real bwrap, calling a broker of each leg through omabox-relay: allowed and refused commands, every
    `_` word, config's reads, a caller in no jail, a jail without the network, a caller gone; the
    protect-ports refusal an expected difference on the direct leg), t_unit_jail_policy (each policy
    and mounts fixture read both ways through `_rust-jail`), broker_side.rs's unit tests, t_jail (the
    real ai-jail, its broker running the binary straight). The native entry's `_enter` (finding 490)
    was dispatched before the front, so a broker running the binary straight ran a caller's `_enter`
    unchecked (found in review, never released: the broker unit still runs bash's front); it is now
    taken first only when no broker caller is set, and `_enter` joined the refused words' cases.

503. **A jailed caller's omabox in the Rust half, its values off the relay's command line** (2026-10-24,
    #324 wave 6-front, A4). Called straight inside ai-jail (no user namespace there, the broker's
    socket in reach: relay_wanted), the binary hands its command to the broker as bash's relay_call
    did (relay.rs): the default box and PATH as entries, paths made absolute, `run --env-file` read in
    the jail, shot's and record's files made beside where they go and filled through fds, `--in`'s
    shot opened and passed, `record -- ACTION` and `--for` run from the jail, each step through
    bin/omabox. **Change** (Rust over bash): bash put each `--pass` and `--env-file` value on
    omabox-relay's command line (`--env PASS_NAME=VALUE`), against finding 66's rule that a value is
    never on a command line; the binary hands them over on an fd instead, a memfd the relay reads and closes
    (`omabox-relay call --env-fd N`, NUL-ended NAME=VALUE entries, added to the relay; `--env` stays
    for the entries that are not the caller's values). What reaches the broker is the same. A jail
    started before an upgrade keeps its old relay and must be restarted (the clean break's release
    notes). Tests: t_unit_rust_jailed (a stand-in unshare that fails, the real relay against a
    stand-in broker on the direct leg, and omabox alone in a HOME's .local/bin as ai-jail maps it,
    bash's file and the binary, with a recording relay: the words, the files passed, what --env-fd
    holds; the values an expected difference: on bash's relay command line, on an fd in the
    binary's), t_jail_recipe (a real ai-jail with exactly the recipe's four maps, the binary in
    bin/omabox's place: up, run --pass, shot, a usage error, a refusal, down).

504. **The version built in, and a host child's environment** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front, A5). The
    binary's `--version`, `version --json` and check's report give the VERSION it was built from
    (`include_str!`), the same bytes as the file while binary and tree agree, and the truth for a
    build older than its tree (a pull without ./install.sh), where reading the file said the pulled
    tree's. Self-spawns stay `root()/bin/omabox` (the reaper's command line, run's throwaway up, a
    jailed record's steps; D4). **Change** (Q4, not contract): a host command omabox runs (guard
    exec, host, a check scenario, labwc) gets the caller's SHLVL and `_` as they came; bash's gave
    it its own (SHLVL as it came for an exec'd one, no `_`; SHLVL+1 and `_` the command's path for
    a child). Tests: t_unit_rust_front ("a host child's SHLVL and _", an expected difference on the
    direct leg), t_unit_rust_handoff (a build in a tree whose VERSION differs says its own).

505. **The suite calls the binary straight** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front, A7). test/run.sh's CLI is
    build/omabox, the binary the suite builds (tools_ready), called as users will call it once
    bin/omabox is it: its own front, no hand-off, nested boxes and the jailed caller in t_jail too.
    BASH_CLI is bash's bin/omabox, for parity's bash leg, `lib` (the functions sourced from its text),
    the fixtures a parity case makes with bash's half (`obb`) and the tests of bash itself (its
    hand-off, its text, a live edit). Parity compares two legs, bash and the binary; the hand-off leg
    (A2's third) runs only with RP_LEGS="rust direct". Under --installed there is no binary: CLI is the
    install's bin/omabox, every command in bash, as before. Tests: the unit tier and the box tests run
    this way.

506. **An up right after a down of the same name was cancelled** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front,
    found by A7). A down that finds no box leaves a `.down-NAME` marker with its start in clock ticks
    (10 ms), and an up cancels when that start is at or after its own (finding 147). From the binary
    a down takes a few ms, so `omabox down B; omabox up B` started both in one tick, and the up said
    "cancelled: omabox down B came while it was starting" every time (3 in 3; through bash's hand-off
    the down took ~50 ms and the tie was rare). **Fix** (the Rust half; bash's up keeps `dt >= t0`): in
    a tie the up cancels only when the marker was written after it was called (its mtime against
    CALL_US): a down already over when the up began is not one that came during it. Tests:
    t_rust_parity_up (down then up at once from the binary, three times, none cancelled; three in three
    were before), up.rs's a_down_over_before_the_up_is_not_one_that_came.
    Amended by finding 513: the tie is decided by pid order now; the mtime rule is kept for bash's
    markers.

511. **The keeper showed the caller's whole call in the box** (2026-10-24, #324, found by the suite at
    27d9613: t_keys_down_up's "the holder is gone with the last held key", failing alone too since the
    native entry, 74b5754). The session's leader in the box (`omabox-session`, finding 494) is a fork
    of omabox, so its command line was omabox's own, the box command's words in it: `omabox run -b B
    -- pgrep -f WORD` always found it by WORD, and `run -- pkill -f WORD` signalled it (its TERM passed
    on to the command's group). The check found the keeper of its own `run` (pid 153 of the two it
    printed; the other, 146, was finding 512's holder). Under nsenter the process that waited stayed
    outside the box's pid namespace. **Fix** (Rust): the keeper blanks its command line in its own
    memory (/proc/self/stat's arg_start..arg_end, read before the fork) to its name: `ps` in the box
    shows `omabox-session` alone, and nothing in the box has the call's words. The waiter outside
    keeps omabox's (`pgrep -f 'omabox run ...'` on the host, as finding 490 says). Tests: t_run_stdio
    ("run -- pgrep -f WORD: nothing in the box has the words of run's own call", fails at 27d9613;
    "the session's leader shows its name alone"), t_keys_down_up.

512. **`keys up:KEY` of the last held key returned before its holder was gone** (2026-10-24, #324,
    the same check as finding 511). The holder answered "ok", closed the connection, then let go of
    its virtual keyboard (30 ms for the compositor to take the last release, and a roundtrip) and
    exited: a `pgrep` from the host right after `keys up` found it in 3 runs of 3, and a check through
    the binary (some 25 ms, where bash's `run` took longer than the holder) found it in the suite.
    **Fix** (tools/keyboard, both halves): the holder keeps the connection of the request that let go
    of the last key open until it exits, and the caller reads to its end, so `keys up` returns once
    the holder and its keyboard are gone (about 70 ms on this machine). Test: t_keys_down_up ("the
    holder is gone with the last held key").

513. **`up B & down B` left the box up** (2026-10-24, #324, #380; t_race at 27d9613, "a down while its
    up starts", 14 runs in 15 on an idle machine). Finding 506's tie rule (a down's marker in the up's
    10 ms tick counts only when written after the up was called) compared the marker's mtime with the
    up's CALL_US, taken at its first line: an up started through `&` reached that line 0.7-1.9 ms after
    a whole down (about 1 ms from the binary) had written its marker, so every such down read as one
    over before the up began. Comparing the two calls' times (#380's proposal) has the same fault: the
    down's call came first in each of those runs too. **Fix** (Rust): the down writes, after its start,
    the pid its pid namespace made last as it writes the marker (/proc/loadavg's last field), that
    namespace and its CALL_US (`TICKS LASTPID pid:[NS] CALL_US`). In a tie, the up cancels when its own
    pid was made by then (at or below LASTPID, round pid_max), in the same namespace: the order the
    kernel made them in, whatever either process's clock read later. `down B; up B` from the binary
    still starts the box (its up is made after the marker); a down of another pid namespace (the
    user's, for a jailed up) is compared by the calls' times, like with like; a bash down's marker
    (its start alone) by its mtime, as finding 506. Measured: `up B & down B` 15 cancels in 15, `down
    B; up B` 0 in 8. **Changes**: a Rust down's marker has three more fields on its line, so bash's up
    (OMABOX_BASH=1), which takes only a lone number, no longer cancels for one (a fallback's up with
    the binary's down); t_unit_rust_parity5 masks the marker's line to compare the halves' downs.
    Tests: t_race (fails at 27d9613), t_rust_parity_up (finding 506's), up.rs's
    a_down_still_going_when_the_up_began_came and down_lines.

514. **`run --pass` of a variable the binary takes out of its own environment said it was not set**
    (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front; t_clip's "refused to an agent" at 27d9613, alone 2 in 2). Called
    straight, main takes OMABOX_BASH (and the hand-off's OMABOX_ROOT, OMABOX_CALL_US,
    OMABOX_ENVIRON_FD) out of the process's environment, and caller_env, with no environment handed
    over by bash, read that one: `OMABOX_BASH=1 omabox run --pass OMABOX_BASH -- ...` exited 125, "not
    in this command's environment". t_clip's parity wraps each leg in such a `run` (the leg's
    OMABOX_BASH passed into its stand-in host), so both legs failed alike and the expected difference
    (finding 441) was not there. **Fix** (Rust): caller_env reads /proc/self/environ, the environment
    as the call came, as bash's reads /proc/$$/environ (finding 74). With that, t_clip's direct leg
    (finding 505), which sets no OMABOX_BASH, had its --pass refused (125) while the bash leg ran: at
    27d9613 every leg was refused alike, so its seven other parity cases compared nothing. Its wrap now
    passes OMABOX_BASH only where the leg sets it (RP_IN_BOX), and so does t_monitors_window's, whose
    four interactive parity cases failed the same way at 8d9069e. Tests: t_clip, t_monitors_window,
    t_run_stdio ("run --pass
    OMABOX_BASH: the caller's value", fails at 27d9613).

515. **Two box tests leaned on the bash front's pace** (2026-10-24, #324 wave 6-front; the suite at
    27d9613, each alone 2 in 2). With the suite calling the binary straight (finding 505), commands
    follow each other some 20-50 ms sooner. t_no_pointer and t_no_pointer_nvidia: `run -- pkill -x
    foot` returns as foot gets its TERM; foot exits 230 (not 143) a moment later, and the next box
    command says that early end of a `run -d` job (finding 406 leaves out only 130, 137 and 143). It was
    the discarded `pointer show`; now it is the `lua` whose 2>&1 the check reads, which got the warning
    above its "false". Both halves exit 230 and warn alike. The test now ends its terminals with a
    KILL (137, not said). t_pointer: a finger scroll that comes within some 0.3 s of a wheel's notches
    gets Qt's scroll begin (0 0 1) twice before its updates (6 in 6 on Qt 6.12; none 0.3 s later, none
    between two finger scrolls): Qt's own, a touchpad's phases still. The check takes leading begins.

516. **A click on a window moved while its workspace was hidden could lose the focus to the window
    under it** (2026-10-24, #324; t_window's "click --in a window shot after the window moved" in the
    suite at 8d9069e and alone, then at 27d9613 too: 7 runs in 7 with another suite loading the
    machine, where 27d9613's own suite had passed it). win_raise's focus on C (floating, moved to
    700,300 on workspace 1 while 7 was shown) switched the workspace and warped the pointer to C's
    centre, 900,450; 3 ms later A, the tiled window C had been over, was active (the box's events:
    `activewindow>>foot,A`, `foot,C`, `foot,A`), and the click said C "did not take focus in 3 s".
    Hyprland's follow-the-mouse focus took the window under the warped pointer by where the windows
    were drawn, C not yet drawn at its new place. **Fix** (Rust): while another window is active,
    win_raise focuses its window again, a quarter second apart, within its 3 s; by then the pointer is
    over it and the focus stays. Bash's win_raise focuses once. Tests: t_window (2 in 2 after).
    Amended by finding 518: only a focus it had and lost is given again.

517. **t_monitors_turned_nvidia compared a burst with a shot while the screen still changed**
    (2026-10-24, #324; "shot --burst --no-pointer: a frame is the shot's image", alone 2 in 2 at
    8d9069e and after, AE 85-116 where 50 passes, though every suite before had passed it). The
    images differed by one level in 41136 pixels, all on the turned monitors, and the burst's first
    frame by more (AE 1432): the tail of a fade, the clicks just before having moved the focus between
    terminals there. The comparison wants a still screen and did not wait for one; the bash front's
    pace had let the fade end. The test waits for the screen to be still before its bursts.

518. **Finding 516's win_raise focused any window again for 3 s** (2026-10-25, #324; the suite at
    e37f275: t_unit_rust_parity's "keys --window: a window that does not take focus (3 s)", whose
    stand-in Hyprland never makes it active, saw four focus dispatches from the binary where bash sends
    one). The loop gave the focus again whenever another window was active, so a window that never
    takes the focus was asked over and over, and a focus change it had not made (an app's, the user's)
    would have been undone while it waited. **Fix** (Rust): it is focused again only when it had the
    focus and lost it, as Hyprland's history says (its focusHistoryID is 1: the window focused just
    before the active one), a quarter second after the last focus, until the 3 s are up; once it is
    active win_raise returns. One focus again 8 ms after the steal was not enough (t_window lost it
    again 2 runs in 4: `activewindow>>foot,C`, `foot,A` twice); a quarter second on it stays (5 in 5).
    A window that never has it is focused once and fails after 3 s, as by bash. Tests:
    t_unit_rust_parity (that case again the same both ways), t_window.

519. **`monitor remove` on an interactive box returned before its screens' new scales** (2026-10-25,
    #382; t_monitors_window's parity "monitor remove, interactive (both ways): the main window tiled
    again", once in the suite at 3b3cf52 and 1 alone in 2, the binary's side reading WAYLAND-1 at
    0.825 where it is 1 with no views left). The remove places the monitors (finding 260's wait
    covers their places) and returns; Hyprland takes the main screen's new scale a while later, and
    the main window, tiled again, resizes on the host after that. Both halves did so; bash's slower
    return hid it. **Fix** (Rust): an interactive box's remove waits, 5 s at most, until each screen
    is at the scale its config gives it (omabox_monitor_scales() in share/hyprland.lua: the main
    screen 1 with no views, else each view's from its window's size, as omabox_place_monitors sets
    them), saying so if the time runs out; a box started by an older omabox has no such function and
    is not waited for. Bash's remove does not wait. Tests: t_monitors_window ("the main screen at
    scale 1 as the remove returns", read at once, the binary only), mon.rs's scale_rows_read,
    t_unit_rust_parity4 ("monitor remove: interactive, the picture laid out again": the stand-in
    answers omabox_monitor_scales() with its monitors' own scales; its log's one more eval is an
    expected difference).

520. **The binary's `check run` read every hole of a checkpoint as new** (2026-10-25, #324 wave
    6-suite; found moving t_unit_check's two check_new_holes cases to a `#[test]`, which failed on
    the first). check_new_holes split each baseline hole (`X,Y WxH N`) at blanks before matching it,
    reading bash's `${old[@]+"${old[@]}"}` as unquoted; no word alone is a region, so no baseline
    hole ever matched, and a checkpoint whose holes were all approved (finding 362: a check fails only
    on new ones) failed under the binary where bash passed it. **Fix** (Rust): each baseline hole is
    matched whole, as bash does. Tests: check.rs new_holes_as_bash (a hole overlapping the
    baseline's is not new; against a baseline from before holes all are).

521. **Three of the suite's checks read bash's text only, and the binary's side was unchecked**
    (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip, from the review of wave 6-suite; #368). Finding 345's fds scan and
    finding 289's on_box kill scan read bin/omabox; the binary had no equivalent, and after the flip
    they would read a test-only copy. The reaper's passthrough check (`< 5`, reap.rs) was tied to
    nothing: a bump of share/passthrough.lua's VERSION would have left it behind. And t_jail_record's
    live case of a box file swapped for a FIFO went with the suite's `lib`, while SECURITY.md's S7
    still named it. **Fix:** finding 345 holds by construction in the binary: exec.rs's `command`
    closes every fd a child is not given whenever its entry takes the box's pid namespace
    (`Plan::pid_ns`), whatever the caller asked (every caller already did: no behaviour changes), and
    t_unit_ns_fds' crate scan holds that entries are applied only there and setns only in enter.rs.
    t_unit_on_box_kill scans the crate's on_box, on_box_io, on_box_bg and TOOL entries for a kill,
    pkill or killall in their function's strings. reap.rs reads the version from passthrough.lua at
    build time (`include_bytes!`; Closes #368). record_stop.rs's box_copy takes how it runs its stat
    and cat (`box_copy_with`), and an `#[ignore]` test runs both on the host against a FIFO with no
    writer: back in its 10 s, nothing copied. The suite also hardened aq_up_gate: its down marker is
    there for a refusal too, so an up that should have refused stops at its lock.

522. **install.sh ran omabox before building it, and wrote the binary in place** (2026-10-25, #324
    wave 6-flip, proposal D2). Its aquamarine step ran `bin/omabox setup --aquamarine` before the
    tools and `build/omabox` were built, and `install -D` wrote `build/omabox` under its own name, so
    a caller could exec a half-written file; a cargo with no toolchain (rustup's) failed in cargo's
    words mid-build. Harmless while bash was the entry; not once `bin/omabox` is the binary. **Fix:**
    install.sh checks `cargo --version` first (a rustup with no default toolchain is told
    `rustup default stable`), builds the tools, then the binary into `build/omabox.new` and renames
    it over `build/omabox`, and only then runs `setup --aquamarine` and `setup`; the suite's own
    build renames too. release.sh builds the tarball as a package does before it writes the
    checksum (a fresh extract, `cargo fetch --locked` into a CARGO_HOME of its own, `cargo build
    --frozen` with no network, the binary's `--version` the tag's): a tag that cannot build offline
    is never uploaded. CI adds `cargo build --release --locked`. `test/run.sh --installed` puts the
    binary where the package's recipe would, by the tree's shape (a `bin/omabox` linking to
    `../build/omabox`: the binary there; a bash one: none). Tests: t_unit_install (a stand-in cargo;
    a cargo that cannot build; tools before any omabox run; `build/omabox.new` then a rename).

523. **The switch: `bin/omabox` is the binary** (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip; proposal D1, D2, D5,
    the verdict's clean break). `bin/omabox` is a tracked link to `../build/omabox`, the binary
    install.sh and the suite build from `crates/omabox` (renamed into place, finding 522); bash's
    16,000 lines moved to `test/oracle/omabox.bash` (`git log --follow -B -C` finds its history;
    export-ignored: never in a tarball or package). Every path written into a HOME names `$ROOT/bin/omabox` and keeps
    working: `~/.local/bin/omabox`, ai-jail's map (bwrap binds the link's target: the binary, alone,
    its ROOT `~/.local`), the broker unit's `listen -- $ROOT/bin/omabox`, the guard hook's `-x` test
    and its stamp. The binary's ROOT is the parent of the directory it really is in (a checkout's
    `build/`, a package's `/usr/lib/omabox/bin/`, a jail's `~/.local/bin/`); its self-spawns stay
    `ROOT/bin/omabox` (after a rebuild, `/proc/self/exe` is "(deleted)"). What went from the binary:
    the hand-off (bash's shaped words, `OMABOX_ROOT`, `OMABOX_CALL_US`, `OMABOX_ENVIRON_FD`,
    `back_to_bash`, the `_rust` hand-off probe; `_rust probe` and `_rust-jq` stay): a caller's values
    of those names now pass through as in 1.0, and `run --pass` reads `/proc/self/environ`. The
    reaper's command line is now `ROOT/bin/omabox _reap NAME CREATED` with no `bash` before it, which
    `down`'s match did not take (it wanted `bash ` before `ROOT/bin/omabox`): it does now, or a down
    would have left the reaper of every box started after the switch until it saw its box gone.
    The suite runs bin/omabox as users do (`CLI`, through the link); parity's bash leg runs a copy of
    the oracle made for the run in the checkout's `build/oracle/` (inside the repo, so a stand-in box
    running each leg's omabox sees it; its error lines still say `.../bin/omabox: line N:`), its ROOT
    set to the checkout, its hand-off cut, and its down's reaper match taking the binary's reaper as it
    took the hand-off's (without that, bash's down of a box up left its reaper: t_rust_parity_up), until
    wave 6b ends; an install has no oracle, so parity skips there. Six `#[test]`s that read bash's text read the oracle and are `#[ignore]`d (a
    tarball has none; `t_unit_rust_ignored` runs them). Not built yet (a fresh clone, a new worktree, a
    pull without `./install.sh`), `bin/omabox` dangles: the shell's "No such file or directory", new
    agent sessions unguarded, ai-jail with omabox's maps not starting: the release notes' first lines.
    Tests: t_unit_layout (the link; ROOT through `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and alone; VERSION compiled
    in; the dangling link; the front's unknown command), ready.rs's reapers_by_their_command_line,
    t_unit_install, t_jail and t_jail_recipe with bin/omabox mapped as users map it. Deleted:
    t_unit_rust_handoff (the hand-off), t_unit_live_edit (finding 66 was bash reading its script as it
    ran; its successor is finding 522's rename), t_unit_cli's `$(save_dir)` grep (a bash `set -e`
    property, finding 163), and bash's NS_FDS and ON_BOX_KILLS scans (finding 521 has the crate's).

524. **CI on the port never passed, and `down` left a read-only box HOME on coreutils before 9.5**
    (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip's fix round). Since CI ran on `port-rust`, its `cargo test` failed
    on two tests. **(a)** rm_tree's `chmod -R -P u+rwX` (finding 374): chmod has `-P` only since
    coreutils 9.5 (2024); 9.4 (Ubuntu 24.04, the CI runner's) refuses the whole command, `invalid
    option -- 'P'`, unheard (its stderr goes nowhere), so nothing was made writable and `rm -rf`
    could not empty a read-only folder an app made in a box HOME: finding 374 undone, and `down`
    said rm's complaint, on any system with an older chmod (Arch has 9.12, so never seen here).
    **Fix:** `chmod -R u+rwX` without `-P`. No chmod follows a link it meets inside the tree; one
    named on its command line it does (`-H`, the default), so a path that is itself a link is left out
    of the chmod, and `rm -rf` removes the link alone (sweep_homes already skipped links in the
    cache). Tests: ready.rs's rm_tree_as_bash with a stand-in chmod that refuses `-P` (the old code
    fails it with CI's very line) and a box whose HOME is a link (the link goes, what it points to
    keeps its modes). **(b)** install.rs's audio_list_as_bash asserted the missing audio programs had
    no space between them, where audio_packages joins them with ", " (finding 462): it failed on any
    machine missing two or more of pipewire, wireplumber, pipewire-pulse and pactl. It now checks the
    list's shape (known names, in order, each once, ", " between). **(c)** A package's `check()`
    runs `cargo test --frozen` in a clean chroot: with only the recipe's depends on PATH, eight tests
    that run a host tool omabox runs failed (tar, grep, awk: seed's copies and secret scan, record's
    size cap, egl_render). Each now asks `exec::tools_or_skip` first and skips, naming the missing
    tool on stderr (`-- --nocapture` shows it). With PATH cut to the binaries of the recipe's depends
    plus cargo and gcc, `cargo test --frozen` passes. **(d)** ci.yml ran the release build after the
    tests, so a failing test hid whether the release built: fmt, clippy, the release build and the
    tests are now steps of their own, in that order.

525. **install.sh installed a stale binary when cargo's target dir was elsewhere** (2026-10-25, #324
    wave 6-flip's fix round). install.sh and the suite's tools_ready ran `cargo build --release` and
    copied `ROOT/target/release/omabox`, but a user's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or `build.target-dir` in
    `~/.cargo/config.toml`, puts the build elsewhere: install.sh then died after a good build (no
    file there) or, with one left from an earlier build, installed that stale binary without a word.
    **Fix:** both builds run with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=ROOT/target` (the variable wins over cargo's
    config). Tests: t_unit_install (its stand-in cargo honours CARGO_TARGET_DIR as cargo does; a
    stale `target/release/omabox` and a user's CARGO_TARGET_DIR: build/omabox is the new build and
    the user's target dir is never made; the old install.sh fails all three checks).

526. **The help and SECURITY.md still described a bash half** (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip's fix
    round). `omabox help config --long` (and `help up --long`, `help --long`) ended its
    protect-ports paragraph with "The Rust half's alone: under OMABOX_BASH=1 it is an unknown key",
    and SECURITY.md's S10 said "the bash half (`OMABOX_BASH=1`) starts no connected box while it is
    set": the shipped binary has no bash half and reads no OMABOX_BASH. Both sentences are gone. The
    oracle keeps its text (it is not maintained), so t_unit_rust_front's four help cases that show
    the paragraph are expected differences (finding 526) and its help.txt check compares the
    oracle's usage text with that sentence taken out. The suite's copy of the oracle also took its
    ROOT from the suite's logical path, where the binary's is the parent of where it really is: run
    from a checkout reached through a link, `version` and `--version` cases differed between the
    legs. It is now `readlink -f` of the checkout (through a link, t_unit_rust_front passes; the old
    copy failed three cases).

527. **A crash's "went down" came before the box was down** (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip; the first
    `--installed` full suite with the binary). A call that found the box's Hyprland gone with labwc's
    line saying how (`omabox lua` of a crash) said "went down: its Hyprland crashed (SIGSEGV)" at
    once, while the box's PID 1 still lived for a few ms (session.sh's `kill -KILL -1`, then its
    exit). A call made at once after it found the box alive and so half torn down: "went down" again
    (t_hyprland_crash's "a later call: dead, and why": every time from an install, and alone from a
    checkout too, though two full checkout runs passed it), or, with its processes already gone,
    "did not answer (hung?)" (seen from a checkout by hand). **Fix:**
    hypr_lost, on labwc's line, gives the box's PID 1 up to 1 s to go before it says so; the next
    call then says "is dead: its Hyprland crashed (SIGSEGV)", as ls does. Tests:
    `hypr_lost_waits_for_the_box_to_end` (said once PID 1 has gone; still said, after 1 s, for one
    that stays); t_hyprland_crash from an install (failed alone before, twice).

528. **A box's copy of the config kept share/'s mode** (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6-flip; the same run).
    start-hyprland.sh made the box's `omabox-hyprland.lua` with `cp`, which keeps the source's mode:
    from a read-only install (the suite's `--installed` tree is 0444; a store-like package would be
    too) the copy was 0444, and a write to it in the box was refused, so t_autoreload's change never
    reached Hyprland. `omabox reload` already wrote it with `cat` (the umask's mode). **Fix:** up
    writes it the same way. Tests: t_autoreload's new "the box's copy of the config is its to
    change", and its reload checks, from an install (failed before).

529. **Three of the suite's checks assumed a checkout, or no OMABOX_RENDER_NODE** (2026-10-25, #324
    wave 6-flip; the same run). (a) t_unit_gpu's "config gpu lists the GPUs on stderr" matched the
    list's header at the start, but a run with OMABOX_RENDER_NODE set (an install's run here must
    name the iGPU: it has no patched aquamarine for the NVIDIA card) gets the "overrides the
    setting" note first, as it should: the check clears the variable, and a new one checks the note
    comes first when it is set. (b) t_rust_parity's "its log has the header" read the gdb.log of a
    parity case an install skips (no oracle): it is skipped with it there; t_gdb checks the header
    from an install. (c) The `--installed` floor, 4255, was an estimate made before any such run:
    it is now 3810, about 90% of the 4238 checks of the first full run with the binary (with the
    fixes of findings 527-528; the checkout's floor is 90% of its own count too).

530. **6b: the contract decisions are the binary's, each held on it alone** (2026-10-25, #324 wave
    6b; LOG's "Contract decisions" of 2026-10-22, the design's Q4). The five decisions landed before
    6b, in wave 4c and 5b: numbers with zeros in front decimal (finding 448), box names ASCII (445),
    lists in byte order, `ls` and `saves` too (446, 470), JSON numbers in standard form (449), and
    `check run SCENARIO` a program, never a builtin or one of omabox's functions (451: documented,
    the Rust half never ran one). Each has its CHANGELOG line under "Changes from the bash omabox"
    (what it was, what it is, what a script changes); check run's now also says what a name of no
    program gets: "cannot run scenario NAME: not found in PATH" in the run's log, status 127,
    `check run` 3. What held them in the suite were parity's expected differences, which go with
    the oracle (finding 531), so each now rests on the binary alone: numbers on shell.rs's
    numbers_are_decimal (and shot.rs's, settle.rs's), and the live box's `check point --ignore 08`;
    names on shell.rs's own_patterns_ascii_in_any_locale and t_unit_bash_changes (`path -b é` under
    C and en_US.UTF-8); lists on the new shell.rs globs_in_byte_order, ready.rs's
    new_reports_in_byte_order and t_unit_bash_changes (`saves`, table and `--json`, in both
    locales); JSON on json.rs's numbers_in_standard_form and the live box's `lua --json`; check run on
    the new check.rs a_scenario_is_a_program_whatever_its_name (`say`, `shopt` and `true` with no
    program in PATH: 127, said; `true` and `false` in /usr/bin run) and the live box's `say` case (the
    live box's cases each stated, no longer compared, in 6b-end: finding 531). The
    bash-shaped artefacts the design left to 6b were gone before it: `clip` names its process
    omabox (finding 441), trap's int_as_bash and sig::subst went with the signal rework (findings
    452-454), the nsenter lines with native entry (finding 490); `git grep -n
    'int_as_bash\|sig::subst\|fn subst' crates/` finds nothing, and clip.rs says `bash` only in a
    comment. A host child's `SHLVL` and `_` (Q4: not contract) have their CHANGELOG line (finding
    504).

531. **6b-end: the port is complete, and bash's omabox is gone** (2026-10-25, #324 wave 6b-end;
    the design's D5 and Q2). Until now the suite kept bash's omabox as it was at the switch
    (`test/oracle/omabox.bash`, 16,086 lines, export-ignored) and compared the binary with it,
    case by case. That ends here, in three steps:
    - First the live box's parity, whose checks no box test made, became plain assertions
      (`cx_case`: the case's fixture as parity had it, then what it must give, FIELD=TEXT, FIELD~ERE
      or FIELD!~ERE over rc, out, err and state). t_rust_parity is t_cli_box (170 cases, each kept);
      t_rust_parity_up is t_cli_up (31); t_ports' two and t_audio's two are stated, the rest of
      t_audio's, t_clip's 8 and t_monitors_window's 4 were their tests' own checks already (one table
      check added there; the agent refusal now names omabox's comm). t_cli_box's monitor cases
