      follow the box's screen and first monitor (HEADLESS-2/3 headless, WAYLAND-1/2 on NVIDIA), so
      `monitor remove` and `output drop` act on both, where they were refusals on NVIDIA; checked on
      both render nodes. Found doing it: t_rust_parity_up's `saves rm` made its save in the user's
      real data dir and compared two refusals (it removes its own now), and `check point -g
      "010,010 400x300"` writes `of region 010,010` in its .point as typed, where shot writes regions
      as read (finding 448): left as it is, not a 6b decision.
    - Then the oracle went: the file and its .gitattributes line, its copy into build/oracle with
      the ROOT, RUST= and reaper edits, BASH_CLI and obb, `lib` (which sourced it) and its sed copy,
      parity() with its bash leg, rp_differs and the expected differences, rust_built, RP_IN_BOX,
      the crate's six #[ignore] tests that read it (each module's inline jq "as bash's",
      jail_verify.py's), gen_recprog.py (recprog.rs is now kept by hand) and t_unit_jail_policy's and
      t_unit_setup's bash halves (each now the binary's answer alone). `_rust-jq --inline` and
      `--recprog` stayed, internal, with no reader (gone in finding 532); `_rust-opts` is
      t_unit_cli_opts'.
    - Then the unit tier's parity tests retired (Q2): t_unit_rust_parity, _parity5, _parity4b and
      _front deleted, some 1,400 cases that each compared a call with bash's; what they held rests
      on each command's own unit and box tests and the crate's #[test]s, which waves 2-6 moved off
      `lib`, but for some cases that held a property alone, found by a review after it and put back
      single-sided in finding 532. Kept, single-sided, where nothing else held the property:
      t_unit_jailed_caller (was t_unit_rust_jailed: every relayed call stated, a value on --env-fd
      and never on the relay's command line, finding 503; S9), t_unit_broker_side (the front's A3
      block: what a jailed caller is let through or refused, every `_` word refused, finding 502;
      S9), t_unit_monitor_add_window (parity4's stand-ins and its cases of an interactive box's
      monitor add: under signals at each step, a slow, late, refusing or busy box, two at once,
      findings 429, 437, 453; gpu's and cpu's temporary dir under a signal, and an INT to omabox
      alone, finding 454; its other ~200 cases went, among them the add's refusals and rollbacks and
      mode's, which finding 532 puts back), t_unit_cli_opts (args.rs's table checked against each
      command's help, where it was checked against bash's CMD_OPTS; help.txt's @ lines never shown)
      and t_unit_bash_changes (finding 530).
    The unit tier goes from 4,061 checks in 29 min 19 s (the four parity tests 27 min of it) to
    2,187 in 3 min 20 s (--installed: 2,127, the same 10 failures as before, #381 and #337); floors
    reset to about 90%: 1960 unit and 4660 full (an estimate from the last full count, 7055, less
    the cases that went), --installed 1910 and 4190. cargo test: 257 and 15 ignored (+3 #[test]s
    in 6b and here, -6 #[ignore]d that read the oracle). The full suite was not run here.

532. **6b-end: what the retired parity held alone, put back single-sided** (2026-10-25, #324 wave
    6b-end). A review of finding 531's deletion found cases of the four unit parity tests that held
    a property nothing else did, under the claim that each was held elsewhere. Each is back as an
    assertion on the binary alone (`cx_case` with its rc, out, err and state, or a plain check),
    in a test named for what it holds, on the stand-ins it needs; the bash leg and the oracle stay
    gone:
    - t_unit_signal_cleanup (new; wave 3b's stand-in desktop as `sd_start`, shared): a group INT,
      QUIT or a TERM while click --mod holds its keys: the keyboard tool lets go as its stdin
      closes, no signal reaching it (it writes "kb signalled" if one does); drag --shot's pointer
      tool lets go of the button on a group INT; shot --no-pointer under a group INT, TERM, HUP and
      a group QUIT (ignored: the shot goes on) during the capture, a TERM while the pointer is
      hidden, while it is given back (143 once it is) and during a foreground child after the hold:
      the pointer shown again, its record gone; INT, QUIT and HUP that came ignored (nohup, a
      script's `&`) stay ignored, for omabox and what it runs (the --after action's keyboard tool
      too); SIGPIPE as it came is what the box's tools get; and record sheet under a TERM to omabox
      alone while ffmpeg takes the frames: 143, no sheet, no `.record-*` left (on wave 4b's
      recording stand-ins, cut to ffprobe and ffmpeg).
    - t_unit_capture_errors (new, the same desktop): pixel's words for grim's image short, past its
      end and not a PPM it reads (findings 441, 442), its frame never left in TMPDIR, a TERM
      included (443); a relative OMABOX_STILL_DUMP refused with nothing in TMPDIR (426); an empty
      image taken twice (#217); shot's record it cannot write (`cannot write .../shots.tsv: Is a
      directory`, 1) and -o past a folder it cannot look into (442); --burst's failed frame from
      the tool or a grim a frame, and a --changed whose box stops answering, leave no temp file
      (427). Every case: nothing left in TMPDIR.
    - t_unit_monitor_add_window: monitor add refused for an interactive box whose aquamarine lacks
      +appid (a system one, an older build) or that an older `up` started (no
      run/omabox.appid-files), nothing asked of the host or the box (finding 429), remove not
      refused; the add's rollbacks (Hyprland does not make it: the record put back; placing fails:
      removed, the record as it was; never at its mode in 5 s: said, left as made) and mode's
      (Hyprland refuses, never takes it in 5 s: box.json not given the size; placing fails: given
      it, said; NVIDIA: labwc's output first, not resized: refused before Hyprland is asked, no
      parent display; the box gone while mode waited for its lock: box.json not given the size).
      Its two group-TERM cases that pinned state alone now pin 143 too (the only cx_case wants
      without an rc; t_cli_box's two take `rc~`).
    - t_unit_jailed_caller: "record stop: the video, its marks and captions placed" and "alone:
      record stop" asserted 1 and "the broker named no file to write" under labels promising the
      files: the stand-in broker answered status --file with its whole log unless the caller's
      PATH named rj-status-only, and the stand-in relay wrote nothing to the fds. Now the jailed
      case has rj-status-only, the alone relay writes what a broker would to each --to-fd,
      --marks-fd and --vtt-fd, and both see the three files placed by name, by content, no
      temporary file left; "alone: record sheet VIDEO" likewise places its sheet.
    - t_unit_bash_changes: `ls` (--json and the table) in byte order under C and en_US.UTF-8, as
      finding 530 said it was held (only `saves` was); with no en_US.UTF-8 on the system a skip
      line says so.
    Each was made to fail by breaking the code it holds, then the code put back: the bg tools'
    SIGINT ignore (exec.rs), sig::catch's keep-ignored, the SIGPIPE re-ignore, ptr's TERM catch,
    record sheet's TERM, pixel's frame trap, the burst error file's removal, a temp file before
    OMABOX_STILL_DUMP's refusal, #217's second capture, monitor add's two gates, its record put
    back and its remove, mode's labwc refusal and its box-gone check, relay_record's placing, and
    the byte-order sort (each restored case failed but one: "TERM while the pointer is given back"
    passes now and then without ptr's TERM catch, the release done before TERM's default end).
    Gone with it: `_rust-jq --inline` and `--recprog`, jqprog::INLINE and INLINE_4B, recprog::ALL
    and each module's JQ_INLINE but install.rs's (which it indexes), and eleven jq programs they
    alone named (the oracle's leftovers: PLACED_MAIN_JQ, DROP_MAIN_JQ, DESK_KNOWN_JQ, NAMES_RE_JQ,
    BW_JQ, LW_FLOOR_JQ, LH_FLOOR_JQ, RENDER_PAIR_JQ, AUDIO_SAY_A/B/C); `_rust-jq NAME` stays for
    the one name the suite runs, LAYER_SPAN_JQ (t_unit_window_select), and the comments that said
    "as it stands in bin/omabox" or "the suite checks" say bash's omabox had them.
    Found doing it, not fixed (as bash's omabox did, the parity cases compared that state equal): a
    shot or drag --shot cut short by INT, TERM or HUP during its capture leaves OUT.part (empty) in
    the output folder and grim's error file in TMPDIR: capture() registers no trap for either.
    The unit tier (its tests one at a time): 2,276 checks in 4 min 21 s, from 2,187 in 3 min 20 s
    (both timed here, the same machine): t_unit_signal_cleanup 42 s, t_unit_capture_errors 6 s,
    t_unit_monitor_add_window 143 s to 156 s (its three 5 s waits). Floors reset to about 90%: unit
    2040, full 4740 (531's estimate plus the checks added), --installed 1990 and 4270. cargo test:
    257 and 15 ignored, unchanged. No box test was touched.
533. **What a signal left behind: up's dead entry, shot's OUT.part, the temp files' window** (2026-10-25,
    #388, #386, #360; found by hand on the Rust omabox, all three in bash too). (1) up's undo kept
    the box dir once box.json existed (finding 163, for a failure's logs), so a Ctrl-C during up
    left the box listed `dead` and its reaper running until `down`. A signal is a stop, not a
    failure: trap.rs records the signal before the undos run (`trap::signalled`), and up's undo
    then clears the dir and kills the reaper as down does, once kill_box saw PID 1 gone (a PID 1
    still exiting keeps its dir, so a box that may run is never hidden). A failure keeps both, as
    before. (2) shot's capture registered neither OUT.part nor grim's error file: its undo, on a
    signal only, stops the grab (its children killed until its thread is over, at most 3 s, so
    grim makes no file after) and removes both. Not under --no-pointer's hold (`ptr::holding`):
    its own INT, TERM and HUP handlers exec `_ptr-release` to give the pointer back, and arming
    trap.rs's over them kept the pointer hidden (t_unit_signal_cleanup caught it), so a
    --no-pointer shot stopped mid-capture still leaves OUT.part. (3) cpu, gpu, record stop (the input's file, its
    `.record-*` folders) and record_ass (an unregistered TMPDIR file) made a file with mktemp and
    armed its undo on the next line; `trap::made` runs both under the undo lock (UNDOING), so a
    signal's undo waits and finds it armed. Inside `made` main runs its children plainly, as in
    an undo, so it cannot wait on FOREGROUND held by the signal's thread. Tests: t_up_signals (the
    name gone from ls, no dir, no reaper, after each signal at each step), t_theme (a failing up
    keeps its dir), t_unit_signal_cleanup (shot under a group INT, TERM and HUP during the capture:
    no OUT.part, no TMPDIR file), trap.rs `a_signals_undo_waits_for_made`.
534. **`guard on` and `off` kept every backup they ever made** (2026-10-27, #398). Each change wrote
    `FILE.bak-SECONDS.NANOSECONDS` beside the agent's settings and none went away: a machine that had
    tracked omabox since 0.1 had five in `~/.claude/` and three beside Codex's `hooks.json`, and
    `setup --remove` left them unnamed. `write` now keeps only the backup of the change it just made
    and removes the older ones, matched by that exact name (the user's own `settings.json.bak`,
    `.bak-mine`, `.bak-20261004` stay), saying how many went. `setup --remove` names the ones left
    ("kept: the guard's backups of your agents' settings: ..."). Tests: guard.rs
    `backups_are_ours_only_oldest_first`, t_unit_guard_settings (one of ours and the user's own after
    an off), the setup --remove case in test/run.sh. The backup just made is told from the older
    ones by its name, not its path: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude/` spells FILE with a doubled slash
    that the listed paths lose, and a path compare removed every backup, the new one too (guard.rs
    `write_keeps_its_backup_through_a_doubled_slash`). Pruning only on a rewrite left an upgrade's
    backups alone (a VM upgrade test, 2026-10-27: from 1.0.0 all 18 stayed, since install.sh's guard
    step finds the guard on; from 0.5.4 Codex's `config.toml`, unchanged since 0.2.0, kept its four):
    "already on/off" now keeps only the newest too and says how many went (t_unit_guard_settings
    "on again with an older version's backups"). The same test found a 0.x checkout's bar widget
    notifying "cannot list boxes" while install.sh builds (`bin/omabox` links to a binary not built
    yet; the old release's QML does it, so only the 1.0.1 upgrade note can help).
535. **A box took a protected port the host had let go of; a missing or failing nft waited 10 s**
    (2026-10-27, #364 items 1 and 4). (1) protect-ports (S10, finding 459) left each port out of
    pasta's `-T`/`-U` (box to host) only: `-t 127.0.0.1/auto` and `-u` (host to box) still forwarded
    it, so with the host's service on it down or restarting, a box server on that port took the
    host's `127.0.0.1:PORT`, and a browser's `localhost:PORT` reached the box. All eight rules now
    carry the `~PORT,` exclusions (`-t 127.0.0.1/~P,auto`, and the ephemeral range's
    `-t 127.0.0.1/~P,32768-60999,auto`; pasta takes the address prefix before the exclusions). (2) up
    looked for nft on the caller's PATH, but launch.sh runs pasta's shell with `PATH=/usr/bin`: an
    nft only in `~/bin` passed the check, and a missing or failing nft ended pasta's shell with its
    line in box.log while up waited 10 s for a pid and said "bwrap did not start". up now looks in
    up_box's `LAUNCH_PATH` (what launch.sh sets) and names it; and its wait for the pid reads box.log
    for pasta's shell's own failure lines (the nft rule's, and --addr's, exact lines), saying at once
    what failed with the first line before it (nft's or ip's error). Tests: t_protect_ports (a box's
    TCP and UDP servers on a protected port nothing on the host holds stay off the host's 127.0.0.1,
    with a port not protected as the control; pasta's `-t`/`-u` words; under a user and mount
    namespace of the test's own whose `/usr/bin/nft` is a stand-in, an empty file with an nft on the
    caller's PATH refused in ms naming /usr/bin, and one that fails said in ~0.1 s, no box left up:
    each failed before, 10 s and "bwrap did not start"); net.rs `pasta_opens_what_it_should` (every
    `-t`/`-u` rule too); exec.rs `executable_in_the_path_given`; up_box.rs `net_failed_says_what_failed`.
536. **`run --pass` through a relay older than the binary exited 2, as if its command had** (2026-10-27,
    #380). Since 1.0 a jailed caller's `--pass` and `--env-file` values go to omabox-relay on an fd
    (`--env-fd`, finding 503). A jail started before the upgrade still maps 0.x's relay, which answers
    `--env-fd` with "unknown option", exit 2, before the broker is reached; `run` hands on any status
    but its own 125 as its command's, so the caller saw its command fail with 2. The new relay's own
    usage errors (a bad `--env-fd`, `--env`, `--fd`, an unknown word, no `--`) were 2 as well, though
    OMABOX_RELAY_FAIL (125 for `run`) already set its other failures. **Fix**: the relay's call
    returns OMABOX_RELAY_FAIL's status for its usage errors too (2 when it is not set); and before a
    call that needs `--env-fd`, the binary asks its relay whether it takes it, without the broker: a
    call to a socket path longer than any (`NO_SOCKET`), `--env-fd` on /dev/null, OMABOX_RELAY_FAIL
    unset, ends with 1 from a relay that read its options and 2 from one that did not. An older relay
    is refused there with run's 125 (1 for `keys --pass`), saying to restart the jail; a call with
    nothing to pass goes to it as before. The question costs one exec of the relay, only on calls
    that pass values. Tests: t_unit_relay (each usage error 2, and 125 with OMABOX_RELAY_FAIL=125),
    t_unit_jailed_caller ("alone, an older relay": a stand-in that parses as 0.x's), relay.rs
    `takes_env_fd_tells_an_older_relay`.
537. **`broker off` left the broker's socket file behind** (2026-10-27, #393). The socket unit listens
    on `%t/omabox/.broker/sock` and the user manager makes that file (and `.broker/`) when it starts
    the unit; stopping it closed the socket but kept the file, so after `off` a dead socket stayed,
    and anything that looks for it (a jailed omabox's `relay_wanted`) saw a broker that was not
    there. Two parts, since either alone misses a case: the unit now says `RemoveOnStop=yes`, so any
    stop of it (`off`, or `systemctl --user stop`) takes the file; and `off` itself removes
    `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omabox/.broker/sock` when it is a socket (a file of that name that is not one is
    not ours) and then `.broker/` only when it is empty, which also cleans what an older omabox's unit
    (no RemoveOnStop) leaves on the first `off` after an upgrade. It uses the runtime dir, not
    OMABOX_BROKER_SOCK (where a jail looks). The suite's broker case ran `off` on the real
    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; it now runs on a stand-in one, since `off` removes files there. Tests:
    t_unit_broker_units (the socket and its folder gone after `off`, another file there kept with
    its folder, a non-socket `sock` kept; RemoveOnStop in the unit, which `systemd-analyze verify`
    accepts), broker.rs `clear_sock_takes_only_the_socket_and_an_empty_folder`.
538. **install.sh without a terminal: logs kept, the command to run, a software render node said**
    (2026-10-27, #395). An agent's run (stdin not a terminal; a VM with sudo needing a password, #390)
    stopped where it should, with three rough edges. `--check`'s failure named the box's `box.log`
    and `home/*.log`, which the EXIT trap's `omabox down` had removed: a failed up or shot now copies
    them to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omabox/install-check/` first (replaced by every check; one that passes
    removes it) and says so; the box still goes down. The package stop printed `missing: …` then
    sudo's own error, which varies: with stdin not a terminal (where pacman reads its `[Y/n]`; also
    `./install.sh </dev/null` in a pseudo-terminal nobody answers) it now stops before sudo with the
    line to run, `sudo pacman -S --needed …`, then install.sh again. A render node that renders only
    in software (virtio-gpu without virgl: `labwc.log` "Software rendering detected") passed
    `compgen -G /dev/dri/renderD*`, and the box died "while starting". It is told without starting
    anything: on PCI (virtio-vga, an omavm guest's) the node's `device` in sysfs is virtio-pci's
    and has no `features`; its child `device/virtio0` is the virtio_gpu device, whose `features`
    lists the negotiated bits as 0/1, bit 0 virgl and bit 4 context init (venus, the other way to
    render on the host's GPU). Read in two omavm guests (Omarchy 4.0.6): `01000…` without accel3d,
    `11001…` with. `device/` itself is read too, for a virtio-gpu not on PCI (virtio-mmio). With
    bits 0 and 4 both 0 on every node, install.sh stops and says a box needs GPU rendering. Only
    every node: one beside a real GPU is `up`'s to say (#396). A first version read `device/` alone,
    from the kernel's sources, and missed the PCI layout. Tests: t_unit_install (no terminal: no
    sudo, the command; in a terminal sudo as before; a fake sysfs via `OMABOX_TEST_SYSDRM` laid out
    as the guests' with their two feature strings: without virgl stops, with virgl, venus only or
    another driver passes, virtio-mmio's `device/` stops; `--check` with a stand-in omabox whose up
    dies: logs kept, box down; one that comes up: its screenshot, nothing kept).

539. **setup's widget line said "is not known" when run right after setup** (2026-10-27, #397).
    Without a terminal setup prints `omarchy plugin enable chaves.omabox`; run at once (the 1.0.0
    package test, Omarchy 4.0.6), it failed with "plugin 'chaves.omabox' is not known; run:
    omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins". A race, not a missing reload: the shell's PluginRegistry
    watches its plugins dir (`inotifywait -m -r`, Omarchy 4.0.0 to 4.5.0-rc1 alike) and reloads on the
    new link, but through a 150 ms timer and a scan: in a 4.0.6 VM `ln -s` then `omarchy plugin
    enable` failed 3 times of 3, and the shell listed the plugin about 0.3 s after the link. A box's
    shell has no watcher at all (finding 196), so there the line failed until a rescan. Only the
    terminal's "yes" path rescanned (finding 133). setup now asks the shell (`omarchy-shell shell
    listPlugins`) whether it lists the widget; if not, it rescans as `omarchy plugin add` does
    (`omarchy-shell -q shell rescanPlugins`; `-q`, `rescanPlugins` and `listPlugins` are in every
    4.x tag) and lists again every 200 ms until it does, up to 4 s. A shell that lists it already is
    left alone (a rescan reloads every plugin; a re-run of setup re-makes the link and the shell keeps
    listing it), no shell running costs one failed call, and a "no" remembered calls no shell (the
    user said no; t_unit_install relies on it). A shell that still does not list it after 4 s gets
    the line with both steps (`omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins, then omarchy plugin enable ...`).
    In the 4.0.6 VM, setup then `omarchy plugin enable` worked 3 times of 3 (setup ~0.35 s; a re-run
    40 ms, no rescan). Omarchy 4.5 has the same watcher and timer, so the same race (read from its
    QML, not run on a desktop). Tests: t_unit_setup (stand-in shells: none, one that lists it, one
    that lists it after a rescan, one a rescan does not change, a "no" remembered), t_setup_prompts
    (in a box, the line run at once enables the widget); both failed on the old code.
540. **check point kept a region as typed** (2026-10-30, #384). `-g "010,010 400x300"` went into
    the `.point` file as `of region 010,010 400x300` (and `crop ...` with `--window`), and grim's
    other forms, `X,Y,W,H` and `X,Y W,H`, as typed too, while shot writes regions as read (finding
    448). So the same region typed two ways made two different `.point` lines. check point now keeps
    `-g` as geom_parse reads it, written in grim's form with its numbers decimal (settle::geom_text):
    `00,010 300,200` is `of region 0,10 300x200`. Tests: settle's `geometry` unit test, t_cli_box's
    "check point -g 00,010 300,200: kept as read" (failed on the old code).
541. **shot -o x.ppm wrote a PNG without a word** (2026-10-30, #346). shot writes PNG whatever FILE
    is called (grim's PNG, then magick's for --fit, --zoom and --changed, and baselines, --changed and
    `click --in` read PNGs), so an agent that asked for x.ppm to read raw pixels got a PNG and went
    on to write a PNG decoder. Honouring the extension would touch every path that reads the shot
    back; a note does not. shot now says `shot: FILE holds a PNG (shot writes PNG only, whatever the
    name)` on stderr when FILE's extension is another image format's (ppm pgm pbm pnm pam jpg jpeg
    webp bmp gif tif tiff avif jxl qoi heic raw, any case; for a jailed caller, its --as name), and
    `help shot` says so with the magick line that converts one. The shot itself is unchanged, so a
    script that names its PNG x.jpg keeps working. Tests: shot's `png_named_note` unit test,
    t_unit_capture_errors' "shot -o x.ppm: a PNG, said".
542. **check point cut an --ignore region to the shot without a word** (2026-10-30, #342). An agent
    gave `--window APP -g "568,78 760x875" --ignore "230,130 430x52"`, the region relative to the
    crop by mistake (the docs say the window's coordinates): the `.point` file kept `ignore 0 52 92
    52`, a 92-pixel sliver, and nothing was said; one wholly outside was said and left out, one
    partly outside was not. And approve's summary, "(0 with regions left out)", counted only the
    unstable regions found between runs, so with several `--ignore` checkpoints it read as if the
    ignores were dropped. check point now says `--ignore "X,Y WxH" is partly outside the shot (SPACE;
    it covers WxH at X,Y): cut to WxH at X,Y` (ignore_cut, in the coordinates given) and keeps the
    cut region as before; the summary counts a checkpoint with `ignore` lines as one with regions
    left out. Tests: check's `ignore_px_as_bash` unit test (#342's own numbers), t_cli_box's "check
    point --ignore partly outside -g: cut, said", t_check's summary count (desk now has an
    `--ignore`).
543. **tree cut names and text at 80 characters for --json and --find too** (2026-10-30, #314). The
    tree tool cut every name and text to 80 characters (a text read at most 200) and a value to 40
    as it read them, so `--find` matched the cut string and `--json` carried it: an agent's check of a
    status band whose part it needed sat past character 80 got exit 1 from `--find "next:"`, and the
    same cut name in `--json` left it unsure whether omabox or the app cut it. The tool now reads
    names, text and values whole, up to 4000 characters (FULL), and cuts them only where the text view
    prints them (NAME_W 80, VALUE_W 40, ending in …, as before); `--find` matches the whole line,
    `--json` carries whole strings, and its `path` whole ancestors (the text view's path stays cut).
    Comparisons that read names (a value or text equal to the name, a label repeating its parent's)
    now see them whole. `help tree` says so. Test: t_tree's Qt window has a check box named past 80
    characters: `--find` matches its end, the line cut at 80, `--json` the whole name (failed on the
    old code: `--find` exit 1).
544. **Record cases failed without wf-recorder and ffmpeg** (2026-10-30, #405). Both are optional
    (the package's optdepends), and most record tests skip without them, but t_cli_box's eight record
    cases and t_main's "record --audio refused" failed instead (record asks for its tools before the
    box's audio): 9 of 13 box failures in the 1.0.1 package's installed suite in a VM without them.
    They now skip with the same guard, naming the tools.
545. **A box whose used file was gone was never reaped; a stray folder ended ls** (2026-10-30, #371).
    The idle reaper reads the idle time from the mtime of `<box dir>/used`; with the file gone it
    went on polling and never took the box down until a command touched it again (bash's reaper died
    on an arithmetic error there, finding 471). It now makes the file again, so the idle time counts
    from then. And a folder in the runtime dir with a box.json whose name no box can have (`bad
    name!`, made by hand or by another tool) ended `ls` and `ls --json` with select_box's refusal,
    exit 2, nothing listed: list_names now leaves such folders out (every command that lists boxes),
    and `ls` names each on stderr ("'NAME' in DIR is no box's folder (no box can be named so): left
    out"), exit 0. Tests: t_unit_bash_changes (ls on such a folder), t_idle (its used file removed
    after up: it still goes down).
546. **Back-to-back runs got slower: a marker a run, kept 10 s** (2026-10-30, #392). Each `run`
    leaves `runs/c.START.END` (#300, finding 406: a `run -d` job killed during a run or within 2 s of
    its end is not warned about), dropped only 10 s after it ended, and each run lists the folder: six
    batches of 100 runs in a row went from 3.1 to 6.6 ms a run (630 markers in about 3 s). A run's
    end now merges its marker with every ended one within JOB_RUN_GRACE_MS (2 s) of it, until none
    is left that meets it, into one `c.FIRST.LAST`: job_run_stopped's answer is the same for every
    time (the gaps it closes were inside the earlier run's grace already), and back-to-back runs keep
    one file. A file is removed only once one covering it is there, so runs ending at once lose none.
    Measured on a box: three batches of 200 runs, 2.46, 2.52, 2.53 ms a run, one marker. Test:
    jobs' `job_note_as_bash` (50 runs back to back keep one marker beside one apart; what
    job_run_stopped answers), failed on the old code.
547. **Omarchy 4.5.0-rc2's bar is a full-screen layer: `tree --layer omarchy-bar` could not tell it
    from the wallpaper** (2026-10-30, refs #315). On rc2 (proart since 10-28) the shell's
    `omarchy-bar` layer is 1920x1080, the size of `omarchy-background`, both of one pid, so the tree
    tool's frame by size found two and refused (exit 6: "which one is the layer's cannot be told");
    t_tree_layer's two checks of an empty layer and t_cli_box's "tree --layer: the bar" failed on
