    for one. A popup whose card has items beside the wallpaper is still #315's case.
548. **wait until: 127 retried to the timeout, its stderr hidden, a false success through `!`**
    (2026-10-30, #400). An agent's `wait until --timeout 120 -- <host path>/left.sh` polled 120 s and
    ended `unsatisfied: command still failing after 120.04s (exit 127)`, the command's own "not
    found" never shown; `sh -c "! <host path>/script | grep -q X"` was satisfied at once (the
    pipeline failed in the box, the `!` made it 0). Now: a try that exits 127 (not found) or 126
    (cannot run) ends the wait at once, `unknown: command not found in the box (exit 127) after Ns`,
    exit 1 (no retry changes it; `unknown` is wait's "could not tell", as for a box gone); each try's
    stderr goes to `<box dir>/until.err` (host-only), and a wait that did not succeed says its last
    three lines on stderr ("the command's last words"); and a command whose words (a `sh -c` string
    too) name a path under the box's folder here (its HOME's host path: /home/sbx in the box) or
    under the caller's $TMPDIR (not /tmp: the box has a /tmp of its own, so a /tmp path cannot be
    judged from the word) is said before waiting. The "unknown:" lead of the box-down line is kept:
    it is wait's documented result word (`help exit-codes`), for still and change too. Tests: wait's
    `until_words` unit test; t_cli_box's wait until cases (not found: at once, 1, its words; one
    still failing: its words; a `!` of a host path: said before).
549. **Omarchy 4.5.0-rc2's bar surface spans the screen: every click said it "may go to omarchy-bar"**
    (2026-10-30, #407). rc2's `omarchy-bar` (top level) is as big as its screen, transparent past the
    strip it draws (Bar.qml: a drag takes input on the whole surface so the pointer stays on it;
    growing the surface for a drag flashed), with an input mask on the strip while idle
    (`mask: dragActive ? null : stripInputRegion`) and the strip's thickness as exclusive zone.
    `hyprctl layers` has no input region, and finding 421's rule took a layer spanning its output
    for one with input on its items only (the notifications, the dock), so every `click` in a box
    with the stock bar printed "a layer spanning the screen, \"omarchy-bar\" ... may go to it", and
    `windows` listed the bar as possibly over every window; t_click_layer failed 3 checks on rc2 (on
    the code before this too). Finding 421 also said the bar "takes input all over": true while the
    surface was the strip. **Fix**: LAYER_SPAN_JQ's `bar_strip`: a screen-sized `omarchy-bar` is the
    strip along the edge its output reserves (`monitors`' `reserved`: top, bottom, left, right, the
    first non-zero), applied where WIN_JQ (click, windows) and DESK_TARGET_JQ (what got the input)
    read layers; with no edge reserved (the bar hidden, a fixture without `reserved`) it is left as
    it is. The strip is then a certain layer on a reserved edge, as the 4.0 and rc1 bar was. By
    namespace, since an all-screen layer whose output reserves an edge was 4.0's notifications
    too (finding 398). Tests: t_unit_window_select (rc2's bar at the top and bottom, and with no edge
    known), the contract (`omarchy_contract_45`: Bar.qml's mask, exclusive zone and screen-sized
    surface), t_click_layer on rc2 (failed on the old code).
550. **click --find: the tree's node clicked by name; a Qt dock's contents placed** (2026-10-30, #318).
    `omabox-tree --click TEXT [--index N]` walks the window as `tree` does but keeps what `tree` leaves
    out (hidden nodes, what lies outside the window) to say why a match cannot be clicked, and prints
    "X Y" (the middle of the node's bounds cut by the window's and every ancestor's that has bounds)
    and its line; `click --find` clicks there with the real pointer, the input path a test exercises
    (#318: the AT-SPI action is not used). An exact name (any case) wins over a part of one, and
    anything else over a `label`/`static` of its name (GTK4 names an entry after its mnemonic label:
    both match "Email"). Several in view: exit 8 (`click` 2) with the lines; none in view: 9 (`click`
    1) with why: hidden (not SHOWING and VISIBLE, itself or an ancestor), no bounds, out of view (a
    GTK4 scrolled window's rows below the fold are inside the window: only the viewport's bounds
    cut them), disabled. GTK4 does not publish a hidden widget at all: "nothing is named". **Qt dock
    widgets** (finding 244's exception): the dock's contents are a `frame` that says 0,0 in window
    coordinates, its children relative to it, while its SCREEN extents are where it is drawn
    (Designer's Widget Box: window 0,0, screen 0,84; its filter field said `@4,4`, drawn at 4,88).
    The Qt Quick popup rule (finding 364's offset from the screen coordinates) now takes a nested
    `frame` too; where a toolkit's screen coordinates equal its window ones the offset is 0 and
    nothing moves. Also: an unnamed non-container node takes the name of its LABELLED_BY target, and
    a node is read once (by bus name and path) however many parents list it. Tests: t_click_find
    (GTK4: active window, part and exact names, label vs entry, two in view and --index, disabled,
    scrolled out, nothing; Designer: a dialog's Close, the dock's place, four docks' Close buttons),
    t_tree_layer (`click --layer --find` on the stub panel).
551. **run's "WORD is relative to DIR" note fired on words that only share a folder's name** (2026-10-30,
    #325). cwd_path_word (#251) took any word of the command that was not `-*`, `/*` or `~*` and named
    something in the caller's directory for a path: from a plugin checkout with folders `stash`,
    `console` and `rail`, `run -- omarchy-shell stash modules` (an IPC target) got the note and its
    advice to restart the box with `--overlay`, 10 times in 6 subagents of one session, all false;
    once on stderr into a `2>&1 | jq`, which failed. Now a word counts only when it reads as a path:
    it has a `/`, is `.` or `..`, is the command itself, a script's command (`sh -c`'s first word, or
    one after `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `then`, `do`, `else`), or `cd`'s folder. A bare argument that
    names a folder (`python3 tests`) is no longer said; one with a `/` (`tests/x.py`) still is.
    Test: t_unit_run_cwd_note (the issue's commands: none; a script's later command: said), failed
    on the old code.
552. **Ctrl-D at a setup prompt ended setup without a word** (2026-10-30, #373). setup's `[Y/n]`
    prompts (the widget, a stale `~/.local/bin/omabox` link, the guard) ended the command with exit 1
    at the end of input, as bash's `set -e` did after `read` failed. Every prompt defaults to yes, so
    reading Ctrl-D as the default would act on a key that means "stop": it is now a no, said once on
    its own line ("(end of input: no, to this and any question after it)"), and setup goes on to its
    end. The widget's no is remembered (`widget-declined`, never asked again); a Ctrl-D is not, so
    the next setup asks again. Test: t_setup_prompts (Ctrl-D at the widget's question: said, not in
    the bar, not remembered), failed on the old code.
553. **Setting protect-ports said nothing about boxes up already** (2026-10-30, #374). `up` reads
    protect-ports once (finding 480, S10): a connected box that is up keeps reaching the ports it
    could reach at its start, and the rule needs nft in /usr/bin. A user who set it after seeing an
    agent's box reach their database would take the database for covered at once. `config
    protect-ports VALUE` (and `default`) now names the connected boxes up when the set of ports
    changed ("boxes up already keep the ports they started with: NAMES (down and up again to apply
    it to them)"; the same set in another order is no change: config reads it as a set), and warns
    when nft is not in /usr/bin, where up then refuses a connected box. Test: t_protect_ports (a
    change names its box; the same set again says nothing), failed on the old code. The nft warning
    is not run here (this machine has nft).
554. **A run -d job that traps SIGTERM was warned about after `run -- pkill`** (2026-10-30, #329).
    #300 (finding 406) left out a job killed while an `omabox run` ran, or 2 s after, but only for
    statuses 130, 137 and 143. foot catches SIGTERM and exits 230 (its own "failure in foot" code),
    so a stop-and-relaunch loop (`run -- pkill -f 'app-id X'`, then `run -d -- foot --app-id X`) got
    "exited with status 230" 4 times in one subagent. Leaving out any status during any run would
    hide real crashes (agents run commands all the time), so a run that kills is marked apart: its
    words (or a `sh -c` script's) hold kill, pkill or killall (kill_cmd), and its marks are `ok.` /
    `ck.` instead of `o.` / `c.`, merged only with their own kind (finding 546). A job that ends in
    a kill's window is left out whatever its status; in a plain run's window, 130/137/143 only, as
    before. A word `kill` that is only an argument (`pgrep -x kill`) counts too: it errs to silence,
    for that run's window alone. The hint is now `(log: omabox log -b NAME run)`, as the other
    branch's `(log: PATH)`: "since the last command (omabox log ...)" read as if that was the last
    command. Tests: jobs' `job_note_as_bash` (a kill's own mark, a job ending in it, kill_cmd),
    t_replace (a job that exits 230 on SIGTERM, stopped by `run -- pkill`: not said), which failed
    on the old code.
555. **A foreground run and a plain path skipped the session's box** (2026-10-30, #327). #296 made `run -d`
    (and `down`) name the session's boxes when the name derived here has no box; a foreground `run`
    went on to a throwaway (an agent's IPC calls answered "Target not found." three times from a box
    without the plugin under test, nothing saying which box), and plain `path` printed the dir of a
    box that is not there, exit 0. Now both refuse as `run -d` does, naming the session's box or
    boxes, when the name was derived, it has no box (path: no dir) and the session has boxes up
    elsewhere; a throwaway (no session boxes) and a path printed before `up` stay as they were. And
    bare `omabox help` says how the box is picked without -b (it was in `--long` only). Test:
    t_unit_agent_session (both, from another repo with the session's box up), failed on the old code.
556. **The guard refused `omarchy plugin list` as "omarchy-shell"** (2026-10-30, #332). 45 of Omarchy
    4.5's commands call `omarchy-shell` by name (omarchy-plugin-list's `$(omarchy-shell shell
    listPlugins)`), so the guard's shim answered for them, naming a command the agent never typed;
    under `| grep` the refusal read as "no match". The shim now reads its parent's words
    (`/proc/$PPID/cmdline`: the script, also in a `$(...)` subshell, a fork of it) and, when one is
    an Omarchy command (`omarchy-*`, not omarchy-shell), names it: "not running omarchy-plugin-list
    here: it asks the user's desktop shell ... through omarchy-shell. For a box's: omabox run --
    omarchy-plugin-list ...", and for that one where the plugins are (`~/.config/omarchy/plugins`).
    Exit 4 (0 with -q) as before. Read-only queries still do not pass: they reach the user's shell,
    which the guard keeps an agent from (the issue left that call open; not changed). Test:
    t_unit_guard_omarchy_shell (a stand-in omarchy-plugin-list calling it from `$(...)`).
557. **A bound folder deleted and made again on the host showed empty in the box, with no word**
    (2026-10-30, #391). A box binds a `--ro-bind`/`--overlay` folder (and the repo, its git dir, the
    plugins' and the rest of `up`'s own) as it is at `up`; `rm -rf DIR; mkdir DIR` on the host leaves
    the box the old, deleted directory: empty, every command succeeding. It hit two of five subagents
    sharing a built site's folder another agent remade. `up` now writes each bind's source with its
    device and inode in box.json (`mounts`); `run` (foreground and -d) compares them, and a source
    that is gone or another directory now is said once a box and folder ("note: DIR, bound into box
    'B' at up, was deleted and made again on the host since: the box still has the folder it bound
    at DEST, empty if it was deleted (down, then up again binds the new one; a folder kept, its
    files remade inside it, needs neither)"; said ones in `<box dir>/noted-mounts`). A box started
    by an older omabox has no `mounts`: nothing said. The skill's reference says it under Mounts.
    Test: t_mount_replaced (a folder remade after up: said once, the box sees none of the new one).
558. **The Omarchy contract's bar item failed on any 4.5 tree but rc2** (2026-10-30, after #407; seen
    by #408's author on a dev tree). It asked every 4.5 tree for rc2's bar: a surface as big as its
    screen, `mask: dragActive ? null : stripInputRegion`. rc1's bar is strip-sized, which bar_strip
    leaves alone, and 4.5.0's (`v4-5-0`, 10-29) masks it as `dragActive ? null : (underFullscreen ?
    noInputRegion : stripInputRegion)`, so the item failed on both. It now checks the mask and the
    exclusive zone only where the surface spans its screen, and takes any mask that names
    `stripInputRegion`. The click report still names the bar for a click on its strip over a
    fullscreen window, where 4.5.0's bar takes none (`windows` already drops top layers there): not
    changed. Test: t_unit_omarchy_contract (rc1's bar and 4.5.0's mask hold, a full-screen bar with
    no mask fails); the contract passes on rc1, rc2 and `v4-5-0` trees.
559. **A crash was sometimes said as a hang: the box ended between two looks** (2026-10-30, #351).
    After a call got no answer, `hypr_lost` looks whether the box is alive, then for its Hyprland's
    host pid. The box outlives its crashed Hyprland by ~75 ms; when it ended between the two looks,
    the second found no pids, which reads as "cannot tell", and the crash was said as "did not
    answer (hung? ...)". t_hyprland_crash failed on it 4 to 8 times in 20 (bash era; the Rust port
    kept the order). Now no pids with the box gone is "went down", with labwc's how. The issue's
    second race, a later call finding the box still up, was finding 527. Test: the unit test
    hypr_lost_box_ends_between_looks (alive at one look, no pids at the next).
560. **Inside ai-jail, a project without `.git` got no project in the box, and nothing said so**
    (2026-10-31, #394). A jailed caller's repo is the jail's folder its cwd is in, taken only when it
    has a `.git` (repo_top runs no git on the jail's folders). In one without, `up` and a throwaway
    `run` worked and the box had nothing of it. Both now say, once a command: "note: DIR is not a git
    repo, so this box does not have it (a box takes a jail's folder only when it has a .git): up
    --ro-bind DIR (or --overlay, to write in the box) mounts it" (a folder a box may not mount: why
    not). Only in a jail (Diogo, 2026-10-31): outside one a box never takes the folder it happens to
    start in (finding 63), and a note on every `up` from ~ would be noise. Tests: t_unit_jail_policy
    (norepo_note: said for a folder without .git, not for one with, not outside a jail), t_jail (in a
    real ai-jail: said, the box without the folder, then `up --ro-bind` as it says: the box has it).
561. **The click report named a top layer over a fullscreen window as where the click went** (2026-10-31,
    #409; from finding 558's reading of 4.5.0's bar). `DESK_TARGET_JQ` (a `--wait` 124's "the click at
    X,Y was on ...", `--json`'s `target`) counted every top and overlay layer at the point. On a
    monitor whose workspace has a window in real fullscreen (mode 2) Hyprland passes top layers by
    (finding 379), and 4.5.0's bar masks itself to no input there too, so a click at the top of a
    fullscreen window was said, `certain`, to be "on layer omarchy-bar (over ...)". `WIN_JQ` already
    drops them (`windows`, `--window`). Now the report drops top-level layers at a point inside a
    mapped window in fullscreen 2 on a monitor's active workspace; overlays still count, a maximized
    window (mode 1) keeps the bar over it. Test: t_unit_wait_facts (failed on the old code). Not seen
    in a box: no box test puts a window in fullscreen under the stock bar.
562. **A click at the screen's X Y said nothing of a layer over the point** (2026-10-31, #361). Since
    finding 379, `--window` input names a top or overlay layer over its point; `click -b BOX X Y`
    never looked, so an agent's click near a window's top right went to a notification toast, exit 0,
    nothing said, and only a later `--window` click said why. Now `click`, `scroll` and `drag` (its
    start: the press's surface keeps the pointer for the drag) at the screen's X Y (and `--in` a
    screen shot) read one snapshot (desk_snap) before sending, find the window there as the click
    report does (finding 561's fullscreen rule included, through WIN_JQ's `layers`), and say the
    layer over it in `--window`'s words, the point given as "the screen's X,Y", when it certainly
    covers the point (smaller than its output: "is over the screen's X,Y, on window ...: ... input
    there goes to it"). Never refused (there is no window to raise or keep). *Decided* (2026-10-31):
    a layer spanning the screen says nothing here, unlike `--window`'s may: on Omarchy 4.5 the
    notifications column and the dock stay mapped while idle and span the screen, so every plain
    click under them would speak with no toast up; #283's narrowing would let it speak where a toast
    is. Nothing is said where no window is under the layer either: a click on the bar or the desktop
    is meant for the layer. `--wait`'s 124 already names a spanning layer as possible (findings
    396, 398). Tests: t_unit_wait_facts (`probe screen_layer`, new), t_click_layer (a screen click
    under the spanning layer only: nothing said; under a panel, a click, scroll and drag say it;
    failed with the call left out), t_wait_facts (the 124's
    button layer said before its click); t_unit_signal_cleanup's `click --mod` cases moved off the
    stand-in bar, which now says itself.
563. **A Hyprland notification was not missing from shots: it is drawn top right** (2026-10-31, #359).
    The issue's `hyprctl notify` then `shot -g 0,0,1300,200` of a 3440-wide monitor had none, read
    as a capture that misses the overlay (its guess: no damage). Not so: Hyprland 0.56's
    notification overlay (`src/notification/NotificationOverlay.cpp`) draws at the top right of the
    focused monitor, below its reserved top, sliding in over 600 ms, and damages its box, so grim gets
    it: a full shot right after `notify` has it half slid in, one 1 s later whole. The monitor-layout
    warning is the same overlay (`MonitorLayoutController::checkOverlapsAndNotify`, 15 s), logged
    as "Monitor NAME: detected overlap with layout"; a notify's own text is not logged. The
    config-error bar never shows in a box (finding 352). Now `omabox hyprctl notify`, after
    Hyprland's `ok`, says where ("note: Hyprland draws it at the top right of the focused monitor,
    NAME, sliding in over 0.6 s: omabox shot -b B -g X,Y,W,H shows that corner": the right half of
    its top third, in layout pixels); a notify Hyprland refuses, or monitors that cannot be read,
    say nothing. The skill's reference says it beside the config-error bar's line. Tests:
    t_hypr_notify (the note, its region's shot has the notification, the screen's left none),
    failed on the old code; hyprctl.rs notify_corner (a scaled, turned second monitor).
564. **`tree --layer` could not read an Omarchy 4.5 bar popup** (2026-10-31, #315). Every 4.5 popup
    is a `KeyboardPanel`: `omarchy-keyboard-panel`, a full-screen overlay with the card inside it,
    of the shell's pid, beside `omarchy-background` (and, on rc2, `omarchy-bar`) of the same size,
    so the tree tool found three frames of that size and refused (exit 6). Read in a box with the
    clock's popup open: the panel's frame is the only one `active`, with the card's items under it;
    the other two are empty. `--active` (finding 384) already tells such frames apart, but only for a
    layer holding the keyboard exclusively (kb_layers, `interactivity == 1`), and the panel takes it
    exclusively only for a moment on open, then on demand (2). Now layer_read asks Hyprland for
    every mapped layer that may take the keyboard (kb_takers: address and interactivity) and, among
    the layers of the pid and size, takes the one exclusive one, else the one that takes it at all:
    only a layer that can take the keyboard can have the active frame, so `--active yes|no` holds;
    two of them (or none) still cannot be told. Not done: a frame with items winning over empty ones
    (the issue's other idea): `tree --layer omarchy-bar` with a popup open would read the popup's.
    A popup that lost the keyboard (focus moved to a window while it stays open) still cannot be
    told. Tests: the unit tests kb_hint_picks_the_one_that_can_hold_the_keyboard and
    layer_argv_as_bash; t_tree_layer (a full-screen overlay on demand beside a full-screen
    background of one pid: its tree, and the wallpaper's says it publishes nothing).
565. **An editable combo box's typed text was not in the tree** (2026-10-31, #341). `tree` read
    the Text interface only for text roles, and a combo box only for its Value or a closed menu's
    selected item. Chromium's `<input list>` and `role=combobox` input (Qt WebEngine's likely too,
    Chromium inside: not measured) are a `combo box` [editable] with the text on it and no child: a
    filled path field printed `combo box "new path" [editable]` and nothing `--find` could match.
    Qt Quick's and GTK4's combo boxes have no Text interface of their own; Qt Quick's editable one
    has an entry child that already says it (an AT-SPI probe in a box). Now an editable combo box's
    Text is its `'text'`; a closed one's stays out (Chromium's is U+FFFC, its menu), and its choice
    is still `=value`. Test: t_tree (Chromium: the typed path found by `--find`, in `--json`, a
    closed select `=two`).
566. **`omabox log` read a hyprland.log that lagged what Hyprland had logged** (2026-10-31, #328).
    Hyprland 0.56 logs through hyprutils' CLogger into a file stream it never flushes: the file
    grows in 8 KiB steps (measured: 191887 bytes, unchanged through a reload and 35 s, then 200081
    after 30 more reloads), so the last 0-8 KiB of lines are only in Hyprland's memory. Its rolling
    log (`hyprctl rollinglog`, the last ~4 KiB, whole lines, byte for byte as the file gets them) has
    them: in a fresh box its first 745 bytes were the file's last, and 3335 bytes past it were in
    no file. `log --grep` for a reload's or a plugin's lines found nothing, as if they never came
    (the issue's frozen file was this; plain sessions show it too). Now `log hyprland` of a live box
    (not `--crash`, not `-f`) asks `timeout 2 hyprctl rollinglog` and adds what is past the file's
    end: the longest overlap of the file's end with rollinglog's start, at least rollinglog's first
    line (a file ending mid-line in "DEB" is not an overlap with "DEBUG ]: ..."). No overlap means
    the file is behind by more than 4 KiB (about half the time, as the buffer fills to 8): rollinglog
    is added after it and stderr says the lines between are in neither yet. `-f` still follows the
    file (`tail -F`), which gets them in 8 KiB pieces, as the reference says. Tests: the unit test
    `rolled` (an overlap added, mid-line ends, no overlap, a chance overlap of part of a line,
    repeated lines not doubled); t_log_rolling (a `[Lua]` print not in the file yet: in `log --grep`,
    once in `-n all`; it fails on the old code).
567. **"listed but not enabled" for a running service, and for a widget another plugin places**
    (2026-10-31, #326). The shell's `listPlugins` gives a plugin with a bar widget `enabled:
    inBar(id)` (what `omarchy plugin enable/disable` toggles), not whether the shell loaded it. So a
    service with a widget (a notification plugin), loaded from its own `plugins[]` entry with its
    widget off the bar, was warned as disabled at every up and restart-shell; so was a widget another
    plugin places through its own config and IPC, where shell.json does not show it (finding 197's
    `hosted` covers only a widget in a mounted plugin's entry). Now plugin_check asks what the
    registry's `isEnabled` asks: a plugin with a widget and another kind, in its own `plugins[]`
    entry and not in `disabledPlugins`, is `loaded` (a service) or `enabled`, unsaid. A widget in no
    layout while another mounted plugin runs with more than a bar widget (a service, panel, bar...)
    gets a note naming those plugins, how to check and how to put it in the bar
    (`putBarWidget ID '{}'`), not a warning: its state is `off the bar`. With no such plugin it is
    still a warning, now "disabled: not in the bar's layout", with the same `putBarWidget` line
    (a plugin without a widget keeps "listed but not enabled"). Test: t_plugin_hosted (a service
    fixture answering on its IPC while it reads loaded; on the old code: both warned).
568. **up on a GPU that renders only in software said only "died while starting"** (2026-10-31,
    #396). On a VM's virtio-gpu without virgl (finding 538) wlroots, in labwc, finds the node's EGL
    device is software and refuses it ("Software rendering detected, please use the
    WLR_RENDERER_ALLOW_SOFTWARE environment variable"); its GLES2 renderer fails, Vulkan finds no
    device, and labwc goes on with pixman, which offers no dmabuf: the box's Hyprland (labwc's -S
    child, its stdout in labwc.log, so no hyprland.log) aborts with `CBackend::create() failed!` and
    the box ends in under a second. None of died_starting's reasons was there. It now reads the head
    of labwc.log (256 KiB, through box_home_file) first: that line says "a box needs GPU rendering:
    NODE renders in software only (no 3D acceleration)"; the GLES2 renderer's "Could not initialize
    EGL" without it says "labwc found no EGL on NODE (EGL: its first message)". NODE is box.json's
    render node; on virtio_gpu it adds install.sh's virgl line, and with another GPU here (other_gpu)
    `OMABOX_RENDER_NODE=… omabox up --new`, as the llvmpipe note does. The same reason goes into
    "Hyprland not up after Ns" when the box hangs instead (made here: Mesa's GBM forced to software on
    the RTX, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 GBM_BACKEND=dri`, where Vulkan comes up and Hyprland waits).
    Reproduced on this machine without a VM: `--env __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES=/nonexistent.json
    --env VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/nonexistent.json` fails the same way on any GPU (no EGL, no Vulkan,
    pixman, the abort). The box is still left dead for its logs (finding 63). Not done: choosing
    another node up front when `gpu` is auto and the first one is software (a choice for Diogo).
    Tests: t_unit_up_software (ready.rs died_starting_says_a_software_render_node: the reason, the
    node, the VM line, the logs, and as before without them; render_why_cases), t_up_software (a real
    box with no EGL: said, with its node).
572. **down continued the processes that entered a box by pid number** (2026-10-31, #377). kill_box
    lists them (procfs `entered`: the box's user namespace, not its pid namespace), SIGKILLs PID 1,
    then SIGCONTs each so a stopped launcher can reap its command. A pid that ended between the
    list and the SIGCONT, and was taken by a stopped job of the user's, was continued; PID 1's
    SIGKILL, pasta's and its child's had the same gap after their checks (box_pid, box_pasta).
    Each is now pinned by a pidfd (`pidfd.rs`'s `Pidfd::pin`: open, check again through /proc,
    then the pidfd still alive, so what the check read was that process) and signalled through
    it; the wait for PID 1's end is the pidfd's too. Test: ready.rs's kill_box_continues_no_reused_pid
    (re-run in a pid namespace of its own, `unshare -Urpf`, where ns_last_pid makes the pid be
    reused: the stopped job stays stopped), failed on the old code; t_unit_rust_ignored runs it.
    The same gap, closed the same way: down's SIGTERM to the box's peek windows (pinned, then found
    peeks again), kill_tree (shot's and settle's stuck tools: each pinned while its parent's child),
    save's SIGSTOP/SIGCONT of the box and `run --replace`'s TERM/KILL (each pinned while in the box's
    pid namespace, `jobs.rs`'s `pin_in_box`), and the followers `log -f`/`events -f` end on a
    signal (a pidfd kept from their start, signalled from the handler). The kills left by number
    are safe: to this process, to an unreaped child of ours or its group, or a signal-0 probe.
    Tests: down's down_ends_only_a_peek_still_one and settle's kill_tree_ends_only_our_children,
    both failed on the old code; jobs' pinned_only_in_the_box.
573. **A down by another omabox left the box's reaper running** (2026-10-31, #383). kill_reapers
    found a box's reaper by its command line only, `ROOT/bin/omabox _reap NAME ...` with the ROOT of
    the omabox running `down`, so a down from a package of a box a checkout started (or from
    another worktree) left the reaper until its next poll saw the box gone. The reaper now writes
    its pid and start time to `<box dir>/reaper.pid` (written whole, renamed into place) once it
    knows it stays; kill_reapers ends that one first, while its start time is the recorded one and
    its words are a reaper of NAME with any ROOT (`reaper_of`), then the command-line matches as
    before, each through a pidfd. A reaper of an older omabox has no record: the pattern only, as
    before. A down in the moment before a new reaper wrote its record falls back the same way. Test:
    ready.rs's kill_reapers_by_their_record (another ROOT's recorded reaper ended; a record naming
    another box's reaper, or with the wrong start, ends nothing), failed on the old code.
574. **A save SIGKILLed during its copy left the box paused** (2026-10-31, #369). `save` stops the
    box (SIGSTOP to its pid namespace, finding 470) and lets it go on every way out a trap sees: a
    refusal, a failure, INT, TERM, HUP. A SIGKILL (or the OOM killer) runs none, and the box stayed
    stopped, read as hung by every later call, until someone sent SIGCONT by hand. Now, before it
    stops the box, the save starts a watch, `omabox _save-watch NS PID...` (main.rs's first lines, as
    `_enter`; refused through the broker), in a session of its own (setsid: a kill of the save's
    process group or session misses it), its stdin a close-on-exec pipe only the save writes. It
    takes a pidfd of each of the box's processes (the pids the save pinned, #377, each kept only
    while it is in the box's pid namespace NS once its pidfd is open), says `ready` (no ready, no save: "could not start
    the watch"), and waits. The save resumes the box, then writes it a byte, and the watch ends; its
    stdin closing with nothing written means the save died without letting go, and the watch sends
    SIGCONT through the pidfds (never to a process that took one of their pids since). Test:
    t_save_killed (a `cp` of the test's first in PATH holds the copy open; the save SIGKILLed in it:
    the box runs again within 5 s, the watch gone; a save after it works and clears the killed one's
    copy). It failed before the fix: the box stayed stopped.
575. **S1's self-check looked only at where each of the box's mounts is** (2026-10-31, #363; the
    check is finding 456's). It took each mount point of the started box's mountinfo through
    seat_path with no runtime dir: a `/dev/dri` folder bound whole (its cards inside, the mount point
    `/dev/dri` no seat path), a seat path bound at another destination (`/dev/input` at `/opt/x`) and
    a mount inside the runtime dir's path (a host `wayland-1` at `/run/user/UID/wayland-1`) all
    passed. Now (up_box.rs's seat_mounts, dri_seat, seat_rdev): each mount's source is named through
    omabox's own mountinfo (the mount of the same major:minor whose root holds the box mount's root,
    that mount point plus the rest), and a source that is a seat path or holds one ends the box at
    whatever destination it has (one in the box's own dir is its own: run dir, placeholder, covers);
    any mount point strictly under the runtime dir's path ends it (the box's own run dir is at the
    path itself, still compared by inode); every `card*` in the box's `/dev/dri` must be the empty
    placeholder file; and a character device mounted under `/dev` (or from a devtmpfs) that is a
    card (226, minor below 128) or an input device (13) by its number ends it. Device numbers are
    looked at only there: a stat of every mount point could wait on a FUSE or network folder bound
    in. A source no mount of omabox's shows (the box's own tmpfs, an overlay) is not named; the
    binds' own refusals stay the first line (none of these was ever made by `up`). The mountinfo of
    omabox itself that cannot be read fails closed too. Tests: up_box.rs's unit tests
    seat_mounts_a_box_as_up_makes_it_passes, seat_mounts_finds_the_seat_by_source_and_place (15
    fixtures; failed on the old check), seat_mounts_without_a_runtime_dir, seat_devices_by_number,
    dri_cards_must_be_placeholders; t_seat_check (a stand-in runtime dir with a folder of the test's
    bound inside it: refused, its processes gone; an older omabox started that box). A test with a
    stand-in `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` must give `XDG_CACHE_HOME` one too: up's sweep_homes removes every
    HOME whose box its runtime dir does not have, which is every real box's.
576. **A signal's undo could run alongside main's in-process work** (2026-10-31, #367; found in the
    port's review, not seen happen). A trap's thread waited for main's foreground child
    (finding 453), but with none running it began the undo at once while main went on until its
    next child or sleep: `up` making its box dir or seeding the HOME (what were bash's `mkdir -p` and
    `cp` children, which bash's trap waited for) could make a dir again after the undo removed it,
    a box dir with no box.json. In a busy section of main's (sig::busy: `up` from its dir's making
    on) the thread now also waits until main is at rest (parked for the stop, or waiting for the
    foreground lock), bounded by the same first 10 s, after which the undo goes on regardless, said
    as a stop that waits is said. Only there: a first try waited for main everywhere and broke
    shot's cleanup on a signal (#386's t_unit_signal_cleanup cases: the PNG left), as shot's main
    waits in-process for the very capture its undo stops. Tests: sig.rs's
    term_waits_for_mains_in_process_work (the undo sees a file main made 300 ms after the TERM),
    mains_endless_in_process_work_is_bounded and an_undo_outside_a_busy_section_runs_at_once;
    t_up_signals (a TERM or HUP while up seeds the HOME).
577. **`jail_read` opened a jailed caller's path before checking where it led** (2026-10-31, #367;
    found in the port's review). It opened the path (O_NONBLOCK, no O_NOCTTY), then read back where
    the fd led and refused one outside the jail's folders: a link inside to a file outside had that
    file opened (a device's open run, a terminal possibly made the controlling one), and a file
    inside was read whole, however big. It now finds where the path leads first without looking
    outside them (jail_path), opens that as a path only (O_PATH, O_NOFOLLOW), checks the fd (inside,
    not hidden, a regular file), and only then opens it again through the fd to read (O_NONBLOCK,
    O_NOCTTY), at most 1 MiB (a plugin's manifest, a .git file, a commondir); a bigger one is
    refused. Test: jailpath.rs's read_opens_nothing_outside_and_is_bounded (inotify sees no open of
    the file outside nor of a FIFO inside; 1 MiB read, a byte more refused).
579. **A down from another pid namespace did not cancel an up made just before it** (2026-10-31,
    #404, left from #380 and finding 513). In a tie (one 10 ms tick), finding 513 orders a down and an
    up by their pids, which holds only in one pid namespace; a down of another one fell back to the
    calls' wall-clock times, which is the fault 513 fixed: an up made first but slower to its first
    line than the whole down read as started after it, and its box survived the down. With the up 6
    ms busy before its exec and the down in `unshare -Upf --mount-proc`, 6 in 6 at 24d53d6. (The
    issue's case, the user's down against a jailed agent's up, is not one: a jailed caller's commands
    run in the broker, a child of the user's systemd, in the user's pid namespace, so 513's pid order
    already decides it.) **Fix** (Rust): the down's marker line gets two more fields, CLOCK_BOOTTIME in
    µs as it writes the marker and the time namespace it read it in (`... CALL_US BOOT_US
    time:[NS]`); the up takes, first thing in main, when it was made at the latest
    (procfs::made_us: CLOCK_BOOTTIME less its thread's CPU time, CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, and its
    wait for a CPU, schedstat's run_delay, both counted from the fork; a sleep, a read from disk, is
    the only thing left out, and it makes the time later, never earlier). Of another pid namespace
    and the same time namespace, the down came when the up was made by then. CLOCK_BOOTTIME is one
    clock for all pid namespaces and no wall-clock step moves it. Measured: 10 cancels in 10; `down
    B` (other namespace) then `up B`, 7 of 8 in one tick: 8 boxes up in 8. Left: a marker of the
    start alone (a bash down's, an omabox older than 1.0) is still read against its mtime, the
    issue's case 2, until 0.x relays are no longer expected (Diogo's call). An older 1.0.x up reads
    the first four fields only. Tests: t_race ("a down of another pid namespace while its up starts",
    fails at 24d53d6), up.rs's a_down_of_another_pid_namespace_by_boot_time, down_lines,
    made_us_is_before_now_and_after_boot.
    Two more found on the way, both fixed. **A pid namespace with the host's /proc** (`unshare -pf`
    without --mount-proc): down and up read their start from /proc/<own pid>, there another process,
    pid 1 the host's init; a down's marker said init's start (older than any up) and an up took it
    for its own, so every down of its name in 10 minutes cancelled it. Both read /proc/self now.
    **The relay hop:** a jailed agent's up is the process the broker forks once the caller's relay
    has connected, a few ms (or, for a slow caller, any time) after the agent's call; a user's down
    in between found no lock, left its marker, and the up, made after it, went on. A broker's up is
    now its caller's: the pid and start of OMABOX_BROKER_PEER, which the relay's listen sets from the
    socket's SO_PEERCRED (the kernel's, in the broker's pid namespace; nothing the caller sends can
    set it, its variables come renamed OMABOX_RELAY_*), its start read between two looks through the
    caller's pidfd (broker_side::caller). A jail can only make its call look older than it was (a
    process it made earlier connects), which cancels its own up sooner, never the user's. Tests:
    t_race ("a down in a pid namespace with the host's /proc", "...an up there", both fail at
    df286ca), t_jail_down_race (a real ai-jail: a caller that sleeps a second before it connects, the
    down in that second; at df286ca the box came up).
581. **Protected ports: an address the host gained after up was reachable** (2026-10-31, #399 item
    2; S10). The nft rule pasta's shell sets (finding 459) listed the host's addresses as `up` read
    them, so a server on all addresses (0.0.0.0, `::`) on a protected port was reached from a box
    through any address the host gained later: a VPN coming up, a docker network made. `fib daddr
    type local`, the issue's first option, cannot do it: the rule runs in the box's network
    namespace, whose fib knows the box's own addresses (pasta copies the host's main one onto the
    box's tap), not the host's bridge or VPN ones. The rule now matches two named sets (`@host4`,
    `@host6`, both rules there even with no IPv6 address at up), and the box's reaper keeps them the
    host's: it hears of every address the host gains or loses on a netlink socket
    (RTMGRP_IPV4_IFADDR, _IPV6_IFADDR; poll(2) wakes it on the event; without the socket, a look
    every second), reads the addresses again and, when they differ from what it last set, flushes
    and fills both sets in one nft transaction. nft runs in pasta's user and network namespaces,
    entered through a pidfd of pasta's child (the box's bwrap; `Entry::pasta`), without root: the
    user owns pasta's user namespace. Nothing of the box can see or change that process. Addresses
    the host loses leave the sets. The kernel sends an IPv4 address's event before it adds or
    removes that address's local route (`__inet_insert_ifa`/`__inet_del_ifa` notify, then the
    inetaddr chain updates the fib), so a reaper woken by it could read /proc/net/fib_trie a moment
    early: t_protect_ports_ns caught an address the host lost still in the set, once in three runs.
    host_addrs now adds the links' IPv4 addresses from an RTM_GETADDR dump (already the new list at
    the event; fib_trie's local routes stay for an address that is only a local route), and the
    reaper looks once more 250 ms after each event, for a lost one fib_trie still had. Since then
    nine runs, three at once, passed. A connected box with a protected port now always gets a reaper
    (box.json `protect`: true, only that it has the rule, not which ports, #374), which says so in
    reap.log. A security review then found two gaps, both fixed (reap.rs's Sched). (1) A look that
    failed (the reaper's first, were pasta not up yet; nft refusing) was tried again only at the next
    address event or poll (5-60 s): an address gained meanwhile stayed out of the rule that long. It
    is now tried again 250 ms after, doubling to 2 s while it fails, with no event needed; a failure
    is said once in reap.log, and "set again" once one works. (2) Nothing limited the looks: every
    batch of address events was a fib read, a dump and maybe an nft run in every protected box's
    reaper, and the nft run had no timeout, so a hung nft stalled the reaper's polls (its box's
    teardown among them). Events now make at most one look per 250 ms (the first at once), with one
    more 250 ms after the last (which also covers fib_trie's lag above); nft is killed after 5 s
    ("nft did not answer in 5 s: killed"), a failure as any other. Not covered: a connection in the
    moment between the host gaining an address and the reaper's nft (15-30 ms here for a lone
    change, five added, measured from outside; up to 250 ms more in a burst), while a failing nft
    keeps the addresses last set, and after the reaper is killed.
    Tests: t_protect_ports_ns (two addresses added to the test's own network namespace after up,
    v4 and v6: their protected port not reached, TCP or UDP, within 5 s in the rule, the port not
    protected reached; one removed leaves the set; failed before: reached on all four, the set
    unchanged; then a second box whose reaper's nft is a stand-in under a mount namespace of the
    test's own: failing, an address gained meanwhile is in the rule within 3 s of nft working, with
    no event since; 40 changes over 2 s are 9 nft runs; one that hangs is killed and the address
    set after; each failed before: 60 s, 40 runs, never killed), reap.rs `guard_looks_when` (the
    schedule: at once, one per 250 ms, the trailing look, the failures' waits), net.rs `rules` (the
    sets, protect_sets' transaction) and `link_addresses` (the dump's parsing; this machine's links'
    addresses all in fib_trie).
582. **Protected ports tested over UDP and IPv6, without root** (2026-10-31, #399 item 1; S10).
    t_protect_ports checked TCP only, and IPv6 only where the host has a global IPv6 address. The new
    t_protect_ports_ns runs everything in a network namespace of the test's own (a user namespace's,
    no root): dummy links with the addresses pasta copies into the box (d0: 10.239.0.1, fd39::1, the
    default routes) and a second set as a docker bridge's or a VPN's (d1: 10.239.1.1, fd39:1::1). up
    runs there as the user (a user namespace mapped back, as protect_ports_nft's), so its pasta and
    reaper take that namespace for the host; the servers (TCP and UDP on `[::]`, v4 and v6) too. The
    real host's network is never touched. Checked from the box: a protected port on d1's IPv4 and
    IPv6 addresses and over its loopback not reached, TCP or UDP, the port not protected reached on
    each (the control).
584. **An `up` with another runtime dir removed the HOMEs of running boxes** (2026-10-31). Box HOMEs
    live in the cache (`~/.cache/omabox/NAME`), box dirs in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omabox`. `sweep_homes`
    took a HOME as gone when this runtime dir had no box dir of its name, so an `up` with another one
    (a test's stand-in, another login) and the same cache removed every running box's HOME: it
    happened to two of them that day. `up`'s own `rm_box` likewise removed (then shared) the HOME of a
    box of the same name in another runtime dir. Now `up` writes a record beside the HOME
    (`NAME/box-dir`: the box dir, written before the HOME is made) and a HOME is swept only when the
    box dir its record names is not there and no process uses it: no mount namespace has it mounted
    (each one's mountinfo, by device and root in that file system: a box binds it at `/home/sbx`) and
    nothing has it as its cwd, root or an open file. A HOME with no record (an older omabox's) goes
    only when this runtime dir has no box of its name and nothing uses it. `rm_box` takes the HOME only
    when it is this box's (its record, or for an older one this box dir's `home` link) or no box's,
    and `up` of a name whose HOME is another box's is refused, saying where that box is or that the
    HOME is in use. No other sweeper judges by the runtime dir alone: `.down-`/`.expired-` markers live
    in it, save leftovers go by their writer's pid, failed-run logs by count. Not covered: an omabox
    in a pid namespace of its own that sees neither the runtime dir a box was made in nor its
    processes still takes it as gone. Tests: t_home_sweep (a second `up` with a stand-in runtime and
    state dir and the same cache: the first box's HOME kept, read by the box; a gone box's HOME and an
    unused older one taken; the same name refused; an older box's HOME, its record removed, kept while
    the box runs), t_unit_rm_tree's record cases, homeuse.rs's `a_bound_home_is_used`.
587. **A `run -d` job could be stopped or waited for only by a host pgrep** (2026-10-31, #299). Five
    agents needed to stop, swap or wait for one job and found no command: one ran a host `pgrep -f`
    loop, telling the box's process from the same program on the desktop by `/proc/PID/environ`, and
    a second try matched its own bash and killed it; others waited with `wait until -- sh -c '!
    pgrep -f …'` (it matched itself) or a sleep loop over `run-*.log`. `--replace` with other
    arguments said "still runs: stop it" with no command for it, and did not say it started the new
    job beside it. Now `run -d` says the job's pid ("started in box 'B' (pid N, log: …)"); `omabox
    jobs [--json]` lists the running jobs from their records (PID, AGE from the log's name, PROCS of
    its session, LOG, COMMAND); `omabox stop PID... | --all` stops them as `--replace` does (one
    `job_stop` for both now), a PID being the job's or any of its session's in the box (a window's).
    Its signals, and `--replace`'s, which sent kill(2) to a host pid number, go through a pidfd: the
    pid is opened first, then /proc of it checked to be the listed process (the box's pid namespace,
    its NSpid there, its start time); a pid reused before the open shows another process there, so
    it is never signalled. `wait job [PID] [--gone]` (no PID: the latest job) is satisfied once the
    command's status file (share/run-job.sh's) is written or nothing of it runs, with how it ended;
    `--gone` waits for its whole session. To answer for a job that ended and was dealt with, its
    record now moves to `$D/jobs-done/` instead of being deleted, so `wait job PID` after the end is
    satisfied at once rather than "no such job". `wait log [PID] RE [-i]` greps the job's log inside
    the box (`timeout 2 grep -m1 -E`, the box's file read as the box sees it, 4 KiB at most kept),
    every 100 ms; a job already gone with no matching line is unknown (exit 1): the job's end is read
    before its log, so a line written as it ended is not missed. `--replace`'s note now reads
    "no earlier job with these arguments, none stopped; X (pid N, ARGS) still runs, and the new job
    starts beside it (omabox -b B stop N stops it)". Tests: jobs.rs `jobs_lookups` (records, the
    latest, jobs-done, a job by any pid of its session, ages); t_jobs (list, stop by a window's pid,
    a pid that is no job's refused, wait job on an exit 3, again after it was said, a launcher with
    --gone, wait log -i, a line that never comes, a job that ended without it, a bad expression,
    stop --all); t_replace and t_cli_box's lines updated. The old binary has none of these commands
    (`jobs`: unknown command).
588. **A host path the box does not have failed in it with no word of why** (2026-10-31, #301). Agents
    passed `run` the path run -d had printed for its log (`<dir>/home/run-NS.log`), `$(omabox path
    --home)/…`, a scratch file under the host's /tmp, a `--plugin` folder's helper by the path given
    to `--plugin` (the box has it at `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/ID`), and `env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<build
    dir>` (the app quietly loaded the system's library). Each failed, or did something else, with an
    error naming the file and not the cause. `run` (on a box up, -d and a throwaway's) now looks at
    the absolute paths its command names (a word, a `KEY=VAL` or `--opt=VAL` value split on `:`, a
    `sh -c` script's words; `--env`/`--env-file` values too; 64 words) and says, before it runs, what
    each is in the box: the box HOME's or runtime dir's host path, with the path in the box ("note: P
    is box 'B''s HOME as the host has it (omabox path --home): in the box it is /home/sbx/X"); the box
    folder, which the box does not see; a file in a mounted plugin's folder or a `DIR:DEST` bind
    (box.json's `plugin_dirs`/`plugin_via` and `mounts`), with its path there; else one the host has
    and the box's root (`/proc/PID/root`) does not, with the box HOME or the `--ro-bind` of its folder
    as the way in (`down, then up …`; a throwaway's `run --ro-bind …`), or why a box may not mount it
    (refuse_src: /dev, the runtime dir…). 3 notes at most, then a count; not for a jailed caller (as
    #235, #251). A path the command makes in the box that the host has too is said as well (true, if
    not needed). run -d's "started" line names the log as the box has it too ("(log: HOST, /home/sbx/
    run-NS.log in the box)"; `--print-log` still prints the host path alone), and `up` says where a
    `--plugin` folder it mounts at its id is ("note: plugin ID: DIR is /home/sbx/.config/omarchy/
    plugins/ID in the box, not at its own path"; not for one linked to its own path, finding 241).
    `wait until` has its own note since #400 (wait.rs's host_path_note), left as it is. Not done:
    `path --home` saying on stderr that the path is the host's (the issue's "could"): every call
    would print it, and the agents' scripts read it with `$(…)`; run's note says it where it matters.
    Tests: repo.rs host_path_words_found, host_path_said; t_host_paths (each shape in a real box and
    a throwaway); t_cli_box's run -d cases. A path in /proc is never noted: the box has a /proc of
    its own, which the host cannot read as the box does (`/proc/PID/root/proc/self` is the reader's),
    so `run -- readlink /proc/self/fd/0` was told its stdin "is not in the box" (found by the full

    /home/sbx/run-NS.log in the box)".
589. **An app the compositor dropped for a protocol error just "exited"** (2026-10-31, #335). When
    Hyprland (libwayland-server) closes a client for a protocol error, libwayland-client writes the
    error event to stderr before the app's next dispatch fails: `INTERFACE#ID: error CODE: MESSAGE`
    (wayland 1.26 here; `@ID` in older ones; `[destroyed object]: error …` for an object the client
    had let go). A `run -d` job's stderr is its log, so the reason was one line deep in it while
    omabox said "exited with status 1". Now every place that says a job's end (job_ended: run -d's
    first moments and run -d --wait's unsettled end; job_note: the next command's warning) adds
    "its Wayland connection was closed for a protocol error: LINE", the last such line in the log's
    last 64 KiB, from where it starts in its line (a toolkit's prefix left out), control characters
    as spaces, 300 characters at most. The log is in the box HOME, which the box writes: read on the
    host through box_home_file, opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and taken only as a regular file (S7).
    A `wait window`/`wait layer` that gives up (124) runs job_note too, so a job that died during
    the wait is said by the wait, not by the command after it. Hyprland's own words for the bind of
    a global that is not there are "global wl_compositor (N) is unavailable" (older
    libwayland-server: "invalid global"). GTK 4.24 and Qt 6.12 keep libwayland's line off stderr
    (each sets its own wl_log handler; seen in a box): a GTK app writes only "Gdk-Message: TIME:
    Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display.", a Qt app only "The Wayland
    connection experienced a fatal error: Protocol error". So with no libwayland line, the last
    toolkit line is said, as what it is: a protocol error only where it says so (GTK's errno 71,
    EPROTO, in any locale; Qt's strerror text "Protocol error", which follows the app's locale, so a
    Qt app in pt_BR writes "Erro de protocolo" and is said as "its Wayland connection failed: …", as
    is any other errno); a connection shut down (GTK "Lost connection to Wayland compositor.", Qt
    "The Wayland connection broke. Did the Wayland compositor die?") as "its Wayland connection was
    lost: …". libwayland's line wins over a toolkit's (it names the object). Tests:
    t_unit_proto_error (jobs.rs proto_line_found, wl_end_words, job_note_says_proto_error: the line,
    a prefix, the last of two, each toolkit line as GTK and Qt wrote it, a link not read),
    t_proto_error (a fixture client built by the test binds a global that does not exist: run -d,
    --wait, the next command's note and `wait window` say it; a plain failure does not; a GTK 4 and
    a Qt 6 fixture make the same bad bind through their toolkit, or shut their connection down: each
    said as a protocol error or as lost; on the old code 5, then 4 checks failed).

591. **One window at a width took three hand-made dispatches** (2026-10-31, #362). Checking an app

592. **`click --in SHOT` clicked whatever had come over the point since the shot** (2026-10-31, #333).
    `--in` mapped the shot's pixel to the screen (finding 81) and checked only the file, the mode and
    a window shot's window; a menu, a dialog or a tiled neighbour that opened since took the click.
    Now every screen shot (whole, `-g`, `--monitor`, `--changed`'s; not `--burst` frames) reads the
    desktop beside its capture (desk_snap, started just before grim: one batched hyprctl read) and
    writes it, with the pointer, to `$D/layouts.tsv` under the shot's path and stamp (the last 20
    kept past 40; a snapshot is a few KB). `click`, `scroll`, `drag` (both ends) and `pointer` `--in`
    a screen shot read the desktop now and ask DESK_TARGET_JQ (the click report's, finding 561's
    fullscreen rule included) what is at the point in each: its kind, window, layer and point in the
    window, plus the window's size. Any difference is refused before anything is sent, exit 1:
    "click --in: the screen changed at X,Y since SHOT: then on foot "A" (its 388,238; the window
    1896x1056), now on layer t333-panel (over foot "A") (since the shot: layer t333-panel opened);
    take a new shot" (the since part is DESK_FACTS_JQ's line). *Chosen* for the issue's open
    question: only a change at the point refuses; a toast, a clock or a window opening away from it
    does not (a screen-wide digest would refuse after every notification). The window's size is in
    it because a window tiled beside a new one keeps its corner but lays its content out again. A
    window shot is not checked: its point follows the window and raises it (Raise), and its gone
    and resized refusals stay. A layer spanning the screen counts by its namespace only (finding
    562: a toast inside Omarchy 4.5's mapped notifications column is not seen). A shot with no
    layout line (an older omabox's, a `--burst` frame) or a desktop that cannot be read is not
    checked. Tests: shotcmp.rs layout_at_the_point (a window over the point, one elsewhere, the
    window moved, resized, a layer), t_in_changed (a quickshell panel over the point: click,
    pointer, scroll and drag refused with nothing sent; away from it and after a new shot clicked;
    a tiled window opening; the panel gone; a window's shot not checked). It fails on the old code.
593. **`wait change` missed a change made just before it started; there was no "since this shot"**
    (2026-10-31, #344). omabox-still compares each frame with the one before, from its first: a
    redraw the shell finished before that frame (after an edit to `shell.json`, an IPC call) was
    no change, and the wait timed out. Now `wait change --since SHOT` starts the tool, and once it
    has its first frame takes a new frame of what SHOT covers the way shot took it (grim -l 1, `-g`
    for a part of the screen, `-T stableId` twice for a window, finding 81) and compares it with
    SHOT (shots.rs diff_box, as `shot --changed --since`): a difference answers at once ("changed
    since SHOT at X,Y WxH; seen after 0.16s"), else the tool's first change does; a change between
    the two frames is in the second, so nothing falls between. `wait still --like SHOT` takes a new
    frame every 200 ms until one has no difference ("like SHOT after Ns"; 124 says the last
    difference). Shared with #333 in shotcmp.rs: reading a shot (load, which shot_point now uses),
    the pointer then (layouts.tsv). No difference: `--ignore`'s regions, the pointer where it was
    and where it is (a screen shot draws it), `-g`'s outside, and unless `--strict` a caret alone
    (caret_shaped, the 4 px by 40 rule of tools/still and `--changed`, now one function). A clock in
    the region is a difference (left to `--ignore`, as for `wait still`). Refused: a shot scaled or
    zoomed (its image size is not what is captured now), a crop of a window, `-g` with a window's
    shot or outside the shot, `--window`, `--like` with `--quiet`, from a jailed agent (the path is
    the jail's, as for `shot --since`). Tests: t_wait_since (the issue's case: a plain `wait change`
    124, `--since` at once; `-g`, a crop, a window's shot, `--json`, `--like` while different and
    back after BackSpace, a blinking beam caret alone, refusals), t_unit_wait (the usage refusals).
    They fail on the old code.
594. **A plugin into a box that is up: `plugin add`, `plugin remove`** (2026-10-31, #345). To check
    a plugin in a box started without it, an agent linked its folder into the box HOME's
    `plugins/<id>`, ran `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins`, then `omarchy plugin enable <id>`, which
    kept saying "plugin '<id>' is not known; run: omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins". Settled in a box:
    a hand-made link to a folder the box has at its own path (in its repo) does load; the enable failed
    because it ran before the rescan was done (the race of finding 539: `rescanPlugins` returns before
    its scan, and the enable 1 s later worked). A link to a folder the box does not have can never
    load, and a host `omarchy-shell` reaches the desk's shell, not the box's. `omabox plugin add
    PATH|ID [-b NAME]` now does what `up --plugin` does: the plugin resolved as up resolves it,
    refused where up refuses it (bwrap.rs's checked_ro: refuse_src and the seat's paths), linked from
    the box HOME when the box has it at its own path (finding 241's rule, own_path_among, over
    box.json's `mounts`, each one's source still the folder up bound: one deleted and made again is
    the old one in the box, #391), else mounted read-only; then the shell rescans and is listed until
    it lists the plugin (4 s), `omarchy plugin enable`, and plugin_check's words and plugin_status.
    `plugin remove ID` takes out one the box has (up's too): `setPluginEnabled false` while it is
    listed, unmounted or unlinked, rescanned, box.json without it. The mount (latemount.rs): bwrap
    mounts in the user namespace that owns the box's mount namespace (its first; the box's PID 1 runs
    in a second one inside it, for --uid), so `setns` straight into the box's user and mount
    namespaces was refused (EPERM: from the inner one there is no capability over the mount
    namespace), and an `open_tree` clone made in a user namespace of our own could not be attached
    there (`move_mount` EPERM). A child joins the owning namespace (found with NS_GET_USERNS on the
    box's mount namespace, read while a pidfd of its PID 1 shows it alive), makes a mount namespace
    there, opens the folder with no link followed (openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS) and clones it
    (open_tree, recursive), sets it read-only, nosuid, nodev as bwrap's --ro-bind is, enters the box's
    mount namespace through the pidfd and attaches it at `plugins/<id>`, opened with no link followed
    and no mount crossed (RESOLVE_NO_XDEV): the box HOME is the box's to write, so a link there never
    takes the mount elsewhere and nothing is mounted over a mount. The box can neither unmount it nor
    make it writable (checked). A first version checked the clone by reading its fd's path back,
    which for a detached tree is "/": every mount was refused. What the box HOME holds is read and
    written from inside the box (on_box). A link made by hand is replaced (said); a folder there
    that is not omabox's (an `omarchy plugin add` clone) is left, refused. Not for a jailed caller
    (the broker refuses commands it does not list): `up --plugin` there. A security review found
    three gaps, fixed the same day: (1) the mount joined PID 1's namespaces as they were then; where
    ptrace is allowed a box process could have PID 1 unshare a user and mount namespace of the box's
    own, and the mount, attached there, could be made writable. up now records PID 1's mount
    namespace and its owner's inodes in box.json (`mount_ns`) when bwrap names it, before anything of
    the box runs; plugin add/remove refuse other ones (a box from before has none: down, up), and the
    child joins the mount namespace through the fd checked, not PID 1's. (2) An unjailed `plugin
    add` on a jail's box mounted without the jail's covers (S9): refused now (box.json's `jail`),
    `up --plugin` there. (3) Text of the box's (a replaced link's target, `omarchy plugin enable`'s
    words) reached the terminal raw, escape sequences included (OSC 52): its control characters but
    newline and tab, and bytes that are not UTF-8, are `?`, 400 bytes at most; the in-box scripts'
    stderr is dropped. `up NAME --plugin X` on a
    box without X (finding 134) now names `omabox plugin add X -b NAME`. Tests: t_plugin_add (one
    outside the box mounted read-only, nosuid, nodev, the box unable to unmount or remount it, in
    the shell and its bar, loaded; one in the repo linked, its helper reaching the repo; the same
    again said, another dir with the id refused; the issue's hand-made link replaced and enabled at
    once; a folder not omabox's left; a plugin in the runtime dir refused; remove of a mounted, a
    linked and an up --plugin one, then added back; a link put on the mount's way by the box: refused,
    nothing mounted where it leads; an OSC 52 link target said with ?; a changed mount_ns record
    and a jail's record refused), t_unit_plugin_cmd (usage errors, a box not up), latemount.rs's
    only_the_namespaces_up_recorded and ns_ids_reads_a_process, plugin.rs's
    plain_keeps_escapes_off_the_terminal,
    cmd::plugin's unit tests (linked only through a same-path mount still bound), broker_check (a
    jailed caller refused), t_up_again (the new words). On the old code `plugin` is an unknown
    command (exit 2).
595. **The accessibility tree had no wait: agents polled `tree --find` in loops** (2026-10-31, #319).
    `wait until -- …` runs in the box and cannot read the tree, so sessions wrote `for …; omabox tree
    --find X; sleep 0.4` loops, background loops to catch a short-lived alert, `while omabox tree
    --find TITLE | grep -q dialog` to time a sheet. `wait tree TEXT [--window SEL | --layer SEL]
    [--gone] [--shot FILE]` (treewait.rs, a poll_until probe) reads the tree with omabox-tree --find
    TEXT, its matching unchanged, every ~100 ms in the window SEL picks (none: the active one, picked
    again each read) or on the layer: satisfied at the first read holding TEXT (one read, so a state of
    a second is caught; the line gives the line holding it), `--gone` at two reads in a row without
    it (as a window's gone, one read mid-rebuild is not an answer) or when the window or layer is
    gone. A window not there yet or not on the bus yet (no tree, exit 3/5/6/7) is waited for, said at
    the 124; no accessibility bus, a read that hung, several windows matching are said at once (1, 2).
    The 124 says what the tree had instead: the lines holding TEXT's name (its first "quoted" part,
    else what comes before ` [`, ` '`, ` =`), read once at the end, else omabox-tree's words.
    `--shot FILE` (shot -o FILE, its stdout held back; refused in ai-jail as drag --shot is) is taken
    by the probe at the yes that ends the wait, before the line, which names it. `--expect tree TEXT`
    on keys, click, scroll and drag `--wait` (Settle::opt, so run -d does not take it): once the
    screen is satisfied, treewait::expect reads until --timeout from the watch's start, once at
    least, in the window the input went to (--window's, click --find's window or layer; none: the
    active one); not held: 124, "but the tree does not hold TEXT (instead: …)", and "sent all the
    same (the screen settled; 124 is about the tree)"; --json adds `expect` {tree, met, detail}. A
    window closing between the probe's pick and its read is gone, not a failure: the read's refusal
    is held back (say muted, fd 2 to /dev/null: win_lines writes there itself). The issue's own
    example, `--expect tree '"Dark mode" [checked]'`, was 124 after a click: the clicked box reads
    `[focused checked]` and the substring took states as printed, in order. So omabox-tree's --find
    (tree --find, wait tree, --expect alike) also matches a TEXT ending in `[STATE ...]` as a set:
    each named state among the line's (any case, whole words, so `checked` is never `unchecked`),
    any order, and the rest of TEXT held by the line before its states; a line the substring
    matched still matches. A read had omabox-tree's fixed 30 s `timeout`; with an app's main loop
    asleep a `wait --timeout 1s tree` took 6 s (libatspi's 2 s per call). Each read is now given
    the wait's time left (secs_left: 0.5 s at least, 30 s at most; tree::read_within, layer_read's
    SECS); one killed then is "did not answer in time (busy or hung?)", not held. Tests: t_wait_tree (GTK4: held, instead, --json, a window not
    there, --gone both ways, click --expect held and not, keys --json's expect, --shot, a closed
    window, `[checked]` against `[focused checked]`, a hung app within its second), t_tree (states
    as a set, in any order and case; as printed; `[unchecked]` not `[checked]`), t_unit_wait (the
    refusals), treewait.rs name_and_lines (secs_left).
596. **`drag` in a browser canvas draws** (2026-10-31, #323: absolute motion with a button held was
    reported as no drag there; finding 101 had tested foot only). Chromium 155 in a box, a page whose
    800x500 `<canvas>` draws a line on `pointermove` while a `pointerdown` holds (pointer capture)
    and counts every pointer and mouse event in its title: `drag --window` (10 steps) gave 1
    pointerdown, 10 pointermoves with `buttons` set, 1 pointerup (the mouse events the same) and the
    line in the shot; `--steps 1` one move with the button held, `--glide 500ms` 13; `pointer -- move
    down move up` (one absolute motion between press and release) a line too. Each `move` is its
