    no change. Not measured: Firefox (not installed here), a canvas app that wants several frames of
    motion before a drag starts (a threshold over time rather than distance).
597. **Chromium's tree, re-checked on 155: yes with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, and a better
    no without it** (2026-10-31, #323; another project's notes said Chromium gave no tree in a box).
    Chromium 155.0.8059.84, a box (AMD iGPU): with the flag, in a normal window and in `--app`, the
    whole tree (browser chrome, the page, a `canvas` by its aria-label) in 40 ms, as finding 244
    said. Without it, what it gives depends on IsEnabled when it starts: off (a box before its first
    `tree`) and it never joins the bus, and `tree` said "pid N is not on the box's accessibility bus
    (an egui/winit app on AccessKit ...)", the AccessKit reason, misleading here; on, and it joins
    with its frame only (finding 244's "frame and its title", which `tree` already notes with the
    flag). `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1` or `GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1` in its environment changes nothing:
    the flag is the only way. So the "no" was a Chromium started without it. Now the helper tells a
    Chromium or Electron process (a thread named `Chrome_IOThread`, which both have) off the bus:
    "pid N, a Chromium or Electron app, is not on the box's accessibility bus: start it with
    --force-renderer-accessibility". Seen: a box started before the helper was rebuilt kept the old
    helper (its bind mount holds the deleted file): `down` and `up` again after `make -C tools/tree`.
    Test: t_tree (Chromium without the flag, IsEnabled set off before it starts: said so, exit 1).
599. **A sibling subagent's `down` ended a box another was using, and nothing said who**
    (2026-10-31, #295; follows 88, 377, 411). A Claude Code session's subagents share its
    `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and its process (`CLAUDE_PID`): their shells carry no id of their own
    (checked: the same env but for PWD, the same parent), so finding 88's name and 93's agent are
    one for all of them. Agent A ran `up` in a scratch folder (`default-SESSION`); B saw the
    session's suffix in `ls`, took the box for its own and took it down; A's next command said only
    `no box '...' is up`. What omabox can tell apart is the agent session and the directory a
    command runs in, so it records those and says them: `up` writes box.json `session` (the 8
    characters, null outside a session; not for a jailed caller, whose box goes by its jail), each
    command's use (need_box, path, log, run, an `up` of a box up, the end of `up`) writes
    `SESSION<TAB>DIR` into the box's `used` file (its time is still the idle clock; the waits that
    keep touching it leave it as it is), `ls` prints `  started in ~/a (this agent session)` last
    under a box (`; last used in ~/b (...)` when another caller; `ls --json`: `session`), and a
    `down` (not the reaper's) of a box used in the last 10 minutes and started or last used by
    another caller (another session, none, or this one in another directory) says first `warning:
    box 'X' may be another agent's: started in ~/a (this agent session), used 40s ago; taking it
    down (its next command will say who did)`. It still takes it down (Diogo's plan for 1.1: warn,
    not refuse, inside the 1.x promise). The down leaves `.taken-NAME` (when, its session and
    directory; pruned after a day, removed by the name's next `up`), and the name's next command,
    where it said `no box 'X' is up`, says `box 'X' was taken down at 15:54:03 by an omabox down in
    ~/b (this agent session); start it again with: omabox up X` (and `run` gives no throwaway in its
    place). A box from before (no `session`) is not warned of. Limits: two subagents in one
    directory are one caller (only a per-agent id would tell them apart: none is exported), and one
    agent that `cd`s to a scratch folder for `up` is warned by its own later `down` from its repo
    ("may be"). Not done (choices for Diogo): refusing without `--force`; the "this session's boxes
    are ..." hints (need_box, #136) still name a sibling's boxes as the session's; `up` of a name up
    already does not say it was started elsewhere. Tests: t_unit_agent_session (a stand-in box: ls's
    line, the warning, the note from `windows -b` and `run -b`; all four fail on the old code),
    whose.rs (the warning's cases, the note, ls's line).
600. **`check run` always drove the whole scenario** (2026-10-31, #376). A project's scenario of 37
    checkpoints cost 2.5 min a run and 7-9 min with --approve, for a change to one screen; one long
    session spent 1.9 h in `check run`. Now `check run --only ID,GLOB` (repeatable; IDs or fnmatch
    globs, checked as ID characters plus `* ? [ ] !`) passes the list to the scenario as
    OMABOX_CHECK_ONLY (cleared when there is none, so an outer run's does not leak in), `check point`
    of an ID it does not name says "skipped, not in --only" and exits 0 having taken nothing (no
    wait, no shot, no box asked), and the new `check wants ID...` answers a scenario's "is this
    section wanted" (exit 0 any of them, always without --only; 1 none): the time is in driving the
    app to a screen, which only the scenario can skip. The comparison skips the baseline's
    checkpoints not named (counted, `N skipped (--only)`, `counts.skipped` and `only` in --json), so
    they are not missing. A check refuses (exit 2, before any box) a pattern matching none of the
    baseline's IDs, listing them: a typo would otherwise cost a run to learn. --approve --only drops
    only named checkpoints the scenario no longer takes, keeps the rest byte for byte, takes a
    window's largest speck from its kept checkpoints too (finding 363's rule), draws baseline.png of
    the approved ones, and keeps check.json when it says another setup than this run's (said: it
    stays true of the rest; a whole --approve brings all to this one). Chosen, where the issue left
    it open: a subcommand (`check wants`) beside the variable, since a glob list is awkward to match
    in bash. Tests: check.rs only_names_checkpoints_by_id_or_glob, only_checks_and_approves_the_named;
    t_unit_check (refusals, wants, the skipped point; they fail on the old code); t_check_only (a
    real run: a section skipped by `check wants`, a check of one, --approve --only).
601. **report.png was the same small sheet at any box scale** (2026-10-31, #402). check.py lays the
    report out for a model's look (finding 361: 1456 px wide, pairs at most 706x360, 14 pt), so the
    shots of a scale-2 or scale-4 box were scaled down into it and its text looked soft beside them:
    unusable full size in a README or a video. That default stays. `--report-scale N` (2 to 4, on
    `check run` and on `check diff --report`) draws a second file, REPORT@Nx.png (baseline@Nx.png
    and its pages baseline-K@Nx.png at --approve): check.py's same plan, laid out at 1 exactly as
    report.png (the same cards, crops and what fits), then every length drawn N times (an integer, so
    each exact): text at N x 14 pt, marks, strokes and corners, each crop resampled from its shot to N
    times its 1x size, so on a box of scale N a crop is at the shot's own pixels and on scale 1 it is
    pixel-doubled (`-scale`). At scale 1 check.py's arguments are byte for byte the old ones. Said
    after the report ("report at 2x: PATH (for people ...)"), `report_scaled` in --json. Chosen,
    where the issue left it open: an option, not an automatic report@2x.png on a scaled box (it costs
    a magick run nobody may want, and a scale-1 box's report for a video needs it too). Tests:
    t_unit_check (the 2x copy twice the 1x one each way, report.png unchanged, the overview's 28 pt
    and its page names; they fail on the old code); check.rs only_checks_and_approves_the_named and
    t_check_only (report@2x.png of a real check, twice report.png).
605. **A window shot failed "grim failed: it ended with status 139" while the window changed size**
    (2026-10-31, #387). Hyprland fails a window's frame copy (ext-image-copy-capture's `failed`)
    when its buffer changes size during it, and grim 1.5.0's handler for that prints
    `capture->output->name`, which a toplevel capture (`-T`) has none of: a NULL dereference, SIGSEGV,
    nothing said (the box's core limit of 1 byte keeps no core). The backtrace, from grim under gdb in
    a box (`ext_image_copy_capture_frame_handle_failed+28`, debuginfod-symbolized), confirms it; grim's
    main fixed it after 1.5.0 (155adb1, "Avoid NULL deref in
    ext_image_copy_capture_frame_handle_failed()"), where it ends 1 saying "failed to copy capture
    source". Reproduced: a float resized every 30 ms, shot with `-w`, failed 8 of 40 times. t_window's
    `--active` failures under the full suite were this: B had just been shown on workspace 5, alone
    there, and redrew at its new width during the shot. Now a window's grab (the priming one and the
    one kept) whose copy failed (139, or 1 with those words) is taken again, up to 3 more times 100 ms
    apart, its failed tries' words dropped; past them, the 139 is said as what it means. Not done: a
    `--zoom` window shot, whose status is magick's when grim gave it nothing. Tests:
    t_unit_capture_errors (a stand-in grim ending 139 once, three times: taken; every time: 4 tries,
    then said; a screen's 139: asked once), t_window_resizing (20 shots of a window resizing every
    30 ms: none fails; on the old code 4 of 20 did).
606. **A crashed Hyprland could be called hung while its exit was under way** (2026-10-31, #222's
    t_hyprland_crash under load). After a fatal signal (or gdb --watch passing one on) the process
    exits: its socket closes at the start, so the call that crashed it gets no answer, then it tears
    down its memory, its last thread in R or D, before the zombie. Sampled in a box: 49 ms R, 91 ms
    D, 152 ms R, gone at 189 ms, with `/proc/PID/stat`'s flags carrying PF_EXITING (0x4) throughout
    (0x40860c). hypr_lost took two looks 0.2 s apart at a Hyprland in R or D as one that runs, so an
    exit longer than that read "did not answer (hung?)": the likely cause (inferred, not caught in
    the act) of t_hyprland_crash's load-only failures (its gdb case, 1 of 14 loaded runs here; both
    crash checks in the 2026-10-20 runs). Now a Hyprland with
    PF_EXITING is going, not running: hypr_lost waits on, up to 10 s, for the box or labwc's line,
    and says it went down. Not reproduced on demand in a real box (the exit is too short here unless
    the machine is loaded); the unit test drives it. Test: hypr.rs
    hypr_lost_an_exiting_hyprland_is_going (exiting: went down, before and past 10 looks; running
    and not exiting: still hung; it fails on the old code).

## Dead ends (kept so we don't retry them; probes in `spike/dead-ends/`)

- Headless output inside the real Hyprland: shares seat/focus with the user; black-output bugs.
- Docker: user not in `docker` group (= root); image drift vs host packages.
- Qt offscreen: Qt-only, no shell/tray, clicks don't deliver.
- sway / weston / cage as the parent compositor: protocol versions (finding 2).
- Keeping labwc's lazy Xwayland off the host's abstract X11 sockets without a network namespace
  (finding 89): `WLR_XWAYLAND=/bin/false` or a missing path still binds the sockets, and host X11
  clients then hang or fail; copying the host's `/tmp/.X*-lock` files into the box does not hold
  them, since their pids look stale from the box's pid namespace.

The spike installed sway, weston and cage to try them as the parent compositor; omabox needs none
of them, nor wayvnc (finding 34). It needs labwc.

## Open

Bugs, ideas and pending work live in the GitHub issues; the reasoning stays here. Known gaps:

- Omarchy 4.5 on the host (#292, findings 415-423): the default stays workspace 9 (the first
  monitor's); `special:omabox` is offered for a place of omabox's own (finding 423). Boxes run no OWE
  daemon: no video wallpapers or intros (an opt-in `up --owe` for footage would be #309).
- 1.0.1 runs on Omarchy 4.0.x and 4.5 (finding 422); 1.1 drops 4.0 (#312): every 4.0-only spot
  carries `omarchy<4.5` (`grep -rn 'omarchy<4.5'`).

- Visual checks (findings 357-363, #252): a checkpoint's speck comes from its --approve runs (3):
  noise past twice what they saw (16 px at least; 8 where they agreed) reads as a change; only the
  bar's clock is frozen, so an app's absolute dates and "today" displays drift from run to run and are
  `--ignore`d (the preload library that pinned every process's clock is parked on the
  `parked/clock-preload` branch until a project needs it, finding 360); holes (finding 362) show
  only where the wallpaper is behind (a popup over a window hides them) and not where a gap opens
  onto the open wallpaper; an exploratory mode (an agent walking the UI, getting only flagged
  changes) is not built; not inside ai-jail.
- The aquamarine build step goes once Arch ships a release with #415 (`UPSTREAM.md`, → #48). A system
  aquamarine patched downstream with #415 is recognised by the symbol it adds (finding 246).
- More of the box's stack from a local build, per box, as `--hyprland` does (finding 116, issue #44;
  `--omarchy DIR` is done, finding 135; `--quickshell PATH` is done, finding 358): `--lib DIR`
  (library dirs ahead of the system's; `/opt/omabox/lib` comes first now) is parked until a project
  needs it (→ #81). A `--hyprland` or `--quickshell` build whose RUNPATH points outside its own
  folder finds those libraries on the host (`ldd` passes) but not in the box.
- Portals (findings 12, 148): ScreenCast needs PipeWire in the box (started by hand it worked; an
  `up --audio` box has it now, finding 313, ScreenCast there not rechecked); portal
  errors are not logged (dbus-daemon drops an activated service's stderr).
- AMD and Intel iGPUs, an RTX 4070 SUPER (finding 77) and an RTX 5070 Ti (finding 124: the full
  suite, nothing skipped, 2026-09-30) tested; other NVIDIA cards, multi-GPU and other setups: → #84.
- Marks (finding 85) are for peek only: an interactive box is not marked (no window of ours to draw
  in; an overlay would touch the real desktop; → #81). A peek that starts while a `click` is
  deciding whether to write can miss marks until it is opened again (the file removed under it; since
  finding 233 the box's other peek windows share the new file); not seen.
- The window confirm-close opens for a box kept running (finding 70) has no `render_unfocused`, so
  `shot` gets no frame from it while it is hidden (finding 90). The host could give it one: a Lua
  `window.open` hook matching the box's client, then `set_prop` and a re-check. Untried (→ #81).
- A jailed agent's `--plugin`, `--theme-dir`, `--omarchy` or `--hyprland` inside a project the jail
  hides a path in, and an `--overlay` of one, are still refused (finding 292): the broker reads them
  on the host, and an overlay's covers cannot be checked. Reading through the jail's own mounts
  (`/proc/PID/root`, no link followed, as jail_verify walks) would allow the first four.
